records.Description: This project provides for the installation of a pumping station at Union Reservoir and a pipeline to pump reservoir water to upstream delivery points. Phase one includes the pumping station and first segment of the pipeline to the Rough and Ready Ditch. Phase 2 is a continuation of the pipeline to a point west of Longmont to allow delivery of water to Lake McIntosh and the Oligarchy Ditch. A final phase will provide for delivery to Burch Lake and pumping capacity at that location. The project is not funded in the current five-year program.

records.Project: 2.0 MG Dakota Ridge Water Storage Tank
records.Description: A 2.0 million gallon water storage tank is needed to meet future demands in the P2 zone. The timing of the tank is estimated based on the proposed development in the area. The storage will allow the proposed 29th Street pump station P2 expansion to operate more efficiently rather than having existing pumps running continuously. This is anticipated to be a buried tank.

Programming and conceptual design were completed in 2014 for a new combined Public Works and Parks maintenance operations building. The conceptual design estimated the need for a 25,000 sf building on a 2-acre site. The project may also include a salt/sand storage area. The capital plan funds a feasibiility update in 2024 ($99,000) to evaluate colocating on the Marshall CDOT site. Funding of $675,000 is programmed in 2027 to begin design.
The County plans to rehabilitate the public bathroom facilities at Arapahoe Plaza 1610 and 1690.
This project will replace the roof on the CentrePoint Plaza county office building, 14980 East Alameda in Aurora.

This project will design and construct a new 6-15-acre neighborhood park south of 10th Street and west of 71st Avenue in accordance with the Parks and Trails Master Plan. These parks typically include a play space area and landscaping.

This project provides for the expansion of/addition to the fleet maintenance garage to create the additional repair bays needed to keep pace with the City's ever-growing fleet. The current facility includes 15 work bays. The expansion will allow for repurposing bays specifically for CNG vehicles that already exist and are used for heated storage for storm water equipment. An additional building will be constructed for the storm water equipment and to expand vertically with office space above the bays when needed.

This project includes design and implementation of a new outdoor fitness area, which has been a long-requested community need. It will require removal of the open air storage shed, reconfiguration and expansion of the east parking lot, construction of a new storage area for ice pavilion equipment, and installation of a brick monument at the northeast entrance to the park.

The Olde Course maintenance building is at the end of its life cycle and creates a hazardous workplace. The existing three-story building will be replaced with a one-story structure with additional cold storage.

Fire station #5, at 251 Knobcone Drive, has a number of significant deficiencies and is nearing the end of its functional life cycle. It lacks adequate space for a dayroom, kitchen and sleeping quarters, and has insufficient apparatus bays. The building has aging mechanical and electrical systems, plus deficient roofing, door hardware and overhead doors, and electrical systems.

This project provides for a new potable water storage tank, which will be needed as demand grows, to provide a volume of water to fight extended building fires, to help meet peak hour demands, and to provide emergency storage in the event there is an interruption of treated water delivery to the distribution system.

This project will remodel restroom facilities located below the historic gazebo. Architecture/design services will be needed to review the historic integrity of the building and to determine if the existing restrooms can be remodeled or if it will be necessary to construct a separate stand-alone facility for the park (possibly closer to the playground area).
This project provides for expansion of the service center to accommodate the growth of the Water, Wastewater and Power Divisions.

Several leaks have resulted. This project will repair the aging and failing portions of the concrete walls and will include replacement of all filter media, which is required every 10-15 years.
This project provides for fire facility improvements.

Additional studies will determine the optimal location of the expansion, which is currently anticipated to be an additional 4 mgd at the Ralston water treatment plant and an additional 8 mgd at the Arvada water treatment plant.

Phases 1 and 2 of this project have been completed. Future improvements will include a drying shed, vehicle wash bay, and site work/paving/utilities. To aid in the operational flexibility, mixed liquor return pumps will be installed.

The existing restrooms at Quail Creek Park have no running water and the toilets are vaulted over pits. Utility lines are now available. This project will rebuild and upgrade the restroom facilities.

No source of funding has been identified at this time.

A new city administration building would relocate some departments and council chambers from the Municipal Annex and Municipal Building, allowing for current needs and future growth for the next 20 years. The project is scheduled to be initiated beyond the five-year planning period.

The project will provide recommendations on land use, urban form and infrastructure needs to serve the redevelopment site.

records.Description: As we reported previously, the University of Colorado at Colorado Springs expects to advertise for design of an addition to the Engineering building. Carolyn says she has no specific time frame to advertise the RFQ.

We reported previously that Avon might require services related to a property the Town is looking at for a housing project called Swift Gulch Housing. They have already surveyed the property. Matt says they are still moving toward seeking architectural/engineering services, possibly as soon as this second quarter.
In about June or July, Lakewood plans to advertise for an evaluation and repairs at its 50-meter swimming pool.

Within the next few weeks, the School of Mines plans to advertise for architectural/design services for a project that will renovate an existing facility to convert it to an early childhood education/daycare center.
An RFP should be out now or very soon for architectural/design services for a 6,000 sf pre-manufactured storage building for the Sheriff's office.
Later this year or early in 2022, the District pans to seek design services for a remodel of the administration building.
This summer, Frisco plans to seek design services for a small scale storm water pumping vault.
Before the end of June, the Town expects to advertise an RFP for a Town Hall Needs Assessment.

This summer, Carbondale plans to issue an RFP for design of Phase 2 amenities at the Red Hill Trailhead. The project will include sign manufacturing. Eric says their plans are not yet finalized, so he has no additional information at this point.

The District has applied for a BEST grant this year. They should know the results in May or June. In the meantime, they passed a bond in November of 2019 for $16.4 million to be used as matching funds for the grant, if and when it is awarded.

The City plans to issue a design-build RFP for improvements at this park to include a playground and restroom/shelter facility. Andy says they are in the initial planning phase now, and he is not sure of the timing of the design-build RFP.

As we reported previously, the City expects to seek design services to replace its indoor pool facilites. They decided to use an on-call consultant for the Master Plan. An RFP for full design services should be issued in late February or early March.

records.Project: Old Town Hall Site Park Support Facilities
records.Description: As we reported previously, the Town expects to require consultant services for design of restrooms and, possibly, other park support and space for a community pavilion at the old Town Hall site. They have already contracted for removal of the old building. This project will involve programming, schematics and construction documents for at least the restrooms. Justin now says the RFP should be out soon.

As we reported previously, Boulder County Housing expects to require an architectural/engineering development team for a 400-home project called Willoughby Corner in Lafayette. Justin now says they expect to issue an RFP before the end of this first quarter.

As we reported previously, Mike expects to release an RFQ for a Master Service Agreement with one or more firms for Structural Design and Inspections. He now says he hopes the RFQ will be released in the next couple of weeks.

We reported previously that the City was in the design phase for a new 8 million gallon water storage tank to replace an existing 7 mg tank. They were considering using the construction manager at risk delivery method. Jim now says they have decided NOT to use the CMAR delivery method, but will hard bid the construction.

We reported previously that, at some point, the City would need assistance with the recertification of its levee system. Deacon says they do not yet know the full scope and he has no further details at this time. The scope and timeline are contingent on FEMA feedback, which they have not yet received. We will provide additional information when available.
As we reported previously, Boulder expects to advertise around the second quarter of this year for a new airport engineering contract. These contracts typically remain in effect for up to five years.

As we reported previously, Greenwood Village plans to issue an RFP for a study to ensure structural integrity of the bridge rail on the Yosemite Street bridge over I-25. Jeremy now says he expects a spring RFP.

Previously, Chuck said he expected that the Authority would issue an RFP later in 2021 for design of a new maintenance facility. He now says they decided to move the project up. It should be advertised now or very soon.

DIA now plans to advertise in February for on-call architectural/engineering services. Projects may include modifications and additions to existing facilities and systems, design of new facilities, building evaluations, studies, estimating, scheduling, reviews and construction administration. The SBE goal for the project is 30%.

records.Description: As we reported previously, DIA expects to advertise an RFQ for on-call architectural and engineering services, subject to an SBE Defined Pool. Projects may include modifications and additions to existing facilities and systems, design of new facilities, building evaluations, studies, estimating, scheduling, reviews and construction administration. The current schedule indicates a February RFQ.

records.Project: Greeley Rec Center Locker Room Remodel
records.Description: In the next couple of months, the City expects to issue an RFP for design of a locker room remodel project at the Greeley Recreation Center.
Sometime this month, Lakewood plans to issue an RFP for design of a "small" remodel project at the Head Start building.
Around mid February, Maiker Housing Partners plans to issue an RFP for owner's representive services for a couple of projects, to include predevelopment consulting.

The District passed a $4.9 million bond in 2019 to match a hoped-for BEST grant in 2020 for a replacement Junior/Senior High School. They were not awarded the BEST grant last year, but applied again this year. A firm has worked with the District on some preliminary planning. If the grant is awarded in May or June,, the Board will need to decide whether to continue to the design phase with the same firm or to seek competitive proposals.

Tom reports that the District will require architectural services for a golf course clubhouse project. He said he thought the RFQ had already been issued. The District advertises on BidNet, and the project is not advertised there at this point.
Within the next few months, Colorado State plans to advertise an RFQ for As-Needed Professional Services contracts. Lindsay says they have not yet determined specific scopes or schedules.
records.Type: AS, DR, MS, PK, PL, ST, SV

records.Description: In the next few months, Durango plans to advertise an RFP for the initial phase of development of the Community Park in Three Springs, to include design of 8 lighted pickleball courts, parking, restroom facilities and and off-leash dog area.
In the next month or so, the County plans to release an RFP for a feasibility and site master plan for a MakerSpace/Busines Incubator project.

The County's capital budget includes funding for a remodel of the Old Main Post Office building. Lee says they are not yet sure exactly what improvements will be included. A significant amount of money will be needed for roof, HVAC and window replacement improvements. We will follow up.
In the next month or two, Cherry Creek Schools expects to advertise for design of secure vestibules District-wide.
In the next 12-24 months, the District anticipates seeking design services for a Day Treatment Center.
In the next few months, the Town plans to advertise for architectural services for the renovation of an old building complex for public use.
The current plan includes a proposed new animal shelter, to be initiated after 2025.

This funding proposal considers a remodel of the current facility and new construction of a 26,000 square foot expansion on the south side of the museum, to increase exhibit space, classroom space and event space. The scope also includes a 200-seat auditorium, a children's area, a rooftop terrace, and a permanent exhibit showcasing the work of local artists. The project will address climate control and security needs that will allow the museum to broaden and diversify its exhibit offerings. The project is currently on the unfunded "Horizon Projects" list.

records.Project: Rodeo Grounds Per the Master Plan
records.Description: A master plan identified various improvements at the Rodeo Grounds. The project is currently unfunded.

Previously, the City hired a consultant to work on phased improvements at The Bay. They might need additional consultant services for future phases. Phase V includes a new lazy river, a water walk and new slides. This phase is scheduled to begin after 2025.

This project includes the design and construction of a new wastewater main and lift station to provide for future development along the Highway 402 corridor plus the southeast corner of the City's wastewater service area. The main will be designed to maximize gravity flow, but will need a regional lift station to collect wastewater. The City has agreed to provide wastewater service to the Olson Annexation upon development.

This project will renovate the Tantra Park shop for continuing use for Park Operations maintenance staff. The 3,000 sf facility, constructed in 1984, needs repairs and renovations to major building systems. No specific scope of work has yet been developed for the project.

This project will construct an addition to the ice arena's Zamboni room storage garage, to house the two ice resurfacing machines. It will include the installation of an ice melting pit inside the new addition. At this time, the project is unfunded.

This project provides for new community park development to meet park standards identified in the Master Plan. The plan indicates a need for a community park in the northwest quadrant of the community. The project provides for land acquisition, design and development of a 60 to 75-acre park. The City previously hoped to initiate the project in 2024. It is now included on the unfunded "Horizon Projects" list.
This project provides for replacement of building #2 at the City's Service Center. The project is not currently funded.

The City plans to complete the design of the Meeker Home park: Add a gazebo, pathways, a second bathroom, sculptural elements, outdoor artifact elements and landscaping to make it a more appealing destination in the University District. The project is currently unfunded.
This project provides for expanded library space. The City may pursue grant funding to partially pay for the project.
This project provides for restroom improvements at Rotary Park.

The Town's capital plan includes a project to construct a cinder de-icer facility for Public Works. The existing uncovered cinder pile leaches de-icer into the soil and drainageways when it rains or snows. The cinders also often freeze into large clumps making it difficult to load into the snow plows. A dome-style structure is planned at the location of the existing pile. It will be partially obstructed from public view.

The City has identified the need for renovations/improvements at the Englewood Recreation Center. Englewood has programmed $1.5 million in 2022 for the work. An additional $3.6 million may require a future bond issue. The 2022 project includes renovating the men's and women's locker rooms, entryway improvements, HVAC upgrades, and improved landscaping.

records.Project: WWTF - Odor Control Monitoring and Imp.
records.Description: This project will modify the inlet air ductwork within the dewatering building at the wastewater treatment facility so the new air ionization units are easily accessible for cleaning and other routine maintenance. Because of the large amount of air used to mix and aerate the stored primary effluent, a new biofilter will be required to treat the foul air from the basin.
The City has programmed funding in 2020 for renovations at Centennial Park, 4630 South Decatur Street, to include irrigation, shelters, restrooms, pathways, playgrounds and athletic fields.
This project provides for renovations at Cushing Park, 700 West Dartmouth Avenue. The City expects to seek bond funding for the project in the future.

This project will relocate and replace Fire Station 6, currently located at 1325 East 4th Street. The station was built in the early 1970s as a small, single-bay station. The location provides no opportunity to expand the station or to create a living situation that accommodates both male and female employees. A new location will need to be selected, and may include purchasing property. No source of funding has been identified to complete the project.

This project will renovate the City Park Administration building. The building, which adjoins the popular George L. Williams Pavilion, was originally built as a WPA project. The project is not currently funded.

The 18-acre park is located at the intersection of Eagleridge Boulevard and Outlook Boulevard. The project will include a 10-12 acre turf area for activities, a playground, shelter, landscaped gardens, parking, a dog park, outdoor basketball courts, trails, lighting and park signs. The City's capital plan indicates it would like to begin the project in 2021. However, it is currently unfunded.
Due to deteriorating pool lining, the swimming pool at Bessemer Park needs to be replaced. The City has indicated it would like to complete the project in 2022. However, at this time, it is unfunded.

This project will upgrade the current restroom and concession building at Community Park, allowing for additional year-round restrooms, equipment storage and improved concession areas. It will also repair the roof to stop leaks and add insulation to improve energy efficiency.

This project provides for renovations at Jason Park, 4299 South Jason Street. The park contains a pavilion, ballfields and courts, and an off-leash dog park. No funding is currently available. The City hopes to pass a future bond to finance the project.
This project provides for renovation of the Pirates Cover amusement park. The project is proposed in 2021 but is not funded.

records.Project: Interlocken East Park - Restroom and Shelter
records.Description: Broomfield has programmed funding to replace the Interlocken East Park restroom facilities and (upper and lower) shelters, which were constructed in 1985.
The solids dewatering capacity at the wastewater treatment facility needs to be increased by adding a third centrifugal dewatering unit.

This project will require a space needs study, then an anticipated remodel and expansion of the police and courts facility. Additional space is needed for Patrol supervisors, the community resource unit, the communications center, property room and evidence processing areas, and the Criminal Investigations Unit.
Kroh Park contains 38.54 acres, of which the lower 12 acres remains undeveloped. This project will develop those lower acres, and may include a dog park and parking.

Fire station #3, at 900 S. Wilson Avenue, was constructed in 1980. The building has a number of significant deficiencies and is nearing the end of its functional life cycle. The project was previously programmed in 2025. It has been moved to the "Horizon" list of unfunded projects.

This project provides for construction of a new 60,000+ sf recreation center in the northwestern section of the community. A 2015 Recreation Center Feasibility Study indicated that the City was well short of the recognized standard for recreation centers. Previously proposed in the funded capital plan, it has been moved out to the unfunded "Horizon Projects" list.
The Town has programmed future funding for new community and neighborhood parks.
records.Type: AS, DR, MS, PK, PL, ST

records.Description: This project provides for restroom facility improvements at the Elmwood executive course. The project is currently unfunded.
This project will renovate the greenhouse at Mineral Palace Park, located at 1500-2100 N. Santa Fe Avenue. At this time, no source of funding has been identified.
The City plans to design and construct a 2 million gallon clearwell, with piping and chemical injection, in tandem with the existing clearwell.
The City plans a program to assess 56 existing park structures, including docks and picnic shelters, restroom facilities, and concession buildings.
This future project provides for a new building and remodel of the existing service center building. Funding is anticipated beyond the current five-year planning period.

This project will implement enhancements at parks and facilities through the system. Currently undeveloped park sites such as Violet Park in north boulder and Eaton Park in Gunbarrel have planned amenities that need to be implemented to meet service levels of surrounding neighborhoods. The project may also include amenities at developed park sites, such as restrooms, ballfields, additional sport courts and play areas.
The City identified a number of desired projects that are not funded in the current capital plan. One of them is the renovation of Howelsen Lodge.
One of the larger projects desired but not funded in the current capital plan is development at Bear River Park. Current facilities consist primarily of a skateboard park.
This project would renovate the existing City Hall building. At this time, the project is not funded.
This project would construct a new septage receiving station. The capital plan shows the project in 2022; however, it is currently unfunded.

The City proposes a future project to replace the primary clarifier mechanism at the wastewater treatment plant. The project is currently unfunded, and may involve future debt financing. The capital plan indicates that the City would like to complete the project in 2024.
The City proposes a future project to replace the digester cover at the wastewater treatment plant. At this time, the project is unfunded.
The City proposes to replace the current Fire Station #1. Station 1 is the City's largest fire station, located at 425 West 7th Street. At this point, the replacement project is not funded.
The City has identified the need for a new branch library. At this time, the project is not funded in the 10-year program.

Adding a downstream storage reservoir would increase the City's water rights portfolio firm yield by providing a place to store reusable water sources when the exchange potential is limited, for later exchange when river flow conditions improve. The 1600 acre-foot reservoir and surrounding property downstream from the wastewater treatment plant were purchased in 2019. Design of necessary piping and a pump station is planned to begin in 2030.

records.Project: Active Adult Ctr. Front Desk, Lighting, etc.
records.Description: This project provides for front desk improvements, billiard lighting and a new outdoor entrance and courtyard shelter at the Recreation Center/Active Adult Center.
The City plans to construct a building over the existing tank farm at the Boyd Lake water treatment plant. The building will provide winterization to the existing alum chemical tanks.
The entrance and office area at the Union Colony Civic Center need to be remodeled to provide accessibility to the ticket windows and to increase the work area of the staff in this area.
This project will install three filter trains at the Upper Basin water treatment plant.
The City has programmed future funding for development/improvements at the Geer Natural Area, to include an elevated trail, shelters and restrooms.

In an effort to consolidate reasources and long-term storage of evidence, the police department entered into a memorandum of understanding with the Douglas County Sheriff's office in 2018. The agreement stipulated that all items of evidentiary value be transferred from the Town's property evidence room to the Sheriff's Property and Evidence Facility at 2865 Highway 85 in Castle Rock. This leaves approximately 1,700 square feet of usable office space that needs to be repurposed. The area requires remodeling, electrical upgrades, etc.

records.Project: Paul Derda Rec. Center - Outdoor Playground
records.Description: This project will install a public outdoor playground at the Paul Derda Recreation Center, designed for children from toddler through age 12, and will include a small covered area with at least one picnic table.
Broomfield plans to add rooftop photovoltaic solar panels and all associated infrastructure to the new Broomfield Community Center.
The City proposes a future expansion of the courts facilities at the Police/Courts building.

This project will address necessary rehabilitation of the brick structure at the Spruce and Pearl parking garage. Work will include replacing necessary bricks and addressing any structural issues that arise during assessment.

The County has identified the need for a new fleet facility. The current shop was built in 1938 and is in disrepair. Funding for a new facility is not included in the 5-year plan, as County leadership has not identified the project as a priority for replacement at this time.
The Town's capital plan includes proposed funding in 2022 to design and construct an expansion of the Town Hall.
This project will replace the old two-stall restroom at Dr. Rich Weiss Park. It will also remove and rebuild a wooden deck.

This project includes removal of the current building and construction of a new fire station built at the same location. The estimated gross square feet of the building is 21,667. The total cost estimate includes $16,250,250 for construction and $500,000 for land acquisition, plus a $1,625,025 contingency.
The City would like to complete boathouse improvements at the HARP (Historic Arkansas River of Pueblo) Gateway Center at Gateway Park. At this time, the project is not funded.
This City has identified the need for restroom upgrades at fire facilities. At this time, the project is unfunded.
The City has proposed funding to renovate the tennis clubhouse and bleachers at City Park. At this time, the project is not funded.
The County has programmed funding in 2026 for space planning for the detention facility (jail).
This project provides for a remodel of the Senior Center building.

This project provides for a new 500-750 thousand gallon finished water tank for the water treatment plant. The existing Mesa tank cannot be taken offline for servicing, and there is no backup should the Mesa tank fail. The new tank will allow for additional storage during summer flows, can be used with a built-in pump to recharge the clearwell, and can provide water for the fire training center.
The City's long-term, unfunded "Horizons" list of projects include a project to complete a North Transit Center.

The Olde Course clubhouse is near the end of its life cycle. The current building will be replaced with a new clubhouse facility, the size and exact location of which is still being determined. Staff is undertaking a feasibility study and is taking the project through preliminary planning processes. Following that, a design concept and updated cost estimates will be known.

Plate settler technology utilizes many plates (lamellas) situated at 45-55 degree angles, which increase surface area and expedite particle sedimentation. Plate settlers, with their affixed trough systems, allow for cleaning during operation with no interruption in process flows. Installation of plate settlers will result in higher quality settled water, which in turn will increase filter runs and save money, water and energy on filter backwashes.
The County has programmed future funding for design and construction of a food composting facility.
This project provides for master planning/renovation of suites at the Budweiser Events Center.

The Equalizer Project constructs new infrastructure to deliver water from the Poudre River to the Greeley-Loveland Irrigation Company ditch, and will secure options to purchase existing or potential gravel pits on the Lower Poudre near Greeley. This phase will construct the pump station and pipeline to a connection point at 83rd Avenue.

Storage areas in the Active Adult Center will be remodeled to allow for fitness classes. Large fitness equipment for the classes will be included in the project and mirrors will be added to the walls. The basement restrooms will also be remodeld. At this time, the project is not funded.
The restrooms at Centennial Pool are not ADA compliant. Design is required to meet ADA guidelines. The project is not currently funded.

records.Project: Active Adult Center Remodel Basement Restrooms
records.Description: The City needs to remodel the restrooms in the basement of the Senior Center to be ADA compliant. At this time, the project is unfunded.
This project will construct a 300 x 60-foot equipment storage, wash bay, restrooms and office facility. The project is not currently funded.

As demand grows in the Town's water distribution system, it will be necessary to add potable water storage to the system. This storage tank will provide a volume of water to fight extended building fires, to help meet peak hour demands, and to provide emergency storage in the event there is an interruption in treated water delivery to the distribution system.
This project provides for the addition of a fitness pad at Hamey Park, to be located next to the Firestone Trail.

records.Project: 23 Acres W. of Prairie Heights MS
records.Description: This project provides for visioning, design and construction of improvement on 23 acres west of Prairie Heights Middle School.

The City has programmed funding each year for four years for improvements at the water treatment plant, to include filter, chemical feed, flash mixer, softening, solids handling, taste and odor improvements, etc. Costs are estimated at $1 million in 2022, $2 million in 2023, $4 million in 2024 and $5 million in 2025.

records.Project: Raw and Potable Pump Station Imp's
records.Description: This project will rehabilitate aging infrastructure at the City's two raw and two potable water pump stations. Costs are estimated at $500,000 in 2021, $1 million per year in 2022 and 2023, $2 million in 2024 and $2.5 million in 2025.
Renovations at Jason Park will include irrigation, shelters, restrooms, pathways, playgrounds and athletic fields.
This project will complete restroom and concession improvements at Highland Heritage Regional Park.
The City's capital plan includes proposed funding in 2022 for a Fire Training Center.
This project provides for South Neighborhood Park improvements.
The City has programmed future funding to expand the pickleball courts at Centennial Park.
This project provide for expansion of the driving range and learning center development.
The City has programmed funding for 2023-2025 for rehabilitation of the airport terminal.

This park Improvement project will replace sun-damaged playground plastic components at the Recreation Center playground, pavilion and restroom improvements plus concrete repair and replacement at Founders Park, and tennis court replacement at Centennial Park.

Park improvements planned in 2023 include permanent restrooms at the amphitheater, utility connections and greenroom addition at Philip S. Miller Park; playground and court replacement at Castle Highlands Park; The Meadows Pond renovation near the Grange; and an alternate trail for Ridgeline Open Space at Wolfensberger.

This project will include demolition and disposal of the existing liner and mixing system; installation of a new mixing system designed to reduce air emissions/odors; and installation of a concrete floor to improve durability, life span and to improve dewatering and solids removal. During 2018, the wastewater treatment facility took the equalization basin offline due to multiple odor complaints.
This project provides for redesign and restructuring of the second floor employee workspace at the City and County building to accommodate efficient workforce growth, productivity and safety.
Beyond the current planning period, Broomfield plans to construct a new cemetery maintenance facility.

records.Project: Prairie Lakes Open Space Phase I
records.Description: The City plans to complete phase I improvements at Prairie Lakes Open Space.
This project provides for improvements at Benedict Park.
The City's capital plan includes proposed funding in 2024 for design of renovations at Parklane Park. Construction is not anticipated in the five-year program.
The City plans to design improvements at Central Community Park in 2024. Construction is anticipated beyond the five-year planning period.

A master development plan for the Museum would be an invaluable document that would provide a roadmap for future growth. It would include any adjustments that might be required by the Quail Campus master development plan. A well conceived master development plan will provide the city a tool for making decisions and for raising private funds. At this time, the project is not funded.

As we reported previously, Loveland plans to seek consultant services for design and construction documents for Willow Bend Park. Bryan says he hopes to issue an RFP in the spring for landscape architecture and civil engineering services.

Joe reported previously that, at some point, the College planned to create new space for the dental hygiene program. Earlier this year, he predicted that they would begin design in about the spring of 2021. Now he says, in light of COVID and the resulting state budget shortfall, the timing is unknown. The project will involve opening up existing space, and completing electrical and mechanical improvements. He says the "bones" of the building are in good shape.

As we reported previously, the City plans to issue an RFP for an alternative study and design for the Kossler-Boulder Canyon Hydro Penstock Rehabilitation project. Douglas now says the RFP should be advertised in the first quarter of 2021.

Previously, Douglas reported that the City anticipated a January, 2021 RFP for design of the Betasso water treatment facility disinfection capacity and corrosion control project. He now says they are in the process of "speaking with" six to eight engineering design firms.

Steve reported previously that the District might seek design services for a metal water tank. They had not decided whether to advertise or to give the project to a firm with which they are familiar. They now have decided to delay the project for a couple of years because it is connected to a pipeline project and, so far, not enough commercial construction is going on in that area to warrant the improvements.

The City plans to issue an RFP later this month or right after the first of the year for design-build services for three city parks. Improvements will include renovations of a skate park, three picnic shelters, a restroom, two playgrounds and one parking lot.
Carolyn reports that the University expects to move ahead soon with consultant services for its Career Center improvements.
In the next few months, Hayden plans to issue an RFP or RFQ for Owner's Representative services for the construction of the Hayden Center and Hayden Business Incubator.

In November, the District passed a bond for $94.315 million. They are already working with an architectural firm for some projects. In the next month or two, they expect to issue an RFP for Owner's Representative services.

The District passed a $94.315 million bond in November. Dr. Baugh reports that, while they have an architecture firm on board for some projects, they will probably need consulting services for delayed maintenance projects, an energy net zero project, housing projects, HVAC projects and "several more."
John reports that the College will potentially advertise for design services for a student center remodel project.
In the first quarter of next year, Longmont expects to dvertise for construction related services for water and wastewater treatment plants.

records.Project: Outdoor Adventure and Alt. Sports Master Plan
records.Description: In the first quarter of 2021, Denver plans to advertise an RFP for an Outdoor Adventure and Alternate Sports Masrer Plan. Work will entail a system-wide plan to look at opportunities for outdoor recreation and activation.

The District is currently in the selection process for an Owner's Representative for the Grace Best Educational Facility project. When we asked about plans for seeking architectural/engineering services, Bob reported that, once the Owner's Rep was selected, they would plan the remainder of the project.

Previously, Andy reported that the City expected to issue an RFP for demolition and design-build of a prefabricated restroom with one male and one female facility. The project also included a chase room large enough to eliminate the on-site shed to provide additional storage security, and a 20 x 40 shelter as an unattached but proximate shade structure. Andy now says funding is proposed in 2021 for locker room design, but not for construction.

As we reported previously, the County expects to advertise an RFP for architectural services for design of a new Transit Operations Center (bus and administration/office facility). Dale still expects to advertise the RFP this fall.

As we reported previously, the District applied for a BEST grant this year for a new high school to replace the existing John Mall secondary school. The state listed the project as #45 on the priority list. Of the total cost, the state proposes to provide about $11.75 million. The District hopes to pass a bond issue in November for the matching funds for next year's round of project approvals.

Previously, the City advertised for design-build services for the Public Safety Training Center Incinerator Site-Ready project. In April, Bryn informed us that the project was subsequently cancelled and would be reissued at an unspecified later date. She now says she still does not have a schedule to re-issue the RFP.

The wastewater treatment plant is nearing its design capacity. The wastewater master plan will outline specific improvements to accommodate future growth, while meeting State discharge permit requirements. The cost shown here is a conceptual estimate and will be fine-tuned in the future. In the next few months, the Town plans to seek consultant services for design and construction management for the expansion.

The Town advertised in April for design services for a new lift operations center. They subsequently selected OZ Architecture. They now expect to issue an RFP around the end of October for Construction Manager/General Contractor services.

We reported previously that Maiker Housing Partners in Adams County anticipated issuing an RFP for a renovation project. At this point, we have no more specific details. Sarah now says she estimates they will send out the RFP within the next couple of months.
In August, Bill reported that an RFP should be issue in the near future for a Facility Capital Needs Assessment for the Town of Eagle. He now says the project has been postponed until next year.

The City has advertised its RFQ to pre-qualify construction contractors for the new North Boulder Library project, for which they expect to break ground in the first quarter of 2021. Qualifications are due by 4:00 Tuesday, October 27. For details and to download the RFQ, go to www.bidnetdirect.com , log in and select City of Boulder.

DIA's latest schedule calls for an October RFQ for various on-call engineering tasks which may include studies, designs, contract documents, bidding services, construction administration, testing and reporting, scheduling and cost estimating, and surveying. Projects may include the rehabilitation of pavements, electrical and lighting systems rehabilitation, drainage, etc. Landside projects may include civil design, roadway design, hydraulic and stormwater design, traffic studies, electrical design, etc. The Division of Small Business Opportunity Office has established a 25% MWBE goal for this opportunity.
records.Type: AS, CM, DR, GT, MS, ST, SV, TR

records.Description: Depending on the success of a grant, Carbondale may issue an RFP in the spring for playground improvements.
An RFQ should be out now or very soon for Airport Engineering services for the City.
An RFP should be out now or very soon for On-Call Architectural Services. Services will be needed primarily for Parks facilities.
Brian reports that the City hopes to issue an RFP in the next few weeks for on-call roofing consulting services.

An RFQ should be available as soon as today for a Consultant Short List for 2021-2022 projects at Douglas County. They seek qualifications in eleven disciplines, which are listed in the RFQ. The request should be posted on the BidNet website.
records.Type: AS, BR, CM, DR, EV, MS, SW, ST, SV

records.Description: We reported on this project previously. Jim now says they are finalizing the RFQ and he expects to advertise soon for design-build services.

Previously, Jeff reported that it was possible, but not definite, that the City would seek consultant services this year for design to remodel the City Hall building. In June he said the project was on hold due to budget uncertainties caused by the COVID19 situation. The latest information is that they are working with a UCD professor who is having his class prepare preliminary drawings. Eventually, they will need to hire an architect for final design; however, that will likely not occur before the first quarter of 2021.

As we reported previously, the County's 2020 capital program includes a project for architectural/engineering/design services for the expansion of the community senior center in Frisco. At this point, the project remains on hold.

We reported on this project previously. DIA plans to advertise in August for design, construction, operation and maintenance of the modernization of the Aircraft Deicing System. The project will provide for receipt, storage and distribution of deicing fluid, and collection and disposal of spent fluid. The Division of Small Business Opportunity Office has established a 10% MWBE goal for the project.

records.Project: East District Bucking Horse Park, etc.
records.Description: We reported on this project previously. Brian now says Fort Collins will issue the RFP in mid August for construction manager/general contractor services for a new East District Bucking Horse Park and Maintenance Facility.
The City expects to advertise soon for civil design and geotechnical engineering for an additional water tank above Garfield County Airport.
The University of Colorado Colorado Springs may require consultant/design services in the next few months for a project to re-roof the library building.

Within the next week or two, Jefferson County expects to advertise for design of the Quincy Phase 2A roadway widening project. Mike says this segment will be largely focused on the construction of a mechanically stabilized earth (MSE) wall.

This project provides for land acquisition, design and construction of a new recreation center in the Westwood neighborhood of Denver. An RFP for professional services is anticipated before the end of this quarter.
Kris reports that the Town is about to post an RFP on the BidNet website and on the Town's website for a Facilities Master Plan.

As we reported previously, the Aspen/Pitkin Airport's plans include the design and construction of a new terminal. The current schedule still indicates that the project will probably be initiated after the completion of a runway or taxiway project. However, it is possible, depending on how and when the federal funding is made available, that this project could move ahead of the runway/taxiway project. You can follow the planning process at asevision.com. At this point, everything is on hold, especially with the COVID issue.

As we reported previously, Loveland Housing expects to advertise for architectural/engineering services for design to renovate 72 existing apartment units at the Brookstone Apartments. Darcy now says the project should be advertised for design in June or July.

We reported on this project previously. The City plans an RFP for design of the Eagle Bend pump station improvements project. The project will include evaluation of the station pumps, demand and pump sizing, and the conditions of the building systems. At this time, the project remains on hold.

As we reported previously, Aurora expects to seek design services for improvements to the Griswold solids handling system, which will include design of new sand drying beds and a backwash recovery system. The timing of the RFP is still uncertain.
We reported on this project previously. Aurora plans to advertise for design of a SCADA Backbone tower for coverage of south Aurora water infrastructure. The RFP timing is uncertain.

We reported previously that it was possible Snowmass Village would issue an RFP for architectural services to design the remodel of one of its housing developments. At this point, Betsy indicates that the project is on hold for the time being.
The City's capital program for 2020 includes a project for design for sizing, and civil engineering for a potable water storage tank. At this time, the project remains on hold.

Steve reported that the District had decided to apply for a BEST grant this spring for a new elementary school. He recently indicated that the grant was "still alive" at the state level, but just barely. Even if awarded, the District would have to cover approximately half of the cost of the project. He believes it unlikely they could pass a bond for the District's half of the cost. Consequently, he doubts they will pursue any major building projects for the next two years or more.
As we reported previously, the City plans to advertise for geotechnical and structural analysis of Arvada Dam. Jacob now says the RFP was delayed, but should be released in the next few weeks.

We reported on this project previously. Kris says the National Guard has received funding for pre-design and design services for a 6,000 sf new building to house maintenance shops and work bays at Fort Carson. They expect the structure to be a pre-engineered metal building. She anticipates they will advertise sometime this month for architectural/engineering services.

As we reported previously, the District expects to release an RFP for a playground at Rouse Park, for which they have received a GOCO grant. Kyle says they have received the necessary contracts from GOCO and are putting the RFP together. They have no specific release date.
In June, the City plans to issue an RFP for Solar PhotoVoltaic Design and Construction for commercial projects.
The City plans to issue an RFQ in about a month for studies and design for a new substation, needed to handle growth. The substation will meet a requirement of the City's NPDES discharge permit.

records.Project: CO Air Nat. Guard Readiness Ctr. Ft. Lupton
records.Description: An RFQ should be out now or very soon for architectural/engineering services for the expansion and alteration of the Colorado Air National Guard's Readiness Center in Fort Lupton.

The southwest county service center was developed in 2000-2001. With the growth in the area, additional facilities will be required to house all of the County functions necessary to serve the area. The County proposes that an additional administration building be constructed on the Southwest Weld County Service Center site. The capital plan includes $1 million in 2024 for initial planning and design. Construction would occur in 2025 or beyond.
The current capital plan includes funding for improvements at O'Brien Park North.

This project provides for a two-story, 50' by 80' building for use by the police department for vehicle and evidence storage. The first floor would also be used for storage of large items (such as vehicles) waiting for evidence processing. The second floor would be secure storage for long-term evidence and department property.
This project provides for improvements to the sedimentation tank at the water treatment plant.
This project includes a Town Hall space needs assessment, with the potential for property acquisition, design and construction of a new facility.

Currently, the Sheriff's office does not have a dedicated training center. Besides classroom space, the department needs a facility to provide the dynamic training that is required for firearms, emergency vehicular operations, K9 training area, SWAT and explosive ordnance and demolitions training.

The Community Corrections Program has been operated by private contracts since the early 1980s. In 2008, the Commissioners decided to construct its own Community Corrections facility. A 30,000 sf building was completed in 2010. The site can accommodate a doubling of the facility size at some future date at a cost estimated at $5 million.

The Southeast County Service Center was acquired as a used building in the early 1980s. With growth in the area, a new 20,000 sf building was constructed in east Fort Lupton. Another new 20,000 sf building is proposed in 2021.
This project will construct new grandstands.
The Town plans to complete phase III improvements to the festival site in 2023.
The Town has included a project in its five-year program to upgrade the mechanical wastewater treatment plant.
This project provides proposed funding in the coming five years for increased water storage capacity east of the Uncompahgre River.
The Town's 10-year plan includes a project to expand the existing or build a new Public Works facility.
Beyond the current ten-year planning period, Ridgway anticipates expanding its Town Hall.

records.Project: Town Hall and Comm. Center Imp's
records.Description: This project provides for improvements to the Town Hall and Community Center buildings.
In its five-year program, the Town has allocated funding for a new/additoinal community room.
The Town's longer term plan includes a project for full plan implementation of Heritage Park, to include Visitor's Center improvements.
The City's capital plan includes proposed funding for design and construction of a new parking structure.
The Town plans a future project to install a charging station and metal storage building for the electric trolley. The building is planned to be constructed on Events Complex land.
This project provides for First Street Bridge lift station improvements.
The County proposes a multi-phased modernization of the jail. Phase 1 would include administrative, support and public lobby upgrades.
Phase 2 of the County's proposed jail modernization project would address Booking, Intake and Release area upgrades.

The County proposes to design and construct a new alternative sentencing facility, to include work release, community corrections, day reporting and, possibly, community workers' housing. The facility would replace the Longmont Community Treatment Center and, possibly, the Boulder Community Treatment Center.

The County's proposed projects for the next 1-5 years include a full renovation of the Boulder Community Treatment Center. The project scope is dependent on the solution of the alternative sentencing facility. The facility could be repurposed for other community housing or program needs.

This project would expand the administration area and add one bay to the shop processing and flammable storage areas to meet current space shortages. The County would like to complete the project in the 1-5 year time frame.

Expansion of the emergency operations center will address current space shortages. The project has several options on scope and scale, from a small interim expansion to a large long-term expansion. The County would like to initiate the project in the coming five years.
This project will construct an expanded tipping floor and extend the building to add covered baled material storage. The County has included the project in its 1-5 year time frame.
This project provides for a mixed-use development to support construction of 100 garage parking spaces and a 10,000 sf office park. The Housing Authority will be the lead agency.

records.Project: Open Space and Transp. Complex Addition
records.Description: This project proposes an addition and/or renovation to the complex's offices to address overcrowding in the building. The County would like to initiate the project in the 1-5 year time frame.
This project provides for renovation of the existing DTC hearing room to increase capacity, address ADA issues, and upgrade the AV system.

The County has identified the need for renovation of the Assessor space to separate public and private areas, to create efficiencies in the work spaces, and to update life safety egress for the whole building.

This project will add 500 square feet to the holding area to increase capacity. It will also construct a locker room and fitness room for employees. The project could be phased as two separate projects.
The County plans to renovate the Finance space in the west wing to accommodate increased staff and to create a more efficient use of the space.
The City has programmed funding beginning in 2023 for preservation of the Old Powerhouse.

In the 5-10 year time frame, the County would like to replicate the "hub" concept for Health and Human Services and Workforce Boulder on one site in the City of Boulder. A location is yet to be determined.
The County would like to consolidate the transactions functions (Assessor, Treasurer, Clerk and Recorder) with the Health and Human Services complex to meet future vision objectives.
This project will implement the fairgrounds master plan to modernize the business plan and to update facilities.
This County plans to modernize the facility through renovation of the jail, courts, mental health, medical and support spaces.
This project will construct an addition to the Open Space Transportation Center to include bays, a large equipment vehicle wash, and administration conference/training rooms.
This project will replace the 30+ year-old road maintenance facilities that do not meet storage and maintenance needs of current equipment and material storage.
Based on 20th District Court docket growth projections, the County plans to renovate the old clerk of courts area to create two new courtrooms.
Constructing an automated car wash for Road Maintenance would maximize efficiency, save time and staff and free up bays.
This project would provide covered storage for vehicles such as ATVs, firefighting equipment, etc.
The current volunteer center at Walden Pond is a 25-year old modular building in poor condition. The County proposes a "B" frame replacement.
This project would provide covered storage for the Sheriff's department for vehicles and equipment, including ATVs, for wildfire and search and rescue. The facility would be located in Nederland.

Consolidating Permits with the Health and Human Services and Transactions Complex would meet future vision objectives: To consolidate Land Use, Transportation and staff from Public Health/Environmental Health.

This project would relocate maintenance operations services currently on Alaska Avenue to available land at the Open Space Transportation Center, to consolidate transportation services and to free up the Alaska site for alternate use or sale.
In the 5-10 year time frame, the County wants to develop a site for integrated services in Lafayette, including Headstart and other services.

As we reported previously, the County expects to advertise for architectural services for design of a remodel of the existing Summit County Emergency Operations Center (911). The timing has not been determined.

As we reported previously, Loveland expects to seek a firm for design and installation of the Willow Bend universally accessible playground. Bryan now says they hope to begin a consultant selection within the next two months.
Previously, Justin reported that Avon planned to advertise this spring for design to remodel the cabin at Nottingham Park. He now says he expects the project to be delayed a couple of months.

Previously, Matt reported that, sometime this year, the Town planned to seek consultant assistance for planning and design service for a replacement of the Town Hall. The old Town Hall is scheduled for demolition. We were unable to connect with Matt prior to this Update. We will provide additional information as soon as we receive it.

In February, we reported that the District planned to advertise sometime this year for design-build services for a family sports center to replace the existing air dome. Brett now says that, due to the COVID 19 pandemic, the project is on hold.

We reported previously that, sometime this year, the District planned to seek design-build services for a Littleton Golf and Tennis facility to replace the existing clubhouse and air dome. Brett now says the project is on hold due to the COVID19 pandemic.

The County's capital program for this year includes a project for architectural/engineering/design services for a new search and rescue facility in Frisco. Dale says they hope to advertise in the second or third quarter. However, the timing is uncertain due to the COVID19 virus situation.

Chris reported previously that it was possible that the City would be looking at a city hall building as funds were budgeted to explore options this year. The lastest information is that the project is on hold until they get a better understanding the economic impact of the current COVID19 situation.

As we reported previously, Northern Water plans to issue an RFQ for on-call engineering services. The contract(s) will remain in effect for three to five years. Professional services will include structural, pipelines, geotechnical, etc. Jobs will vary in size and range. Examples of jobs identified to date include grading/concrete design on the campus back patio, design of a canal trash rack, and assessing/designing mitigation for aging siphon infrastructure. Landon now says the RFQ is delayed until they can have an informational meeting with potential firms.

records.Project: Centennial Training Ctr. Hail Damage Repair
records.Description: Previously, Kris reported that the Army National Guard/Department of Military and Veterans Affairs expected to advertise for damage investigation and preparation of contract documents for hail damage repair at the Centennial Training Center to include roof repair/replacement and HVAC equipment replacement on three buildings. Kris now says the project has not been advertised and, at this point, it is unclear whether or not it will be.

We reported previously that this project might or might not be advertised based on prior design expertise. The status remains the same. Work will include expansion of the fire water supply system for four aviation buildings at Buckley Air Force Base in Aurora. Improvements will include water storage tank expansion and reconfiguration/addition of fire service supply lines. Professional services will include survey, geotechnical investigation and civil design.

Subject to change due to the coronavirus situation, the City anticipates issuing an RFP within about a month for an aquatics consultant to complete preliminary plans and a feasibility study in preparation for a master plan for an indoor aquatics facility.
In May or June, the District expects to issue an RFQ for architectural/engineering services for design of a CTE center.

Winter Park anticipates an April or May RFQ for architectural design services for a Lift Operations Center. Conceptual design of the site calls for two structures: 1) A bus parking/wash bay/administration building (500' x 150'); and 2) a heavy fleet maintenance facility (300' x 80'). The project will be CDOT/FTA funded.

records.Project: New Vehicle Storage Building at HAATS
records.Description: The Department of Military and Veterans Affairs plans to advertise an RFQ soon for design of a new vehicle storage building at the High Altitute Army National Guard Aviation Training Site (HAATS) in Gypsum. The facility will be approximately 6,000 square feet. They will require survey, geotechnical investigatoin, site planning and building design services.
As we reported previously, Fort Collins expects to issue an RFP for design of a new parking garage at 245 Mason Street. An RFP should be issued soon.

records.Project: Phase 2 Water Line and Storage Tank
records.Description: As we reported previously, Erie plans to seek consultant services for design of the Phase 2 water line and storage tank project. Kris now says the project is on hold pending the acquisition of easements.
Geraldine reports that is it possible the University will require architectural/engineering services in the next few months for renovation of the baseball/softball complex.
Before the end of February, Pagosa Springs expects to issue a RFP for design and engineering services related to development of 21 acres for multiple uses, including parks.
records.Type: AS, DR, MS, PK, PL, ST

records.Description: Fort Collins expects to issue an RFP soon for a City Hall Master Plan Refresh.
The City expects to advertise soon for a Park Maintenance Shop at 3000 Environmental Avenue.

This project provides for refurbishment and replacement of facilities at the West Senior Center, to include HVAC, electrical and plumbing systems. It also will renew all surface finishes including carpet, paint and ceilings, and will provide improvements to restrooms and add a fire sprinkler system. It will replace roof sections as required.

This unfunded project would provide for a second full-service recreation center. It would include a competitive swimming pool with a large spectator area, a leisure pool, an NHL size hockey rink, and other recreational amenities defined by a Competitive Pool and Ice Rink Feasibility Study. A branch library may also be included in the facility.
This project will expand the existing backstage area to accommodate larger groups of performers, their equipment, related storage, and loading dock access.

Currently, the main entry to the auditorium has one set of doors. A vestibule will be added to the main entrance to prevent the weather from disrupting the interior lobby climate and to provide greater comfort and security for patrons.

This project will include four lighted tennis courts, a lighted basketball court, 2 shelters, 2 lighted baseball/softball fields, an inline skate rink, parking lot with 115 spaces, landscaping and irrigation. The capital plan includes $500,000 in 2022 and $4,490,000 in 2023. Additional funding required beyond 2024 is estimated at $2,113,226.

This project will fund the demolition of the Great Western Reservoir Water Treatment Plant at 112th & Simms. The plant has been out of service since 1997, and the City has no future plans to use the existing building.
This project would design and construct a tank (Lowell and Sheridan) for reuse water. The reuse water would serve the development in the northern portion of Broomfield.

Previously, the City hired a consultant to work on phasing improvements for The Bay. This project provides for design and development of construction plans, then construction of phase IV improvements. This phase will add improvements to the leisure pool, new slides and new pool deck drainage.

In accordance with a contractual agreement, this project will design and construct a 10-acre neighborhood park in the Promontory neighborhood. Design will not be initiated until the developer reaches contractual obligations of 450 homes.

This project will replace the Water Resource Recovery Facility's secondary digester floating cover. The cover has tipped and failed on several occasions in recent years, taking the system offline and limiting its ability to handle gas and interrupting wastewater treatment.

Various improvements are recommended to address current conditions, including building envelope, general interior construction components, mechanical systems, plumbing systems, and electrical systems within the site. The City has programmed design funding in 2024. Construction would occur beyond the five-year planning period.

The administration/office portion of the water treatment plant was built in the early 1980s and has not had a major upgrade since the original construction. The proposed improvements would include remodeling the existing offices, break room and bathrooms, and repurposing a portion of the east chemical building into conference space.

The current restroom facilities at Bronco Park are decaying due to high amounts of vandalism. The facility also has deficiency issues with plumbing and other aspects due to aging equipment. This project will replace the existing restroom facilities.

This project would design and build commercial grade park restrooms to replace the facilities currently offered inside the youth enrichment facility. The existing restrooms have been repeatedly vandalized due to a lack of typical public restroom features such as vandal resistant fixtures and timed door locks. The facilities are currently unavailable due to extensive damage.

The City plans to add a second, ADA accessible, "family" restroom in the City facility at 519 4th Avenue. The building is used for Community Services programs and activities. The project is currently unfunded.

Major upgrades include protection from the wind. Probable solutions include covers, floating and stationary barriers. Work will include design and construction of a cover, gear box and weir adjustments for the west clariflocculator. Plans include design of the cover, gear box and weir adjustments for the west clariflocculator in 2021, and installation of the cover for the west basin in 2022.

records.Project: Park S. of 10th St. and W. of 71st Ave.
records.Description: This project provides initial funding to construct a 40-acre community park consisting of: playground(s); picnic shelter(s); a recreational activity site and open turf/play area; athletic fields for practices; and off-street parking. The site will also include a permanent restroom and other amenities as the final site and community needs would allow, such as a pond, non-potable irrigation, lighting, sidewalks/trails, native areas, landscaping and trees.

The capital plan includes funding each year to serve as a pay-as-you-go financing mechanism toward the future construction of a replacement municipal court facility, or an alternative such as the acquisition and renovation of an existing facility. $2.9 million was appropriated previously. A total of $3 million was programmed in 2019-2020. The capital plan also includes $1.5 million in 2021, $1.5 million in 2022 and $1 milion in 2023.
This project provides future funding for fire station renovations. Specific locations and improvements will be identified as the year gets closer. Consultant services may or may not be needed.
Future funding is programmed for aerobic/anoxic capacity expansion for 25,000 lbs. biological oxygen demand (BOD) capacity at the Bid Dry Creek wastewater treatment facility.
The City's capital plan includes proposed funding for replacement of the Northridge water storage tanks.
This project provides for a clear well redundancy and tank conversion option to finished water at the Northwest water treatment facility.
This project provides for master planning of the recreation center campus. Design and construction of improvements will be considered after the planning process is completed.

records.Project: ADA - Rec. Center Locker Rooms Remodel
records.Description: This project will include a complete remodel of the men's and women's locker rooms, to include new sinks and counter tops, toilets and urinals, shower stalls, seating/benches, and new lockers. It will add hand dryers and GFI outlets. New flooring will be made of non-slip materials in all areas.

records.Project: Brush Creek Pavilion Park and Playground
records.Description: This project provides for park and playground improvements at Brush Creek.

records.Project: Community Park Ball Field Complex Imp's
records.Description: This project will update backstops, dugouts and score shacks at the Community Park baseball/softball fields, and outfield wing fences to John Shaw Field.
The County has programmed funding for tenant improvements to the Department of Motor Vehicles facility at Lima Plaza.
This project will complete phase 2 tenant improvements at the warehouse clerk and recorder offices.
The Town has programmed $250,000 in 2022 to begin work on Timnath Ranch Park. Additional "desired" funding is included in the capital plan at $2.5 million in 2023 and $300,000 in 2024.
The Downtown Superior master developer will build civic space for the Town. This project includes design and construction of tenant improvements, including furniture, fixture and equipment.
One of the City's desired but unfunded projects in the current capital plan is the construction of an indoor pickleball facility.
The City has identified the need for a Recreation and Teen Center. The project is not funded in the current capital plan. The cost estimate shown here includes land costs.
This currently unfunded project would develop a new sports field complex. The cost estimate includes the cost of land acquisition.
This project will renovate the 30-year-old playground, pavilion and basketball court at Lonesome Pine Park.
The District plans to remove and replace the playground at Bobcat Park.
This project will construct a playground, pavilion and basketball court at Centennial Ridge.
This project will renovate and replace the playground and pavilion at Cherry Park. The District anticipates receiving grant funding for the project.
This project provides for renovation of the 27-year-old playground at Cornerstone Park.
The District plans a project to renovate the lobby and control desk area at the Goodson Recreation Center.
This project provides for pool renovation at the Goodson Recreation Center. It will primarly address hot tub and pump room concerns, and explore enclosing some patio area.
This project will convert the two racquetball courts at the Lone Tree Recreation Center into one multi-purpose fitness studio with mirrors, a sound system and closet.
The District's capital plan includes a project to develop a new regional park in Ridgegate East.
The City proposes phase 1 development at Eagleridge Park. The project is shown in 2021-22 in the capital plan; however, no source of funding has been identified.
The Town hopes to acquire and retrofit a facility for a community center.

records.Project: Holding Cell/Sally Port at Town Hall
records.Description: This proposed project would construct a holding cell/sally port at the Town Hall.
This project calls for expansion and relocation of various Public Works facilities.
The Town has programmed funding to expand/relocate the water treatment plant. At this point, the project is not funded.
This currently unfunded project proposes one or more water tanks at the West Interchange/CR215.
The Town's capital plan proposes constructing two new wastewater lift stations. At this point, the project is not funded.
This project proposes to retrofit existing wastewater lift stations. No source of funding has been identified.
This currently unfunded project proposes to upgrade Cottonwood Park with restrooms, a pavilion and a new stage.
The Town has proposed to construct a new multi-field sports park. At this point, the project is not funded.
The Town has proposed to develop a new events center. At this point, no source of funding has been identified.

The Town has proposed to design and construct a new event venue, to provide options for concerts and other large events, for the benefit of residents and tourists. No cost estimate has yet been provided.

This project provides for additional stabilization efforts at the historic town waterworks facility. State Historic Preservation grants are anticipated to help complete this multi-stage effort. Phase I occurred in 2018.

The retaining wall on the east side of Webster Lake needs to be replaced. Many of the wall caps have been removed and/or broken, and cannot be replaced as the material is no longer manufactured. Additional drainage and slope issues will be addressed when the wall is replaced.
This project provides for the disposal and replacement of the indoor arena at the Fairgrounds.
The City has identified the need for a future additional administration building. At this time, the project is included on the unfunded "Horizon Projects" list.

records.Project: WTP Filter Building Concrete Wall Repair
records.Description: Filter Building 2 at the water treatment plant provides half of the filtering capacity for the City. The concrete housing the filters has aged and portions have become soft, degraded, and experienced isolated leaks. This project will repair the aging and failing portions of the concrete.
The capital plan includes funding for upgrades to the wastewater treatment plant's dewatering building.
The County plans an expansion of the administrative office building.
This project will construct Laramie River Employee Housing improvements.
This project will renovate the campground at Carter Lake.
This project provides for design and construction (rebuild) of the wastewater treatment plant central plant.
This project will construct a small sheriff sub-station in the north end of the Valley. The facility will be capable of hosting 2-3 deputies at one time.

The airport terminal parking lot needs to be replaced to address drainage, to improve snow removal and to improve customer experience. Customers would like the option of covered parking. A parking cover could be built using solar PV panels. The renovated terminal will use geothermal heating and cooling or ground source heat pumps (GSHP).

The Crested Butte shop was built in 1985. Many systems and building components are past their expected useful life and some are failing. Replacement and renovation are necessary to maintain efficient building operations. A multi-year approach is recommended starting with the envelope and then moving to electrical and mechanical systems.

A visual inspection and structural evaluation of the existing barriers along Yosemite Street adjacent to the bridge over I-25 indicate portions of the railing are showing signs of deterioration and are in need of replacement.

The existing three primary clarifiers were built in the 1960s and 1980s. The next phase of plant improvements will address the most critical up-front aspects of the treatment process. The project will include replacement of the influent pumps and motors, primary clarifier mechanisms, and primary sludge and scum piping, valving and pumps. It will also construct two new gravity thickeners and a new gravity thickener pump station, plus upgrades to the primary treatment electrical.
This project will construct a new Fleet Maintenance facility at the Service Center, to maintain the growing city fleet.

records.Project: New Community Park S. of 10th, W. of 83rd
records.Description: The City plans a new community park in an area south of 10th Street and west of 83rd Avenue. The City has agreed to purchase approximately 38 acres. Development of the park is anticipated beyond 2024.
The City has programmed future funding for a new police station.
This project provides for a remodel of the third emergency operations center/dispatch area at the County Justice Center, located at 4000 Justice Way in Castle Rock.
This project provides for a restroom addition at the multi-purpose barn north at the Fairgrounds.

records.Project: Paul Derda Rec. Ctr. - Climbing Wall Space
records.Description: Broomfield plans to remove the climbing wall from the Paul Derda Recreation Center and to repurpose the space into a multi-use area that can be used more effectively by patrons and programs.
This project wil add a 2- to 5-year-old (preschool) playground play structure to most appropriately fit the available area at East Park in Interlocken.
The City has proposed funding beyond the current planning period for a new branch library building.
This project proposes a new maintenance facility building at Broomfield County Commons.
This project provides funding for design of phase 2 improvements at the recreation center. Construction funding is not included in the five-year capital plan.

records.Project: ACJC Misc. Op., Maint. Bathroom, etc. Imp's
records.Description: This project will complete various operational, maintenance, bathroom and safety upgrades in Courthouses 1 and 2 at the Arapahoe County Justice Center.
This project provides for additional security measures in the lobby of the detention facility.
The County has programmed funding for land planning for the Justice Center.

Improvements to the wastewater treatment facility will meet water quality standards, extend the life of the plant, and reduce operating costs. The capital plan includes $3 million in 2021 for design of improvements that will be recommended as the result of an alternatives analysis. Construction is proposed in 2023; however, at this time, construction funding has not been identified.

The Town plans to remodel the restrooms at Nottingham Park. The existing restrooms are due for remodel because of their location in the park and the ongoing vandalism that occurs in the facility. The remodel will incorporate vandalism-resistant fixtures and security features. A design RFP should be released in the spring.

We reported previously that Pueblo planned to seek civil engineering consultant services for an evaluation of the cemetery, to include looking at needed repairs and upgrades to curbs, walls, etc. Steven now says it may be closer to the end of 2020 before the project is initiated.

Previously, Stephen reported that Front Range expected to seek design-build services for Longs Peak Rooftop Unit (RTU) and Roof Replacement at the Student Center on the Larimer Campus. He now says the project scope has been reduced and he does NOT plan to advertise for architectural/engineering services.
