He will not use the design-build approach, but will advertise the roof and mechanical parts separately for construction only.

As we reported previously, the City expects to seek consultant services to help develop the East Boulder Subcommunity Plan recommendations and implementation plan. Services may range from architecture and engineering to economic analysis, housing and transportation. At this point, Kathleen says she has no further information about the scope or schedule. Additional information is available on the City's website at https://bouldercolorado.gov/planning/east-boulder .

As we reported previously, Denver plans to issue an RFP for design of Greek Theater improvements at Civic Center Park, as part of the Elevate Denver bond program. Mike now says the RFP should be advertised in the second or third quarter of the year.
As we reported previously, during the first quarter of 2020, the District expects to issue an RFQ for design and oversight for inlet and outlet structures for a lined gravel pit.

The District passed a $125.5 million bond issue on the November ballot. They have hired RLH as their owner's representative. They have also hired a CM/GC for a high school renovation and probably a middle school renovation project. Previously, Bridgette reported that they would advertised for a/e services for a new high school and for elementary modifications. Now they say they will use an architect under a longer term contract.
In the spring, Steamboat Springs expects to advertise an RFP for design services for hangar development at the airport. The project will include moving a fuel parking area.
As we reported previously, Pueblo expects to advertise for design-build services for a concession stand/restroom project at Minnequa Park. Steven now says the RFP should be out as soon as next week.
We reported previously that Pueblo expected to advertise for preliminary design services for an addition to the Ice Arena. Steven now says the RFP should go in the next few weeks.

We reported on this project previously. The City plans to issue an RFP for design of playground improvements at Inspiration Point Park, 4901 Sheridan Boulevard. We were unable to reach Mike prior to this Update to confirm the timing of the RFP.

Earlier this year, Deana reported that Canon City expected to re-issue an RFP for a pre-campaign analysis of the Royal Gorge Area Rec/Aquatics Center project. The project is now called the Royal Gorge Area Rec/Aquatics Center Next Steps Feasibility Analysis. An RFP is now anticipated in November or December.

We reported previously that the University expected to advertise for design services for roof and window replacements at the Hasan School of Business building. An RFP should go out in the near future.
An RFP should be advertised very soon for design/build services for the Mountain Campus Experiential Learning Center.

Previously, Scott reported that that the City might need a new parking structure. He now says it appears they will pursue a public-private partnership, whereby a private entity will control the design and construction process, then turn the facility over to the City at some point.

The College is in the process of hiring architectural/engineering services for the Applied Technology Campus Expansion and Remodel project. They are currently reviewing proposals. Previously, they indicated they would probably use the CM/GC delivery method. Tracey now says they have decided to hard bid the construction.
Mike reports that it is possible, but not definite, that the School of Mines will advertise in the next few months for design of the Innovation Hub building.

records.Project: Stadium at Pine Creek High School
records.Description: In October or November, the District expects to issue an RFP for design-build services for the stadium at Pine Creek High School.

Jacque reported that the District was looking at doing an Engineering, Procurement and Construction (EPC) contract. However, she did not specify for what project. We have since tried to contact her for additional information but have not reached her or received a response. We will follow up.

We reported previously that Longmont expected to issue an RFP for a new neighborhood park called Fox Meadows. This 9-acre park may include picnic areas, playground, restrooms, dog exercise areas, small skate park areas, shelters, pathways, sports courts, multi-use fields and landscaping. We were unable to connect with Kathy prior to this Update to obtain an updated schedule.
We reported previously that Boulder expected to post an RFP for site selection and design services for a new Fire Station #3. Sam now says they still expect to issue the RFP later this summer.

As we reported previously, Carbondale plans to advertise an RFP for an Aquatics Facility Master Plan. The Town has a pool that was built in 1970 and needs renovation or replacement. The consultant will conduct a master plan containing a financial feasibility study, community outreach feedback, present and future program analysis and a conceptual design. Eric now says the RFP should be issued about mid August. They will advertise the RFP on their website at www.carbondalegov.org .

As we reported previously, the University expects to advertise for a master plan update. A couple of months ago, Carolyn said and RFP should be issued in the next few months. She now says they are not on schedule, but it should still be coming up.
We reported on this project previously. Jen now says that the Town will probably advertise an RFP before the end of August for design of a park pavilion.

We reported previously that Longmont expected to advertise for on-call engineering and construction management services for water and wastewater treatment projects. The ad has been posted and proposals are due by 2:00 Thursday, August 22. The notice and full RFP are available at www.bidnetdirect.com . Log in and select City of Longmont.

In the next month or so, the Authority expects to seek consultant services for a lift station evaluation, plus design and construction oversight of an electrical and controls building. Emily says this project needs to be expedited so it is possible they will not advertise it publicly.
The District has been approved for a BEST grant for the replacement of the West Park PK-2 Elementary School. Wendy reports that they expect to issue a design RFP in the next few months.

DIA anticipates an August RFQ for on-call architectural and engineering services. The scope of work varies on an individual basis that may include, but is not limited to, facility assessment, modifications and additions to existing facilities and systems, and design for new facilities. The Division of Small Business Opportunity has established a 17% level of M/WBE participation for this opportunity.

As we reported previously, Aurora plans to issue an RFP for design and construction documents for relocation of the existing boat rental area at Aurora Reservoir. The RFP should be out in the next few weeks.

Previously, Emily reported that the Authority expected to issue an RFP for final design of a third clarifier at the Lone Tree Creek Water Reuse Facility. In April, she indicated that they could decide to sole source the project. She has now confirmed that they did, in fact, decide to sole source it.

The District's current schedule calls for a mid-June RFP for Owner's Representative services for the new PK-12 school facility, which will also include athletic facilities. The District passed a $5.5 million bond in November of 2018 for the project, which is subject to additional funding through a BEST grant. They have been included on the short list for funding this year. Final approval is scheduled June 12 or 13.

DIA expects to seek design services for multiple structures and deferred maintenance projects. Services may include facility condition assessments, design and construction drawings, etc. for structural repairs, mechanical (HVAC) upgrades, and other technical related services. They expect to award three contracts not to exceed $1.5 million each. The project includes a W/WBE goal of 5%.

As we reported previously, this project will design and construct a new sanitary sewer lift station to serve portions of the city tributary to the Ashcroft Draw basin, including St. Michaels. An RFP should be issued in the next month or two.
records.Type: AS, CM, GT, MS, SW, SV

records.Description: As we reported previously, the City's capital plan includes funding for a library project, either a new building or a remodel. They have selected an Owner's Representative for the project, which is now predicted to be a 16,000-20,000 library building plus outdoor areas. Sarah now says she hopes to issue an RFP for an architectural/engineering/design team in April or May.

The Olde Course clubhouse facility is approximately 60 years old and is in marginal condition. The lack of appropriate seating and storage space detracts from the golf experience. Infrastructure of the building, including the roof, cooling system and drain tiles are deteriorating. This project proposes to replace the building. Bryan reports that an RFP should be issued in the summer for conceptual design services, pending Council approval to move forward.

We reported previously that the City planned to advertise an RFP for design, procurement and installation of a replacement playground at Dwayne Webster Park. Bryan now says they expect to issue this RFP in mid summer.
Previously, Dennis reported that Thornton expected to advertise an RFQ for on-call roof inspection services. He now says the project has been cancelled.

DIA now anticipates an April RFP for engineering support on an on-call basis for the Automated Guideway Transit System (AGTS) or Airside concourse train system. Many projects will include support for system capital improvements, such as maintenance facilities, train storage, train relocation, and other expansion projects. The Division of Small Business Opportunity has established 15% M/WBE goal for this project.

Ann Marie reported previously that the District expected to issue an RFP for Design/Engineering services sometime this month. She now says the project is delayed, but she hopes to be able to provide additional details in the next month or two.

The Littleton Center is 41 years old and has many systems and operational issues. The building has failing HVAC and electrical systems, and operations are affected daily from a customer service standpoint. This project updates several office areas to enhance customer service, improve work operations, upgrade safety and security, and allow for further improvements in the future. Future projects will address other areas, including the council chambers. The City may seek design services later in 2019.

As we reported previously, Sterling expects to issue an RFP for architecture services for a new exhibition building/storage space at the museum. At this point, Wayne says the RFP should be out by the end of April.
As we reported previously, CSU plans to advertise an RFQ for architectural/engineering services for the South Campus Animal Resources Facility. The RFQ should be released as soon as this week.

As we reported previously, Avon expects to release an RFP for a study of the West Main Street area, which includes a vacated fire station (351 Benchmark building) and the Town Hall. The goal is to develop a design once the two buildings are demolished, which may not happen until 2020. The Town wants to extend the Main Street mall from Mikaela Way to Lake Street. The budget for the initial effort is $50,000. An additional $175,000 is anticipated in 2020 for design. Justin now says the project is on hold for at least 60 days.

The City expects to advertise in the next couple of weeks for design-build services for a new playground at West Lincoln Park. They advertised for the project previously and, that time, included a picnic shelter. They subsequently cancelled the original solicitation. They have decided to delete the shelter from the project.
Steven reports that it is possible, but not definite, that the City will require architectural services for some office space renovations. At this point, he describes the project as "up in the air."
In the next month or two, Northglenn plans to issue an RFP for an update of the Water Treatment Plant Master Plan.
An RFP should be issued soon for design-build services to remodel an existing storage building to provide additional laboratory testing space for the District's in-house lab.
Sometime this summer, Avon expects to issue an RFP for a water quality vault design.

As we reported previously, Denver expects to advertise for design to replace the Police District 5 building, which is located at 4685 Peoria Street. The current schedule still calls for a design ad in the first quarter of 2019. Dana was unable to confirm this prior to this Update.

As we reported previously, the City's bond program includes funding for ADA improvements/corrections mandated by the Department of Justice. They paln to issu an RFP for design based on Phase 2 findings to implement ADA improvements. The project should be initiated in the next month or two.

We reported previously that Winter Park expected to release an RFP for construction manager/general contractor services for a new Public Works Operations faciity. Gerry now says the RFP should be out now or very soon.
As we reported previously, Pueblo Water expects to issue an RFP for design-build services for a hydro power plant. Seth now says the RFP should go out within the next three months.

Previously, Bryan reported that the City planned to advertise an RFP for design, procurement and installation services to replace the playground at Derby Hill Park. He now says they need to complete some drainage improvements before they can install the new playground. They are close to putting the drainage improvements out to bid. Soon after these improvements go out to bid, they plan to issue the RFP for the new playground.

As we reported previously, Loveland plans to advertise for design, procurement and installation of a new playground to replace the existing playground at Namaqua Park. The RFP should go out in the next couple of weeks.
As we reported previously, the School of Mines plans to issue an RFQ for design services for a new parking garage. The RFQ should still be coming up soon.
As we reported previously, the College expects to issue an RFP for design-build services for a remodel of the East Wing on the Westminster campus.

We reported previously that the College planned to advertise for project management/owner's representative services for the Whalen Gymnasium Expansion and Renovation project. The RFQ/P should be out now or very soon.

As we reported previously, the City plans to advertise for design services for playground improvements. They have budgeted for one or two this year, with the specific locations to be determined by the Parks Board. Allan still hopes to issue an RFP in February.

The Department of Public Safety expects to seek architectural and engineering services for some port of entry improvements in Trinidad. At this point, Angela is unable to provide additional details regarding timing or specific improvements. We will follow up with her.
In the next couple of months, Louisville expects to issue an RFP for design of a new dump station at the wastewater treatment plant. The project will also include site lighting.

Alyssa reports that the City has submitted a grant applicatkon to History Colorado for a historic residential survey. They will not know whether or not the project will move forward until they find out about the grant. We will follow up.
This summer, Winter Park expects to seek architectural/design services for a Transit Facility.

The Downtown Development Authority requests proposals no later than 3:00 Thursday, February 21 for Architectural services for interior renovation of the Opera Galleria atrium. A MANDATORY pre-proposal meeting will be held at 1:30 Wednesday, February 6 in the Opera Galleria building, 123 N. College Ave. Questions are due by 5:00 Tuesday, February 12 and should be directed to Todd Dangerfield. The RFP is available by going to www.bidnetdirect.com , logging in, and selecting City of Fort Collins.
Lochbuie expects to advertise soon for General Engineering Services. Essentially they are looking for a firm to serve as the Town Engineer.
records.Type: AS, CM, DR, GT, SW, ST, SV, TR, WR

records.Description: The Jeffco Housing Authority should have an RFP out now or very soon for architectural consulting services for an existing property.
In the next few months, Greeley expects to advertise for design of the Poudre Ponds slurry wall and site restoration.
The City's capital plan includes proposed funding in 2021 ($400,000) and in 2023 ($400,000) for replacement of sewer lift stations.

This project provides for the development of the Ute Creek golf course maintenance facility, including offices, employee areas, a heated repair area, cold storage, site improvements, and utilities. Last year, the capital plan included this project in 2019. The new capital plan lists the project as "unfunded."

This unfunded project provides for the design and renovation of the lobby, women's locker room, men's locker room, and public restrooms. It also adds family changing rooms at the pool. This project removes the original concept of completing a new addition to the building (hence the reduction in the cost from the previous estimate of over $4 million).

This project consists of demolishing and replacing the existing building with a station meeting all current building, fire, ADA and energy codes plus providing the facilities required for efficient and effective emergency services. At this point, the project is not funded in the five-year capital program.

Lift station B is a major component in the sanitary sewer system since it is the second largest lift station in the system. A facility assessment would provide recommendations and prioritize necessary improvements to extend the life of the facility. Repairs will be made based on the recommendations of the assessment.

records.Project: Goldsmith Gulch (Orchard Rd. at Silo Pk)
records.Description: The City's capital plan includes proposed funding for design and construction of a drainage structure to eliminate the overtopping of Orchard Road at this location. Funding is also included to replace the deteriorating retaining wall adjacent to the path on the north side of Orchard Road. The schedule will depend on funding from Urban Drainage. Urban Drainage will likely manage the design process.

This project would improve the library entry plaza, including a redesigned fountain/water feature. It would also enlarge the plaza area by removing the current raised grass planter and adding seating and new plantings.

The City proposes to replace the existing fire station #2 with a new building on the west end of the same site (Reservoir Road/23rd Avenue). The new station will accommodate the two existing fire companies and include three apparatus bays, a training room and space for storage. The project is currently unfunded.

records.Project: Lake Arbor Golf Course Maintenance Bldg.
records.Description: This project will replace the Lake Arbor Maintenance and Storage Buildings at 8600 Wadsworth to meet ADA requirements and to meet City building standards. The existing building is a steel pre-fabricated building that is not ADA compliant, has only one restroom and no formal office areas. It is heated with electric baseboard heaters, is poorly insulated and energy inefficient. The first step will be a complete site assessment plan.

This project involves expansion of the Prairie Waters Project north campus. The work involves phased expansion of the campus from a firm capacity of approximately 8.5 million gallons per day (MGD) to 40 MGD in future years. The project includes drilling additional wells and construction of related appurtenant facilities.

The existing Fire Station #2 building was built for all male crews and the day room and kitchen are too small for the 3-4 firefighters who are assigned there 24/7. The apparatus bays have asbestos ceilings and are too small for training on modern fire apparatus inside the building. The building also does not meet current building codes and provides inadequate storage. The site has inadequate parking and driveways on a blind curve. There is no room for expansion without encroaching on neighbors or street right-of-way. This project provides for either renovation or replacement of the station. It is currenly unfunded.

Recommended repairs and replacements include the building envelope, general interior construction components, mechanical systems, plumbing systems, and electrical systems within the site. The project is not funded in the current five-year program.
The City plans to replace filter valve actuators, filter media, filter valves, residual lagoon asphalt and upgrade backup power with automated processes.
This funding is for an infrastructure evaluation and gate replacement as recommended in the Source Water Master Plan.
The City has programmed future funding for an expansion of the Recreation Center. The current capital plan shows funding of $250,000 in 2023. Additional funding will be required in the future.

records.Project: New Ridge Basin Water Treatment Plant
records.Description: The City plans to construct a new 14.0 million gallon-per-day Ridges Basin water treatment plant.
This project provides for an extension of the Children's library. The extension will be designed specifically for newborns to five-year-olds.
This project provides funding for a long-term permanent solution for the safe, secure and temperature controlled storage of evidence and found property.
The County plans to rehabilitate the bathrooms at the Courthouse and to add one restroom in the basement of the Arapahoe County Justice Center.

The City plans to replace the existing 1995 Alfa Laval DS 706 high solids dewatering centrifuge unit and Schwing sludge cake pump located in the dewatering building on the south plant at the Water Pollution Control Facility. Equipment evaluation, selection and design are scheduled in 2021 with procurement and installation of the new centrifuge in 2022.
The City has programmed funding for future park development. Specific improvements will be identified as the year approaches.
This project provides for improvements at Havana Park, located at 10600 E. 11th Avenue.
The City anticipates constructing a new First Creek sewer lift station.

The City has programmed future funding for additional Lower South Platte water storage at Everist. The project will include storage purchase and infrastructure necessary to use Everist storage as part of the Lower South Platte/Prairie Waters integrated resource system.
This project would replace the antiquated and undersized Parks Shop and Administrative Offices. The project is currently unfunded.

A two-story addition of 20,000 gross square feet will include a number of new components. Potential new facilities include: An elevated two-lane walking/jogging track; cardiovascular and circuit training equipment; two racquetball/handball courts; a bouldering area to augment the climbing wall; a play room for younger members of the community; a babysitting room; a multi-use room to accommodate group fitness activities and pickle ball games; and supporting facilities such as a massage/fitness evaluation room, stretching areas and storage area.

Fire Station 7, located at 840 Pueblo Boulevard, will be renovated or replaced. It is a single-bay station lacking in function and with no opportunity to create male and female accommodations. It may be possible to expand to the north, which would require purchasing land from Elmwood Golf Course. Operationally, it would make more sense to relocate the station.
This project provides for renovations, repairs, and upgrades to the existing Fire Department training facility. The project will address both structural and functional needs.

The water storage tanks have been in operation for about 21 years and will require some major rehabilitation work, including sandblasting and recoating/painting. This work has never been performed in the past.

The retaining wall on the east side of Webster Lake needs to be replaced. Additional drainage and slope issues will be addressed when the wall is replaced. The permanent restrooms also need to be repaired. While the building structure itself is in good condition, plumbing and mechanical issues create a need for a lot of maintenance.
A new well will be needed to maintain fire flows as West Gunnison is developed.

This project will complete the final phase of the Huntington-Caley master planned improvements, to include secondary trails, Caley Pond walkways, sculpted berms, an informal lawn, a natural play area, shade structures, and a parking lot.
This project proposes to replace two fairway restrooms to meet current ADA standards. Restrooms currently are open only during spring and summer months. At this time, the project is not funded.

The City plans to implement general park improvements at Centennial Park to improve vehicular and pedestrian access and to reduce overall access points off 23rd Avenue. Improvements will include roadways within the park connecting parking areas, new walking paths, improved access to the neighborhood to the west, and landscaping improvements. New site amenities for Centennial Pool include sand volleyball, shade structures and an expanded lawn for patrons. A master plan was completed in 2017.
records.Type: AS, CM, GT, PK, ST, SV

records.Description: This project will construct three or four medium to large pavilions for covered shelter, and associated pathways and ADA accessibility at Island Grove Regional Park, near the Aven's Village playground area and softball field.

The City's capital improvement plan includes an unfunded project for master planned improvements at Centennial Park, including upgrades to Butch Butler Field restrooms/concessions, site lighting, additional pathways, and swimming pool upgrades.
records.Type: AS, DR, GT, MS, PK, ST, SV

records.Description: This project provides for a site or sites to be developed to house Water and Sewer construction crews and their equipment.

This project provides for a major remodel of Fire Station #4 on Heritage Road. Living quarters with additional space are required and a major overhaul of the second floor is also needed. The apparatus bays will need some modifications, including new doors and windows for energy savings. The current facility (built in 1983) presents some safety concerns regarding housing additional people and will need to be brought up to current building and fire codes.
Expansion of the aquatics area of the Golden Community Center would include two additional lap lanes, a lazy river, and a therapy pool.

The City proposes the future design and construction of about 20,000 square feet to house the Golden History Center. The History Museum has outgrown its current aging and insufficient facility. The new facility would ideally include a kitchen, multi-use program space, and a theater and/or other spaces that could provide additional revenue opportunities not currently available.

The redevelopment of the museum space on the north side of the creek was recommended in a 2011 Clear Creek Master Plan. Once a proposed project of moving the History Museum to the south side of the creek is completed, redevelopment of the north side is proposed to create urban terraces and the placement of a small concessions building at that location.

This proposed project would be a major step in redevelopment of the park. It includes redesign and construction of a new building, including new restrooms. The existing playground and shelters would be replaced.

The Bachman property is located in the southwestern part of the city. It has been left vacant with the intention of developing a new neighborhood park. This project is proposed to plan and develop the new park.
records.Type: AS, DR, MS, PK, PL, ST

records.Description: This project provides for a pavilion at the Peninsula Recreation Area.
This project provides for rehabilitation of the 7 million gallon water storage tank at the College Mesa water treatment plant.

records.Project: CR 8 Lift Station and Force Mains
records.Description: This project will design and construct the Northeast Broomfield Lift Station and force mains as shown on the North Park Utility Plan, to serve the northeast area of Broomfield. This area currently has no sanitary sewer service.

Temporary repairs have been completed, including a face rehabilitation and repairs to the reservoir inlet structure. Both the inlet structure and the outlet structure require full rehabilitation/replacement.

This project provides for development of gravel pits and infrastructure to support Kirby Dersham and Challenger Reservoirs, part of the Lower South Platte water supply system. The infrastructure is expected to include a pump station, slurry wall and interconnect projects.
The County plans improvements at Mann Lakes.
This project funds roof replacement and repair projects at various City facilities. Consultant services may or may not be needed for these improvements.

A remodel of the interior of the library will add meeting rooms, study rooms, space on the second floor for public computers, and access to public wifi. The project also includes restroom remodels, improved security, updated library technology and improved staff work spaces. The project is not funded in the current five-year program.

records.Project: Coffman St. Mixed Use Dev. Parking Garage
records.Description: A new structured parking facility would replace the existing surface parking lot on the east side of the 500 block of Coffman Street. The garage would include approximately 80 City/Downtown Development Authority public parking spaces along with additional parking for Boulder County, parking for an affordable housing project and for office/commercial space.

The City has identified the need to expand the vehicle storage, garage storage and parking for the Police department. The project will include 40 outside parking spaces for trailers and vehicles, plus six large garage bays for the Mobile Command Vehicle, SWAT truck, SWAT bearcat, bomb trailer and crime scene trailer. The facility could be located north of the existing police building. The cost estimate includes $400,000 for construction and $4,000 for art.

The Town proposed a project in the 2019 capital plan to initiate design for the demolition of the existing Town Hall. The Council delayed the project, moving it out to 2020. The project will demolish the 1980 portion of the facility and leave the addition that was constructed in 2007 to support special event operations and to house IT and utility infrastructure for the park.

With the addition of the Rendezvous Event Center and expanded trail system, the Town wants to address the need for additional spaces fo the parks, events and trails programs. This facility would be used for storage of event items and equipment, and provide work space for the parks and trails crews. Design, surveying and engineering are programmed in 2020 with construction expected in 2021.

The Northwest Water Treatment Facility has been in operation for 17 years. The plant uses a specialized water filtration technology called membrane filtration as the primary means of treating water for potable use. Three of the eleven racks of membrane modules have reached the end of their useful lives. This project will replace the three racks and certain supporting instruments that help to control the filtration process.

A previous master plan indicated that replacing the 50 year-old Semper water treatment plant woud be more cost-effective than rehabilitating the existing plant. The city hopes to pass a bond in 2019 for over $56 million for land and easement acquisition, process selection and pilot testing to serve as the basis for final design. Design and permitting will follow using a multi-year phased implementation. The capital plan proposes future funding of $125 million.

records.Project: Water Treatment Facil's Chem. Systems, etc.
records.Description: The City has three potable and reclaimed water treatment facilities. All three require various repairs and replacement of assets as part of their normal operational life. This project includes repairs and/or replacements of pumps, sludge collection systems, concrete, instrumentation, controls, electrical systems, chemical tanks, and chemical feed systems. Miscellaneous process improvements may also be included.
The five-year plan includes proposed future funding for renovation of the administration building at City Park.
This project provides for capacity improvements at the wastewater treatment plant.
The District anticipates an expansion of the North water reclamation facility.
This project provides for Canyons water storage tank improvements and pipe section with the flow control valve.
This project provides for Ridgegate water storage tank improvements.
The District anticipates the need for a 5 million gallon reolacement of the Butterfield water storage tank in 2026.
The District anticipates an expansion of the Rueter-Hess Water Purification Facility.

Driven by multiple factors including the creation of the Development Center, city growth, and efficiency concerns, the space at the Municipal Building needs to be re-allocated to accommodate current and new departmental staff. This re-allocation will require renovation of portions of the facility. The City has programmed $252,000 in 2021 and $504,000 after 2023 for various renovations.

This project encompasses several improvements: Morning Drive Pump Station ($2,284,010), which will be upgraded to resize facilities to meet current and future needs; Southwest Booster Station ($289,880), a new station at a location yet to be determined; a 3.5 MG storage tank at 43rd Street ($707,420); and a 2.0 MG storage tank at Dakota Ridge ($10,234,010), which will allow the proposed 29th Street pump station P2 expansion to operate more efficiently.
As part of a plan for water treatment plant expansion projects, the City plans to replace the components of the #2 sedimentation sludge collection station.

The Phase 3 expansion of the water treatment plant will increase capacity from 38 to 48 million gallons per day. The project will be driven by growth so the timing is uncertain. The primary improvements needed to increase capacity include the addition of a new flocculation/sedimentation building, eight additional filters added to filter building A, and additional solids handling capacity (sand beds or ponds).

This project includes a major renovation of the existing water treatment plant administration building, which was built in 1980, plus renovation of portions of the former chemical building. The improvements will include new office space, a conference/training room, new break room, new restrooms, and other miscellaneous improvements.

The existing wastewater treatment plant administration area is in need of updating. The flooring and wall covers need to be replaced and the old (and no longer in service) SCADA anunciator panel and associated wiring need to be removed.

In 2017, a conceptual design was completed for a proposed museum and visitor center building and improvements to the existing building. The proposed 2020 funding is for additional design for both the renovations and the new building, to reach the 30% design level and to obtain more specific cost estimation that will help inform decision-making about funding of the project.
The City plans to complete restroom and shelter improvements at Writer's Vista Park.

The ski hill is a beloved community asset, and its continued operation is desired by many. The replacement will also be a surface lift similar to the existing system. The City expects to fund the project with the Parks and Recreation tax. Consultant services may or may not be needed for the project.

records.Project: A St. Complex Traffic Ph. I Const./Ph. II Des.
records.Description: As outlined in the A Street Complex Master Plan, the staff would like to move forward with the construction of Phase 1 and design of Phase II for the current and future home of Transportation Services. Phase 1 construction will remodel current offices and construct a usable Traffic Operations Center. Phase II will include an internal floor plan change to improve operation use, plus external changes to the building and landscaping.

The concession area will be remodeled, to include adding a new store front/counters, new refrigerator, popcorn machine, ice machine and microwave. The two meeting rooms will be painted. Televisions built into the cabinets will be removed and projectors and drop down screens will be added.

The existing 27-year old orchestra shell at Unnion Colony Civic Center is made of fiberglass and is beginning to show signs of wear and tear. Newer orchestra shell products produce better results, using more dense materials. They also store more compactly. It is possible a shortened wall solution could be implemented that would eliminate the need for the proposed $117,000 project to enlarge the doors to the dock.

records.Project: Rec Center/Senior Courtyard and Front Desk
records.Description: This project provides for a new front desk, billiard lighting, and a new outdoor entrance and courtyard shelter at the Recreation Center/Active Adult Center.
The current restroom facility at Meeker House is not ADA accessible. An upgrade will include an enclosed entrance and space with a small interpretive/classroom space.

In 2017, a blower evaluation study was performed and this project was divided into two phases. The first three of the existing six turbo blowers were to be replaced in 2018. Phase 2 will replace the remaining three K-Turbo blowers. This phase will also include expansion of the blower building.
This project will remodel the men's, women's and family locker rooms at the Golden Community Center.

This project will renovate the interior and exterior of this 1867 building at the Golden History Museum to make it into a functional program and rental facility. A feasibility study was completed in 2016. Renovation will include electrical, plumbing upgrades and strengthening to accommodate group assembly. Renovation of the backyard, including the historic laundry house, will permit multiple uses for programming and event rental.
This project will design and build a climate-controlled collections storage facility at the Golden History Museum.

records.Project: Solar Photovoltaic Projects, Water Treatment Ponds
records.Description: Ten 500kW solar photovoltaic panels can generate electricity to meet 100% of the RV park and additional electrical needs for the city.

A feasibility study completed in 2018 identified one or more hydroelectric projects to be sited at City reservoirs in Clear Creek County that could yield a significant source of renewable energy for the city. These improvements would occur at the Upper and Lower Urad and Guanella Reservoir locations.
The Town has programmed funding in 2022 for a Public Works administration offices building.
This project provides for rehabilitation of the Aircraft Rescue and Fire Fighting/Snow Removal Equipment facility at the airport, to include lighting, flooring, wall coverings and restrooms.
This project will expand the terminal boarding gate at the Durango-La Plata County airport.
This project provides for an expansion of the terminal baggage claim area at the Durango-La Plata County airport.

records.Project: Airport Terminal Facility Imp, Ph. IV
records.Description: This project will complete Phase IV improvements at the airport terminal.

records.Project: Airport Terminal Facility Imp. Ph. V
records.Description: This project will complete Phase V improvements at the airport terminal.
The City plans to construct a new 1,350 sf CMU block/metal roof concrete slab storage building with two bays and additional secure chemical storage.
Klack Cabin is one of the oldest dwellings in Breckenridge. The Town is considering moving the building in 2020 to a better location for public access, and restoring it in 2022.
As part of a program to complete improvements/repairs at City aquatics facilities, this project will address high and medium priority items for the East Boulder Recreation Center.

For a copy of the RFP, go to www.bidnetdirect.com , log in and select Parker Water and Sanitation District.

This project will demolish existing trickling filter basins and construct a third primary clarifier to increase the capacity of the primary treatment system to 12 mgd. The primary clarifier will be constructed in the area now occupied by the decommissioned trickling filters.

The 29th Street steel water tank is one of the most utilized storage facilities supporting over a quarter of the City's water customers. This project will provide a second 5.0 million gallon storage tank at this critical location. The additional storage will offer redundancy and reliability for water customers in northwest Loveland.
The City has allocated funding in 2020-2021 to design a new 3.0 million gallon water storage tank. Construction funding is anticipated beyond the five-year planning period.

The City requires a fire station in the southeast area of the community. The station is expected to be a single company station of 12,000 square feet, with additional bays for specialized rescue apparatus.

The City plans to expand Little Salt Wash Park.
The City's capital plan includes proposed funding to remodel and add on to Fire Station #2.

An additional final clarifier at the wastewater treatment plant will be needed to meet population growth. The clarifier will be 90 feet in diameter with 16 feet sidewater depth. The expansion will be required when plant flows regularly exceed 9 mgd. This project would effectively increase the plant hydraulic rating from 10 mgd to 12 mgd.

The City has identified the need for a new fire station on the west side of the service area, to improve response times to meet the 5 minute 59 second standard. The station is expected to be 9,000 square feet, for six firefighters, three engineers, and three lieutenants.
The County's capital plan includes proposed future funding for a new business park office building.
The Facilities Master Plan projected the need for a future branch library. The current schedule calls for design of a new branch library in 2025 with construction in 2026.
A new building is needed to store the loader, boat, miscellaneous equipment and supplies for the Water Division. Currently these items are stored outside.

This project includes increasing plant capacity from 38 mgd to 46 mgd. The primary improvements necessary to achieve this increase will be the addition of a new flocculation/sedimentation building, eight additional filters at filter building 4A, and additional solids handling capacity (sand beds or ponds). The project will be growth driven, so the timing is not certain. The current capital plan anticipates initiating design in 2027.
The existing digesters 1 and 2 need to be renovated. The rehabilitation project will include piping in and out of the complex, digester lids, internal coating and mechanical equipment replacement.

This project includes planning, design and construction of select connecting infrastructure between the existing transportatoin system and transit stops, including sidewalks, bike lanes, and bus stops and shelters.

Projects include demolition of abandoned process buildings and renewal of ancillary infrastructure. 2021 and 2022 funding includes renewal of the electrical, instrumentation and control system, buried piping, sludge storage tank and digester components.

The restrooms at Community Park adjacent to the tennis courts are old and not ADA-compliant, and need to be replaced. This project will replace the existing building with a modern facility much like the restrooms in Midway Park at the Girl Scout shelter.
The City plans to design and construct a new parking garage in the 2021 time frame.

records.Project: Civic Center CPTED and Grounds Enhancements
records.Description: This project includes aesthetic, functional and crime prevention (Crime prevention through environmental design or CPTED) improvements to the civic center complex. The focus will be entryways, hidden and underused areas and grounds. A library/children's plaza will be developed. The project includes landscaping improvements and irrigation system improvements. The goal is to improve security, safety and approachability of City campus locations through use of CPTED. The project is not currently funded in the five-year program.

This project includes construction of a series of retaining walls to reduce the slope of the hill. Plant material installed should be xeric in nature and provide color and interest from both the roadway above and the sidewalk at the lower level.

Design and construction of a new hydroelectric facility is to be integrated into the Barker Dam Outlet Works project. The capital plan includes $50,000 in 2022 for an analysis study and $457,218 in 2023 for design. Construction is anticipated in 2024.
This project provides for new restrooms at Rotary Park.

The City plans to renovate the lobby, women's locker room, men's locker room, public restrooms and to add family changing rooms at Centennial Pool. The project removes the original concept of a new addition to the building.

Two storage facilities exist at the Price Park location: A 7 million gallon below-grade reservoir built in 1955 and a 2 million gallon below-grade reservoir built in 1922 that is no longer in service due to age and condition. This project will demolish the two old reservoirs and construct a new 5 million gallon above-ground concrete storage tank and associated appurtenances. The project is currently unfunded and will likely require voter approval of a future bond.
The City's capital plan includes proposed future funding for Phase 1 improvements at Ruston Park.
This project provides for park development at Riverdale Bluffs Park.

Longmont Power and Communications has expanded its fleet with additional vehicles and equipment to support NextLight broadband services. The current garage space has no additional capacity. The City is considering constructing a canopy in the open parking lot area inside the secured Service Center parking lot where vehicles and equipment can be parked/stored underneath it. The project is not funded in the current five-year program.

The Parks Department's master plan indicates several key themes that relate to health and wellness, youth activity, community engagement and asset management. To continue to support these themes, the department will complete repairs, renovations and upgrades to recreation centers. Pending the outcome of planning efforts, this project will fund the initial implementation of projects outlined within the plans. One critical project that has been identified includes renovating the front desk area at the North Boulder Recreation Center.
The Town's capital plan includes a future project for field development at Diamond Valley Park, per the master plan for the park. Earlier phased development is scheduled to occur in 2018 and 2020-21.
The Town's capital plan includes proposed funding for restroom design and construction at Main Park.
Beyond the current five-year planning period, Windsor proposes funding for a museum collections and exhibit fabrication building.
This project provides for a new Martinez Open Space picnic shelter and connector trail.
The County's capital plan includes proposed funding for restoration of historic structures at Hidden Mesa.
This project will replace the existing dilapidated stage structure at Highland Heritage Regional Park.

This project would acquire land and develop a community park along 107th Avenue south of 10th Street and west of 71st Avenue. Improvements would include playground(s), picnic shelters, a recreational activity site and open turf/play area, athletic fields for practices and off-street parking. It would also include a permanent restroom and other amenities. At this time, the project is unfunded.

This project would redevelop the entry area of the Waste Diversion Center to enhance security and customer access. It would also reconfigure some of the back area to separate the customer drop-off area from the working industrial area. Improvements would include: 1) relocation and updating of the trailer that receives customer payments; 2) fencing around the entire facility; 3) improvements to the entryway drive; and, 4) a reconfiguration of some of the recycle bins to enhance after-hours use. The project is not currently funded.
This project will complete improvements to optimize the aeration system at the wastewater treatment plant.

This project will construct a new maintenance complex that will accommodate all park maintenance crews to include vehicle and park equipment maintenance bays. It will also support the relocation of the Central Stores and City Archives. The new complex will utilize energy efficiencies with a southern exposure and will be constructed to the City Council strategic goal of LEED silver compliance.
This project provides for future improvements to the Binney water purification facility.

Based on recommendations of the aquatics facility study, the City has programmed future funding for implementation of key indoor aquatic facility enhancements. In 2019, the East Boulder Community Center pools will be renovated and improved in partnership with Facilities and Asset Management ($2,250,000). In 2021, the City is considering improvements to the outdoor Spruce Pool and indoor South Boulder Recreation Center pool to provide water play features for children and youth ($510,000).
The City's capital plan includes future funding for improvements to the filter media at the Charles Allen water treatment plant.
This project will complete a new soccer complex. The current capital plan includes funding in years 2020-2022. Additional funding will be required in future years.

The City proposes to construct a 40-acre community park north of 10th Street, east of 71st Avenue and west of 35th Avenue. It will include playground(s), picnic shelter(s), a recreational activity site and open turf/play area, athletic fields for practices, off-street parking, a permanent restroom, and other improvements such as lighting, irrigation, sidewalks/trails, landscaping, etc. The project is currently unfunded.

records.Description: This project provides for a feasibility assessment, potentially followed by design and construction of a maintenance building at the Sid Copeland Water Treatment Plant.
The Town anticipates funding in 2020 for design and construction of a Boardwalk Park Lake storage operations building and yard.
The Town's long-term plans include development or maintenance work at Jacoby Farm Park, in accordance with the Parks, Recreation and Open Space Master Plan.

records.Project: Semper WTF Replacement Eng. Design, etc.
records.Description: The City has programmed funding in 2019-2020 for Phase 1 design and permitting for the replacement of the Semper water treatment plant. The plant is the larger of the City's two plants and treats the vast majority of the City's potable water. The plant is nearly 50 years old with a significant number of its assets at or beyond their predicted useful life. A 2015 study concluded that replacing the plant would be more cost effective than rehabilitating the existing plant.
The City plans a major renovation of Fire Station #4, located at 4580 West 112th Avenue.
This project proposes future funding for a new sports complex at Crossroads Park.
This project will complete improvements such as trails, parking, restrooms, wildlife viewing bunkers, fishing ponds and river access in the Kodak Watchable Wildlife open space.
This project provides for improvements at the Kyger open space, to include trails, parking, restrooms, and wildlife viewing bunkers.
This project provides for future development of Tacincala Park.
This project provides for future development of Harmony Ridge Park.
This project proposes future funding for development of Fossil Creek Park.
The Town has programmed funding for interpretive landscaping, to include demolition, earth work, irrigation, pavement, electrical, hardscape, fencing, planting and structures.
This project provides for design and construction of renovations of the Easton House museum.

This project will remove the equestrian stables office building and replace it with a new tuff shed to serve as the office and a new tuff shed for City ski area storage. The tack shed will be refurbished and moved to improve summer trails access.

records.Project: Lift Station A and Forcemain Replacement
records.Description: The main lift station that pumps 99% of all sewer flow north approximately 9 miles needs to be replaced. In addition to the replacement of the lift station, the main forcemain, currently prestressed concrete, is no longer suitable for repair and requires full replacement. A study has been conducted to determine the best locations for both the lift station and the forcemain. Additional services of construction observation/inspection and quality control may also be included in the project.
This project provides for the replacement of the Hamilton shop.
This project provides for upgrades to the indoor arena at the County Fairgrounds.
This project proposes funding for improvements to the building, ball fields, fencing and park at Loudy Simpson Park in Craig.
This project will construct a play area and shade for spectators at the Youth Sports Complex as outlined in the 2017 master site improvement plan.

This project provides for installation of an external stairway to the 2nd floor of the microstrainer building and modification of the building for offices, records storage and meeting space. The 2nd floor currently has only one stairway egress and does not conform to current building codes.
This project will modify the existing decommissioned filter building for usable office space, meeting rooms, and records storage.

The City plans a project to remodel the men's, women's and family locker rooms at the community center. Staff projects that, by 2025, the locker rooms will be sorely in need of refreshing, including tile and grout, lockers and overall layout. Additional safety and ADA features may be added.

This project proposes to design and construct a new climate-controlled collections storage facility for the Golden History Museum. The museum cares for 15,000 objects currently kept in a rent-free location in Denver West. The facility is not climate-controlled and is not as secure as the City would like. It is also possible that a paying tenant could preclude the City's continued use at any time. A new facility would be approximately 8,000 square feet.

This project provides for master planning, redesign and improvements at Grampsas Park. The existing park amenities were in place before the City took over the property. They were created for Coors and the family's personal use.
records.Type: AS, DR, MS, PK, PL, ST

records.Description: The City has programmed funding each year for replacement of components of the potable water plant, to assure reliable operations and ongoing treatment of safe water for residents and businesses in the city. These projects may or may not require consultant services.
The Town proposes design and construction of a maintenance facility. It hopes to seek funding through the State Department of Local Affairs.

records.Project: Rose Mill/Big Horn Crossing Water Storage
records.Description: The Town's capital plan includes proposed funding in 2019 for water storage upgrades at Rose Mill/Big Horn Crossing.
The Town's capital plan includes proposed funding in 2019 for reception, office, storage and caretaker unit improvements at the Peninsula Recreation Area.
The City has programmed funding to design and construct Well 25.
This project provides for design and construction of Well #6.
This project provides for the design and construction of a new well.
This project provides for design and construction of a new/expanded wastewater treatment plant.
The County plans to submit a Fishing-is-fun grant or a GOCO grant application to create a loop trail, trailhead and parking facility, to eventually be part of the St. Vrain corridor trail.
The City has programmed funding each year for four years for facilities remodels and replacements.
This project provides for improvements at Cundiff Park.
This project provides for improvements at Mason Center Park.
The City has programmed funding for a new Santa Rita utilities administration building.
The City's capital program includes proposed funding for a vactor garage at the Santa Rita facility.
This project provides for reconstruction of Wakeman Dam.
The County plans a project to construct a picnic shelter and connector trail in the Martinez open space.
The County has programmed funding over four years for improvements to the Rueter-Hess Reservoir recreation area.
This project provides for a redesign of the IT data center.

Renovations at this park will include: Removal of four 12 x 12 shelters; removal of one 32-foot hexagonal shelter; installation of two new 24 x 36 shelters; removal of the existing playground and installation of new inclusive playground and surfacing material. The project will also include parking modifications along Forest Street, and a fenced area with electrical outlets, lighting and a 10 x 12 storage building.

This project will include: Adding infield mix and completing minor grass repairs at Prairie Middle School; adding a backstop and dugouts to the new field in Reunion at 111th and Quintero; adding infield mix to the west field and an infield to the east field at Stuart Middle School; and constructing new fields at Turnberry, Second Creek and Thinning Elementary, and at Ragweed Draw.

Drilling of a new well and on-site treatment will provide immediate additional treated water to the potable distribution system. The project will include chlorine treatment injection, approximately 500 linear feet of underground baffle piping, and a tie-in to the existing distribution system.

A gateway welcome arch over East Main Street has been requested by business owners, the wayfinding committee and others for many years. The project will also provide a place for the Beautification Advisory Board to hang a holiday skyline and a place for event banners.

The City has programmed funding in 2019 to stabilize and rehabilitate three historic buildings - a pumphouse, an outhouse and the Broomfield-landmarked Honey House. These buildings, located at the Broomfield Depot Museum, are all in poor condition.
A complete upgrade of Blue Star Park will include improving or replacing outdated amenities, degrading roadways and concrete, pedestrian paths, and shelters.
This project will construct a 1,350 sf CMU block/metal roof concrete slab storage building, with two bays and additional secure chemical storage.

records.Project: Paul Derda Rec. Center Space Assessment
records.Description: Funding is proposed in 2021 to conduct a study to review the capacity and needs of the Paul Derda Recreation Center. The study will review the option of either expanding the center, leaving it as is, or finding another location.
This project provides for new water treatment plant capacity.

The Open Space and Mountain Parks Department currently has approximately 13,000 square feet of office space. A completed space analysis found that the department needs approximately 35,000 square feet. This project involves moving the current staff to a temporary location, designing and constructing a new campus on the site of the existing campus. The current capital plan anticipates design and permitting in 2019 and construction of new facilities in the following three years. The plan allocates $4 million for the project during the current planning period. Additional funds may be needed.

The Flatirons Golf Course is the City's only course. It is in need of repairs to the many cart paths. Due to the recent removal of the event center and needs to improve the clubhouse, this project will provide funding to begin the repairs and redevelopment of the site in conjunction with additional leveraged funding sources.

Violet Park is an undeveloped neighborhood park along Violet Avenue east of Broadway. This project would allow funding for initial development of the park in conjunction with the planned Fourmile Canyon Creek Greenway improvements through this reach of the creek. The Greenway project will provide funding for the multi-use path while the park funding will allow for the initial phase of development of the park.

The Silver Lake hydroelectric station is located on the raw water transmission system near the Lakewood Reservoir. This project will complete needles/seats rehabilitation in 2019 and a 10-year inspection and overhaul in 2023.
The City anticipates expenditures each year for playground renovations at various parks. These projects may or may not require consultant services.
The City has programmed funding each year for three years for pump station improvements.
This project would complete Southwest Park improvements. It is not currently funded in the five-year program.

The County has programmed funding for initial development of Willow Bay Park. The County acquired the 174-acre Willow Bay open space property in 2017. They intend to develop a regional park on the property.
This project provides for Phase 1 roof replacement at the Justice Center.
The County plans to design and construct a new grandstand at the Regional Complex.
The County has programmed future funding to implement the Regional Park Master Plan.
The County has programmed funding beginning in 2019 for a new Fleet/Public Works facility.
This project provides for a new animal shelter.

As we reported previously, the District expects to seek consultant services for 100% design of an extensive renovation of Holly Park. Ken now says funding is in the 2018 budget for design; however, he is not sure exactly when the RFP will be issued. The improvements will be completed in conjunction with the widening of Riverbottom Drive.

We reported on this project previously. The planning start was delayed for programming, space utilization and conceptual design to reconfigure the administration areas of the Combined Support Maintenance Shop at the Firestone facility. The RFQ for this project has not yet been issued, but should still be coming up, possibly in the next few months.

As we reported previously, the City plans to initiate an engineering analysis and evaluation of the outlet works at the Milton Seaman Reservoir. The original outlet gates have withstood over 60 years of operation. The cast iron gate seal channels have corroded and eroded to the point of compromising the brass seals, allowing water to leak past the gates. In October, Adam said an RFP should be issued in late 2017 or early 2018. We did not reach him this time to confirm. If the information changes, we will let you know.

The District passed its mill levy override on the November ballot for various improvements, repairs, etc. Scott indicated previously that they did not plan to begin a selection process for architectural/engineering or other professional services until they knew the results of the vote. He now says it is too early to provide information about specific projects or plans for hiring architectural/engineering firms. We will follow up.

As we reported previously, the District anticipates advertising to "renew" its pre-qualified architects list. Melissa says they will advertise an RFQ but she has no definite date when that will happen.
We reported on this project previously. Cherry Hills Village plans issue an RFP within the next week or two for general on-call engineering services.

records.Description: As we reported previously, Steamboat Springs plans to advertise an RFQ for a new airport engineering contract. The RFQ should go out by the end of the year.

records.Project: New Facilities, Rocky Ford & Grand Junction
records.Description: Shelly reports that the University plans to RFP for design-build services for new facilities at the Agricultural Experiment Stations located in Rocky Ford and Grand Junction (Orchard Mesa Research Center). The RFP should be issued in the next month or so.

David reports that the City expects to advertise "soon" for new on-call architectural contracts. He said he was not sure whether they would advertise in the next couple of weeks or wait until after the first of the year.
In the next couple of months, the Housing Authority expects to seek architectural/engineering design services for improvements/revitalization at Sun Valley Homes, 990 Alcott Way.
In the next few months, the Housing Authority expects to issue an RFQ for Development Consultant Services.
In the next several weeks, Metro plans to issue a design-build RFP for new grain bins at the METROGRO farm near Deer Trail.
In the next month or two, Colorado State University expects to issue an RFQ for design services for a new Foothills Research Laboratory in Fort Collins.

The District has issued an RFQ for Owner's Representative services. Responses are due no later than 4:00 Sunday, December 10. The work will involve several projects: The District was awarded a BEST grant for various school upgrades that are estimated to cost about $7.5 million. In addition, the City passed a ballot measure to provide the cash match for potential BEST grants for two school reconstruction projects. If the BEST funding is approved in the next cycle, these projects will likely be included in this contract. The RFQ is available on the District's website at http://www.canoncityschools.org/apps/pages/rfps_rfqs_bids .

The District recently advertised for Owner's Representative services for a variety of school repair and upgrade projects. Once the Owner's Representative firm is on board, it will assist the District in a selection process for architectural/engineering services for the various projects. They hope to select an Owner's Rep by the end of December.
After the first of the new year, Crested Butte plans to advertise for design and engineering services for water treatment plant upgrades.
In the first quarter of 2018, the City expects to advertise for design-build services for a fire station.
Contingent on budget approval, scheduled for December 15, the City plans to seek consultant services early in 2018 for some park improvements.
Subject to budget approval, scheduled for December 15, the City expects to seek consultant services early next year for some building improvements.

Ross reported that City facilities suffered extensive hail damage in the hail storm earlier this year. They have received insurance money for repairs. In August, he said he was not sure whether or not they would hire a roofing consultant. We were unable to reach him before this Update to find out further information.

As we reported previously, the School of Mines expects to advertise for design-build services for a building addition/new shop building. Mike says the RFP should be advertised within the next month or so.
As we reported previously, the City plans to issue an RFP for a feasibility and concept design for a replacement water storage tank. The exact timing for release of the RFP has not been determined.

records.Project: Diversion and Metering Grating Condition Assess.
records.Description: As we reported previously, between now and the end of the year, Metro expects to issue an RFP for a Diversion and Metering Facility Grating Condition Assessment. The study will evaluate the condition (structural integrity) of existing grating in larger diversion and metering facilities on the interceptor system and prioritize potential capital projects to address the worst cases.

As we reported previously, Longmont expects to release a request for qualifications for a wastewater plant methane/renewable natural gas fueling station project. Cal says it will probably be a design/build project. They plan to convert all of their sanitation fleet to natural gas using the methane generated by the wastewater treatment plant. Cal now says they will issue an RFQ for design-build teams. He hopes it will go out sometime in October.

As we reported previously, the East Otero (La Junta) School District was awarded a BEST grant for $8,207,468 for a primary school addition and renovation project. The District must contribute an additional $3,191,793. Rick reports that they will go to voters this fall for the District's matching funding. If they are successful, they will advertise for architectural/engineering services at that time.

records.Project: The Gardens on Spring Creek Improvements
records.Description: The City expects to issue an RFP sometime this month for design-build services for improvements at The Gardens on Spring Creek, an 18-acre botanical garden.

The District has not set a specific schedule to begin selecting architectural/engineering firms for its Phase III bond projects. Paul estimates they will solicit proposals from their pre-qualified list of firms in the late fall of 2017 or early winter of 2018. Phase III projects include work at about ten elementaries plus middle schools and high school campuses. The complete list is posted on the District's website at http://bond.bvsd.org/projects/Pages/default.aspx .

Justin reports that the Town expects to require design services for improvements on Town Owned Properties to implement the master plan, if the Council adopts the plan sometime this month. He did not provide any details about what types of projects would be included in the plan implementation. We will follow up.
In the next month or so, Castle Rock expects to issue an RFP for design of a building remodel for the Fire Department.
Kevin reports that, in the near future, Carbondale expects to issue an RFP for a feasibility study for a "small micro-hydro" project.

The County plans to place a capital projects bond question on the November ballot for design and construction of a new jail. If the measure passes, they will require architectural/engineering design and a variety of other consultant services.

If the County's 2018 budget includes new funding for capital projects, Alf reports that they will need to advertise to establish a new short list of pre-qualified engineering firms. It is also possible they will receive new grants for bridge projects, safety projects, etc. Assuming they have the projects to justify the need for services, they will probably advertise around the end of the year or very early in 2018 to develop a new short list.

records.Description: John reported previously that it was possible he would need to advertise for a Golden Gate Canyon State Park Study. We were unable to reach him to confirm whether or not this project is still coming up. We will let you know if we find out any new information.

records.Project: Gardens at Spring Canyon Park - Visitors Ctr.
records.Description: Previously, Brian reported that Fort Collins planned to seek design services in the fall for the expansion of the visitors' center at the Gardens at Spring Canyon Park. He now says they are discussing the project, and may decide to put it out as a design-build.
As we reported previously, the School of Mines expects to advertise for design of a Green Center abatement/roofing project. Mike says the ad should be out now or very soon.

records.Project: Cundiff Park and Santa Rita Park
records.Description: We reported previously that the City planned to issue an RFP for design of development/improvements at Cundiff Park and at Santa Rita Park. Cathy now says they hope to release the RFP in about a month.

As we reported previously, the Department of Transportation expects to advertise for statements of interest and work plans for Wall Inspection services. Lynn now says the RFP should be posted around the middle of August.

As we reported previously, the Department expects to seek architectural/engineering services for design of envelope repairs and fire protection upgrades at the Longmont Readiness Center. Bob now says the state has identified funding, but it will not be available until 2018. They will likely seek architectural/engineering services next year.
The Town should have an RFP out now or very soon for architectural/engineering services for a new Public Works building.
Emily reports that the Town might issue an RFP in the near future for engineering services for a skating rink.
The City expects to advertise in the next week or two for a new 5-year airport engineering contract.

records.Description: Bob reports that the National Guard has an outdoor firing range at Fort Carson that will require a new operations building, ammunition building and bleachers. They may seek architectural/engineering services in the next few months.

Bob reports that they are reprogramming two or three spaces at the Fort Carson Regional Training Facility, which will require interior remodel documents. They may issue an RFP in the next few months for these services.

An RFP should be out now or very soon for construction manager at risk services for the Lower Basin Water Treatment Plant project. This will be a membrane filtration-based treatment facility with an ultimate design capacity of 5 million gallons per day. Initial construction will result in a facility with a firm capacity of 2.5 mgd, expandable to a firm 5 mgd primarily through the addition of future pumping and treatment process equipment. A design was completed in 2012. Phase 1 of this project will include design completion and preconstruction.

The Office of the State Architect, on behalf of Arapahoe Community College, requests design-build proposals no later than 4:00 Friday, September 8 for an "innovative and collaborative educational facility for the benefit of the greater Castle Rock community." A MANDATORY pre-proposal meeting will be held at 1:00 Friday, August 18 at the ACC Castle Rock campus, 4700 Castleton Way, Suite 100 in Castle Rock. The RFP is available at https://www.arapahoe.edu/rfp-castle-rock-campus . Questions are due by email by 5:00 Thursday, August 24. (I cannot find an email address in the documents where questions are to be sent, sorry!)

DIA expects to advertise sometime in August for professional engineering services including, but not limited to Civil, Electrical, Environmental, Geotechnical, Signage and Structural Engineering in order to aid in the completion of projects. They plan to issue two (2) On-Call Contracts from this RFP. There is a 18% M/WBE Goal established for this project.
