records.Description: The District has been approved for a BEST grant to complete an addition to the Delta Middle School, subject to formal approval by the State Board of Education. Jim reports that they expect to advertise in the late summer for architectural and engineering services. They plan to select three firms for interviews before a final selection.

The University advertised in November for architectural/engineering services for the Sports Medicine and Performance Center. As we reported previously, they expect to advertise in the late summer or early fall for design/build services for this project.

As we reported previously, Metro expects to issue an RFP for its 2018 Facility Plan. The RFP should be issued around mid June. They do a new plan every five years to take a comprehensive look at the entire transmission system and the treatment plants, to identify how future flow and loading projections, population projects, regulatory drivers, technology and asset condition might affect future capital needs.

Previously, Jason indicated that the airport expected to advertise later this year or early in 2018 for a new on-call airport engineering contract. They recently advertised and hired a firm for some project-specific improvements. Jason now says they have decided not to advertise for a new on-call contract for a couple more years, as they have no scheduled projects at this point.
As we reported previously, Avon expects to issue an RFP for design of Wildridge retaining wall stabilization services. The RFP should be released in the next couple of months.

Shelly reported previously that it was possible CSU would advertise within a few months for design-build services for a new riding arena on the Foothills campus. She now says that funding has not yet been secured for the project, so the timing is uncertain. We will follow up.
The District, through its owner's representative CBRE, expects to issue an RFQ this fall for architectural/engineering services for design of improvements at Cherrelyn Elementary School.
Manitou Springs plans to issue an RFQ for architectural design/plan preparation for the remodel of its City Hall. Their target date for release of the RFQ is June 15.
In the next couple of months, the Colorado Department of Transportation plans to advertise a Request for Interest and Work Plans for nonproject-specific tunnel design services for Region 1.

Bob reports that he expects the Department will advertise in the next several months for design and construction management services for the renovation of the old 28 Road armory in Grand Junction. It will be repurposed as a Volunteers of America service center for veterans.
In the next few months, the City expects to advertise for design of a vehicle wash facility.

Deer Trail School District 26(J) requests qualifications and proposals no later than 2:00 Friday, June 16 for architectural and engineering/design services for a new Pre-K to 12 school. An optional site walk will be held at 10:30 Monday, June 5. For further information or a copy of the RFQP, contact the Owner's Representative, Cooperative Strategies, at snewell@coopstrategies.com .

We reported previously that Pueblo expected to issue an RFP for a master plan for a historic clubhouse and tennis court. The RFP has been on hold. Steven now informs us they did not receive the GOCO grant they were hoping for so, for the time being, the project remains on hold.

We reported previously that the Housing Authority expected to issue an RFP for on-call architectural and engineering services. Jinnell has now clarified that this RFP will be specific to the Sun Valley site. They are still in the process of developing the RFP.

Previously, Dave reported that the City expected to issue an RFP for evaluation of alternatives and development of conceptual plans to replace the Sunset Mesa water storage tank. He now says that their water supplier has brought up a possibility of building a new water supply and transmission main. The City wants to review this possibility to determine its impact before moving forward with the tank project.

As we reported previously, the College expects to seek architectural/engineering services for program planning and possible design of internal renovations to the cafeteria and community room. Renee now says they are working with an architect to prepare cost estimates. She anticipates issuing a design RFP in the fall.
As we reported previously, the City plans to advertise an RFP for master planning and further construction plans for its river levee project. Bill says the RFP should still be coming up soon.

The District recently advertised for On-Call Professional Architectural and Engineering Services. Kris reports that they might use the firms awarded contracts from this solicitation for bond-funded projects. but they might also advertise separately for larger projects, as they deem appropriate.
Rich reports that he expects the Airport will advertise this fall for a new engineering on-call contract.

records.Description: In the next month or so, the City hopes to issue an RFP for an architectural assessment of some existing fire stations.

Contingent on budget approvals for the 2017/18 fiscal year, Arapahoe Community College plans to advertise for architectural services and project management services for improvements at the Parker campus.
In the next month or so, Castle Rock expects to issue an RFP for design of a vactor load-off-facility, for truck loading, etc. at the Operations Center.

DIA should be advertising today or very soon for design and support services for tenant/airline improvement projects, construction administration support for life safety construction projects, and other life safety assignments that may be required. These services will include commissioning, testing, performing studies, preliminary designs, site inspections, construction documents, plans, specifications, cost estimates, and construction administration for various life safety system additions, improvements, and modifications.
This project provides for Scott Carpenter Pool improvements/redevelopment. An RFP may be issued in the next few months.

Englewood citizens passed the measure to fund a new $27 million police facility. Dave reported previously that they planned an RFP for owner's representative/construction management services. He now informs us that they decided to enter into a cooperative agreement with the School District and will use CBRE as the Owner's Rep, the firm already selected by the District.

We reported on this project previously. In December, Dave indicated that they expected to issue an RFP for design/build services. They now have an Owner's Rep on board, and Dave says the next step will be to hire an architectural firm. The Owner's Rep (CBRE) will prequalify firms beginning with the issuance of an RFP. However, Dave says that, at this point, he does not know how widely they will distribute the RFP. They also have decided not to do a design/build. The current plan is to use the construction manager/general contractor delivery method.

As we reported previously, Frisco expects to seek design/engineering services for an addition to the Public Works shop, scheduled for construction in 2018. Jeff now says the RFP should be issued in mid to late April.
In the next few months, the City expects to seek design/build services for restroom/shelter replacements.
In the next month or so, Larimer County expects to issue a general RFP for architectural and engineering services, primarily for Facilities projects.
In the next few weeks, Larimer County expects to issue an RFP for architectural/engineering services for satellite maintenance shop improvements.
John reports that he might have a need to advertise in the next few months for a Tarryall Reservoir Study.
Shelly reports that it is possible the University will advertise in the next few months for architectural/engineering services for the Health Education Outreach Center.

Larry reports that the City will advertise in the next couple of months or so for design and services during construction for a Golden Pond Spillway Repair project. This is a FEMA flood recovery project.
Dependent on funding later this year, the Department has programmed a project to reconfigure the administration areas at Building 1500 at Buckley.
Dependent on funding later this year, the Department of Military and Veterans Affairs plans to begin a project to reconfigure the administration areas of Building 1005 at Buckley.
In the next few months, Boulder's Parks Department may seek consultant services for design of improvements at the Boulder Reservoir Visitor Center.
Diane reports that the City expects to issue an RFP in late March or early April for design of Clubhouse improvements at Thorn Creek Golf Course.

The City's current capital plan includes funding for two-phased improvements at Kroh Park. This project will include development of the lower 12 acres, off Monroe Avenue. Site development may include: Multi-use fields, a volleyball area, a picnic shelter, restrooms, and off-street parking.

Portions of the South pipeline damaged in the 2013 flood have been replaced. This project will rehabilitate the remaining portions of the pipeline. The work will consist of lining approximately 11,300 feet of 24-inch concrete pipe and rehabilitating and/or installing more than 20 manholes. The project is currently shown in the capital plan as unfunded. The City plans to apply for a federal CDBG grant to fund the project.

This project provides for development of this neighborhood park in the southwest Clover Basin area. The City has programmed $100,000 in 2018 to lead the design process. The developer will construct the park.

Violet Park is an undeveloped neighborhood park along Violet Avenue east of Broadway in North Boulder. This funding will allow for initial park development in conjunction with the planned Fourmile Canyon Creek Greenway improvements.

Albion Dam is in need of repairs. It will require evacuation and implementation of more permanent repair to the trash rake and pipe inlet area that can serve until the dam rehabilitation project is scheduled.

Aurora's Utilities Department plans a new maintenance facility in the future. The project was previously programmed in 2014. It has now been moved out to be initiated in 2021. Additional funding may be required beyond 2021.

The project includes development of a neighborhood park to include a shelter, playground, native and non-native grass, landscaping, electrical upgrades, and portable restroom facilities. Trailhead parking will be installed concurrent with park development.

records.Project: Public Safety Training Center Phase III
records.Description: This project will develop a multi-use facility suitable for the training needs of multiple City departments, including Police and Fire. An effective training center includes a live burn house, multiple story search and rescue/apprehension tower, shoot house, and a storage/administration building. The cost estimate includes $3,453,240 for construction, plus permitting, furnishings, moving, miscellaneous and other costs. The project is not currently funded.
records.Type: AS, CM, DR, GT, MS, PK, ST, SV

records.Description: The City's capital plan proposes funding for a new Street Division Facility. At this time, no source of funding has been identified. The project would require purchase of property and construction of a new 50,000 sf building, plus three additional facilities: One 1,500 sf for vegetation/chemical storage; one 10,000 sf for salt storage; and one 4,500 sf for storing supplies and material. The cost estimate includes $570,000 for design, $7.7 million for construction, $1 million for land and $380,000 for project management.

This project provides for improvements to the maintenance facility at North Lake Park, plus an additional picnic shelter, a water spray park, 60 new parking spaces and landscaping improvements. Realignment/improvements for road access to the train depot, and relocation of the existing maintenance shop may also be considered as part of the project.

This project initially provides for an analysis of the potential for a hydroelectric facility on the city's portion of the Carter Lake Pipeline. Design and construction would follow if preferred. The funding plan calls for an alternatives analysis in 2018 ($50,000), potential design in 2019 ($250,000) and construction in 2020 ($2.5 million).

This final phase of the El Pueblo Museum will complete the newly named Dr. William Buckles Pavilion. It will consist of: A six-foot-wide observation walkway with glass flooring; interior lighting for displays and interpretive panels; exterior lighting; ventilation; storefront doors; secondary electrical service; and pigeon control on exterior truss girders. The building is located at 315 N. Union Avenue adjacent to the El Pueblo Museum.

Renovation of the Mineral Palace Park greenhouse will include heaters, restrooms, plant racks, etc. The greenhouse has been closed and used primarily for storage. The proposed renovations would allow the facility to be reopened and to serve the community by offering program opportunities and as a functioning greenhouse.
This project provides for expansion and renovation of the H2O'Brien municipal swimming pool.
Parker's future capital plans include expansion of the fieldhouse on an adjacent 5-acre site.
This project provides for a second recreation center, to be located in the Reata West subdivision.
This project provides for the addition of covered parking at the Police building.
This project provides for the development of a rail plaza at Boulder Junction, pending coordination with private development in the location of the plaza.
records.Type: AS, DR, MS, PK, ST, TR

records.Project: Snow and Ice Material Storage Expansion
records.Description: The City's current storage area for snow and ice control material is inadequate in terms of use and flexibility. This project will rebuild the snow and ice material storage facility to increase storage capacity and flexibility.
The City plans a project to rehabilitate the 7 million gallon water storage tank at the College Mesa water treatment plant.
This project provides for improvements to the Carnegie building.

This project provides for construction of a storage facility for large Public Works vehicles. It will consist of a covered, non-heated structure, to prevent snow from landing on the V-Box located on the back of the snow plow.
The City plans to replace the sediment basins at the College Mesa water treatment plant.

records.Project: Ridges Basin High Pressure Water Line/Station
records.Description: The City has programmed future funding for a Ridges Basin high pressure water line and booster pump station.

The existing modulating valve vault will be rehabilitated to ensure it is safe, efficient, and robust for current and future water delivery. Upon further study, it is anticipated that a formal valve vault will be constructed, pipes properly abandoned, a second modulating valve installed, with pipe coating and additional safety improvements to be completed.
This project will replace two playgrounds at Challenger Regional Park.

records.Project: Community Park N. of 10th St./W. of 71st
records.Description: This project provides for a new community park of 40 acres, to include: playground(s); picnic shelters; a recreational activity site and open turf/play area; athletic fields for practices; and off-street parking; plus a permanent restroom and other amenities. At this time, no source of funding has been identified for the project.

This project will replace the secondary (final) clarifier mechanisms with a full radius scum trough for two 85-foot diameter suction header clarifiers, and one 120-foot diameter suction header clarifier. The existing clarifier mechanisms are over 30 years old and their scum troughs are unable to effectively remove foam from the clarifiers when it accumulates. This can lead to a degradation of effluent quality and, potentially, to permit non-compliance.

records.Project: WPCF Dewatered Sludge Cake Pump Repl.
records.Description: This project replaces the 1996 Schwing sludge cake pump located in the dewatering building on the south plant at the Water Pollution Control Facility. The pump delivers solids from the dewatering centrifuge to the sludge hopper for temporary storage or directly to a truck for immediate biosolids land application.

A site or sites will be developed to house Water and Sewer construction crews and their equipment. The building in which the crews are currently housed is in poor condition and is not centrally located.

The Town's capital plan includes a project, but no identified funding, for a future parking structure to be located somewhere in the core of Town. The location has not yet been determined and, nor has a cost estimate.

This project will remodel the former fire station located in the Centennial Park near the Longmont Youth Center and other recreational amenities. The facility will be remodeled to house additional recreation programs for all ages with an emphasis on activities for seniors and youth. Programming is expected to include: Drop-in and programmed activities; preschool progams; mobile recreation programs; an expanded summer day camp location; senior health and wellness; and community rental opportunities. At this time, no source of funding has been identified to complete the project.

When the Museum was designed in 1999, additional gallery space was included in the conceptual plan, for future expansion on the west side. Current thinking suggests an addition above the current gallery space. A donor has inquired about the status of the addition, which is why the City would like to proceed with design. With a design in hand, they will be able to discuss the space and how its construction could potentially be funded through contributions and private donors. At this point, the project is unfunded.
This project provides for discharge relocation at the wastewater treatment plant.

The City plans to construct a 3,000 gallon-per-minute (4.2 mgd) water pump station to provide water to the northwest portion of Arvada. The new station will replace an older pump station located inside the Ralston water treatment plant. The new pump station will be located next to the existing water storage tanks just east of the Ralston plant.
The City's capital plan includes proposed funding in 2018 for city office upgrades at the Armory, as part of the Civic Space Relocation Project.
This project will complete restoration improvements at Anderson Cabin.
The City plans to complete structural and roof renovation on the barn at Cozy Point Ranch.
The City plans a future second phase of housing development at Burlingame.
This project provides for the development of single family residences as part of Phase II development at Burlingame.
This project provides for a new equipment storage building for Utilities.
The city has programmed funding in 2019 for capacity recovery at the Griswold water purification facility.
This project provides for improvements at Central Community Park.
The City has programmed funding in 2021 for a Tennis Center.
The City plans upgrades at the Aurora Pump Station in 2018.
This project provides for additional Lower South Platte water storage.

This project provides for capacity recovery improvements to the Griswold water purification facility. The project was previously anticipated farther in the future, but was moved forward due to the urgency of improving the lagoon recovery.

The City has programmed funding each year for space needs analyses of General Fund departments in support of a master plan, to accommodate staff growth or unanticipated relocation. The projects may or may not involve consulting services.

This project will add office space to the outdoor ice rink building to accommodate better staff monitoring of the outdoor ice sheet while freeing up office space to provide Summit Youth Hockey with administrative space.

The lower section of Ski Hill Road has a rock wall that supports the sidewalk. These walls have been deteriorating over the years and a recent vehicle collision with the wall has further degraded the wall. This project will reconstruct the walls with rock that will last longer, and will place a bumper rail to prevent vehicle damage to the wall. It will also replace the sidewalk on top of the wall.
This project will remodel the existing golf course clubhouse to upgrade the finishes and reinvest in the infrastructure.
This project provides for a second reservoir outlet tower at the College Mesa water treatment plant.
This project will complete improvements at Romans Park, 1748 East Floyd Avenue.
This project provides funding to expand Pirates Cove Family Fun Aquatic Center, 1225 West Belleview.
The City plans a project to replace the anaerobic digester lid at the wastewater treatment plant.
The City has included proposed funding in its capital plan to renovate the third floor of the City Hall building.
The City has programmed future funding to design and construct a new baseball complex.
This project provides for a new/expanded recreation center.
This project provides for an expansion of the Brighton Oasis Family Aquatic Park, located at 1852 East Bromley Lane.

This project provides for an expansion of the Eagle View Adult Center, at 1150 Prairie Center Parkway. The center serves primarily adults over the age of 55 and provides social, education and recreational opportunities.
The current restroom facility at Meeker House is not ADA accessible. This project will upgrade the facility to include an enclosed restroom entrance and a small interpretive/classroom space.

The City proposes to construct a 40-acre community park south of 10th Street and west of 71st Avenue. Improvements would include playground(s), picnic shelter(s), a recreational activity site and open turf/play area, athletic fields for practices, off-street parking, restrooms, and other improvements such as lighting, landscaping, sidewalks/trails, etc. At this time, the project is not funded in the five-year program.
records.Type: AS, DR, MS, PK, SW, ST, WR

records.Description: The Parks and Recreation Commission Recreation Center expansion feasibility study recommended the expansion of recreation center-based facilities by constructing a new center in the northwest section of the city. To meet the recognized standard, the new recreation center will be needed within the next 10 years.

The clubhouse and maintenance buildings at the Olde Golf Course are both in need of replacement. The clubhouse is over 60 years old and should be replaced with a facility that offers greater capacity for guests and an indoor instruction area. The maintenance building is over 55 years old, is too small to meet current needs and is in poor condition. It does not meet modern building codes.
The Town anticipates constructing a new parking structure in Old Town in 2020.

records.Project: Public Works Facility Design and Const.
records.Description: This project provides for the design and construction to relocate and replace the public works facility. The initial cost estimate may be revised once the facilities master plan is completed in 2017.
The Town has identified the need to relocate and replace the transit facility. The project is not funded in the current five-year program.

Windsor is one of 11 municipalities and water districts that participated in a study of the feasibility of a regional water treatment plant (or plants). The Town has budgeted funding in 2017 for an additional engineering study of how to convey and treat NISP water. Based on the studies to date, Windsor estimates its future contribution to a plant or plants at $32,560,000.
This project provides for the renovation of the Eaton House museum.
This project is anticipated beyond the five-year planning period, and will entail development of Village East Park.

This project will provide a detailed space study for the Public Safety Center. The results of the study will inform the larger issue of a lack of space for new full-time employees expected on the City Hall campus, and could result in a more comprehensive approach to the solution.

The Semper water treatment facility is the larger of the City's two plants. The facility is nearly 50 years old with a significant number of its assets at or beyond their predicted useful life. A study completed in 2015 confirmed that it would be more cost-effective to replace the plant than to rehabilitate the existing facility. The purpose of the 2018 study will be to confirm a layout for the new facililities and the best location for its construction.

Previously, Bob reported that the Department of Military and Veterans Affairs hoped to solicit design proposals for a roof replacement at the Aviation Readiness Center at Buckley. In October, he said the project was not funded for the current fiscal year. He now says they still expect to seek design services in the next few months or so.

We reported on this project previously. Lakewood plans to seek architectural services for restroom redesign at the Public Safety Center. Ross expects an RFP to be issued during the first quarter of 2017.

In October, Roger reported that, in the coming six months, Loveland expected to issue an RFP for design of wastewater/water quality laboratory improvements. He now says they plan to solicit proposals from three or four firms, and will not advertise.
As we reported previously, CSU expects to issue an RFP for improvements at the Design Center building. The RFP should go out in the next couple of months.
As we reported previously, CSU plans to issue an RFP for renovation of the Corbett-Parmelee dining hall and kitchen. Shelly now says the RFP should go out within the next couple of months.

Adams 12 Five Star Schools was successful in passing a $350 million bond on the November ballot. The latest information we received is that they expect to advertise in the next month or two for the 2017 projects. These projects will include renovations and reconstructions at Mountain View, North Star, STEM lab, Stukey, Westview, and Woodglen.
After the first of the year, Crested Butte expects to issue an RFP for construction management services for the upgrade of the wastewater treatment plant.
In February, CDOT expects to advertise for one new retaining and sound wall inspection contract.

The District requests qualifications no later than Friday, December 9 for architectural and engineering services. They will solicit proposals from firms they pre-qualify through this process. Projects will include a new innovation academy and various renovations and upgrades. The RFQ is available by going to http://www.cherrycreekschools.org/FacilityOperations/Documents/Architect%20and%20Engineer%20Statements%20of%20Qualification.pdf .

The County's 2017 budget includes funding for master planning for a multi-event center. We do not have a schedule yet but, at some point, they expect to advertise for architectural/planning services for the project.

The District was successful in passing a capital projects bond in November. They have advertised for the first few projects. NV5 has put together a tentative schedule of future projects. In the second quarter of 2017, they expect to advertise for design of the Valley View K-8 school. Later in 2017, they will seek design or design/build services for the G408 school, and design for a new PK-8 school to accommodate growth. We will provide additional information in future Updates.

In January, the District expects to seek construction management/general contractor services for projects at Clayton Elementary and Charles Hay World Elementary. Donovan Nolan is with CBRE, the firm the District has chosen as its Owner's Representative.

Karin reported previously that the District had been awarded a $12.4 million BEST grant, funding to replace Columbine Middle School. They will go to the voters in November for additional funding of $21.3 million. If that passes, they will "immediately" send out and RFP for architectural/engineering services.

We reported back in 2014 that the University of Colorado at Colorado Springs envisioned a Sports Medicine and Performance Center. Gary now says he expects they will seek consultant services next spring for programming services.
records.Agency: Univ. of Colo. at Colo. Springs

records.Description: Mitch reported previously that Metro expected to seek consultant assistance to help further evaluate the North Secondary Blower and Aeration Complex situation with the intent of better defining the overall scope of work, etc. Mitch now reports that they have decided on a somewhat different approach. They will do some in-house analysis to better define the scope, then they plan to roll the project into a 2018 Facility Plan. They will probably get a consultant on board in about mid 2017 to begin the Facility Plan, with the aim of completing it by the end of 2018.

Previously, Brian reported that Fort Collins might advertise for design of a new Parks shop in the southeastern area of the city. He now informs us that the project did not get funded for the new budget year, so it will be delayed at least two more years.

As we reported previously, Greenwood Village expects to issue an RFP for architectural design of a restroom addition at the Curtis Arts and Humanities Center. Suzanne says they the RFP should be out soon.

The District will place a $150 million bond on the November ballot. One of the major projects is a replacement of Adventure Elementary, for which they received a BEST grant. They must match the grant with bond funds. They will also complete various additions, remodels and upgrades, and a couple of school relocations. The complete list of projects is on the District's website at http://www.mapleton.us/District/Department/55-District-Task-Force . They will begin a/e selections only after they know the results of the vote.
As we reported previously, Kirk anticipates that the University will advertise this fall for design of roof projects at University Center and Harrison Hall. He does not have a specific schedule.

The University has been working on a feasibility study for a new indoor practice facility. They have estimated the cost at $12 million, which will include a baseball diamond. Gary now says he expects to advertise sometime "soon" for design/build services, but doest not have a specific date.
records.Agency: Univ. of Colo. at Colo. Springs

records.Description: As we reported previously, Commerce City expects to advertise for architectural/engineering services for design to renovate the existing recreation center. Courtney now says she anticipates releasing an RFP in October or early November.

A few months ago, Kim indicated that the District was underway with its Phase I projects from its most recent capital projects bond. Phase I includes the majority of the large projects. She said that, sometime in 2017, they expected to begin seeking architectural/engineering services for Phase II projects. She now says that, as they finish Phase I projects, they are beginning work to advertise for Phase II projects. You can view a list of the Phase II projects and their status by going to http://bond.bvsd.org/projects/Pages/default.aspx . Some of the Phase II projects are already in design. RFPs will go to firms on the pre-qualified vendor list.

As we reported previously, DIA plans to seek design services for expansion of Concourse A to the east and west and Concourse C to the east. The Concourse A west expansion will include ten new airline gates and 14 new hold-rooms. The east expansion will include 12 new airline gates and 15 new passenger hold-rooms. The Concourse C expansion will include 10 new airline gates and 12 new hold-rooms. The project will include a 17% M/WBE goal. The current schedule indicates a November RFP for design.

records.Project: Concourse A Expansion West PM Team
records.Description: As we reported previously, DIA plans solicitation for project management services for the Concourse A West expansion project. The expansion will include 10 new contact airline gates and 14 new passenger hold-rooms. It will include a basement and two sub-cores with commercial concession space and office space. The project will also involve the apron paving work required to park ad service aircraft at the gates. It will include a 10% M/WBE goal. The RFP is now anticipated in October.

As we reported previously, one of the projects to be completed pursuant to a bond that passed in May is the Lutz Sports Complex, to include a new four-field baseball/softball pod complex with lighting, parking and restrooms/concessions. Justin says they are reviewing their plans for this and a couple of other projects. He does not have a specific advertising date at this point.

Pursuant to a bond passed in May, the District plans to renovate the splash pad at the Apex Center and to construct a 7,800 sf outdoor splash pad, to renovate the aquatics area center pool, and to renovate the indoor playground. Justin says they are reviewing their internal plans related to this and a couple of other projects. He is not sure exactly when they will advertise for design.

As we reported previously, one of the projects to be completed pursuant to a bond that passed in May is the Long Lake Regional Park. The District plans to construct two new baseball/softball fields to complete the first five-field complex, with lighting for all five fields. They will also build a restroom/concession building and new synthetic multi-sport turf fields for lacrosse, rugby and football, plus parking and lighting. Justin says they are reviewing their internal plans related to this and a couple of other projects. At this point, he is not sure exactly when they will advertise for design.

records.Project: Town Facilities Master Planning, Parking Study
records.Description: In the next week or two, Avon expects to advertise for master planning of town facilities, plus a parking study.

In our project ID #78402, we reported that the University expected to advertise next spring for programming services for a Sports Medicine and Performance Center. Gary also says they will advertise in the summer for either design or design/build services.
records.Agency: Univ. of Colo. at Colo. Springs

records.Project: Hydraulic Gates, Outlet Works at Reservoir
records.Description: In a Special Update in early August, we reported that Greeley expected to issue an RFQ/P this fall for design of hydraulic gates at the outlet works of a reservoir. Adam now says it appears the project will be advertised closer to the end of the year.
Mike reports that the School of Mines anticipates advertising within the next few months for design services for a new parking garage.
Matt reports that Avon expects to issue an RFP very soon, possibly this week, for a planning and parking study.
In the next month or so, Central City plans to issue an RFP for Phase 2 of the rehabilitation of a historic building.
This fall or early winter, CSU plans to issue an RFP for design of Food Innovation Center improvements.

Denver International Airport expects to advertise this month to qualify firms for addition to a pool of companies with specialized skills that the airport may require from time to time. Projects range in size and across categories, and consultants will be utilized on an on-call basis.
An RFP should be out very soon for on-call roofing consulting services for the City of Pueblo.

As we reported previously, Adams 12 has a $350 million bond on the November ballot. They currently plan to advertise this month for construction management/general contractor services for the new Anthem Pre-K to 8 school.

Aurora Public Schools has placed a $300 million bond on the November ballot. If it passes, projects will include several major remodels, the replacement of Mrachek Middle School (for which they have received a BEST grant), and various repairs and upgrades at all schools. They typically advertise once a year for architectural/engineering/professional services qualifications, then select firms using that list. They may advertise sometime this month for the next round of consultant qualifications.

DIA anticipates advertising this month for new on-call architectural/engineering contracts, to replace existing contracts that are nearing maximum expenditure capacity. They expect to contract with five firms for fees not to exceed $3 million per firm, for projects extending beyond 2016.
records.Type: AS, DR, GT, MS, ST, SV

records.Description: DIA plans to advertise soon for on-call professional services to address repair and moisture protection needs at DIA garages, terminal roadways and bridges.

The City has proposed an expansion of the recreation/senior center. They have been working on a feasibility study and community survey. Council has given preliminary approval to place a $28.6 million bond on the November ballot, which would be used to expand and renovate the rec/senior center and pool facilities at Memory Square Park. If they are successful in passing a bond, they will begin these improvements. We will follow up.

Previously, Gary reported that the University might advertise for development of a program plan for the Health/Wellness #2 building, which is one of four of the City's "City for Champions" projects. In April, he said they did not yet have the occupants of the building identified so that a program plan could proceed. At this point, he has no further update. We will continue to monitor progress.
records.Agency: Univ. of Colo. at Colo. Springs

records.Description: The District recently selected an Owner's Representative for the Vikan Middle School. They expect to advertise within the next couple of months for architectural/engineering services for the renovation and expansion of the school. The project will add five classrooms (7,000 square feet) and complete mechanical upgrades.

This project provides for an expansion of the Northeast Elementary School. The District recently selected an Owner's Representative for this project. They expect to advertise within the next couple of months for architectural/engineering services.

The District recently selected an Owner's Representative for this project. They plan the addition of six classrooms and mechanical upgrades at Overland Trail Middle School. They expect to advertise within the next couple of months for architectural/engineering services.

The District is finalizing the selection of an Owner's Representative for the renovation and the addition of classroom space at Brighton High School. They expect to advertise within the next couple of months for architectural/engineering services. The project is scheduled for completion by the fall opening of the school year in 2019.

Voters in this District passed a bond in early May. One of the projects to be completed is the replacement of the Secrest Recreation Center on West 66th Avenue. The new facility will include 21,521+ square feet with a small weight room, community/aerobics area, teen center, small gym, locker rooms and a warm water therapy pool. The existing swimming pool and inline hockey rink will remain. Justin says they expect to issue a design RFP around November.

As we reported previously, voters approved a capital projects bond in May. One of the projects to be completed is a new 8500+ sf recreation center with a six-lane pool, small weight room, and community/aerobics area. Justin says a design RFP should go out around November.

Pursuant to a bond passed in May, the District plans to renovate eight outdoor tennis courts at 6430 Miller Street, to include new lights and fences. They will also add four new indoor courts and create controlled access to all areas of the tennis complex. Justin reports that they expect to issue a design RFP around November.
Robert reports that the County might seek design services in the next few months for a Summit Stage bus transfer center improvement project. He does not have any additional information at this point.
It is possible that, in the next few months, the County will seek consulting services related to the implementation of the County Commons Master Plan.

The City plans for a tax initiative on the November ballot. A 0.5% sales tax increase would fund several public safety improvements. The biggest project is a new fire station #11 in the north part of the city. If the initiative passes, they will seek architectural/engineering services for the project.

The City will seek a sales tax increase on the November ballot, with the hope of raising about $7 million over several years for Public Safety improvements. These will include remodels of several existing fire stations, in part to accommodate women fire fighters. If the ballot initiative passes, they will likely need architectural/engineering services for some or all of these remodel projects.
In the next few months, the Colorado Department of Transportation expects to seek consultant services for tunnel construction management services in Region 3.
In the next month or so, the University expects to issue an RFP for design-build services for the Williams Village East Residence Hall improvements project.

records.Project: Denver Co. Jail E. Housing Unit Bldg. 24
records.Description: An RFQ should be issued very soon for construction manager/general contractor services for the Denver County Jail East Housing Unit Building 24 project. The project will consist of the build-out of Levels 6 (18,280 sf) and 7 (6,120 sf). The build-out will provide 48 double-bunk detention cells and associated improvements to house 96 female offenders.

As we reported previously, Castle Rock completed some feasibility study work for a future new fire training center. In October, Art said they were thinking of buying an existing building and renovating/remodeling it. In that case, they would probably need architectural services to design the remodel/renovation. The project has been on hold while they were getting a fire station project started (see our project ID #79753). They currently have a firm evaluating the training center situation as an add-on to a previous contract. The Town has no specific plans to move forward into design. We will continue to follow up.

As we reported previously, Cherry Hills Village expects to seek architectural services late this year for design of a new Public Works facility. Jay now says he hopes to issue an RFP in the next couple of months.
We reported previously that Cherry Hills Village might seek architectural services for a new city/village center. Jay now says he hopes to issue an RFP in the next couple of months.

As we reported previously, Mesa County plans to seek design services related to repairing structural problems at the Animal Services facility. The project will be advertised through the City of Grand Junction's Purchasing Department. Greg now says the RFP should be out in the next couple of weeks.

Previously, we reported that the City might require design/consulting services in 2016 for a parking structure related to the Olympic Museum and Hall of Fame project. Greg now says he is working on an RFP for preliminary design of the parking garage. Once they see the cost estimates, they will decide whether or not they can afford to move forward with the preferred project. If so, they expect to contract with the same firm for final design. If not, they might still negotiate with that firm to design and build a project that is within their funding capability.

We reported previously that Avon might seek architectural/design services for Town Hall improvements. Justin now says he expects an RFP to go out soon for design to remodel an existing building into a Town Hall.

Previously, Peter reported that the College might issue an RFP for design of a 30,000 square foot building in Breckenridge. At this point, he says he does not know when the project will be initiated. It will require Board approval to proceed. It is possible this will happen by fall.

Bob reported previously that the Department of Military and Veterans Affairs might have a design project later in the spring for a new Space Battalion Readiness Center at Fort Carson. The facility is expected to be about 85,000 square feet. Bob says it is moving forward through the federal (USPFO - U.S. Property and Fiscal Office) contracting system.
We reported on this project previously. John expects to issue an RFP within the next three or four weeks for design services for the Upper Michigan Dam improvements project.

The District recently selected a design firm and CM/GC firm for Phase I of the Brighton Heritage Academy. Phase II will entail a roof replacement and mechanical upgrades. Katie reports that they expect to seek design services in the next few months for these improvements.

records.Project: Brighton Heritage Academy Phase II CM/GC
records.Description: The District recently selected a design firm and CM/GC for Phase I improvements at the Brighton Heritage Academy. Within the next few months they expect to advertise for construction manager/general contractor services for Phase II improvements, which will include a roof replacement and mechanical upgrades.

Fruita expects to issue an RFP in the next week or two for an evaluation of the existing dam at Fruita Reservoir #2. The state has directed the City to evaluate the stability of the dam due to prolonged scrapes and blushing of the downstream face. They need to complete the evaluation and recommendations for corrective action by the end of the year.

In the next couple of months or so, the University expects to require architectural/engineering services for the core and shell renovation of the National Cybersecurity Intelligence Center at 3650 North Nevada in Colorado Springs. The a/e services may be part of a design-build solicitation and contract.
records.Agency: Univ. of Colo. at Colo. Springs

records.Description: The Authority plans to issue an RFP as soon as this week for a planning and design charrette for an evaluation of redevelopment possibilities for a property the Authority owns at 140 East Oak Street.

Pat reports that it is possible, but not definite, that the City will seek consultant services for a levee certification needs assessment. He says he won't know for sure for "awhile." We will follow up.

Within the next few weeks, Westminster expects to issue an RFP for a facilities assessment. They will seek a firm to inventory all of the city buildings and to evaluate the lifespan of the existing mechanical and other building systems, and then to organize the information into a database so the City can develop long-term budget projections.

records.Project: Gang Hangar and Self-Service Fuel Facility
records.Description: Adam reports that he is in the early stages of trying to get approval (including funding approval) to move ahead with a new gang hangar and self-service fuel facility at the airport. It appears nothing will happen with the projects for awhile. We will follow up to see how the approval process is going.

DIA anticpates a late June RFP for design, construction, maintenance and operation of a full-service passenger lounge. The Airport has identified approximately 8,350 square feet on the A concourse for this facility. The Airport intends to enter into a separate expenditure agreement with the Operator related to the service of the lounge area. The project will include a 30% ACDBE and a 25% M/WBE goal.

Andrew reported previously that the City's on-call architectural and engineering contracts would expire at the end of this year. He expected they would issue an RFQ before now to begin the process to get new contracts in place beginning in 2016. The RFQ has not yet been released but Andrew still says it should be out soon.
records.Type: AS, DR, MS, PK, PL, ST

records.Description: As we reported previously, Durango expects to issue an RFP for design-build services for a softball complex and tennis courts. The RFP should go out this spring. The softball complex portion of the project will consist of the renovation of an existing facility and a new restroom/concession/storage building. The tennis courts will be a new six-court facility.

The County recently selected an architect for a remodel of the County Courts wing. They plan to advertise in the near future for construction manager/general contractor services for the project. An alternate contact is Scott Prestien, sprestien@iconenergyco.com .

As we reported previously, the City expects to post an RFP for a master developer for the former Fan Fare site - a 10.3 acre site at 333 S. Havana Street. The site is owned by the Aurora Urban Renewal Authority. They expect proposals will be submitted by teams that include planners, architects, developers and financial consultants. Firms that would like to be notified directly when the RFP is available may contact Melissa Rogers at the email address shown here and ask to be placed on the email notification list. The RFP should go out in late April or May.
records.Type: AS, DR, MS, PK, PL, SW, ST, WR

records.Description: Denver expects to issue an RFQ in the next couple of weeks for architectural and engineering design services for the Denver County Jail E Housing Building 24 project.

Michele reports that the City expects to advertise this month for a large planning and architectural project. However, she was unable to provide any specific information about it. She says the details are still being worked out and she does not want to provide tentative information that could be changed.
CU's plans include a project to complete capital renewal improvements at the Hellems Arts & Sciences building.
The University's long-range plan includes proposed funding for renovation of the CU Denver building.
This project provides funding for improvements to and an expansion of the Town's Pavilion.
CU Boulder hopes to build a new 138,500 sf aerospace engineering sciences building. The current capital plan shows funding beginning in FY2016/17.

records.Project: District 6 - Greeley West HS Fields, etc.
records.Description: This project provides for construction of a multi-purpose field, track and restroom. The project may involve relocation of the existing baseball field. Design will focus on tying the adjacent Greeley West Park to the proposed improvements. The City will collaborate with District 6 Greeley West High School to complete the project.
The County's five-year capital program includes proposed funding to expand the jail facility, beginning in 2018.
The University's five-year capital plan includes a proposed project to complete capital renewal improvements at the Henderson Museum of Natural History on the Boulder campus.
This project proposes funding for 22,908 sf of capital renewal improvements to the Guggenheim Geography building on the Boulder campus.
The University's capital plan includes proposed funding beginning in fiscal 2016/17 for renovation of the existing engineering building on the Colorado Springs campus.
records.Agency: Univ. of Colo. at Colo. Spgs.

records.Description: This project proposes funding for a 219,880 square-foot Interdisciplinary Building 1 on the Anschutz campus of the University of Colorado Denver.

records.Project: Health Sci. Lib. and Ed. Bldgs. Renovation
records.Description: The University's five-year plan includes a project proposed to begin in 2019 to renovate the Health Sciences Library and Education Buildings on the Anschutz campus.
The University of Colorado Denver hopes to initiate the renovation of the Engineering and Physical Sciences building on the Denver campus. Funding is requested for the 2016/17 fiscal year.
This project proposes future funding for a 37,600 pre-health instructional lab wing on the Denver campus.
This project provides for new grandstands in 2019.
This project provides for Tier II improvements to the Pavilion.
The Town has programmed funding in 2020 for Tier III improvements at the Pavilion.

records.Project: Festival Site Imp's & Catering, Ph. II
records.Description: The Town has programmed funding for improvements to the festival site and catering area.
The Town's capital plan includes proposed future funding to complete renovations at the Town Hall building.
This project provides for rehabilitation of the digester at the wastewater treatment plant.
This project provides for exterior improvements to the County Courthouse.

records.Project: PW and Fleet Mtnce. Master Plan
records.Description: The County has programmed funding in 2017 for master planning for the Public Works and Fleet Maintenance facility.
This project provides for clearwell improvements at Hilltop.
This project provides for bathrooms/4-way transit stop improvements.

The Town has proposed five additional phases (phases II through VI) of improvements at Big Mine Park, located at 2nd and Whiterock. Big Mine is the Town's only year-round recreational park. It includes nordic skiing and a Disc Golf Course, among other amenities. At this time, no source of funding has been identified to complete the proposed improvements.
This project provides for rehabilitation of a 5 million gallon steel water storage tank.
This project will complete tenant improvements in the Clerk and Recorder offices at the Administration I building.

records.Project: Altura Plaza - A/D Works! Tenant Imp's
records.Description: This project provides for tenant improvements to the A/D Works! area of Altura Plaza.
The County's capital plan includes proposed funding to replace the roof on the Tri-County Health building on Broadway.
The County plans to replace the roof on the District Attorney's Office building.
This project will replace the roof on the Altura Plaza building, 14500 East 14th Place in Aurora.
This project provides for a new aircraft de-icing facility at the airport.

records.Project: Centennial Park Butch Butler Storage Garage
records.Description: This project will construct one approximately 12' x 32' garage building to replace thre smaller, aging structures. The project is currently unfunded.
The City plans to replace the picnic pavilion/shelter and restroom facilities at Sunrise Park. The project is not funded in the current five-year program.

The City plans to demolish the existing restrooms and design and build a new prefabricated restroom with one male and one female facility. It will also include a chase room large enough for secure storage so the on-site residential shed can be eliminated.

This project will construct a new neighborhood park south of Highway 34 and west of 65th Avenue in accordance with the Parks and Trails Master Plan. The scope will be determined in the future based on neighborhood and site-specific needs. The project is currently unfunded.

This project provides for design and construction of a new neighborhood park of 6-15 acres west of 71st Avenue, in accordance with the Parks and Trails Master Plan. The exact location has not been determined. The scope will be determined by neighborhood and site-specific needs. At this time, the project is not funded.

The City plans to acquire land and construct a new community park east of 85 on the formerly Dill Farm (District 1) property. The new 40-acre park would include: playground(s); picnic shelters; recreational activity site and open turf/play area; athletic fields for practices; and off-street parking. It would also include a permanent restroom and other amenities as the site and community needs would allow. The project is not currently funded.

records.Project: Comm. Park, N. or 10th/E. of 71st/W. of 35th
records.Description: The City plans to construct a new community park north of 10th Street, east of 71st Avenue and west of 35th Avenue, to include an open turf/play area, athletic fields for practices and off-street parking. It will also include a permanent restroom facility and other amenities as the site and community needs would allow. At this time, the project is not funded.

records.Project: Comm. Park, S. of 10th St., W. of 71st Ave.
records.Description: This project would consist of a 40-acre community park with playground(s), picnic shelters, a recreational activity site and open turf/play area, athletic fields for practices, and off-street parking. It would also include a permanent restroom and other amenities. At this time, the project is unfunded.
The existing plant #2 was decommissioned over 10 years ago. This project will demolish the plant and reclaim the grounds.

As we reported previously, the Northern Colorado Water Conservancy District's plans include a $250 million dam and reservoir project (Windy Gap Firming project). The final EIS was published by the Bureau of Reclamation in November of 2011. Jeff now expects the design RFP will be issued this month.

The City's capital plan includes proposed funding for architectural design for a new City Hall building. Claud informs us that the funding is a placeholder. At this point, he says the project is on hold. We will monitor progress and let you know if and when it is activated.

The Evergreen Fire Protection District hopes to remodel or rebuild its oldest fire station. The station was built in 1964. We must have misunderstood the conversation we had with Mike a couple of months ago. We thought he said it was possible they would issue an architectural/engineering RFP sometime during the first quarter of 2016. Mike now says it may be several years before they initiate the project. Sorry for any confusion.

Art reported previously that the Town's long-term plans included a new fire station to go on line in 2018. An RFP should be out now or very soon for architectural/engineering services for site and building design.

As we reported previously, Fort Collins anticipates issuing an RFP for design of park structures, including shelters and restrooms, at Maple Hill Park. A couple of months ago, Kurt expected to issue the RFP in December or January. He now says they decided to refine the RFP and plan to issue it in the next couple of months.
An RFP should be out now or very soon for exhibit development/design for the Colorado History Museum.

records.Project: South and Foothills Campuses Master Developer
records.Description: Shelly reports that she expects the University will issue an RFP in the next month or so (pending approval from the Office of the State Architect) for a master developer for the South and Foothills campuses. This will be the first step in a P3 process they would like to use for some future development.
records.Type: AS, DR, EV, GT, MS, PK, PL, SW, ST, SV, WR

records.Description: This District anticipates putting a capital projects bond on the November, 2016 ballot. While it has not been officially approved by the Board, they have gone ahead and advertised for architectural services for a new 50,000 sf Innovation Center, a new PK-5 elementary, and a 250,000 sf high school classroom addition. Once the program is approved, they will figure out what other consulting services will be needed, and may begin advertising for those services prior to the vote. At least some of the projects will use the CM/GC delivery method.
records.Type: AS, CM, DR, MS, PK, ST, TR

records.Description: In the next month or so, the Department of Military and Veterans Affairs plans to issue a request for statements of work for design of a new parachute facility at the Watkins Special Forces Armory in Watkins.
Elizabeth reports that she expects an RFP will go out this first quarter for design of structural rehabilitation of the finished water reservoir at the Wemlinger Water Purification Facility.

Breckenridge recently selected the design engineering firm for its Second Water Treatment Plant project. Within the next couple of months or so, they expect to advertise for construction manager at risk services. The selection process will be managed through the Owner's Representative.

Routt County requests proposals no later than 1:00 Monday February 29 for construction manager/general contractor services for the District 1 Road and Bridge Shop Expansion and Remodel project, RFP #480. A pre-proposal conference will be held at 8:00 Monday, February 8 at the District 1 shop, 24500 CR27, Oak Creek 80467. Questions must be submitted in writing and submitted to Marti Hamilton no later than 5:00 Monday, February 22. For further information or a copy of the RFP, contact Marti Hamilton or go to http://www.co.routt.co.us/Bids.aspx .

The existing bath house is the original structure, with minimal improvements made throughout the years. The proposed improvements include electrical and plumbing repairs, plus functional and aesthetic improvements to the shower and changing areas.

This project provides for ballfield and park improvements at Emerald Park, located adjacent to Emerald Elementary School. Improvements will include: a new irrigation system; new backstop and fence structure; new turf; improved infields; a new park shelter; and replacement of the old basketball court and horseshoe pits.

Phase II development of the east side (21 acres) of the Loveland Sports Park will include additional skate park features and lighting, additional multi-purpose sports fields, a restroom, shelters (2), parking areas and site amenities.

The Gondola Lot Master Plan is completed and the Town has some property included in the development. The scope of the Town's participation could include the river restoration, a parking structure and other public benefits. The dollar amount shown here is a placeholder.

This project consists of a new water quality lab building for water and wastewater regulatory and non-regulatory laboratory analysis. The primary reasons for the need include: Safety issues with lack of egress in areas with explosive gases; lack of adequate space to perfom analysis; inability to separate areas that need to be utilized for sterile analyses; incubators and ovens with lack of adequate ventilation causing health issues; and corrosive environment with lack of adequate ventilation, which creates safety issues.

records.Project: West Woods Golf Club Practice Area
records.Description: This project will upgrade/rebuild the practice areas at the West Woods golf club. It will downsize and move the 10,000 sf putting green, create a new range tee south of the existing tees at the former putting green location, add practice bunkers and a short game practice area at the north end of the range, and investigate the possibility of relocating/removing the south chipping green for expanded parking or a gazebo for weddings and other special events.

This project will construct an underpass under South Park Avenue connecting the existing Riverwalk on the north side and Main Street Station on the south. CDOT and the Town have created construction plans, which are 70% complete. Therefore, it is probable that no new consultant services will be needed. The project will include a new bridge, pedestrian walkway, rock retaining walls, curb and gutter, lighting and signage.
records.Type: AS, BR, DR, MS, PK, ST

records.Description: The Town's capital plan includes proposed funding for future parks that could be built in Meadows Filing #18, Liberty Village, Terrain or Castlewood Ranch Filing #2. The current cost estimate is based on the assumption of a five to six-acre park site.
This project provides for a Parks and Open Space maintenance building.

This project will accomplish major renovations to accommodate new and changed programs and to ensure building code updates. The East Boulder Community Recreation Center was built in 1991. The current capital plan allocates $452,000 toward the project. No source of funding has been identified for the remaining $648,000.
This project would include the update of the 1998 ADA Transition Plan for Parks and Recreation Facilities and sites to evaluate conformance to Federal mandates.

records.Project: New Substation, SE Corner of Service Territory
records.Description: This project provides for a new electric substation in the southeast corner of the service territory, to better accommodate load growth expected near I-25 and Highway 402.

This project is recommended based on the 2007 Solids Management Study and will provide onsite dewatering capability to reduce the volume of digested biosolids hauled off site and to reduce dependence on liquid waste hauling. The project will be built on the WAS thickening building and will incorporate centrifuges or related technology for dewatering and solids cake loading into biosolids hauling trucks.
The City plans to build a new playground and shelter at Orr Park.
The City plans to replace the Hillcrest water booster pump station.
The City plans to build two new water storage tanks of 3 million gallons each at the Ridges Basin water treatment plant and Airpark.
This project provides for architectural design and construction of a replacement airport terminal building.
The City plans to upgrade or replace the fire training tower in 2020.

The City Council has expressed an interest in developing a field house. The project is intended to be a partnership with other entities, such as the school district and/or other municipalities. The facility would provide year-round opportunities for sports such as lacrosse and rugby, plus general use by the public. The Town anticipates contributing $4.5 million of the cost, with the other half coming from other participating entities.

The City has programmed funding at various times to address additional wastewater treatment facilities required to meet new effluent regulations. The 2018-2020 funding is to address needs associated with phosphorus related requirements.

This currently unfunded project would relocate Fire Station #3 out of the 100-year floodplain, and combine the new station of 17,000 sf with Fire Administration offices of 11,000 sf. It would also construct storage for the fire vehicles and equipment into one new facility. The building cost is estimated at $11,412,500 with additional costs up to $8.6 million for land.
The City plans to add a classrooms, offices and a conference room, totalling 4,000 new square feet. At this time, the project is unfunded.
This unfunded project would construct a concrete driver training area totaling approximately 200,000 square feet. It would also provide a 10,000 sf storage facility for training props and equipment.

The area around Fire Station #6, at 5145 N. 63rd Street, has experienced significant development since the station was constructed in 1979. This project provides for a remodel of the existing station. At this time, the project is not funded.
This project would remodel and expand Fire Station #5, currently located at 4365 19th Street.

Fire Station #1 at 2241 13th Street, at 7,941 square feet, is too small and poorly designed. It needs to be 17,000 square feet to house one fire engine, one ladder truck and crews plus a battalion chief. At this time, no source of funding has been identified to complete the project.

Fire Station #7, at 1380 55th Street, would be remodeled to provide a total of 8,006 square feet t house one fire engine, the hazardous materials team and crew. The current 5,081 sf building was constructed in 2000. The project is not funded in the current capital plan.

The City plans to construct a third police community station in the Candelas area of the city. The new station is planned to be substantially similar to the West Woods and Lake Arbor stations, though potential building collaboration with the Arvada Fire Protection District may hasten a different plan.

This project provides for the design and construction of a new recreation facility, to include a pool. It will be located in or around the Triangle Area along the Ralston corridor. While the City would participate in the construction, it is considering having Apex Park and Recreation District operate the facility upon completion.

This project provides future funding for development of a park site adjacent to Cottonwood Park. The City has an opportunity to develop this site, perhaps as a "bookend" to Community Park. Development would relieve pressure and scheduling issues at Steinbaugh and Community Park.

records.Project: Museum and Public Safety Storage Facility
records.Description: This project would build a 20,000 sf space on the campus of Public Safety's firing range off Highway 119 at County Road 5, to house the Museum's permanent collection (15,000 square feet) and Public Safety's evidence and seized property (5,000 square feet). At this time, the project is not funded in the five-year program.

Candelas is a large residential area extending from Indiana Street to SH 93 north of SH 72. This neighborhood park is located in Filing Four. The park will include more open play turf, a playground, two tennis courts, trail, picnic facilities, retaining walls, lalndscaping and irrigation.

Based on recommendations of the Aquatics Facility Study, these projects would provide implementation of key indoor aquatic facility enhancements of "watertainment" facilities that encourage additional use for all age groups. Features include expanded waterplay for youth, warm water experiences for the aging population, and a variety of family oriented water features, from a "lazy river" to water climbers. Specific projects will be developed with extensive public involvement.

The Parks Department's master plan and the Reservoir Master Plan identified a number of deferred maintenance backlog items to buildings and grounds. The City has allocated $2.25 million to support recent bond funded improvements, including a new bath house and shelter, renovated boat house and improvements to picnic and family areas. An additional $2.25 million remains unfunded at this time. Initial work will include site assessments for major buildings and development of design drawings.

This project involves a planning study to evaluate maintenance operations for efficiency and required asset improvements. It will develop site plans and cost estimates for capital repairs per the master plan, General Maintenance and Management Plan and the Yards recommendation.
This project involves the construction of new office space and an additional vehicle storage bay. A facilities master plan completed in 2015 identified the need for this expanded space.

This project provides for landscaping, a truck washing facility, and equipment storage at 175 Kellogg on completion of the Operations and Maintenance Center and the Administration and Customer Service buildings.
The City has programmed funding in 2017 to expand Baker Park. They also plan to replace the playground and to replace the shelter/restroom building.
This project provides for replacement of the restroom facilities at Cushing Park, located at 700 West Dartmouth Avenue.
This project provides for replacement of the shelter/restroom facility at Bates/Logan Park, located at 2938 South Logan Street.
The City has programmed funding in 2019 to construct a wave rider at the Englewood Recreation Center.
This project will replace the shelter restroom facility at Jason Park, located at 4299 South Jason Street.
This project provides for a future expansion of the Pirate's Cove amusement/outdoor aquatic facility.
This project provides for an expansion of Terminal Reservoir.
This project will replace the 2nd Avenue water line.
This project will complete a structure to provide apparatus and vehicle storage.
The City's capital plan includes a project to complete new storage capacity for transit buses.

records.Project: Sewer Line and Lift Station Imp's
records.Description: The City has programmed future funding for sewer line and lift station improvements. Specific projects will be identified as the year approaches.
This project would replace playgrounds at Centennial, Heritage, Keith Helart, Elephant and Cottonwood Parks. The existing play structures are outdated and in need of upgrading and replacement.

This funding is proposed for renovations at the Sports Complex to be completed in conjunction with improvements Lafayette will be constructing. Louisville's improvements include repaving the parking lot, hardscape for pedestrian circulation, ADA accessibility, a concession building and synthetic turf fields.

Platform tennis is a racquet sport that has been growing in popularity. The game is played on an elevated aluminum deck 1/4 the size of a tennis court and is surrounded by 12-foot high fencing which allows play off the walls as in racquetball and squash. The base is usually enclosed, allowing for a heating system beneath the deck. The City proposes to build a platform tennis facility after the current five-year planning period.

Improvements at the Community Dog Park are proposed as follows, in priority order: establish a small dog area; construct and modify the stone retaining wall around the pond; install a shelter; and install synthetic turf.

Funding is proposed to reorient and repurpose the current four-building campus to encompass a city visitor center, to expand exhibit and community space, and to create appropriate storage for museum artifacts and documents. Implementation of the project may depend on grant funding to augment available city funding.
This project will renovate the existing office-umpire's space into a concession stand and add 500 square feet of office-storage space to the north end of the building.

The Bus Barn lift station is located just east of Loveland High School. The electric service includes single phase power that is converted to 3-phase via an add-a-phase converter. The back-up generator is also single phase. The proposed project will include running 3-phase power to the facility and modifying the generator to 3-phase.

records.Project: Namaqua Hills Water Booster Sta. & Generator
records.Description: The Namaqua Hills booster station was built in the 1960s when the area developed, and subsequently turned over to the City for operation and maintenance. Proposed improvements will generally include replacing aging pumps, valves and controls and adding a backup generator.

The 4-acre training center parcel includes three buildings totalling 9,108 square feet and a railroad spur. Other structures on the property are temporary and will be eliminated when current tenants vacate the property. This project will develop a multi-year improvement plan to meet Fire Department training needs. It may include relocating of facilities, building renovations and enhancements, paving, environmental studies, and museum and other improvements.

records.Project: Service Ctr. - Ph. I New Bldg./Remodel
records.Description: This project funds the design and construction of a second Service Center building and expansion of the existing Service Center. The new building will house Utilities field operations, Street, Fleet and Facilities Services staff.

This project will design and construct the Broomfield Community Center kitchen expansion/remodel and the relocation of the Senior Services administrative offices. The kitchen remodel will expand into the existing office space requiring the relocation of offices to either the Bronze room in the Community Center or to an alternate location.
This project will make needed improvements, renovations and repairs to the parking lot, lobby, storage and sundeck. It will also complete the remaining improvements to the HVAC and roof.

While this project is titled "2 Potable Water Storage Tanks," it consists of construction of one million-gallon tank that would supply the Airport and Interlocken zones by gravity. It will include associated piping.

The North Broomfield lift station is the ultimate lift station to serve the northern area of the city. The lift station will be built in phases. The initial phase will pump wastewater flows to the existing Anthem Lift Station until that facility reaches 70% capacity. Lift station modifications include replacement of the pumps for requirements to utilize the North Broomfield force main to the wastewater treatment facility.

In 2015, City Council accepted the Thornton Facilities Master Plan for the Infrastructure Maintenance Center and the Municipal Services Center. The plan identifies improvements necessary for current and future operations of these centers. Phase 3 includes additional vehicle storage, paving around the site, and construction of material storage bins.
This project provides for a new Fire Station #6 in the area of 140th Avenue and Quebec Street. The new fire station will allow for improved service delivery to northeast Thornton.
The City plans to relocate Fire Station #1 to the area of Thornton Parkway and Steele Street.
This project provides for plaza improvements at Boardwalk Park.
This project provides for the construction of a new Central Fire Station. The station will be an active station replacing the fire station and EMS on Yampa Street.
This project provides for improvements to the buildings at the cemetery.
The City plans a future expansion of its City Hall building.
The City has programmed future funding for improvements to the campground office space and bath house.
The City's capital plan includes proposed funding for remodeling of the Astor House.
This project provides for a future facility for artifact storage.

records.Project: Riverwalk Center Lobby and Park Imp's
records.Description: This project will implement improvements to the grounds and lobby as identified in the master plan. Of the total cost, $3.5 million would be used for the lobby expansion and $550,000 for improvements to the river bank and plaza. Tom says an RFP for architectural services should go out in the next couple of months or so.

Previously, Kris reported that Erie anticipated advertising for design to repair and upgrade the Town's 1.5 million gallon water storage tank. She now says the project is likely to be bid as a design/build project. The RFP should be issued sometime after the first of the year.

We reported on this project previously. The County has acquired the Belvidere Theatre building in Central City. They received a structural assessment grant from the State Historical Fund and were in the process of applying for a second grant to construct a roof on a portion of the building where the roof collapsed a few years ago. Ray Rears said an RFP should be going out for design. Ray is no longer with the County. Tony Petersen says they have no plans to issue an RFP in the near future.

Jay reported previously that the City expected to seek consultant services late this year for final design of a park. The work will require substantial floodplain mitigation. Jay now says the RFP should go out sometime in January.

As we reported previously, the University of Colorado expects to seek construction management/general contractor services for renovation of this existing gymnasium into an academic building. The RFP should be issued sometime in December.
Within the next week or so, Foothills Park and Recreation District plans to seek a structural engineer for a rebuild of a retaining wall at the 11th hold at Meadows Golf Course.
In the next few months, Breckenridge may seek architectural services for design of a roof structure over an outdoor ice rink.

records.Project: FTC Site Plan, Const. Drawings, Ph. 1
records.Description: Following the completion of the Frisco Transit Center master plan, the County plans to advertise for assistance with planning/architecture/engineering work needed to prepare a more detailed site plan and construction drawings for Phase 1 construction of the improvements. They expect to advertise around February.
