In the next couple of months, Crested Butte plans to issue an RFQ or RFP for design of wastewater treatment plant upgrades, to include a second oxidation ditch, new grit removal and screenings systems, and UV disinfection upgrades.
Sometime in 2016, Eagle County plans to issue an RFP for architectural and engineering design services for a terminal and landside expansion project.

We reported previously that the District was conducting a Facilities Master Plan, scheduled for completion this summer. The Board has decided to put a $92 million bond issue on the November ballot. Projects would include a new high school, a new elementary, a new PK-8, plus various renovations and other improvements. Information about the master plan and proposed projects is available on the District's website, http://www.sssd.k12.co.us . If the bond passes, they will begin advertising RFQ/Ps for design, etc. around mid November.

records.Project: Brantner Gulch LS and Force Main Decomm.
records.Description: Previously, Mitch indicated that, later this year or early in 2016, Metro might seek consulting services for a project to decommission the Brantner Gulch lift station and force main. He now says they will not conduct a consultant selection for the project, but will use the consultants already involved with the Northern Treatment Plant/South Platte Interceptor project.

As we reported in August, the City plans to initiate design of Fire Station #15 near Tallyn's Reach. Tom reported previously that, if the prototype study already underway went well, they might decide to continue with the same firm for design of Fire Station 15. It now appears that they will continue with that firm.
In the next couple of weeks, Breckenridge plans to advertise an RFP for consultant/design services for a new parking structure.

Ross reports that the District hopes to pass a mill levy increase this November. If successful, they will issue an RFP for the various services needed to design and construct a new facility and to renovate the current facility in Frederick.

In about mid October, Colorado Springs expects to advertise for construction management/general contractor services for the Pikes Peak Summit Complex project. The project will replace the existing four buildings at the top of the mountain with three new buildings.
records.Type: AS, CM, DR, MS, PK, ST

records.Description: As we reported previously, Commerce City voters passed a ballot measure for various capital improvement projects. One of the largest projects is a new recreation center in the northern part of the city. Carolyn now says an RFP should be issued sometime this fall. Interested firms may go to the City's website at www.c3gov.com/issue2k , click on Procurement Process, and then Vendor Opt In. You will then receive updates on the project as they become available.

We reported previously that Vail expected to issue an RFP for design services for neighborhood park improvements at Booth Creek Park. They completed preliminary design in house. Todd now says he hopes to issue the RFP soon for design development and construction documents for the park redevelopment. This three-acre park includes a tennis court, picnic shelter, playground, restrooms and site improvements.
We reported on this project previously. Tom now says the Town expects to advertise in the next month to six weeks for design of a water treatment plant.

As we reported previously, the Department of Public Safety requested funding in the 2015/16 fiscal year budget for the Loma Port of Entry, on the Utah border. The project will entail replacement of the existing building, scale lanes, pit scales, etc. The state's budget "Long Bill" includes $1,145,000 for the project this fiscal year. Matt now informs us that the State had pre-existing designs for this project, and does not expect to advertise for consulting services.

records.Project: Owner Advisor for Water Treatment Plant
records.Description: As we reported previously, Thornton plans to advertise for owner advisor services for water treatment plant improvements. Dennis now says the RFP should go out in August or early September.

records.Project: Exterior Stone and Window Rest. - Capitol
records.Description: As we reported previously, the State Buildings office plans to seek consultant services for design of exterior stone and window replacements at the Capitol. Lance says the RFP should be out now or very soon.
As we reported previously, Arvada plans to advertise for design-build services for a steel storage building with a two-lane fire range. Kim says the RFP should be issued this week.

In the next couple of months, the City of Arvada expects to issue an RFP for design development including full design documents for the expansion of the West Wood Golf Clubhouse. They have received informal approval of the preferred conceptual design. The RFP for the next phase is subject to final approval of the design concept.
Sometime this fall, the City expects to advertise an RFP for full design of Riverside Park.
In the next few weeks, Aurora plans to advertise for architectural/engineering services for renovation of the Peoples building.
In the next couple of months or so, Avon plans to issue an RFP for planning of Town facilities.

Mark reports that he hopes to issue an RFP in the next couple of months for design/build services to replace the gymnasium bleachers. He anticipates that the work will be completed by a company specializing in bleacher installations.
Jim reports that it is POSSIBLE, but not definite, that the District will issue an RFP for design of a river retaining wall. They might decide to select a firm without a competitive process.

DIA's current schedule indicates a late August RFP for on-call civil design services for 2016. Services may include civil, electrical, environmental, geotechnical, signage and structural engineering. They expect to award two contracts for this work.
records.Type: AS, DR, EV, GT, MS, ST

records.Description: In the next month or two, Douglas County Schools expects to advertise an RFQ for architectural services and roofing consultants for future capital projects.

As we reported previously, this project will install a surface diversion structure along Plum Creek in the reach downstream of the Plum Creek Wastewater Authority facility and Sedalia. The raw water pipeline will move the water collected from Plum Creek at the surface diversion structure south into town to be treated at the Plum Creek Water Purification Facility. The length of the pipeline will depend on the exact location of the diversion structure. Sheri now says it is possible they will not publicly advertise an RFP for this project because of some time sensitive issues that have come up.
Brad reported previously that the City might advertise for ADA compliance consulting services. He now says he is not sure of the timing of an RFP.

Previously, we reported that Grand Junction might seek consultant/design services for a Police Department annex facility. Jay now says they recently were notified that they would receive grant funding for this project, so they expect to issue an RFP in the near future for architectural services.

In April, Peter reported that Colorado Mountain College might issue an RFP for design of a small classroom/storage addition at its facility in Leadville. He now says they have had a change of direction and will not seek professional services for this project.

Rod reported previously that he planned to issue an RFP for design to rebuild the secondary clarifier at the wastewater treatment plant. He now says the Town Manager decided to invite only local engineers to propose on the project.

Previously, Scott reported that it was possible that the County would require consulting services for some facility master planning related to industrial and administrative functions. He now says the RFP should be out soon, possibly this week.

In the next 30 days or so, the Parks and Open Space Department plans to issue an RFP for job order civil engineering services. They anticipate selecting approximately five firms to provide grading, drainage, erosion control and small structures engineering services to assist their landscape architects with in-house park design projects.
In the next month, Aurora plans to advertise for architectural/engineering design for the repurposing of a 37,000 sf, three-story building for use by the Police Department.

records.Project: Fire Station Prototype Space Planning, etc.
records.Description: The City of Aurora requests proposals no later than 3:00 Wednesday, June 10 for space programming and conceptual development services for a new prototype fire station that is scalable in nature, for a minimum of two new fire stations. A pre-submittal meeting is scheduled at 11:00 Wednesday, June 3 at 15151 East Alameda , Suite 3500. Questions should be directed to Bryn Fillinger in Purchasing, at bfilling@auroragov.org .

The Village Greens Park North master plan identified various improvements for the park. The last construction phase, completed in 2013, included the pond construction, disc golf course and mountain bike skills course. This phase IV includes a park entry, restrooms and shelters. Suzanne anticipates issuing an RFP later this spring or in the summer.

We reported previously that Loveland anticipated seeking consulting services for design of an expansion of the wastewater treatment plant. In February, Roger said he was not sure whether or not they would advertise an RFQ. He now reports that they decided to invite three firms to propose on the project and are in the selection process.

Previously, Bill reported that Woodland Park planned to advertise for design of Woodland Station infrastructure improvements to support the Woodland Aquatic Center project. In February, he said they had an RFP ready to go, but they might decide to use a "different acquisition method." He now says they decided not to advertise the project and are negotiating with a firm through a sole source procurement.

As we reported previously, Adams County plans to advertise for design of a wingwall replacement and widening of the E. 88th Avenue bridge over Wolf Creek. The RFP should be advertised in the next month or two. The project will use Off-System Bridge program funding through CDOT. Russ says they are still coordinating with CDOT for funding. He expects to have a better idea of the schedule within the next several weeks.

As we reported previously, Colorado State University plans to seek firms for design-build services for a biology building project. Shelly says the project will go out in the next one to three months for shortlisting of design-build firms.
We reported on this project previously. Shelly now says Colorado State University plans to go out in the next one to three months to short list design-build firms for a medical center project.

As we reported previously, the Department of Military and Veterans Affairs expects to issue an RFP for design/build services for expansion of the Fort Lupton Readiness Center. The project will include a building addition and a substantial motor pool. Bob now anticipates an RFP will be issued in late November or early December.
This fall, Windsor may seek design-build services for some park shelter replacements. Omar says it is also possible they will do the design work in house.

In the next few months or so, Park County plans to advertise for design of the Consolidated Office Building Phase II project. The person who gave us this information specifically asked that we not publish contact information and requests that consultants watch the County's website for the RFP - parkco.us. On the left is a link to Bids and Proposals. You may sign up to receive an email or text message when new requests are posted. (We will also report on any new postings.)

In the next few months or so, Park County plans to issue an RFP for design of the demolition and reconstruction of the Jefferson Road and Bridge shop. The person who gave us this information specifically asked that we not publish contact information and requests that consultants watch the County's website for the ad. The website address is parkco.us. There is a link on the left side to bids and proposals. You can sign up to receive email or text notifications when items are posted. We will also notify you when RFQ/Ps are posted on the site.
In the next one to three months, Colorado State plans to go out for shortlisting of design-build firms for the South College Avenue parking garage project.
In a month or two, CSU MAY issue an RFQ for program plans for the Institute for Biological and Translational Therapies and the Veterinary Teaching Hospital buildings.

Jefferson County requests qualifications no later than 11:00 Wednesday, April 15 for architectural, engineering and planning services. The County (Open Space) plans to award multiple contracts to be used as projects come up. The RFQ is available on the Rocky Mountain Bid System, rockymountainbidsystem.com.
records.Type: AS, DR, EV, GT, MS, PK, PL, ST, WR

records.Description: This project, unfunded as yet but on the list of "high priority" projects, proposes to increase the bedroom size, build a weight room and install new electrical, plumbing and HVAC equipment at Fire Station #7, at 3901 Palmer Park Blvd. The project may be included in a future bond program. The City considered placing the bond on the April, 2015 ballot, but subsequently decided not to do it this year. If and when approved, the project is scheduled in the second year of a five-year program.

This project, unfunded but considered a high priority, will modify living quarters to better accommodate men and women fire fighters. It will repair/replace the apparatus bay floor, repair structural cracking and modify the living quarters to increase kitchen size, sleeping quarters and the weight room due to locker room modifications. It will also include new HVAC systems. The project is included on a list for a proposed future bond. If and when approved, it is scheduled in the third year of a five-year program.

The 60-year old Coliseum facility is in need of major interior and exterior improvements. The work will include HVAC improvements, plumbing upgrades, parking lot stabilization and reconstruction and barn demolition and reconstruction. The project is included as a "first tier priority" in the six-year work plan but no funding has been identified to initiate it at this point.

This project would demolish the existing burn building and construct a new facility. The new facility is projected to cost $2 million for building construction and $700,000 for a water reclamation system. Planning will also include analysis of alternate site locations. The project is considered a first tier priority deferred project.

Parks and Recreation needs a new and upgraded facility for district headquarters maintenance and operations staff. This project will improve workplace health, safety, security and efficiency through upgrades to buildings and exterior storage areas that support maintaining citywide parks, medians and other areas. Many existing facilities have no water, heat/AC, toilets or adequate security. The City's Real Estate Division is working with Parks on land opportunities that may exist for alternative locations for the facilities. The project is a Tier 1 priority, but no source of funding is currently available.

This project would demolish two city-owned structures to allow construction of a new District 6 police station. The structures are located at 1566 Washington Street and 701 East Colfax. The project is considered a first tier priority, but no source of funding has yet been identified to initiate the project.

This project consists of replacement of the existing Ruby Hill pool with a new pool facility (cost estimate $3 million) and completion of the upper north end of the park (the Overlook Phase), estimated to cost $1 million. The project includes creation of a viewing platform with seating, public art and trail connections, amphitheater development, restroom and vendor support. The project is considered a first tier priority in the 2013-2018 capital plan, but no source of funding has been identified to complete the project.
The Town's capital plan includes a project to renovate the East Vail fire station in 2016.

Improvements to the Red Hawk Ridge golf course will include cart paths, permanent restrooms on the course, a chipping green, irrigation updates and other golf course grounds improvements. These may include a walking bridge or passage across #10 ditch, rock wall repairs on #18 lake, rock wall improvements in the parking lot below the range and irrigation replacements and updates including irrigation lines and clocks.
records.Type: AS, BR, MS, PK, ST, WR

records.Description: This project will construct a new water storage tank in the Castle Oaks subdivision adjacent to an existing tank. The capacity will be 2 million gallons. The tank is needed to facilitate water storage and pumping operations for future imported surface water. It will also be used for water coming from Rueter-Hess Reservoir.

The Green Valley Ranch recreation center includes a gym, locker room, showers, meeting room and weight room. This project would construct an indoor pool on land adjacent to the existing building. While the project is considered a Tier 1 priority, no source of funding is currently available.

The current Police Administration Building at 1331 Cherokee primarily serves as the headquarters for the Department and the Manager of Safety's office. Adjacent to the building is a pre-arrangement detention facility, currently unoccupied. The Department of Safety's vision is to redevelop these two parcels into a "Safety Campus," to include demolition of the existing buildings and build-out of user and evidence storage space. The Real Estate Division will complete a study to determine space needs for master planning. A cost estimate will be developed as part of the planning process. The project is not currently funded.

The Denver County Jail building has been in operation since 1956. Many of the building systems and much of the user space is in need of signifant rehabilitation. As part of the Justice Center bond program, the City has completed significant structural improvements. Additional remodel and rehabilitation of existing jail facilities are needed to address life/safety issues, to update facilities and to support various inmate programs. At this time, these improvements are unfunded.

This project includes two projects at Congress Park. The first is design and construction of a new pool facility to replace the existing outdated outdoor pool. The second project will construct a new playground. A needs assessment has been completed. The project is considered a Tier 1 priority but is not funded in the 2013-18 capital plan.

The sculpture park is a triangle of open space adjacent to the Denver Performance Arts Center. This project proposes to install a permanent stage and utility infrastructure. Currently, there is no way to adequately distribute power for temporary uses. Other improvements may include additional lighting and irrigation system upgrades. The project is considered a Tier 1 priority but is not currently funded.
The City plans to complete maintenance shop improvements at Willis Case golf course.

This project continues implementation of the recommendations of the 2003 Kennedy Ballpark Master Plan. Planned improvements include new shade structures on eight dugouts, four new shade structures for spectators and at least one new picnic shade structure for permitted events. The project is considered a Tier 1 priority in the 2013-18 capital plan, but is not currently funded.

This project provides for a remodel/retrofit of the upper and lower computer rooms in 2016 ($1 million), to include power, heating/cooling, and fire suppression. In the future, it is possible the Town will relocate the upper and lower rooms into a combined room.

This project provides for the replacement of the Sand Creek Police substation. The project is contingent on passage of a future bond, the timing of which is undetermined. If approved, it is scheduled in the first year of a five-year program. The timing of the bond election has not been determined.

The City hopes to construct a new police evidence building. The project is contingent on passage of a future bond, the timing of which is undetermined. If approved, the project is scheduled to begin in the third year of a five-year program.

This project provides for expansion of the Police impound facility. If the City is successful in passing a future bond, the project is scheduled in the fifth year of a five-year program. At this time, it is uncertain when the bond may be placed on the ballot.
This project will rehabilitate or replace existing wells as they reach the end of their useful lives. The replacement schedule is based on an assumed 25-year life for each well.

This project provides for construction of a new water tank to facilitate pumping operations. The new 2 million gallon tank will be located in the Timber Canyons subdivision. The project was previously identified to be located at the Tank 14 site; however, operational plans have changed.

This project will remodel the kitchen and bathrooms at Fire Station 4. The kitchen remodel includes replacing the existing cabinets and counter tops with commercial grade cabinets and counters that are better able to withstand the wear and tear of everyday use. The bathroom remodel will allow the fire fighters to have private personal areas.

We reported previously on the Northern Colorado Water Conservancy District's Glade Reservoir (the Northern Integrated Supply Project - NISP). This will be a new reservoir and dam northwest of Fort Collins, plus a large pump station and other related improvements. The dam will be on Poudre River water, but off channel. Carl still says he expects to issue an RFP for preliminary design in late February or early March.

We reported previously that CU Boulder expected to advertise for design or design/build services for a new multi-tenant office building at the research park. In December, Tom said he still hoped the design RFQ would be issued this next summer. He now says it is again on hold, and he does not know when it might move forward. At this point, they expect to use the design/build delivery method.

A new River North Park has been proposed as an opportunity to create a recreational focal point for this area. This project includes development and implementation of a neighborhood park with shelters, walking paths, regional trail connections, plantings, gathering areas and other amenities and features. Concept level planning has been completed. (The cost estimate was developed in a previous year and could be subject to change.)

records.Project: New Gates at Two Buttes Dam
records.Description: As we reported previously, the Division of Wildlife expects to advertise an RFQ for design of new gates at Two Buttes Dam, located in southeastern Colorado. John now says the project is still planned, but he does not have a specific time frame.

As we reported previously, Colorado Springs expects to advertise for design of major improvements at the visitors center at the top of Pikes Peak. Curt now says an RFP could go out in February. An alternate contact, Jack Glavan (719-385-7714) with the Pikes Peak Highway office, says he hopes the RFP will go out in February or March.
As we reported previously, Colorado Springs expects to advertise an RFP for design of Fire Station #1 renovation. Curt now says the RFP should go out within two months.

As we reported previously, Metro might issue an RFP for architectural/engineering services for miscellaneous interior modifications/tenant finish improvements. Dave now says he's not sure when this project will go or what improvements they will need. We will follow up.

Previously, the County issued an RFP for four design/build projects: 1) ADA improvements at Radino Hall; 2) DHS site improvements; 3) New bathroom facilities at Columbine Park rodeo grounds; and, 4) A new storage facility at Columbine Park rodeo grounds. Eric reports that they rejected all of the proposals and are in the process of redrafting the solicitation. It should go out in a week or two.

As we reported previously, Fort Collins Utilities plans to advertise for design and construction services for future anticipated work at its water reclamation facilities. Owen now expects the RFI/RFP will be issued in early March.
Early in 2015, Brighton expects to advertise for design/build services for a new second park at Northgate. The new park will consist of about three acres.
records.Type: AS, DR, MS, PK, PL, ST

records.Description: In December, Justin reported that Avon expected to advertise after the first of the year for architectural services for a Town Hall tenant finish project. He now says that voters rejected the project, so they do not plan to move forward with it at this time.

records.Project: HVAC and Roof Repl., Watkins RC
records.Description: Kris reports that the Department of Military and Veterans Affairs might issue an RFP in the next couple of months for design of a Controlled Maintenance project to complete HVAC improvements and roof replacement at the Watkins Readiness Center. She says the initial design cost is below the threshold that requires public advertisement, but a subsequent phase may put it above the threshold.
An RFP should be out now or very soon for design of a new parking garage for the City.
Within a month or two, the University of Colorado Boulder plans to advertise for the design of renovations at the engineering center.
In the February to April time frame, Brighton expects to issue an RFP for design and construction of Cherry Meadows Park, new park improvements in a 2-3 acre drainage basin area.

records.Project: Planning Study, Downtown Bus Term. Reloc.
records.Description: Colorado Springs expects to issue an RFP for a planning study to look into relocating the downtown bus terminal. Jonni reports that they are waiting to obtain CDOT funding for the project but hope to advertise within the next few months.
The County's capital plan includes a project in 2018 to complete a new Sheriff's office substation in District 5.

This project provides for renovations and upgrades at the recreation center. Funding is proposed at $1 million per year in 2016 and 2017 and $625,000 in 2018. Potential improvements include aquatics expansion, rewiring/reconfiguring the lobby and pro shop space, adding an ADA compliant elevator, expanding programs (fitness and strength training, youth), and other miscellaneous improvements.

This currently unfunded project calls for the remodel of the existing Sunset golf course maintenance building, including ventilation, plumbing, and electrical improvements, plus an additional building and natural gas service.

This currently unfunded project provides for the construction of a new golf course maintenance facility, to be located south of the practice range with access from 9th Avenue. The existing building will be removed when the new facility is completed.

A two-level addition of 1,000 square feet will: expand the Children/Youth resources after school; provide prevention and intervention programs to accommodate special events; add programming space for activities, arts and crafts and activity clubs; provide additional space on the upper level for therapeutic groups, classes and meetings; and expand the cement pad to accommodate a larger area for basketball. This project is currently unfunded.

This project involves remodeling 8,900 sf of office space in the upstairs portion of the Civic Center. Originally, the City envisioned using this space for Affordable Housing/CDBG, Community/Neighborhood Resources, Code Enforcement and Community Services Administrative operations. Because of changes in staff levels and space needs, the City plans to update the space needs study to reflect revised growth and service alignment scenarios. Is is possible other City functions could be considered for this space. At this time, no source of funding has been identified to complete the project.

This unfunded project calls for the expansion and remodel of the administration building (southwest corner of the Civic Center). Construction of exterior walls and roofing will enclose the open areas at the three corners of the building. Improvements will include remodeling of existing offices and conference room, addition of interior access corridors and an ADA bathroom, waiting areas and three offices, and HVAC upgrades. These changes will allow for the City Clerk's office to relocate with the City Manager's office. Planning and design will be combined with the remodel of other parts of the building (see our project ID #74589).

This unfunded project provides for the expansion and remodel of the east wing of the Civic Center Mall area. Construction of exterior walls and roofing would enclose the dock area. Improvements would also include minor remodeling of existing offices and the conference room, plus potential HVAC upgrades. Design of improvements to various parts of the Civic Center may be combined into one project. Projects will be divided for construction.

This unfunded project consists of the expansion and remodel of the west wing of the Civic Center Mall area. Improvements include minor remodeling of existing offices and conference room and potential HVAC modifications. The City may design improvements to various parts of the Civic Center as one project, then to construct individual projects such as this one.

This new neighborhood park would serve the Quail neighborhood. Development of this 20 acres of land may include picnic areas, a playground, restrooms, dog exercise areas, small skate park areas, shelters, pathways, sports courts, multi-use fields and landscaping.

This unfunded project will provide for a new museum collections storage facility to house the artifact collection of the Longmont Museum and Cultural Center (approximately 12,000 sqare feet). The City seeks to purchase and retrofit the RTD South Main bus garage and shop, approximately 12,000 square feet. The project will include walling up vinyl garage doors, adding HVAC, conducting an environmental study and clean-up, covering the oil change pits and disconnecting the bus wash mechanical equipment.

This unfunded project will design and construct an addition to the southeast side of the Longmont Recreation Center. It will redesign the fitness room into a cardio/weight area, and provide a new fitness room and large community room.
The County's five-year capital plan allocates $768,500 in 2016 to replace the roof at the Federal warehouse facility.

This project provides for repairs to or replacement of the Barker Dam outlet works. The outlet facilities are over 100 years old. The current configuration of the outlet gates requires that the reservoir be nearly emptied to perform a thorough inspection every 5-10 years. As currently envisioned, the project would construct a vertical shaft near the north embankment, inlet tunnels and one outlet tunnel, an outlet distribution facility, a pipeline to Barker gravity line and a valve house.
The City's capital plan includes $250,000 in 2017 for a water storage tank in Glenwood Highlands. Additional funding may be required in a future year.
This unfunded project addresses the Longmont Theater, which requires rehabilitation. The theater is located at 513 Main Street.

This project consists of the remodel of the former Fire Station #3, located in Centennial Park near the Longmont Youth Center. The facility will be remodeled to house additional recreation programs for all ages with an emphasis on activities for children and youth. Programming would include: drop-in and programmed activities; preschool programs; mobile recreation programs; an expanded summer day camp location; and community rental opportunities. The project is currently unfunded.

This project provides for implementation of Phase 2 of the Cemetery Master Plan which includes restoration of the existing Branch recycling site, restoration of the historic stone building and a new committal shelter.
This project provides for a new Police operations center. The City would like to get the project funded in an earlier year; however, at this point, the capital plan anticipates funding in 2017.
This project will design and construct a new water building for the City.

records.Project: Civic Center Remodel - Planning and Design
records.Description: Planning and design for the entire Civic Center complex will be completed, and construction for each wing is identified for each of the separate projects: PB-93A Civic Center Remodel - Administration; PB-93B Civic Center Remodel - Community Services, PB-93C Civic Center Remodel-East Wing; and PB93D Civic Center Remodel - West Wing. The design will be completed as one project, with construction divided into individual projects. The project is currently unfunded.
This project provides for Silver Creek Park development/improvements.
The City proposes to design and construct a satellite library.

The proposed pocket park improvement will include land acquisition for a 3/4-acre civic park, grading and drainage improvements, hardscape pavers, retaining walls, landscape, irrigation and civic park amenities to support the park space. Projected costs include $750,000 for acquisition and $1,116,227 for construction.

This project includes the demolition and removal of the existing facility, and the design and construction of a new parks barn/storage facility. The new facility is proposed to be approximately 50% larger than the existing facility and would include appropriate heating, electrical, and plumbing (i.e. eye wash station, utility sink) to meet the needs of the division.

This future project is currently unfunded. It provides for remodeling and refurniishing several areas of the Main Library, including the second floor areas and bridge, relocation of the Arapahoe entrance, the addition of 1,000 square feet to the second floor, renovating the basement and north wing, and various HVAC and minor repairs.
The County proposes a 2018 project to remodel the Converse Ranch farm house, which is located at the Hidden Mesa trailhead.

This project provides for improvements/development at Wildcat Regional Park. No specific plans are in place to initiate this work. The capital plan indicates that "Wildcat Regional Park may be activated at any time."
This project provides for improvements at Macanta Regional Park, in accordance with master planning efforts.
The City has allocated funding in 2018 for a new water pump station on Wilson Road.

records.Project: Evidence and Seized Property Storage Facility
records.Description: This project would provide for a building to house overflow evidence in a secure environment. It would include space for Public Safety specialty vehicles and square footage to support Public Safety training needs and victim outreach. The new facility would meet statutory requirements for evidence protection and retention. At this time, the project is unfunded.

This project will provide a treatment capacity increase of the primary treatment system to 12 mdg maximum per month design to provide additional plant capacity for city growth. The primary clarifier will be constructed in the area now occupied by the de-commissioned trickling filters.

Based on a 2011 study, it is advantageous for the wastewater treatment facility to phase in over time a move from a solids thickening treatment process to a solids de-watering process. The City has programmed funding in 2017 for these improvements.
This project provides for major rehabilitation of the Gregory Hill water storage tank.

records.Project: Countryside PS and Tank Major R&R
records.Description: The City plans to replace the Countryside pump station, and to complete repairs to the water storage tank.
The Town's capital plan proposes future funding for a competitive pool facility in the Reata West subdivision.
This project will demolish the existing trickling filter basins to make room for a new primary clarifier. The project coincides with the Primary Clarifier project.
This project provides for an expansion of the Bob L. Burger Recreation Center, 111 West Baseline Road.
The City's capital plan includes initial funding in 2018 for a water treatment peaking plant, with construction funding programmed in 2019.

The City's capital plan includes proposed funding in 2018 for design of a storage/concession building at the Fruita Civic Center. Construction would occur beyond the current five-year planning period.
The City's capital plan proposes funding in 2018 to expand the recreation center. They expect to seek a grant to partially fund the project.
The City hopes to use a combination of general fund money and a grant to expand the welcome center.
The City's capital plan includes proposed funding in 2015 for a park office and shop.

The City's capital plan included previous funding for preliminary planning/design for expansion of the Nelson-Flanders Water Treatment Plant. These plans could be revised once a decision is made regarding the future use of the Wade Gaddis plant.
The County has programmed funding for the relocation of the CSU Extension Division facility to Lima Plaza.
The County has programmed funding over four years for restroom upgrades at Courthouse 1.
This project provides for tenant improvements at the District Attorney's office building.
This project will replace the roof at the Altura Plaza facility.
This project provides for a new surface water treatment plant, to be initiated sometime after 2019.

The City has identified the need for analysis and repair of the existing Barker-Kossler penstock, including replacements or targeted repairs as recommended from the analyses, which will include those conducted by metallurgical and corrosion experts.

Proposed projects at the City's recreation and community centers will provide facility upgrades and operational efficiencies to fitness areas, aquatic areas and sports facilities. Enhancement projects may include: Pool renovations; fitness and program area expansions; new concession areas; weight room renovations; and increased multi-purpose rooms. At this time, no funding is available to implement these projects.
The City has programmed funding in future years for renovations of fire stations #4 and #3. Additional funding may be required beyond 2019.

records.Project: Park at Little Dry Creek Ph. 1
records.Description: This project provides funding for Phase 1 improvements at the Park at Little Dry Creek.

records.Project: Lift Station and Forcemains Major R&R
records.Description: Three of the City's force mains have reached the end of their useful lives and are in need of repair or replacement. Additionally, some lift station communication and electrical equipment will be replaced. The 2016 project will focus on the Federal lift station, Zuni lift station and North Huron force main. Communication equipment will be upgraded at the Standley Lake lift station.

records.Project: BDCWWTF & N. Huron LS Yard Structures
records.Description: This project provides for major repair and replacement of the Big Dry Creek wastewater treatment facility and North Huron lift station yard structures.

The City plans to design a new pump station, new transmission pipelines and a new elevated water storage tank within the water distribution system. The overall intent of the project is to improve portions of the distribution system to meet the level of service experienced elsewhere in the system for adequate water pressure and flow.
This project provides for repair and replacement of the Northridge pump station and water storage tank.

records.Project: Semper WTF Campus and PS Roof
records.Description: The City plans to repair or replace campus and pump station building roofs at the Semper water treatment facility.
The City plans to repair or replacement chemical storage and pumping systems at the Semper water treatment facility.
This project provide for major repair and replacement at the Standley Lake pump station.
The City proposes to complete development improvements at Lone Treet Park. At this time, the project was proposed but not funded in 2015.

The District proposes several projects at Sheridan Community Park: general park improvements ($270,500 in 2017); playground improvements ($225,000 in 2018); irrigation upgrade ($250,000 in 2016); and tennis court replacement ($250,000 in 2016).
This project provides for new retaining walls at Spring Creek.
This project provides for renovations at Willow Springs. It was proposed in 2015 but not funded so the timing is uncertain.
The Town's capital plan includes proposed funding to construct Salisbury Park North. A master plan was budgeted in 2014.
The Town plans a gym conversion project at the Municipal Service Center.
This project provides for construction of a second floor rooftop patio event room at the PACE arts center.

The Loveland Museum/Gallery's history collection contains approximately 35,000 items. Space is inadequate to store the collection. To better protect the City's historical items, Loveland proposes an off-site storage facility that would provide long-term, stable collection stewardship.

records.Project: New Substation to Replace W Substation
records.Description: This project will install a new electric substation - one of two to replace the West substation - north of West 22nd close to the water tank. The new substations will better accommodate growth in the northwest portion of the service territory.

The recreational facilities at Garden Acres Park have far exceeded their life expectancy and are in need of renewal. This project includes implementation of the park renewal plan including renovation and replacement of the primary features of the park.
The City plans to remodel the Council chambers in 2016.
This project provides for City entryway improvements at Dry Creek Road and Mineral and at Santa Fe Drive and County Line Road.

records.Project: LMD Pool and Park Improvements - Ph. 2
records.Description: This project provides for improvements to the Lamont-Does pool and park.
This project provides for a wave pool addition at the Bob L. Burger Recreation Center.
The City plans to build a new slide and tower at the pool at the Bob L. Burger Recreation Center.
This project provides for construction of an enclosure for the wave addition at the Bob L. Burger Recreation Center.
This project provides for the construction of a new treatment train at the water reclamation facility.

This project will construct a new restroom at Island Grove Park, to be built near the old facility, which will be removed. The new facility will have accessiblt stalls, sinks and other devices in both the male and female restrooms, and will include an accessible family restroom.
The City plans to design and construct a new Wilson Road water pump station.
This project provides for improvements at the Eby Creek pump station, located at the Eby Creek water storage tank.
This project will replace the Cemetery water storage tank on Terrace.
The Town's capital plan includes future funding to replace the water storage tank on Brush Creek Road. It is possible the tank will be eliminated.
This project calls for the replacement of the lower water storage tank at Eby Creek.
This project provides for new bathrooms at the Information Center.
The Town anticipates remodeling the old Town Hall building for use as an incubator, resident art center, etc.

records.Project: Day Shelter, Kiosk, Bathrooms - BMX Track
records.Description: This project will construct a day shelter, kiosk and bathrooms at the BMX track, for events and shade.
This project provides for a new 10.0 million gallon water storage tank at the Ridges Basin water treatment plant.
This project provides for future process revisions and expansion of the wastewater treatment plant.
This project entails a second phase of parking garage improvements.
The City's capital plan includes a project to expand the City Hall space. They hope to fund the project in part through grant funding.
This project provides for restroom improvements at Centennial Park.
The City's capital plan includes a project to construct pickleball courts at Centennial Park.
The City's capital plan includes a project to remodel Fire Station #1 at 29 South Weber Street.
This project provides for the renovation of Fire Station #3, located at 922 West Colorado Avenue.
This project will renovate Fire Station #7, located at 3901 N. Palmer Park Boulevard.
This project provides for the remodel of bathrooms at an unspecified number of fire stations.
The City's capital plan includes a project to complete facilities maintenance/upgrades at the historic City Hall building.
Beyond the current five-year planning period, the City anticipates improvements at the historic Senior Center building.
The City is in the early planning stages for a new City Maintenance Facility. At this time, they have not estimated time frame or cost estimate for the project.
This currently unfunded project provides for Ken Mitchell Pump House improvements, as part of the raw water system.
This raw water project will complete pump house improvements at 148th Avenue. The project is currently unfunded.
This project provides for a non-potable system pump house, as part of the City's raw water system. No source of funding has been identified to initiate the project in the current five-year program.
This project provides for a pump house at the 124th Reservoir, as part of the raw water system. The project is not funded in the current five-year program.
This future project provides for access road and spillway improvements at Erger's Pond, part of the City's raw water system. The project is not currently funded.
This project provides for engineering and consruction of reverse osmosis plant scaffolding.
This project provides for a future new water treatment plant. The project is not funded in the current five-year program.

This project is being considered by Town Council. A report has been completed with cost estimates. However, Council has now decided to consider parking in a larger context. Consequently, this project will be considered when the Council develops a plan to address parking in general.
The Flatirons Golf Course is the City's only course. The course is in need of repairs to the many cart paths. The restrooms also need repairs and renovations to ensure safety and functionality.

This project would construct a 9,700 sf expansion for Police functions, and a 6,400 sf addition for IT offices, with additional parking for 30 to 50 spaces in the parking garage. It would also complete associated renovations to the existing facility. At this point, no source of funding has been identified to initiate the project.

This project would relocate the Park Operations and Forestry service area into the Municipal Service Center (city yards). Additional structures, renovations of existing structures and additional parking would be included. At this time, the project is not funded.

This project would complete improvements at the downtown transit center, to include bus operational improvements, pedestrian improvements, building retrofits, improved bicycle access and accommodations. It would expand the range of multimodal transportation opportunities, including electric vehicle charging, car share vehicles, a bike station and a transportation resource center. Increments of funding have been received from CDOT. However, at this time, sufficient funding is not available to complete the project.

records.Project: Demolition and Redevelopment of W. Sr. Center
records.Description: This project is part of the Civic Area plan implementation. It will demolish the existing West Senior Center building, expand the footprint and build up three stories. At this point, no source of funding has been identified to complete the project.

records.Project: Civic Area Project - City Svcs. Facilities
records.Description: Based on the implementation strategy for the Civic Area Plan, a number of facilities could be replaced in the future: New Britain, Park Central, Atrium, 1301 Arapahoe, FAM and the Municipal Building. Projects could also include parking structures to replace surface parking currently in the High Hazard Zone. At this time, no source of funding has been identified to complete these projects.

This project provides for construction, furniture, fixtures and equipment for a 13,000 sf library branch, including an opening day collection, in the North Boulder neighborhood. A donated piece of land has been identified for the proposed project. No funding is currently available to build the new library.
The County's capital plan includes proposed funding for tenant improvements in the Probation area of Lima Plaza.
The City proposed to design and construct a maintenance building and concession stand building at the Louisville Sports Complex.

records.Project: Hist. Museum Study Center and Archive
records.Description: This project would construct a new building on the Historical Museum campus between the Jacoe Store and Tomeo House to provide archival and artifact storage, display and research space, an ADA-compliant restroom, and office space. The project is anticipated beyond the current five-year planning period.

records.Project: Sid Copeland WTP Pump Station Imp's
records.Description: This project provides for relocation or rehabilitation of the high zone pump station at the Sid Copeland Water Treatment Plant site.
The County plans to design and construct a 10,000 square foot addition to the Human Services facility. The capital plan indicates $2.5 million for construction and an unspecified amount for design.

records.Project: Parker Yard R & B Imp's Phase III
records.Description: The County's capital plan includes a project to complete phase III improvements at the Park Yard Road and Bridge facility, to include a crew building and sweeper storage.

records.Project: Parker Yard R&B Imp's Phase IV
records.Description: This project provides for phase IV improvements at the Parker Yard Road and Bridge facility, to include material bunkers and shop renovation.
The County's capital plan includes proposed funding for site development, design and phase I and II construction of the Moore Road Facility.

records.Project: Castle Rock Road and Bridge Facility
records.Description: This project provides for land purchase, site improvements, design and phase I and II construction of a Castle Rock Road and Bridge facility.
In the next couple of months, Aurora expects to advertise an RFP for design and engineering services for the Moorhead Recreation Center renovation project.

We reported previously that the Airport planned to seek architectural services. At this point, Brian says the RFQ remains on hold. At this point, there are some "things up in the air" related to this contract, so it is uncertain when it will be initiated. They intend to hire a firm for on-call services under a five-year contract. We will follow up.

As we reported previously, Erie may advertise for a new airport consulting contract. The previous 5-year contract extended through 2013. Kris is still not sure when this RFQ/P process will be initiated. Rather than calling her for the status, Kris requests that consultants go to the Town's website at www.erieco.gov and click on the orange "Notify Me" button to sign up for notifications of RFQ/Ps when posted.
records.Type: AS, DR, MS, PL, ST, TR

records.Description: Previously, Jennifer reported that the County might issue an RFP for design of new courthouse offices in Loveland. She also said it was possible they would select a firm from a few they identified through a previous RFP process. Jennifer now says they are using one of the firms they had already been working with.

As we reported previously, the City expected to seek landscape architecture services for construction drawings for the first phase of the Carmody Park remodel project. The project was contingent on receipt of grant funding, which they did not receive. Ross now says they are "regrouping," and still could issue an RFP sometime this next spring for design/construction documents for the park remodel.
Renee reported previously that the College's next big project would be a campus recreation center in Lakewood. She now says an RFP for design should be out very soon.

records.Project: Boyd Lake and Bellvue WTP Imp's
records.Description: As we reported previously, Greeley plans to issue an RFP for evaluation and design of improvements to the filters at Boyd Lake and Bellvue water treatment plants, plus winterization of the Boyd Lake plant. Bob now says he hopes to issue the RFP in the next few weeks.
DIA's latest schedule calls for a December 9 RFQ/P for on-call condition assessment services, for investigation of the condition of a potential wide range of facility items.
In the next couple of months or so, Woodland Park expects to advertise an RFP for design of a major expansion of the wastewater treatment plant.
Sometime in the earlier part of 2015, Westminster expects to advertise an RFQ for open-ended engineering services, to be provided in various disciplines.
records.Type: AS, DR, MS, PK, PL, ST, TR

records.Description: The City's capital plan includes funding for Phase II of the Fire Department complex improvements. Previously, Curt indicated that they expected to advertise an RFP for design. He now says the project has been removed from the program, at least for the time being.

As we reported previously, this project provides for a new ADA compliant bathhouse at the swimming pool in City Park. Steve now says he hopes to issue an RFP around November 1 for architectural/engineering services.

As we reported previously, Dave anticipates issuing an RFP for engineering services for a solids processing improvements project. A couple of months ago, he predicted an RFP would be released during the first quarter of 2015. He now says it could go out in October or November of this year.

As we reported previously, Denver Health currently has a number of "pool" architectural and engineering contracts that have been in place for the past two or three years. A couple of months ago, Tom reported that they were reviewing the existing contracts to determine whether or not to conduct a new selection process. At this point, he says they have decided to extend the current contracts for another two years.

We reported previously that the City planned to issue an RFP for design of clarifier rehabilitation at the Thornton Water Treatment Plant. Dennis now says the project has become a maintenance project and will not involve a consultant selection.

records.Project: On-Call WW Design and Const. Services
records.Description: An RFP should be out now or very soon for on-call wastewater design and construction services. Owen reports that the work will involve all water reclamation facilities, treatment plants and land application facilities. Services will be provided as needed for five years.

The Adams County School District #14 will run a $95.7 million capital projects bond on the November, 2014 ballot. One of the major projects to be completed if the bond passes is a new middle school for approximately 1200 students. Sandy says she is not sure, but they will most likely wait until after the vote to begin consultant selections.
Later this year or in 2015, Lakewood expects to seek consultant services related to renovation of the Link Pool.

The District plans to advertise very soon for either construction manager/general contractor services or a construction bid for its proposed new Elementary #12. Ranette says they are leaning toward using the CM/GC delivery method.
In the next few months, Thornton plans to advertise for on-call architectural design services.

The School of Mines' proposed project to replace Meyer Hall was funded in the State's Long Bill. Meyer Hall contains science classrooms, computer labs, etc. Mike now says he expects they will advertise within a month for architectural/engineering services. (The funding shown here is the amount approved in the Long Bill. It may or may not be the total cost of the project.)

Avon failed to pass a ballot measure in November of 2013 for a recreation center expansion. They plan to place a new issue on the ballot this November. If it passes, they will require design services for the expansion. We will follow up.
As we reported previously, Metro expects to issue an RFP for design of improvements to the Personnel and Support facilities. Dave says he the RFP should be out next week.

We reported previously the the Police Department expected to seek consultant services for redesign of the basement area, which is currently a drive-through bay. They plan to remodel approximately 3000 square feet of the basement to serve as office space for the Patrol Division. Tim now says they are obtaining a basic design proposal from a vendor, to be used in the RFP for contractor services.

As we reported previously, the Department of Military and Veterans Affairs received funding approval and plans to seek consultant/design services for structural repairs, code and component upgrades at the Aurora Readiness Center. Kris now says an RFQ should be advertised as soon as this week on the new Colorado VSS system (www.colorado.gov/vss) .

As we reported previously, the Department of Military and Veterans Affairs has received funding for various upgrades at the Rocky Ford field maintenance shop facility. The improvements will include window replacement and other items yet to be specified. Kris now says they completed a selection through interviews without issuing an RFQ.

As we reported previously, the Department of Military and Veterans Affairs received budget approval for the 2014/15 fiscal year for a project to expand one bay at the Denver FMS facility. Kris now says an architectural/engineering was selected through interviews without an RFQ process.

We reported previously that the Department hoped to complete a statewide facility assessment. Kris now says they will select a firm through interviews without issuing an RFQ. Interested firms may submit informal qualifications to Kris citing related experience. You may call her at the number listed here for additional information.

As we reported previously, the Department of Public Safety expects to seek design services for a modular building and dorm type facility at Camp George West for the Port of Entry Academy. Services will include site selection within the campus (to determine the best location in terms of utility access, etc.), site engineering, and design to place the modular building. The project will probably not be advertised. Interested firms may call Bob for further information and to request an RFP.

As we reported previously, the Department received funding for renovation and expansion of the Sterling field maintenance shop. Kris now says they selected a firm through interviews, without an RFQ process.
History Colorado expects to require architectural/engineering services in the next few months for improvements at the Pearce McAllister Cottage in Denver.
Within the next six months or so, the School of Mines might require architectural/engineering services in connection with a generic/low cost building to be used for a machine shop and other uses.
In the next month or so, Colorado State University plans to issue an RFP for design-build services for the Center for Agricultural Education building.

records.Project: Old Tivoli Theater at Auraria Campus
records.Description: Kathy reports that the University plans to advertise an RFQ very soon for design of an area inside the old Tivoli Theater on the Auraria campus. They plan to advertise on the new state procurement site, www.colorado.gov/vss .
An RFP should be issued now or very soon for design/build services for an expansion of the Western Slope Veterans Cemetery in Grand Junction.

As we reported previously, the Town's capital plan anticipates design and construction of a new Public Works and Parks maintenance shop and office facility. Previously, Alex indicated that they could hire a consultant later this year to assist with planning. More recently, he mentioned they were looking for some help with the planning. We included that information in our May 26 Special Update. Alex may still be interested in having firms contact him.
records.Type: AS, DR, MS, PK, PL, ST

records.Project: New Dining Center for Williams Village
records.Description: We reported on this project previously. The University is has been working on the programming phase for a new dining center at the Williams Village dormitory complex. Tom now says it will go for approval from the Regents in June, and should be advertised in July for design/build services.

Previously, Eric reported that Rio Blanco County expected to issue an RFP for design to remodel the Department of Human Services facility. He now says they will apply for a DOLA grant to fund the project. As we reported previously, they will not know until August whether or not they will receive the grant. If they are successful, they will then develop a scope of work and issue an RFP for design.

As we reported previously, the County expects to advertise for consultant/planning services for a terminal area plan for the airport. Chris indicates that the RFQ is undergoing legal review and should be issued during the first part of this month.

We reported on this project previously. At this point, the project is not funded. Kris says it is possible funding will become available in about September. If so, they will advertise for consulting/design services for this controlled maintenance project, which provides for HVAC replacement, plus a roof and paving at the Watkins Readiness Center.

As we reported previously, Greeley's Culture, Parks and Recreation Department plans to issue an RFP for design/build services for two park restrooms. Andy now says the RFP should go out in about July.

As we reported previously, Aurora plans to advertise for a design team to help design a sports complex expansion. The project will include primarily the addition of fields and associated infrastructure. They expect to use the design-build or CM/GC delivery method. Tracy now anticipates advertising for design and construction sometime this summer.
We reported previously that an RFQ/P would be going out for master planning for the Sun Valley development. Chris now says the project should be advertised any day.
Chris reports that the Authority plans to seek architectural and general contractor services for Phases VII and VIII of the Mariposa development. He does not yet have a specific RFP release date.
It is possible the University will advertise sometime this summer for design services for the 5th Wing addition to the J.S. Caruthers biotechnology building.

Mike reports that the District has "moved up" on the list and is approved for BEST grant funding for a new $35 million middle school. They expect to receive final official approval in July, after which they will issue an RFP for architectural/engineering services.

The Town's capital improvements program includes a project to design and construct residuals handling system improvements at the Plum Creek Water Purification Facility. The Town is currently doing some engineering evaluations. They hope to kick off design in 2015.
This fall, probably in October or November, the City plans to advertise for one or more new on-call architectural services contracts.

records.Project: Garden Acres Park Preliminary Master Plan
records.Description: The recreational facilities at this park have far exceeded their life expectancy and are in need of renewal. This project will require a master plan and/or revitalization plan for the park, plus replacement and renovation of the primary features of the park. $202,000 is budgeted this year for planning and design. Additional expenditures are programmed in 2016 and 2017, for a total cost of $2,852,000. In the next month, the City expects to advertise an RFP for design, to include landscape architecture, architecture, irrigation, surveying, mechanical, lighting/electrical and structural engineering.
records.Type: AS, MS, PK, PL, SV, WR

records.Description: As we reported previously, Thornton plans to advertise for design of Signal Ditch Park and open space, a new community park. Diane now says the RFP has been sent to Contracts, so should be advertised soon.
Late last year, Eric reported that the County planned to advertise an RFQ for on-call architectural/engineering services. He now says they decided not to advertise for these services.

DIA now plans a May RFP for a firm or firms to provide engineering studies, design, bidding, construction services, testing and reporting, scheduling and cost estimating, or other airfield engineering services according to the need. It is possible work will also be required on other parts of the airport.
records.Type: AS, CM, DR, GT, MS, ST

records.Description: Previously, Paula reported that Longmont expected to advertise for design to replace a wading pool with a splash pad at Kanemoto Park. The existing wading pool was destroyed in the September flood. Paula now says the project has been through various decision points, delays, etc. One of the decisions is that they now plan a replacement pool instead of a splash pad. She expects to advertise and RFP soon.

Previously, Don Roche reported that Aurora planned to advertise for consulting services for oversight/inspection services at a medical waste facility, the first of its type in the state. Karen now informs us that, when they thought they were going to seek consulting services, they believed they could use revenues from the facility to fund they oversight. They subsequently found out that the rules do not allow the use of revenues for oversight. For now, they will try staff-led oversight. If that does not work out, they will need to seek funding in the 2015 budget to hire a consultant.
In the next 30 days, Nederland expects to issue an RFP for a housing needs assessment.
If funding is approved by the Legislature in the Long Bill, the Auraria Higher Education Center expects to advertise for architectural/engineering services for a new Metro State University building.

If funding is approved by the Legislature in the Long Bill, the Auraria Higher Education Center (AHEC) plans to seek architectural/engineering services for design of a remodel of the AHEC Facilities Management building.
As part of the bond program package approved by voters in November, 2013, Commerce City plans to complete a couple of neighborhood park projects.
The City purchased the former "Church of the City" at 1530 Josephine Street, as a site for a new central recreation center. The current schedule calls for a design RFP in two to six months.

The City plans to perform a feasibility study ($50,000) and acquire land ($500,000) for a recreation center in the northwest section of the city. It is possible they will advertise later this year for consultant services for the feasibility study.

This project was previously known as the Center for Academic Success. The name has now been changed (reflecting the fact that it is to be built atop an existing parking structure). As we reported previously, the University is in the programming phase for this new student services building. It will be a new building constructed on top of an existing parking structure. Phil now says they will go before the Regents February 21 for approval. If they get the go-ahead, they could advertise for design as soon as February 24.

As we reported previously, DIA anticipates issuing an RFQ for up to four contracts ($2 million each) for on-call professional A/E services related to a variety of potential projects. The latest schedule indicates the RFQ will be issued in February.
records.Type: AS, DR, MS, PL, ST, TR

records.Description: We reported previously that CDOT planned to advertise for consulting services for tunnel inspections. Lynn now anticipates the RFQ will be issued this month.

records.Project: Parker, Lone Tree & Castle Pines Libraries
records.Description: The District recently hired an Owner's Representative for new branch libraries in Parker, Lone Tree and Castle Pines. As we reported previously, they expect to advertise this month for architectural services.

The County has budgeted $500,000 this year for initial work to convert existing library space into offices for the District Attorney. The project will involve remodeling and expansion. An RFP should be issued soon.

records.Project: New Leisure Pool at Pioneer Park
records.Description: Commerce City voters passed a ballot issue in November, for several capital improvements. One of the projects will be a new leisure pool at Pioneer Park. An RFQ/P for design will be issued, but no specific schedule is yet available. Further information is posted on the City's website at www.c3gov.com/issue2k . You can click on Procurement Process, and then Vendor Opt In. You will then receive updates as they become available. Carolyn may have a schedule sometime this month.

As we reported previously, Grand Junction expects to issue an RFP this quarter for design to retrofit one of the secondary clarifiers at the Persigo wastewater treatment plant. An alternate contact is Bret Guillory, bretg@ci.grantjct.co.us .
Sometime this year, the Pitkin County Airport plans to seek consultant services for fixed base operator redevelopment work.
In February or March, Loveland expects to seek consultant services for design to expand the wastewater treatment plant.

In March, Northglenn plans to seek consultant services for design of a new headworks and 3rd secondary clarifier at the wastewater treatment plant. The existing clarifiers are the limiting factor in the overall capacity at the plant. Once the headworks is in operation, the decommissioning of the existing lagoons can commence. The 3rd secondary clarifier will provide redundancy in the system and increase the overall capacity to meet the planned future flows.
In the next couple of months, the Division of Wildlife expects to advertise or consultant services for a Sylvan Lake spillway alternatives study.

The County's capital plan includes $165,000 in 2014 for master planning and related environmental assessment for a new multi-event center. Janalee reports that the project is contingent on a land deal with the BLM. They hired a consultant in 2012 for a NEPA analysis. At this point, they have no specific plans or schedule for moving forward. We will follow up.

Sean reports that the College would require architectural/engineering services for a grant funded interior space remodel project. However, at this time, the project is on hold and is contingent on further funding. We will follow up.
Around the third quarter of this year, Longmont expects to seek consultant services for design of restroom improvements at Spangler Park.
In the next two to six months, Denver expects to advertise an RFP for a project management team for a new recreation center in central Denver.

records.Project: Parker, Lone Tree, Castle Pines Lib. CM/GC
records.Description: As we reported in our project ID #77730, the Douglas Public Library District plans to advertise in February for architectural/engineering services for three libraries. By late spring, they expect to issue an RFP for construction manager/general contractor services for these facilities.
Later this year, Northglenn may issue one or more RFPs for shopping center analyses and/or master development projects. We will provide more specifics when available.
records.Type: AS, DR, MS, PK, PL, ST

records.Description: The Littleton School District is in the process of launching an $80 million capital improvements program. They are currently reviewing architectural/engineering qualifications. "Fairly soon" they will issue an RFQ for contractors. David says some of their projects will be hard bid but most will use the construction manager/general contractor delivery method.

An RFP should be out now or very soon for design/build services for a Grounds Intermediate Processing facility. The project involves removal of an existing industrial building and replacement with a new building in a different location.

Denver's 2014 program includes a project to design and construct a new outdoor concert venue in Ruby Hill Park, to seat up to 7,500 people. The venue will consist of natural grass seating with a building that will contain offices, restrooms, dressing rooms and a performance stage. A late March design RFP is anticipated.

This project provides for the development of a new City office building for the Public Works, Planning and Stormwater departments and other city offices that will ultimately replace some of the offices at City Hall. The existing public works, storm water and community development offices are slated for police department use. The City plans to construct the building in two phases: Phase 1 to be 27,100 sf and Phase 2 18,120 sf.

The Maintenance Operations Center (MOC) will require significant remodeling after the streets, solid waste, and stormwater divisions move out to a new service center. The MOC will be remodeled to better accommodate the Traffic and Facilities Management divisions. It is possible the Facilities Management Division will design the improvements internally. One major change that is not included in the cost estimate shown here is the creation of a full-scale traffic operations center.

This project provides for restroom and concession improvements at Stazio Park. Specifically, it will upgrade electrical and HVAC systems to current building codes, upgrade plumbing systems and fixtures and renew interior and exterior surface finishes.
This project will provide funds for the design and rehabilitation of the Kohler Storage Tank's roofing system and siding to seal the tank from the outside environment.

The Nottingham Park master plan includes a proposed stage to be located near the upper athletic field. The stage will be used for existing events in the park and will be programmed for additional events that enhance the community. The stage will be at least 30 feet wide and 25 feet deep and will include a roof, the associated electrical and back-of-house facilities to operate the stage.

The County's five-year capital plan anticipates a phase III expansion of the correctional facility. The project will add 113,575 square feet for 350 additional beds. This expansion was projected to be needed in the Weld County Jail Occupancy and Future Jail Needs Study completed in August of 2013.
This project will remodel and complete an addition at Fire Station #2.
The Town has programmed funding in 2017 for municipal swimming pool expansion.

The project includes funding for the interior space planning analysis, design and construction of improvements at the North Boulder Recreation Center in response to community demand for improved circulation, weight room expansion and a possible lobby concession area.
The City plans to construct a storage facility with a minimum capacity of 1600 tons of sand (85%) and salt (15%) mixture.

This project includes the addition of a vault-style concession, restroom and storage facility at Northwest Open Space (NWOS), and a children's playground and covered pavilion area. The complex has no permanent structures. The area also has no electricity or water on site. Currently all of the structures are temporary and are in need of improvement. The City plans to apply for a $200,000 grant in 2014 to cover approximately half of the project cost.

Construction of a new police training facility will include a firing range, driving track and classrooms. At final build-out, the facility will incorporate approximately 60,000 square feet. The project is expected to be built in three phases with the firing range to be followed by the driving track and then the classroom space.
records.Type: AS, DR, MS, PK, PL, ST

records.Description: This project provides for a new storage facility for the Electric Department.

The City needs a new fire station on the west side of the service area to improve response times to meet the five minute standard. It is anticipated that this station would be as far west as Glade Road. The City anticipates a 9,000 sf station.

The City has allocated funding each year beginning for new neighborhood park acquisition and development in areas identified in the Master Plan that are currently not served with a park. Funding is programmed at $400,000 in 2015, $600,000 in 2016 and $600,000 in 2018.

The City plans to repair the roof, replace the HVAC systems and replace windows at the Flatirons Event Center. The roof leaks and has been patched many times. No upgrades or energy efficiencies have been accomplished in the facility.

The County has programmed funding of $300,000 per year from 2014 through 2018 to replace three grader sheds. The current schedule calls for replacement of the Kiowa shed in 2015, Johnstown in 2016 and Nunn in 2017.
The County's capital plan anticipates the addition of two courtrooms on the third floor of the Centennial Center building, a part of the justice center complex.
Weld County's capital plan includes a future project to add a new courtroom on the first floor of the Centennial Center building, part of the Justice Center complex.
This project provide for a new roof on the jail building, located at 2110 "O" Street in Greeley.

The Town has included $5.5 million in 2016 as a placeholder for a significant remodel of the municipal building in the event a complete reconstruction does not occur. The cost is an estimate only. Actual costs will depend on the scope of the project.
This project would add two to four shelters throughout the park, develop a walking and exercise path around the perimeter, and repair historic stone walls.
The Town's capital plan anticipates that the Town Hall roof will need replacement in 2022.

Loveland has programmed funding each year for various golf course projects, not yet specified. They may include replacement of equipment, golf course improvements, Mariana Butte Dry Creek, parking lots, bunker, tees and putting green improvements, plus Olde Course maintenance building and clubhouse. Some of these projects may require consultant design services.

The cemetery shop (1,893 sf) was constructed in 1968 and serves as an office area/public meeting place for sales and burial arrangements, and as a maintenance shop. The structure is in need of significant upgrades/repairs to meet ADA requirements ant to meet public office/maintenance shop needs. This project would demolish and replace the building with a new 2,200 sf building near the cul-de-sac west of the existing shop.
The County plans to construct a covered equipment and storage shed at the District I Road and Bridge shop in Marvel.
The County has programmed funding in 2015-2016 for a community corrections building.
This project will reconfigure the existing Columbine library building.
The City anticipates grant funding to build a new public works facility.
This project provides for a new electric substation.
This project provides for renovations to the sewer administration lab.
This project provides for the construction of flush toilet restrooms at the Northern Lights Ballfields. Design is scheduled in 2015 and construction in 2016.
This project provides for future upgrades to public restrooms.
