This project will construct new restroom facilities at the RTD parking lot.
This project provides for a master plan for a potential indoor soccer/basketball facility at the Soccer Complex.

records.Project: Ken Mitchell Cell #3 - Ready Mix 1 Storage
records.Description: This project provides for a Ready Mix storage facility at Ken Mitchell Lakes cell #3.

This project would relocate the fire administration offices out of the public safety building, where they currently occupy 3,737 square feet. A space analysis indicated a space need of at least 10,000 square feet. The project would provide a facility to efficiently store reserve fire apparatus and a stockpile of emergency supplies. The new facility would be located adjacent to Fire Station #7. The project is currently unfunded.

This project would acquire an available facility to be renovated for a citywide indoor sports facility. It would serve as a venue for soccer, tennis, batting cages and golf. The project is included in the City's "Tier 1" priorities in the 2013-18 capital plan, but is not funded at this time.

This District was approved last year for a BEST grant for a new middle school. They were then put on the "backup" list. It is unclear exactly when the funds may become available. At some point, possible this year or later, they expect to seek consultant services for design of a new middle school.

Dave reported previously that the Metro District expected to seek engineering services for the South Headworks improvement project. He now says an RFP is likely in December for South Complex headworks and grease processing improvements.

We reported previously that the University was in the programming phase of a new Football Operations Center. The project will be completed in two phases. At this point, Phil says they expect to go before the Regents in December for approval to proceed, but the timing of a design ad will depend on how the fundraising effort goes. They could initiate the project in January, or it could be postponed for another year. We will follow up.

In October, Mike reported that the County was "thinking about" seeking consultant services for a Facilities Master Plan. At this point, he says it is on hold. If they decide to move forward with it, it will be advertised through the Rocky Mountain e-Purchasing system.
In October, Anne reported that Steamboat Springs planned to advertise an RFQ for airport engineering services. Now she says they decided to renew the contracts with the current airport engineers.

An RFQ should be out now or very soon for engineering services for the Willow Creek Dam project. The dam is located north of Steamboat Springs. They expect to require primarily structural engineering, based on some reports that were completed several years ago.

Tom reports that the City is working on a number of project RFPs to be released in December and January. Some of the projects will include RTD station/station area betterments. He did not provide any further details.
records.Type: AS, DR, MS, PK, PL, ST, TR

records.Description: In the next month or two, Aurora plans to issue an RFP for design of a parking structure at the Iliff RTD station. RTD had planned to construct a surface parking lot, but has agreed to apply its funding to Aurora's parking structure.
Within the next couple of months or so, Aurora expects to issue an RFP for design of a joint training facility.

records.Project: Module Furniture for Remodel - Des. Planning
records.Description: The County expects to advertise in January for interior design planning services for module furniture for a remodel.

The University's projects "under consideration" include design and construction of a 50,000 square-foot, four story, 214-bed residence hall. The project is pending approval from the Board of Trustees or funding from the State.

The University has proposed a project to complete a nurse practitioner center, remodel of the existing pharmacy and construction of a 16,900 sf addition. The project may or may not be initiated in 2014. It is contingent on Board of Trustees approval and/or state funding.

After completing a community survey, the District plans to begin a feasibility study for a new Buchanan Park recreation center. It is possible they will do this in house, or they may seek consultant services.
Geraldine reports that the University will issue an RFP in a month or two for design of the remodel of the Occhiato University Center.

Previously, we reported that the City might seek engineering consultant services in connection with the Grand Staircase rebuild project. Sarah now informs us that they plan to handle this project through a sole source, so will not put out an RFP.
We reported previously that Erie anticipated issuing an RFP for an Erie Lake dam study. Kris now says that, due to recent flooding, this project probably will not move forward at this time.
As we reported previously, the School of Mines expects to advertise for architectural/engineering services for renovation of the Student Center. Mike says the RFQ should be out in the next month.

Once again, just as a reminder, Denver Public Schools advertises every October to update its list of prequalified architectural and engineering consulting firms. The District uses this short list of firms to select for virtually all capital projects. They use various delivery methods for their projects.

Lance reported previously that the State planned to seek consultant services for design of a restroom renovation project at the Capitol building. He now says the project was small enough that they were not required to go through a formal selection process.

Sandy informs us that the School Board approved a resolution to include ballot language in the November election for a new combined middle school. If the voters approve the measure, the District expects to advertise an RFP for design or design-build services for the new school.

Within the next month or so, Greeley plans to advertise for consultant services for a new bus transit/transfer center. Improvements will include a small building, site improvements, a parking lot and places for buses to pull in to pick up and drop off passengers. The project will also include some transit route planning, as the center will be in a new location and will require some rerouting.
records.Type: AS, DR, MS, PK, ST, TR

records.Description: Karen reports that the Poudre Landmarks Foundation is submitting a grant request to the State Historical Fund for construction drawings and interpretive signage for the historic Water Works site in Fort Collins. If the grant is successful (they will know in April of 2014), the City will issue an RFP for the work. We will follow up once they know the outcome of the grant application.

The University plans a new Visual and Performing Arts Center. Recently, they advertised for a design architect. Separately, they expect to advertise in the near future for a local architect of record, or an "Executive Architect." This first phase of the center includes a black box theater with supporting spaces, an intimate 250 seat recital hall, a 750 to 800 seat performance space/theatre, and the Gallery of Contemporary Art. This phase will also include some additional learning/rehearsal space, a public reception functional lobby and ?back-of-the-house? support spaces. Phase 1 will comprise approximately 85,000 square feet.
records.Agency: Univ. of Colo. at Colo. Spgs.

records.Description: Previously, Larry reported that the City expected to advertise for on-call design-build services for water and wastewater treatment plant projects. The RFP remains on hold for the time being. We will provide an update if and when it is reactivated.

As we reported previously, Erie plans to seek consultant services for the South Water Reclamation Facility Modifications project. The project was postponed from 2012. The consultant will evaluate what improvements would be required to the existing wastewater facility should the Town need to reactivate it. Kris now says an RFP should be issued this quarter.

The Aspen Community School, a charter school within the Aspen School District, was awarded a BEST grant earlier this year for a new campus. They successfully raised matching funding for the BEST grant. Recently, they selected a firm as the Owner's Representative for the project. In August, they plan to issue an RFP for architectural/engineering services.

We reported previously that the Department of Military and Veterans Affairs expected to advertise for architectural/engineering services for a new Readiness Center in Fort Carson. They anticipate a facility of about 57,000 square feet. The latest information is that they hope to advertise by the end of August. The solicitation will be announced on the fedbizopps.gov website.

Previously, Steve reported that Westminster planned to seek consultant services for design of a new parking garage at Westminster Station. More recently, he said they were trying to figure out how to package the project. They have decided to seek a developer to design and build the garage and to develop several properties around it. The project may be completed in phases. The bottom line is that the City needs 350 parking spaces in place by the time the light rail line opens in 2016. Steve says an RFP should be out now or very soon.

As we reported previously, the legislature provided funding for the 2013/14 fiscal year to replace the roofs on two barns, to repair structural components of the hay barn, and to repair the outdoor equine arena. Sean now says a design RFQ/P should be out in mid to late August.

As we reported previously, it is possible that Louisville will seek consultant services this year for design of park renovation projects. They have identified needs at three parks - Cottonwood, Pirates and Keith Helart - that they hope to address during the coming five years. Proposed impovements include landscaping upgrades; signage; restroom improvements; the potential addition of new amenities such as bocce, horseshoes, volleyball, etc.; and irrigation upgrades. Allan indicates that the project is currently delayed as they are reviewing ADA issues within the parks and open space system. We will follow up.
Previously, we reported that the County might advertise for architectural services this year for the renovation of the fleet shop. Vickey now says an RFP should be issued in about a month.

In the next month or so, Douglas County expects to issue an RFP for architectural services for the Road and Bridge facility. The facility currently exists but they expect to do an essentially complete reconstruction.
During the fourth quarter of this year, Erie expects to issue an RFP for design of a new water storage tank.
Next spring or summer, Colorado Northwestern Community College expects to seek consultant services for its Yeager roof replacement project.

We reported previously that Adams State College hoped to move forward with a design/build RFP for a life safety upgrade to the auditorium at Richardson Hall. The project was delayed. Erik now reports that they expect to issue an RFP very soon for design/build services for a life safety upgrade to the auditorium. The project will include a ventilation relief system above the stage, fire detection and suppression system, HVAC improvements and ADA upgrades. The project may be combined with a larger Richardon Hall Renovation project (see our ID #77237).

As we reported previously, RTD plans to advertise for design/build services for the North Metro commuter rail segment of the FasTracks system. The project extends from Union Station to about 72nd Avenue. Henry now says the RFP should be out sometime in June.

We reported on this project previously. DIA planned to advertise an RFP in December for on-call civil engineering services, including roadway, structural, hydraulics, environmental and transportation services/engineering. An RFQ should be issued sometime in June.
records.Type: AS, DR, EV, MS, ST, TR

records.Description: As we reported previously, the University is working on the programming for a future renovation of the Glenn Miller ballroom. Phil still estimates they will advertise for architectural/engineering services around July.

Previously, Tom reported that the City expected to advertise for site development and 30% design for a joint Police and Fire training facility. The status remains the same as reported in April. The project remains on hold as they work the programming through Council. We will continue to monitor progress.
As we reported previously, the Bridge Inspections office of CDOT expects to advertise for retaining and sound wall inspection services. Lynn now says the RFP will go out sometime this month.

In the next month or so, Estes Park plans to issue an RFP for a facilities assessment of all town buildings. As an outcome of the assessment, they plan to develop a new five-year capital improvement plan.
Dennis anticipates an RFP sometime in June for consultant services to design improvements at the Big Dry Creek sewer lift station.

The legislature approved funding in the 2013/14 fiscal year budget for roof repairs or replacements of three roofs at the Colorado State Patrol Academy at Camp George West. It also repairs a modular classroom unit attached to the main Academy building. The roofs are over 20 years old and are leaking.
Within the next few weeks, Colorado State University Pueblo plans to issue an RFQ for design of a new 45,000 sf general classroom building.

The legislature approved funding for replacement of the roof on the art and music building at Colorado State University Pueblo. Within the next few months or so, they expect to advertise for design services.

The legislature approved funding for FY2013/14 for renovation of 71,340 gsf of Richardson Hall, plus a two-story addition to provide a new ADA-accessible front door on the southwest corner of the existing building. An RFP should be issued soon. The project may be combined with the separately funded project (see our ID #66829) for auditorium renovation and upgrades.
In the next month or so, CSU plans to advertise for architectural/engineering services for a small classroom addition at the Health and Exercise Science building.

We reported previously that the Aspen Community School, a charter school within the Aspen School District, had been awarded a BEST grant, but needed to raise matching funds. Skye reports that they were successful in raising the funding they needed. They expect to advertise sometime in June for project management services.
The Authority plans to advertise beginning the week of June 10 for general contractor services for the Village at Westerly Creek, Building 2 project.

Previously, we reported that Durango expected to seek consultant services for amendments to its Historic Preservation Design Guidelines. The RFP was delayed from 2012. Greg now reports that the project will not occur this year. We will provide additional information if and when it becomes available.

As we reported previously, Thornton anticipates advertising an RFP for a transit oriented development study/plan for the 104th Avenue TOD area. Dennis now predicts an RFP will be issued sometime this month.
records.Type: AS, MS, PK, PL, ST, TR

records.Description: Previously, we reported that Estes Park planned an RFP for design of a 300-stall parking garage. The project will involve federal funding. A design RFP is still planned sometime this quarter.

records.Project: Orchard Mesa Irrig. Dist. Tail Race Redesign
records.Description: This week, Mesa County plans to issue an RFQ for the Orchard Mesa Irrigation District tail race redesign, which will be a hydraulic and structural project.

Jim reports that it is possible Minturn will enter into a public-private partnership arrangement with a firm to develop a new fitness center. If the project moves forward, it will be handled by the private entity. He did not identify the company. We will follow up.

An RFQ should be out now or very soon for construction manager/general contractor services for the expansion and remodel of the Tomlinson Library building at Colorado Mesa University (formerly Mesa State College).

Dennis reports that the City is currently in the process of executing an intergovernmental agreement with RTD related to a transit oriented development project at 88th Avenue and Welby Road. He expects to issue an RFP sometime this month for a study/planning work.
records.Type: AS, MS, PK, PL, ST, TR

records.Description: If the project is funded by the legislature, the Historical Society expects to seek consultant services closer to the beginning of the new fiscal year (July 1) for design of improvements at the Ute Indian Museum.
DIA anticipates advertising this month for on-call design/build services for security projects at the airport.

Previously, Curt reported that Colorado Springs planned to release an RFQ for a major multi-discipline engineering services contract. He now says he doesn't know what happened with the project. They have a new Public Works Director, and she may be holding it back until she figures out how she wants to proceed (speculation on Curt's part). We will follow up.
records.Type: AS, BR, DR, GT, MS, PK, ST, SV, TS, TR

records.Description: In December, Elaine reported that the Denver Museum of Nature and Science might seek consultant services sometime in 2013 for structural remediation in the parking garage. She now says they decided to have the engineering completed under another project.

In December, Elaine reported that the Denver Museum of Nature and Science might seek consultant services for the replacement of "vertical transportation equipment" at the museum. At this point, she says they do not have funding for the project so it will not move forward in the near future.

As we reported previously, Fort Collins expects to issue an RFP for design of improvements on a 50-acre park site. Improvements will include a ballfield, dog park, parking lot, picnic shelters, restrooms, a playground and, potentially, a water splash park. They will require civil engineering, landscape architecture, structural engineering, soils, hydraulics, etc. Craig now indicates that the RFP should be issued in March.
In the fall of this year, the County expects to advertise for continuing services architectural/engineering contracts for projects with fees under $100,000 per consultant.

Jay reports that he hopes to issue an RFP within the next few weeks for a consultant to conduct an in-depth review of the City's Public Works operations and facilities. The study will include updating the program needs and looking at options for redevelopment on the current site and looking at alternative sites for possible relocation of the operations. The study will need to outline the costs, benefits and feasibility of the options identified.
Diane reports that, in late February or early March, the City will advertise for a senior center facility assessment.
An RFQ should be out now or very soon for architectural services. The County intends to create a pool of firms they can call on when they need services.
In the next few months, Longmont expects to issue an RFQ for design-build services for a wastewater treatment plant ammonia-dewatering project.

In December, Glenwood Springs advertised for design and project management for Ice Rink locker room improvements. Ricky informs us that this solicitation was cancelled and they plan to reissue it as a design-build project in the near future.

Lane reports that the District would like to get funding together to build a replacement track and football field at the high school. The actual work would begin in 2014. They would need to get sufficient funding identified by this fall so that they could apply for a state grant. We will follow up with Lane as the year progresses to see how the project is progressing.
Diana reports that she anticipates the City will issue an RFP in March for construction management/general contractor services on the City Services building.
The Town would like to complete an expansion of the recreation center. At this point, it appears they may request funding in 2015 to initiate the project.

records.Project: Hydropillar 2 MG Elevated Storage Res. Imps
records.Description: This project provides for major renovation of the 2 million gallon hydropillar elevated water storage reservoir.
The City's capital plan includes proposed funding for improvements at Maple Hill Neighborhood Park.

This project consists of the re-design and renovation of the Sunset Campus, including renovation of the shelter, construction of a new pool chemical building, the addition of new play features and replacement of the sand beach with grass. It will also include construction of a new first tee practice green, renovation of the clubhouse and improvements to the golf course entry.

Phase IV consists of the expansion of fleet vehicle repair bays, based on a 2007 space needs study and a 2009 fleet consulting study. The City has determined it needs space for two additional mechanics. The Phase IV expansion will be the final build-out of the site.

The existing Fire Station #2 building was built for all male crews and the day room and kitchen are too small for the 3-4 firefighters assigned there 24/7. The apparatus bays have asbestos ceilings and are too small to conduct maintenance and training on modern fire apparatus. The building does not meet current building, fire, ADA, energy or water quality codes. It lacks proper storage space for bunker gear and supplies and inadequate laundry and fitness areas. The site itself is also problematic. There is no room for expansion without variances and parking is inadequate. The project is currently unfunded in the 5-year plan.

As we reported previously, the County wants to develop this ranch property into an Open Space park. In 2010, they planned to issue an RFQ or RFP for architectural and structural engineering services related to the buildings on the site. Then the project was put on hold. They want to preserve one existing barn if it's feasible. They may tear down and replace another building to maintain the look of the original, but to house restrooms. The third structure will probably be torn down and replaced. In this case the new structure may or may not resemble the original. The current CIP shows funding in 2017.

The Betasso water treatment plant is the city's primary water treatment facility. It has deteriorated during almost 50 years of continuous operation. Pretreatment capacity limitations of the existing flocculation/sedimentation process result in residuals that comprise more water content than desired. The City has allocated funding in 2013-14 for a pre-treatment and residual study, chemical storage tanks and piping and rehabilitation of the combined influent flow meter. Funding beginning in 2015 will be used for design of the major rehabilitation and improvement project.
This project will remodel the downtown Colorado Springs fire station. It is currently unfunded, but considered a high priority.
The City's Water/Utilities Department plans a project to upgrade or replace the clearwell at the North Plant to meet chlorine contact time requirements.

This project provides for replacement of the playground equipment with a new facility in the current location. The Park Master Plan recommended moving the playground to the location currently occupied by restrooms. This plan is recommended to be changed due to funding constraints.
This project provides for a Bear Creek/Marston raw water treatment pilot project.
This project provides for a new caretaker's house at Dillon Dam.
The Department's capital plan provides proposed funding to replace the headquarters facility at Dillon Dam/Lake.
This project provides for a new 5 million gallon distribution storage facility at Montclair recycled water facility.
The City's water capital improvement program includes proposed funding in 2016 for improvements to the Vidler tunnel.
The Town proposes funding in 2015 to remodel the performance stage.
The City has proposed funding in 2016 for a 1.3 mgd expansion of the water treatment plant.
This proposed funding will construct a water storage reservoir at the Scalva Farm location.
This project will replace the main libary's plaza. The aging plaza has cracked and heaving pavers.
The City plans historic preservation improvements/renovations at Legacy Ranch.
The City's capital plan includes proposed funding in 2014 for a 5 million gallon water tank.
This project will replace the aging vehicle wash facility. It is beginning to show structural deterioration and a longer wash lane is needed for many of the vehicles currently in use.

records.Project: Community House at Little Toots Park
records.Description: The City's capital plan includes proposed funding for renovation of the community house at Little Toots Park.
This project provides for improvements/renovations to the Old Chamber (Butterfly) building.
This project will provide funds for deficiency corrections at the existing Barker Dam, including security related projects identified in the Source Water Master Plan.

This project provides for a permanent park restroom at the Recreation campus. The campus includes outdoor tennis courts, an in-line skating rink, skate park, arboretum and trails. Currently, the only outdoor restroom is a portolet at the skate park.

This project provides the capacity increase of the secondary treatment system at the wastewater treatment plant to increase current capacity above the 80% design threshold. The project may be assimilated into the nutrient removal process project (see our project ID #66054) if the current regulatory trajectory continues.

In 2011, a preliminary design and assessment was conducted by CH2M Hill to identify current chemical feed deficiencies and future chemical feed needs for the treatment processes at the water treatment plant. The report indicates that the plant is deficient in chemical storage capacity, ventilation in existing chemical areas, system controls and room for expansion within the existing chemical buildings. This project proposes to construct a new building for alum, polymer, fluoride, on-site generation of sodium hypochlorite and chlorine dioxide and storage to meet current and future water treatment requirements.
One of the City's first priority, but currently unfunded, projects is to build a new police station.
The City has developed a list of "parked" projects, i.e., those for which funding has not yet been identified. One of the "first priority" projects on that list is a new downtown fire station.
This project provides for elevator tower improvements/front elevator restoration at the museum.

The City will need to fund up to $1.8 million in improvements related to the bus station relocation to the flour mill, additional surface parking and/or other TOD-related improvements at or near the Olde Town Station. As preliminary work and design proceed in cooperation with RTD and other parties involved with the advent of the gold Line, the City's role in the project "is subject to innumerable tweaks." It is possible design will be handled through RTD.
The City plans to build a new parking structure to provide 200 parking spaces for commuter rail passengers in Olde Town, in connection withe the Gold Line RTD stop.

The West Woods Golf Club Restaurant will be remodeled for office space, enlarged service areas and increased storage. The project will also expand the loading dock area by extending the brick wall and paved areas to the parking lot to the west and by removing existing landscaping. It will remove the old scoreboard and storage shed by the southwest doors, construct heated office and storage space, remove current office space and cover the stairwell to the clubhouse basement with flooring for new storage space.

records.Project: Arvada Ctr. Front Entry Renovation, Wayfinding
records.Description: Remodeling the front lobby at the Arvada Center will create a more exciting and accessible entrance, move the box office staff to a more secure location, install a greeter/will call station, install ticketing kiosks, install several informational LED screens throughout the center, install a new automatic front door system and new doors to the Main Gallery, install new shades as required and replace existing Donor Wall panels with digital elements.
The City anticipates using Conservation Trust funding to complete the Aurora Sports Park.
The City's capital plan includes proposed funding in 2016 to complete improvements at Cottonwood Park.
This project will increase the capacity of a raw water pump station from 20 to 50 million gallons per day, as recommended in the Treatment Master Plan.
Rehabilitation of the Rampart tower and tunnel was originally planned in an earlier year, but has been postponed to 2018.
This project provides for a new Box Creek water reservoir.
The City's capital plan includes proposed funding in 2017 for a new Terminal Raw Water Reservoir.
This project provides for an expansion of the Binney water treatment plant, in accordance with the Treatment Master Plan.
The Town anticipates completing renovation of the recreation center in the 2015-2017 time frame.

In 2008, the Town worked with a firm to develop a plan for improvements along the Blue River corridor between Coyne Valley Road and Valley Brook Road. The plan calls for a series of parks and public places along the river. Staff will apply for a GOCO grant to implement these plans. Improvements include installation of the River Eddy Park, the Amphitheatre and Oxbow Park, including one bridge across the river. It is possible no new consultant services will be sought for this project.

This project provides for raw surface water storage along Plum Creek north of the town boundaries. Feasibility studies suggest it could cost approximately $10,000 per acre-foot, which allows 300 acre-feet of storage for $3 million. The project is planned as a joint effort with Castle Pines Metro District and Castle Pines North Metro District.
This project provides for the restoration of the Greenland Post Office building.
The County plans the restoration of the Evans Homestead historic structure, located on Palmer Divide Ranch on West Cherry Creek.
The County plans to complete courtroom tenant finish improvements in 2016.
This project will replace a fabric dam at Hampden and Broadway. The dam inflates and holds back Little Dry Creek.
The Town's capital plan includes proposed funding in 2015 for a new snowcat storage building.

The City's capital plan includes a number of "future projects" for consideration. The projects are not funded in the current five-year program. One of these projects is to construct additional housing on Town-owned property.

As a component of the Step Up Main Street Master plan, the Town plans to design and construct Town Hall Park improvements. The project is not funded in the current five-year program, but is on the list of "future projects for consideration."
The existing Public Works facility is overcrowded, with inadequate storage space. The Town has proposed an addition; however, the project is not funded in the current five-year program.
This project provides for ice rink building improvements at the Frisco Adventure Park. The project is included on the list of "future projects for consideration."

records.Project: Park and Ride Facility, US550 and CR220
records.Description: The County has included this project on its list of potential projects over five years in the future. The project will construct a new park and ride facility at US550 and CR220.

records.Project: Park and Ride Facility, US550 and CR310
records.Description: This project provides for a park and ride facility at the intersection of US550 and CR310. The project is included on a list of potential projects for funding beyond the five-year planning period.

This project will construct a park and ride facility at US160 west of Gem Village. The project is included on a list of projects for potential funding beyond the five-year planning period. No cost estimate has been developed for the project at this time.
This project provides for a fire training burn building.
The City's capital plan includes funding in 2015 to replace the Bemis House roof.
This project provides for improvements to the City Center campus.
The pool area needs major renovation to bring the access and entrances up to ADA requirements. The current capital plan indicates funding only for design and engineering.

The pool liner was installed over the existing aluminum pool shell in 1999, and is nearing the end of its life expectancy. In addition to replacing the liner, it is recommended to conduct a structural assessment of the aluminum shell and to thoroughly clean and descale the skimmer chase and the deck drain. The proposed funding of $500,000 could change depending on the condition of the aluminum shell.
The restrooms in the recreation center are original to the building and need to be renovated.
This project includes the addition of two tennis and/or pickleball courts adjacent to the existing tennis courts, plus an ADA accessiblt public park restroom.

This project will provide BOD capacity increase of the secondary treatment system to increase the current capacity above the 80% design threshold and to re-rate the plan capacity to 12 mdg and 28,500 lbs/day BODs. This coincides with the nutrient removal project.

Lagoon 9 is a phased project that will be constructed to increase storage and drying capacity for the water treatment plant residuals. This is required and regulated by the Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment.

The Big Dry Creek wastewater treatment facility is in need of various repairs and replacement of assets as part of its normal operational life. Projects identified for 2014 ($350,000) include repairs/replacement of buildings, roofs, valves and piping, pumps, chemical storage tanks and treatment equipment. The project also includes treatment tank cleaning to remove sediment that could otherwise damage pumps and other equipment. Consultant services may or may not be needed.

Inspections performed in 2010 on the Northwest water treatment facility water storage tank identified the need for structural repairs to the roof supports and the need to re-coat the tank as part of regular maintenance. Additional modifications are needed to comply with new regulations and safe drinking water requirements, and also to improve tank safety for maintenance personnel.
This project provides for full buildout of the North Westminster public transit station plaza.
The City plans to complete process improvements at the Big Dry Creek wastewater treatment plant.
This project provides for process improvements at the Semper water treatment facility.
This project will rehabilitate and/or replace the HVAC system in the Semper water treatment facility administration building.
Denver Water's capital plan includes proposed future funding for rehabilitation of Antero Reservoir.
As part of the recycled water distribution system, this project provides for Park Hill pump station improvements.
This project provides for replacement of the Hillcrest treated water storage tanks.

records.Project: SOS Facility Imp's - Cheesman New HQ
records.Description: Denver Water plans this source of supply facility improvement project - Cheesman new headquarters facility.

John reported previously that Colorado Parks and Wildlife (CPW) expected to seek consulting services to help CPW with a portfolio risk analysis for all of the high and significant hazard dams. He now says he is working on the RFQ and expects it will be released in early to mid December. The project entails a screening level risk analysis for a total of about 36 dams.
We reported previously that the City of Alamosa planned to release an RFP for design of a new ice rink. In October, Heinz indicated that the project was on hold. He now says it has been cancelled.

Previously, Rhea reported that the University of Colorado at Colorado Springs expected to advertise for architectural/engineering services for the design of an expansion of the recreation center. She now says the RFP should be issued after the first of the year.
records.Agency: Univ. of Colo. at Colo. Springs

records.Description: As we reported previously, the City expects to issue an RFP for a space needs assessment for the Police Department, with a particular focus on space requirements for its District 2 officers and the headquarters facility.

Previously, Mark indicated that the City might seek consultant services for design of improvements at the historic Bromley-Hishinuma farm. He now informs us that they decided to continue with a firm that had done some previous work at the farm.
DIA anticipates advertising soon for design/build services for a new 2,000+ space parking structure of similar design and character to the existing Module 4 West parking structure.

Maureen reports that the Authority is working with RTD to build a parking structure in the Old Town Station area (Gold Line), instead of an 8-acre parking lot RTD was planning. They plan to put out an RFQ or RFP for a developer to assist with the structure and to prepare a master development plan. An alternate contact is Clark Walker at the same phone number.
records.Type: AS, DR, MS, PK, PL, ST

records.Description: The Auraria Higher Education Center expects to advertise soon for construction manager/general contractor and for commissioning services for the new 5th Street parking garage.
Around mid December, the Housing Authority expects to issue an RFP for affordable housing development on vacant land.

As we reported previously, this project provides for improvements per the approved master plan. Phase 1 and 2 improvements will include final design and construction of a 70-space parking lot and a 10-court tennis complex. Paula still expects the City will issue an RFP in October for this initial development. (Full development of park amenities will require a future bond issue.)
The City plans a new fire station in the northwest part of the city, possibly in the vicinity of Wilson Avenue and 29th Street. Ken reports that he anticipates advertising for design early in 2013.

As we reported previously, the Department of Military and Veterans Affairs expects to seek architectural/engineering services for code required improvements to the Readiness Centers in Longmont and at Fort Carson. The latest schedule calls for an RFQ during the first quarter of 2013. An alternate contact is Kris Hedberg, kris.hedberg@us.army.mil .

As we reported previously, the District has approved a ballot measure for November. Projects will include: Science, technology, engineering and math focused facilities; renovations and additions across the district; new technology; and safety and security improvements. The additions will include expansions of Grandview and Cherokee Trail high schools. They will begin an architectural/engineering selection process after they know the results of the vote. Mike says the facility additions were designed at the time of original construction.

We reported on this project previously. Several Port of Entry projects are currently scheduled for improvements.At this point, Bob reports that the scale pit projects at Fort Morgan and Monument will be handled by the engineer that has already completed design work for one of them. For the building replacement at Monument, he hopes to use the architect that designed a similar facility at Limon. If he is not able to use that approach, he might still advertise for this project.

Denver Public Schools will place a capital projects bond and a mill levy on the November ballot. Funds will be allocated as follows: Approximately $230 million for repairs and renovations to address health and safety issues in aging schools and to improve energy efficiency; $78 million to address overcrowding and expanded preschool and kindergarten programs; $119 million for new construction in areas of town with the greatest population growth; and $39 million to upgrade technology. The District prequalifies a/e firms periodically and typically selects from that list.

Colorado Springs's Transit Division has on-call contracts in place for architectural/engineering services. As we reported previously, the current contracts will extend through this calendar year. A new RFQ for architectural/engineering on-call services should be issued very soon.

Previously, Lori reported that Douglas County Schools expected to have some funding in place this fall to support some projects for next spring and summer. At this point, she says they still have not made decisions regarding project packages, so we cannot provide any additional specific information about consultant services that might be needed and when. We will follow up again next time.

In August, Ken reported that it was possible the airport would issue an RFP for design-build services for a new hangar building. The project was contingent on finalizing negotiations with an airport tenant. He now says the project is on hold based on a customer request. The airport is ready to proceed, but the project may or may not happen, depending on the tenant.

The Greeley/Evans School District (Weld County District 6) was placed on the "back-up" list for a BEST grant for a replacement of the John Evans middle school. The District will place a bond on the November ballot to raise the matching funds ($8.2 million). Bevan says they will need a variety of consultant services but, to ensure fairness, they will only release information through their advertising channels, such as the Rocky Mountain e-Purchasing system and the District's website. Further information is available at http://www.greeleyschools.org/Page/9338 .
Glen reports that, in 2013, the City might advertise for consulting services to produce design guidelines for the Louthan Historic District.
DIA's current schedule indicates that an RFP should be issued soon for construction manager/general contractor services for the expansion of Concourse C (west side).

Alamosa County requests qualifications no later than noon Monday, October 15 for San Luis Valley Regional Airport - Bergman Field Engineering, Architectural and Construction Administration Services. Projects may include a new terminal building, various runway, taxiway and apron improvements, lighting upgrades, expansion of the ARFF building, etc. They anticipate entering into a contract with a firm for a period of five years.

Larimer County's Facilities Department currently has two architectural and two engineering contracts in place. Previously, Jennifer indicated that they would advertise for new contracts to replace the expiring contracts. At this point, she has no further information and does not know when an RFP might be released. We will continue to follow up.
Telluride has an airport engineering contract currently in place. In August, they will advertise an RFQ for a new airport engineering contract. These contracts typically extend for five years.

As we reported previously, DIA anticipates releasing an RFP for design-build services for a new data center. The latest schedule indicates an RFP will be issued in September. Services will include architectural, mechanical, electrical, fire protection and civil engineering, plus construction services.
We reported previously that the School of Mines hoped to seek design services for a new football stadium. Mike now indicates that an RFQ is likely later this summer.

Within the nect few weeks, Lakewood expects to issue an RFP for consultant assistance with a parking garage and plaza restoration project. The garage is the underground structure at the civic center/city hall building. The garage needs restoration, and the City would like to do some upgrades to the garage and plaza area at the same time.

Mark Garcia, the interim County Administrator, reports that the County Commissioners are considering a new office building. Mark says the discusssion is in the preliminary phase and he has no more specific information at this point. We will follow up.

In the next couple of months, the Arapahoe County Public Airport Authority (Centennial Airport) plans to advertise for airport engineering services specifically for Airport Improvement Program (AIP) projects.
records.Type: AS, DR, GT, MS, ST, SV, TR

records.Description: Ron Kechter in Facilities informs us that the City, through its Purchasing Department, plans to advertise an RFQ for a multi-discipline work order type architectural/engineering contract. The project is being coordinated through the Purchasing office.
records.Type: AS, DR, MS, PK, PL, ST

records.Description: The District has been awarded a BEST grant for a new school building. In November, they will go for a bond for the matching funds. Deana says she does not know when they might seek qualifications or proposals from architectural/engineering firms for design of the new facility. The Superintendent (Thomas Taucher, 970-864-7350) is heading up that effort., He is currently on vacation. We will follow up with him.
The City's capital plan includes proposed funding to relocate the VOR (very high frequency omni-directional radio beacon) facility at the airport in 2013.
This project provides for an expansion of the South Durango wastewater treatment plant.
The County has programmed funding in 2016 for court building improvements.
This project provides for a Sheriff's office/jail annex at the airport.

This project provides for a corrections center 40-bed intensive residential facility in Rifle. In addition to the $2 million for design and construction, the County estimates expenditures of $85,000 for IT equipment and software and $100,000 for furniture and fixtures. The project has been delayed a couple of times. The latest capital plan indicates funding in 2016.
This Conservation Trust Fund project provides for replacement of the restrooms at Rudd Park.
The City hopes to complete interior renovations at City Hall in the 2013-16 time frame.
This project provides for an administration addition to the jail in Glenwood Springs.

This project will construct "immediate need" facilities at the Municipal Service Center: 1) Salt/sand storage building; 2) high pressure wash building that can be expanded to include a drive-through wash bay; 3) covered vehicle parking facility for snow plows; 4) paving of various areas on the site; and, 5) automatic gates at the yard entrance. The project is proposed to begin in 2014; however, at this time, it is contingent on available funding.
The County's capital program includes proposed funding in 2014 for design and construction of an Elected Officials' building in Glenwood Springs.

This project will construct a control structure and 42" pipeline used to release water to the South Platte River. These improvements are necessary to convert Heit Pit into an operational storage facility.
The City plans to build a maintenance and storage facility, for the Downtown Mall, next to Wagner Park.
This project will retrofit the courthouse to better accommodate court facilities.
The County's capital plan includes proposed funding in 2014 to expand the jail medical office.

The County has programmed $2 million in 2013 for architectural design and permitting for an emergency operations building in Glenwood Springs. Construction funding is not indicated in the current five-year plan.
This project provides for the phase I build-out of courtroom space a the ACIC facility.
The County's capital plan includes proposed funding for phase II build-out of courtroom space at the ACIC facility.
The County plans to relocate the probation offices to Lima Plaza.
This project provides for construction of a new wash rack bay.
The County plans to replace the roof at the Detention warehouse facility.
This project will replace the existing radio antenna site.
This project provides for a new outdoor covered hockey rink, to be constructed with a concrete floor. The project is not currently funded in the five-year capital plan.
This proposed project is currently unfunded. It will construct a two-story addition to the south side of the existing clubhouse that would extend over the current turf area.

This project will create multiple activity rooms by repair of existing walls, ceilings and floors and the removal of existing walls, plus the upgrade of electric lighting, storage and sound dampening surfaces. Rooms would include a media/movie room, a multi-use room, a reflection room and expansion of the lapidary room, plus restroom renovations, etc. The project is proposed for 2014 but is currently unfunded.

records.Project: Centennial Village Comm. Dist. - Opera House
records.Description: This project will continue work on the Commercial District at Centennial Village. It will provide additional exhibit space to show 1920s-1940s businesses, additional storage and storefront exhibit cases. The project will include an opera house for temporary exhibitions and to provide rental space for weddings, meetings and dinner theater presentations. Streetscaping will be completed between the existing and new buildings. The project is proposed to begin in 2014 but is currently unfunded.

This project provides for the additional amenity of a spash park to the Family FunPlex west of the pool patio area, similar to the ones at Island Grove and the Sunrise Splashpark. The project is proposed in 2012 but is currently unfunded.

The City hopes to purchase new land and develop multi-use facilities including trail access, parks, water acquisition and a Fire Department burn building. The proposed structure would be used for a variety of firefighting training activities including live fire training, search and rescue, ventilation and SCBA drills. At this time, the project is not funded.

As the City's population grows, the need for water storage also grows. Loveland has proposed future tank projects to supply adequate water and fire service for future population growth. One project is a proposed 5 million gallon tank that will be in addition to the existing 4 million gallon above-grade steel tank at the west end of 29th Street in northwest Loveland. Another project is a proposed 3.5 million gallon tank that will be in addition to the existing tank on 43rd Street.
This project provides for a complete remodel of City Hall, to create a better environment for staff and citizens of Aspen to work and conduct business.

This project provides for the installation of on-site chlorine generation to create chemicals required for water treatment without the hazards associated with shipping and delivery of chemical purchases.

Previously, the City hired a consultant to work on phased improvements at The Bay. It is possible additional services will be needed for future phases. This phase includes improvements to the locker rooms, restrooms and concession buildings.

In the spring of 2011, Ken reported that the District was working on a feasibility study for a future Phase 2 Aquatics Center project. This year, they put a tax issue (sales tax increase) on the April 3 ballot to finance the project. The measure did not pass. At this point, Ken says they are regrouping and asking the community for suggestions. The pool is in bad shape and is overused, and needs to be replaced, but they are not sure how they will get it to happen. We will monitor progress.

As we reported previously, the City's capital plan includes funding for a new or renovated City Shops/Maintenance & Operations facility. It is possible they will advertise for design within the next few months.

Previously, Erik reported that he hoped to receive funding for a Dome indoor track project, with seating, locker rooms, restrooms, synthetic turf and a relocation of the throwing events area. Funding was approved for this project. The College recently advertised for a/e services for the High Altitude Events Center. Erik informs us that the firm selected for the Events Center will also be awarded the track project.

As we reported previously, the School of Mines expects to seek architectural/engineering services for design of a new residence and dining hall. Mike indicates that an RFQ should be advertised this month.

Kurt reports that he anticipated the staff would handle any design needed for some indoor arena upgrades. Recently he has been thinking that they might need to hire an architect for some of the improvements. At this point, no decision has been made. We include the item here to let you know of the possibility. We will follow up.

The legislature approved funding for the 2012/13 fiscal year for replacement of the roofs at the main building and the annex building at Arapahoe Community College. John anticipates seeking design engineering services after the first of July.

records.Project: Life Safety & Exiting Work, 1881 Pierce St.
records.Description: The legislature funded a project for the 2012/13 fiscal year to complete some life safety improvements and exiting work at the Department of Revenue's 1881 Pierce Street facility. It has not yet been determined whether or not they will advertise for consultant/design services. If the anticipated professional services fee is under $50,000, they might not.

records.Project: Jim Hamm's Pond Dist. Pk./McIntosh Dist. Pk.
records.Description: As we reported previously, the Jim Hamm's Pond Park project (phase 3) would complete pathway extensions, a pond overlook and boardwalk, habitat improvements, interpretive features and a bird blind. The City expects the project to qualify for Great Outdoors Colorado grant funding. Paula now says the project will be combined with a smaller project at McIntosh District Park. She hopes to get an RFP out in about a month.
records.Type: AS, DR, EV, MS, PK, ST

records.Description: Aurora residents placed a bond on the November, 2011 ballot for recreation center improvements: A new regional recreation center at Bicentennial Park; a new regional recreation center at E. Vassar Place and S. Telluride Street; a new regional recreation center at Aurora Reservoir Park; and renovations to Moorhead Recreation Center. The measure did not pass. Lori says the citizen group is currently meeting with elected officials and others about future options. She has heard that, if they decide to put a new bond question on the ballot, it will not be before 2014. Information about proposed projects is available at www.arrtf.com .

As we reported previously, the University of Colorado Denver has selected an architect for the design of the new Academic One building to be constructed on the downtown campus. Kathy now expects to advertise in April or early May for construction manager/general contractor services for this new 120,000 sf building.

In February, Kent reported that, within the next couple of months, Mesa State College might advertise for consultant assistance with a steel building project. He now says the project will be a construction bid and will not require consultant services.

records.Project: Baggage, Auto. Guideway Transit System Svcs.
records.Description: As we reported previously, DIA's schedule includes a project for on-call technical services related the baggage system and the automated guideway transit system. The current schedule indicates an RFP will be released in April.
We reported on this project previously. Bob expects to advertise by the end of May for master planning services for a Fort Carson Readiness Center.

Shelly reports that there is a "lot of talk" going on right now about a potential new on-campus stadium at CSU. She says it is hard to say how far it will go. She thinks it is likely the University will hire a sports marketing consultant to help with feasibility studies. They expect to find out about funding availability in another month or so. We will monitor progress.
Breckenridge plans to issue an RFP in the next month or so for a Riverwalk Center Master Plan.
Matt reports that the Downtown Development Authority should have an RFQ out now or very soon for a hotel and conference center developer/development teams.
records.Type: AS, DR, MS, PK, PL, SW, ST, TR, WR

records.Description: Erik reports that Adams State College plans to seek consultant services for a new High Altitude Events Center, which will be an air supported structure over an approximate 200-meter track, with a synthetic turf infill and netting for multiple users. The facility will also have restrooms, storage and a small training area.

The County is currently in design for a new emergency operations center in downtown Pueblo. In the next couple of months, they plan to advertise for a project manager for the project. The project will involve demolition of an existing building and construction of the new facility.
Shelly reports that the University is hoping to obtain funding to initiate a classroom addition project at the Behavioral Sciences building.

Shelly reports that the University has a project for possible funding, for revitalization of Edwards ("Eddy") Hall. If funding can be secured, they will seek architectural/engineering services. They hope to find out within the next month or so whether or not the project will be funded.

The City requests proposals no later than 3:00 Thursday, May 3 for Architectural Services for Upgrades & Improvements to the Parks Maintenance Shop and Rotary Park Restrooms, RFP-ParkMaintShopRotaryParkRRA-E12. A pre-submittal meeting is scheduled at 10:00 Wednesday, April 18 at Greenmount Cemetery, 900 Cemetery Road, Durango. Attendance is recommended. For further project details, go to http://www.govbids.com/scripts/co1/public/home1.asp , and select Vendor Login, then View by Agency, select City of Durango and then RFP-ParkMaintShopRotaryParkRRA-E12.

This project will expand the District's administration building, providing additional office space to accommodate future staffing needs by converting the existing board room into offices, adding a 2nd floor over the existing board room and constructing a new board room.

The Central Plant Treatment Plant Facility Plan evaluated the existing capacity relative to the projected flows, loadings and permit requirements, addressed rehab needs, evaluated short- and long-term process improvements and developed a 20-year implementation schedule. In Phase III, regulatory requirements may drive the need for tertiary treatment or advanced treatment to meet very strict limits for nitrate, phosphorus and/or E. coli. If needed, this project provides for the construction of additional ammonia removal facilities within the existing South Complex.

Future increases in loadings due to projected population growth within the Metro District's service area will eventually require additional digestion capacity. Additional digesters will need to be constructed to meet the projected increased loadings. This project calls for the construction of Digesters No. 13 & 14.

The Solids Management Facilities Study Update determined that the existing centrifuges are approaching the end of their operational life and need to be replaced. Existing Humboldt centrifuges will be removed and replaced with a high-solids centrifuges.

Growth in flows and particularly loadings will occur as population within the Metro District service area continues to grow. This project will construct a third cake storage tank with a live bottom hopper enclosed in a new building.
This project provides for phase 1 thermal drying facilities, as part of the biosolids recycling program.

records.Project: NS Facility Rehab - Phases II & III
records.Description: This project provides for phase II and III rehabilitation of the north secondary facilities.

This project includes repairs designed to restore structural integrity to damaged concrete members and their connections, minimize water intrusion, improve durability of concrete members, slow the deterioration of structural members and improve safety. The project is considered a first tier priority for the 2011-16 time frame. At this point, no funding is available to initiate the project.

The City plans construction of a new fire station to serve current residents and to respond to anticipated population growth in the Stapleton area. Land for the station was purchased by the City in 2010. The project is included in the "1st tier priority" list of projects, but is not currently funded in the six-year capital program.

The City envisions a new 14,000 sf office complex annex to the existing Police District 4 substation to house detectives assigned to the substation. Since the Department decentralized Property Crimes Detectives and reassigned them to the Districts, the existing facility has become severely overcrowded. The project is considered a first tier priority for the 2011-16 time frame, but no source of funding has yet been identified to complete it.
This project provides for North Secondary fixed asset replacement schedule (FARS) improvements.
This project will replace one or more digesters for solids processing, as part of the fixed asset replacement schedule (FARS).
As part of the fixed asset replacement schedule (FARS), this project will replace a sludge handling tank.

Denver anticipates an RFP this quarter for relocation (including right-of-way services) of the Metro Special Weapons and Tactics Team (SWAT) to a new location with improved work conditions. Metro SWAT is currently located in a facility that is in need of major repairs and that has limited work space. We are not able to provide a contact person for this project, sorry!

records.Project: Micro Master Plan for Family Housing
records.Description: Previously, Phil reported that it was possible the University would seek consultant assistance for what he described as a "micro" master plan for some family housing. Subsequently, the funding was retracted. Last summer, Phil said he was working on a "white paper" to persuade the holders of the purse strings that they needed to move forward with the project. At this point, the project remains on hold.

Previously, Dave reported that the District had initiated some internal work on a lift station asset replacement project. He said it was possible that some consultant design support services would be needed. In October, he said they might have a small portion of work related to architectural or roofing inspections for existing buildings to determine the remaining life of structure components. At this point, Dave says he thinks if anything happens with this, it will be late in this first quarter.

The University is currently in the programming phase of renovations at Baker Hall - a housing and dining hall. Phil still expects a program plan will go to the Board of Regents for approval in about June. He hopes to release a design/build RFP at about that time.
The Airport's current on-call engineering contract will expire in April. Georgiann reports that they will advertise soon for a new contract. These contracts typically extend for five years.

David reports that the College has put in a request for state funding to remodel French Hall. He will not know until the Long Bill is passed whether or not the project will be funded (and is a bit concerned about receiving phone calls in the meantime). We will follow up as the state budgeting process progresses.

Mike reports that the Board has approved the District's purchase of a 113,000 sf building that will require renovations before they can move into it. Mike says they will seek architectural/engineering services "at some point," but he doesn't have a schedule yet. We will follow up.
Adams State College expects to advertise for design of a baseball complex with restrooms, a pressbox, storage and minor concessions.

records.Project: Custom Large Grp. Shelter, Sand Crk Pk
records.Description: The City hopes to receive a grant to initiate design for a custom large group shelter at Sand Creek Park. If funding is received, they will seek consultant services for the design.
In the next few months, Aurora may seek consulting engineering services for a new fishing pier at Aurora Reservoir.
Dave reports it is possible the Metro Wastewater Reclamation District will issue an RFP in the next few months for architectural/engineering services for repairs to leaking support buildings.

The Town released an RFP today for design of a new municipal office building. Proposals are due no later than 4:00 Friday, February 17. The project will include confirming and advancing the current schematic design for the new offices and a partial interior remodel and exterior alteration of the existing police department wing.?The selected architectural team will be responsible for preliminary design, design development, design approval and entitlement, construction documents and construction administration. The RFP is available at http://www.vailgov.com/docs/dl_forms/ToV_Municipal_Site_RFP_020112.pdf .

Bob informs us that the Colorado Bureau of Investigation hopes to find a way to establish a facility in Pueblo. At this point, no plans or funding are in place. However, the CBI has apparently talked with a couple of building owners about the possibility of purchasing and converting an existing building. We have no idea whether or not anything will happen with this in the foreseeable future, but will continue to follow up on it.

The Council has identified this building as the future location of the Town Hall, once the Town is able to dispose of the existing Town Hall. The 2012 budget of $250,000 will be used to program the space to the point where the Town could make commitments to lessees. The remaining design budget would be committed once the project moves forward. An RFP should be issued in the next several months.
This project will design and construct a new Red Zone water storage tank. The capital plan includes $3 million for this project in 2016. Additional funding may be required in future years.

This 10-acre neighborhood park will be part of the Kubat Annexation. Construction may include picnic areas, playground, restrooms, dog exercise areas, small skate park areas, shelters, pathways, sports courts, multi-use fields and landscaping. The project is not currently funded.

This unfunded project provides for the relocation of the Parks Maintenance Facility from Roosevelt Park to the former Bradley Auto Salvage site on South Sunset Street. The project involves primarily indoor storage areas. However, the outdoor storage is used by others including recreation services and Head Start, which will need to be accommodated at a location other than 7 South Sunset.

A proposed expansion of the Longmont Museum and Cultural Center, at 400 Quail Road, will consist of a 10,000 sf auditorium and prefunction space that will provide for more programming options. The project is only partially funded.

This unfunded project provides for the design and construction of a 1500 sf addition to the southeast side of the Longmont Recreation Center. It would also enclose the game room to install additional cardio equipment. The project would also inclue the purchase of bikes, treadmills, etc.
This unfunded project will construct a 6,000 sf metal building with a 3-bay shop, 2 offices and a conference room at the current centralized parks maintenance facility on South Sunset Street.

This unfunded project calls for improvements to Collyer Park. Previous redevelopment has been completed as parts of other projects, including new lighting, restrooms and shelter replacements. This project, the final phase of improvements, will design and construct a new playground, gazebo and small skate area.

The City's capital plan includes proposed funding to design and construct a new wastewater treatment plant headworks and third secondary clarifier. The existing clarifiers are the limiting factor in the overall capacity of the treatment plant.
The County plans to design and construct equipment storage facilities for Road Maintenance District III.

This project will replace the two floating-type digester covers at the water pollution control facility. These digesters are 75-foot diameter tanks. The cost estimate includes $143,500 for design, $1,625,266 for construction, $80,000 for project management, plus miscellaneous and other costs.
This project provides for the construction of a fire training burn building.
This project provides for a new high zone 1 million gallon water storage tank.

The City's capital plan includes a project to complete Arkansas River Legacy Phase 3 Parks and Trails improvements. The project will include ADA access and parking, a small parking lot for trail and kayak park users, landscaping, lighting, restrooms, shelters and site amenities, plus trailhead access improvements at 4th Street, Main and Pearl Street. These improvements are needed to complete the connections between the new 4th Street bridge and users at the Kayak Park, and connections from the Blocks neighborhood to the river trail at Main Street and Pearl Street.

The City plans improvements at Westlands Park, primarily to consist of the retaining wall west of the water feature. The project adds amenities to Westlands Park and addresses a maintenance operations issue.
The City's capital plan includes proposed funding in 2013 for rehabilitation of the interior paint of the Gunbarrel water storage tank.

records.Project: Covered Equipment Storage Facility Dist. I
records.Description: The County plans to construct a new covered storage facility for equipment and other storage for Public Works' maintenance district I.

This unfunded project consists of an addition to the Senior Center building on the south and west sides near existing Meals on Wheels designated space to provide additional space for growth of the home delivered and senior center lunch programs. The project will be paid for by Longmont Meals on Wheels, Inc. when funded.

This project will fund improvements to the 5.73 acres of land adjacent to the Water Treatment Plant. The site will provide an expanded yard waste drop-off site with extended hours to meet the needs of Broomfield residents. Funding for upgrades includes grading and surfacing, fencing, bins for storage and, possibly, a greenhouse and Sprung shelter.

This project will be the last of three major improvements at Broomfield's Heit Pit. This phase will provide a connection between Heit Pit and the splitter structure of the outlet facility. Improvements will include a discharge apron along the side of the pit to serve as a reservoir inlet, an outlet tower and a pump station to extract water from the reservoir.
The City's capital plan includes proposed funding beginning in 2014 for remodel of the fire storage facility.
The City's capital plan includes proposed funding in 2013 for improvements to the Museum's collections center.

The City's capital plan includes proposed funding in the 2013-2016 time frame to construct an addition to the ice arena's Zamboni room storage garage. The project consists of constructing an additional garage to house the two ice resurfacing machines and will install an ice melting pit inside the new addition.
Once the new wastewater treatment plant is completed, the City plans to demolish the old wastewater treatment facility.
The City's capital plan includes proposed funding for a new fire training facility.

This Phase 2 project will install a culvert under 37th Street near Lincoln Avenue and a retaining wall along the southeast bend of Dry Creek adjacent to 37th Street at Lincoln Avenue, to mitigate erosion problems within the creek.
Later in 2012, Vail might seek architectural consulting services for the remodel of the Main Vail Fire Station.
The City's capital plan includes a project in 2014 to add a bay at Fire Station #3.

This project which, includes a 2013 design study, would evaluate proposed or adopted state nutrients standards, determine potential discharge limits for the WPCF, review and recommend alternative treatment technologies for the WPCF and develop design and specification documents for bidding. The costs include $630,260 for design, $20,400 for "professional services," $7,631,621 for construction, $245,000 for project management and $95,676 in miscellaneous costs.

This project involves the replacement of one aging Schwing high solids cake pump located in the dewatering building on the South Plant at the Water Pollution Control Faclity (WPCF). The costs include $38,000 for design, $300 for "professional services," $233,800 for construction, $20,000 for project management and $49,944 for miscellaneous costs.
Vail anticipates infrastructure improvements at the Chamonix housing site.
This project includes $1 million for road improvements, $200,000 for a bus shelter and $100,000 for parking replacement.
This project will improve the entry area into the Lionshead parking structure.
This project will address drainage, structures and walls. Specific projects will be identified in the future.
The City's capital plan includes funding in 2013 for an Open Space building.
The City proposes an expansion of fitness facilities in 2014.
The City has programmed funding in 2016 for an extension of LaMont Does Park.
This project provides for a splash park at the Bob L. Burger Recreation Center.
The City's capital plan proposes golf course pavilion improvements in 2016.

records.Project: County Commons Open Space, Tom Frost Res.
records.Description: Proposed improvements include adding a picnic shelter that also serves as an environmental education center, with a presentation table and a sanolet with screening; native trees to provide shade, and parking lot capacity expansion from 10 to 30 vehicles. The pavilion is separated into a Phase 1 project (Tom Frost Interpretive Shelter Project). The project is also proposed for phasing if the entire project is not allowed to be built.

The project includes replacing the roofing system to prevent structural damage. In a 2010 building assessment it was noted that the ballasted EPDM room over the addition was shrinking and pulling away from the parapet at all locations. The shrinkage is indicative that the system is reaching the end of its useful life. The problems include asphalt failing at several locations, cracked lapped joints allowing water permeation, weathered and failing parapet cap flashing joints and leaking skylights at the joint in the metal frame.

This project includes constructing a Broomfield 2-tower site cell, or adding one tower to the existing simulcast cell in Adams County. The current simulcast cell does not provide coverage in the Interlocken and Southwest Business District areas of Broomfield.
The City plans to replace the 120-foot clarifier mechanical drive and superstructure at the wastewater plant. The existing clarifier was installed in 1987.

records.Project: Project K Primary Clarifier at WWTP
records.Description: This project will provide a treatment capacity increase of the primary treatment system to 12 mdg max month design to provide additional plant capacity for city growth. The primary clarifier will be constructed in the area now occupied by the de-commissioned trickling filters.
This project provides for a water storage tank at Cardiff Glen.

Previously, Tom reported that, within the coming nine months, the Town might seek architectural services for design to remodel a historic building. They still expect to hire an architectural firm in January for a programming study for the building.

As we reported previously, the Metro Wastewater Reclamation District anticipates seeking consultant services for its next Facility Plan Update. Dave still anticipates that an RFP will be issued before the end of the year.

We reported previously that the University of Colorado Denver expected to issue an RFQ for a Phase II update of the ten-year master plan of the Anschutz campus. Kathy now says the RFQ is supposed to be released tomorrow, December 2.

In December, the Town of Vail plans to issue an RFQ/RFP for architectural/engineering services for a major remodel and addition to the Vail Golf Course Clubhouse. The project is scheduled for construction in 2013.

records.Project: Water Treatment Plant at Dory Hill
records.Description: Jim reports that it is possible the City will issue an RFP sometime in 2012 for design of a new water treatment plant at Dory Hill.

records.Project: MS Renovation, Alt. HS Program Manager
records.Description: David expects to release an RFP very soon for program management services for the project to complete a renovation and addition to an existing middle school to convert it to an alternative high school.

CSU has proposed a major renovation and additions to the Animal Sciences building. Shelly says they will not have final approval for bonding until February, but might advertise sooner for architectural/engineering services. The project will involve a complete renovation, including all building systems. The University also proposes two additions, one to the north to address the Monfort Quadrangle and to become the main campus entrance to the building. The south addition will include a 170-seat auditorium, second story collaboration space, new accessible restrooms and an elevator.

The City completed a study in about 2002 for a new maintenance facility. For the past several years, they have hoped to fund the project to proceed to design and construction. Suzanne now reports that they are working on an RFP for an updated conceptual design for the site. They hope to release the RFP by the end of October.

records.Project: Del Mar Pool Bathhouse/Family Aquatics Ctr
records.Description: This project funds improvements at Del Mar Pool, including the addition of "sprayground" features, filtration system replacement, renovation and expansion of concession areas, installation of a roof over bathrooms, and replacement of gutters and water circulation systems. At this point, it appears likely the design work will include just the aquatics center, and not additional park improvements. Lori says they will continue a public process through October. They have decided to hire an aquatics consultant as a preliminary step. See our project ID #74320.

We reported on this project previously. Berthoud still expects to issue an RFP for design/build services for water plant process updates. At this time, Stephanie does not know when they will be ready to release the RFP.

records.Project: MS Renovation/Addition, Convert to Alt. HS
records.Description: We reported in August that this district applied for a BEST grant for a middle school renovation and addition to convert the existing middle school to an alternative high school. The district was not awarded the grant, but was included on the "backup grant recommendations" list. The District will hopes to receive a future BEST grant, at which time they would require architectural/engineering services. We will continue to follow up.

The staff is in the early stages of planning for a small consulting project (under $100,000 in fees) for engineering services at the Department's lab. Steve says he hopes to have an RFQ ready by the end of October.

The University of Colorado Denver plans to advertise soon for program planning for the new Academic One building on the Downtown Denver campus. They anticipate a new 120,000 sf building. The University anticipates entering into a contract with the expectation of continuing it through the design phase. As the project moves forward (maybe about a year from now), they will also require geotechnical and surveying services, and construction manager/general contractor services.
