Within the next few weeks, Aurora plans to issue an RFP for consultant services related to a joint Police and Fire training facility. The successful firm will coordinate with Police, Fire and Public Works to prepare a modified framework development plan to provide for a new joint training facility.

We reported on this project previously. The City plans an RFP for landscape architecture services plus other architectural/engineering support for Mehaffey Park development. Gary now says he expects to advertise within the next two months for planning/preliminary design.
records.Type: AS, DR, PK, PL, SW, ST, WR

records.Description: We reported on this project previously. Montrose will require design/build services for an additional 3 million gallon water storage tank. An environmental assessment is complete or nearly complete. Laura reports that she expects to issue the design/build RFP early this month. The design of a 16-inch water line to connect the future tank to the water system will be included in the same RFP, then bid for construction separately around the end of this year. (We previously listed this water line separately as project ID #73367.)

In June, we reported that the District had applied for a BEST grant for a new science building. They have already completed a master plan for the building. The latest information is that they did NOT receive the BEST grant in this round so, for the time being, they will not pursue this project.

The County Architect's office typically advertises every couple of years for new on-call consultants in various disciplines. Alan reports that they will advertise later this fall for new on-call contracts. He anticipates they will award two to three contracts in each discipline. The last time they advertised for these services, the disciplines included architecture, interior design, landscape architecture, civil engineering, soils engineering, structural engineering, mechanical and electrical engineering, roofing/moisture protection, fire protection engineering, drafting, LEED consulting and lightning protection.

The Town's 2011 capital plan included a new three million gallon water storage tank. Terry reports that the project was contingent on receipt of a state grant, which they will not receive this year. He still hopes they will be able to pursue the project in 2012.

Cal plans to seek assistance from one of the City's on-call engineering consultants for some improvements at the water treatment plant. If he is unable to find a firm under an on-call with the needed expertise, the City will issue an RFP more broadly. If an RFP is going to be issued, it should go out within the next month or two.

The Lakewood Housing Authority anticipates building a 100-unit senior housing project. Bill reports that they will likely select an architect from their on-call list, but will issue an RFP in the next 60 days or so for construction manager/general contractor services.

In the next couple of months or so, the University of Colorado at Colorado Springs expects to advertise for design of an academic health services building. Gary says they will most likely complete the project using the general contractor/construction manager delivery method.
records.Agency: Univ. of Colo. at Colo. Springs

records.Description: The South Adams County Water and Sanitation District plans a new building for district administrative offices. In February, they advertised for site selection assistance. A design ad should be out now or very soon.
records.Agency: So. Adams Co. Water & San. Dist.

records.Description: In the spring of 2010, Denver Health advertised for qualifications from architecture and construction firms, to complete work on an as-needed basis for projects with fees and construction costs between $50,000 and $500,000. They subsequently retracted this RFQ. Tom now says he still hopes they will readvertise sometime in 2011, possibly by sometime in July. When they rerun the ad, he expects will require all interested firms to submit qualifications.

In April, Phil reported that the University of Colorado at Boulder students would vote in April whether or not to fund a $63.5 million addition to and renovation of the recreation center. He now says an RFP for architectural/engineering services should be issued around July 1. The project will include a 100,000 sf addition, plus site planning for relocation of tennis courts, parking and some other issues.

In April, Tim reported that Boulder County, in cooperation with CDOT, anticipated issuing an RFP this fall for design of improvements to SH 93 between Highway 128 and Highway 170. Improvements would include road widening, roadside drainage, environmental clearances, a pedestrian trail including a reinforced concrete box underpass, public process, retaining walls, construction phasing with traffic control and an asphalt pavement overlay. Tim now says the project has been changed and we should consider it deleted for the time being.
records.Type: AS, BR, DR, EV, PK, ST

records.Description: Sam predicts a July RFQ/P for architectural services for a City and County/Colorado Mountain College project. The City and County portion will be a library and the CMC portion will include classrooms and a two story parking garage.

In July, Colorado Mountain College anticipates advertising for general contractor services for a combined City, County and CMC project. The City and County portion will include a library and the CMC portion will include classrooms and a two-story parking garage.

The City's capital plan includes funding in 2011 for a West 1 million gallon water storage tank. Anne reports that they anticipate completing this project as a design-build. No specific schedule has been set to initiate it. We will follow up.

records.Project: Re-Creation of Fire Station - Heritage Ctr.
records.Description: Ross reports that the City expects to advertise in the next month or two for architectural/engineering drawings for the re-creation of an old fire station at the Heritage Center.

In the next month or two, the City plans to seek consultant services for design of a trolley museum and trolley restoration area. The City has entered into an agreement with a private foundation to create a space to bring in trolleys and restore them.
In about mid June, the Authority plans to advertise for general contractor/construction manager services for the rehabilitation of the Powers Circle Apartments.

The City's capital plan includes funding in 2011 for improvements to the chemical building at the water treatment plant. A 2009 master plan update recommended various improvements to meet current codes. These include: Provide chemical containment; add a fire protection system, add a means of egress and add emergency showers and eyewash. Amy says the City will seek consultant services for design, but she does not have a schedule at this point.

The Town's capital plan includes a project called the Utilities Operations & Maintenance Center. They have been accumulating funds each year for several years to finance the design and construction of a new facility. Rick reports that it may still be a few years down the road before they are ready to begin analysis and design of the project.

This project provides for park improvements at Bear River. It includes concrete sidewalk, basketball courts, soft surface trails, golf holes, landscaping, turf play field, parking areas and restrooms.
The City's capital plan proposes a historic preservation project to restore Lithia Springs and other city-owned hot springs.
The County's five-year capital improvement plan includes proposed funding in 2012 for a 10-year airport master plan.
The County's capital plan includes proposed funding in 2015 for a new Sheriff/jail annex at the airport.

This project will provide a multi-use sports complex to be developed on city property at the Steamboat Springs Airport. It will consist of a four-diamond ball complex, parking, road improvements, restroom, hardscape and extended outfields for various turf sport layouts.

This project will provide improvements to the park, and a restroom addition to facilitate use. Additionally, it will evaluate the dam spillway of the upper pond to determine if breaching or reconstruction is the better alternative.
This project calls for the restoration of the historic Chamber of Commerce building currently occupied by the Yampa Valley Land Trust.

Upgrades include electrical, lighting, voice/ data upgrades, new cabinets/appliances in the second floor breakroom, install ventilation, new finishes in restrooms, a basement second egress, fire rated ceiling, concrete steps and handrail replacement, refinishing of hardwood flooring, new appliances, exterior site lighting, parking areas, landscaping and lattice screens.
The County plans to build a 5,000 sf fairgrounds administration and shop building.
The Town's capital plan includes proposed funding in 2013 for an expansion of the sewer plant.
This project includes funding for equipment necessary for the Wellness Program plus any necessary renovations to the available space.
This project provides for a new fire station in the South Valley area.
This project provides for a new fire station in the west area of Steamboat Springs.

records.Project: Remodel Police Station into Full Fire Sta.
records.Description: The City plans to remodel the existing police station to convert it to a full fire station.
This project will rehabilitate and restore the First National Bank building.

This project combines two projects: Renovation of the Kittredge West residence hall (approximately $22 million); and demolition of an existing dining hall and construction of a new residence hall (about $37 million). Phil reports that the project will go to the Board in June, after which (assuming approval) CU expects to advertise and RFQ/P for design/build services.

We reported previously that RTD planned a new parking structure at the proposed Sheridan Station on the West light rail line. John now says the RFP should be out soon for design/build services. The station is expected to be located between 12th and 13th Avenues along Sheridan. The parking structure will include approximately 800 parking spaces.

Previously, we were informed that Regions 1 and 3 would either issue an RFQ jointly or separate RFQs for nonproject-specific tunnel inspection services. The contracts typically handle inspections at Hanging Lake in Region 3 and the Eisenhower Tunnel in Region 1. Bill Scheuerman (720-373-4732) recently said Region 1 had received verbal approval to move ahead with the RFQ. Subsequenlty, Joe Elsen (970-384-3332) at Region 3 said his information indicated the two regions would issue an RFQ jointly. At least one RFQ should be released in the next few weeks.

We reported on this project previously. Tom now says he expects the City will issue an RFQ in about a month for consultant services for a raw water and facilities plan. The project includes a needs analysis for the integration of the City's raw water delivery system to meet operational needs at build-out and during the City's design drought event.
Boulder County might advertise in the next few months for a strategic planning consultant to help develop a business plan that might lead to some building expansion somewhere in the County.

The City and County of Denver and the Denver Housing Authority will issue an RFP sometime in April for planning services for the Sun Valley Federal/Decatur Station project. The City of Denver will issue the RFP. Chris Parr, our source of information on the project, is with the Housing Authority. We do not have a specific contact person at the City.

This project provides for: electrical and HVAC upgrades to meet current building codes; upgrades to plumbing systems and fixtures; replacement of the roof; replacement of the filtering system; and interior and exterior surface finish renewal.
Denver Water plans to complete a new flocculation/sedimentation basin at the Marston water treatment plant, starting in 2019.
The City plans to renovate and, possibly, relocate locker rooms to add family locker rooms at the Bay recreation facility.

The City originally hoped to complete a new weight room at the recreation center a few years ago. The project was subsequently delayed for lack of funding. It is not funded in the current five-year program.
The City's capital plan includes proposed funding for an expansion of the Utilities service center.

Proposed improvements include adding a picnic shelter that also serves as an environmental education center, tables along with a presentation table, a sanolet with screening, native trees to provide shade and expansion of the parking lot from 10 to 30 vehicle capacity. The project is proposed for phasing if the entire project is not approved.

Broomfield anticipates a cooperative project with Westminster to develop McKay Lake Regional Park. The City has allocated $25,000 in 2012 toward design. The McKay Landing developer provided $1,381,083 for the project. These funds remain in escrow until the project can be built.
This project provides for a new Cardiff water storage tank, which will provide a second 0.5 million gallon tank.
The City has proposed design and construction of a new City Shop facility, with funding beginning in 2013.
The City's long-range plan includes proposed funding of $400,000 in 2014 and $7,550,000 in 2015 for a new water treatment plant at Ridges Basin.

The City plans to acquire land and recreational surface rights related to Hyatt Lake. The project is located west of Eldridge Street and south of 64th Avenue. The proposed funding would purchase the lake and complete trail improvements. At this time, no source of funding has been identified to complete the project.
This future project provides for replacement of the flocculation paddle wheels and solids collection mechanisms at the Marston water treatment plant.
This currently unfunded project calls for the construction of a commercial mixed-use development with potential retail, plaza, housing and/or office, to be located at the 3rd & Kimbark parking lot.
This unfunded project would provide for outdoor handball courts to be added to an existing park facility or new park facility.
Cerro Summit is a winter recreation area offering sledding and tubing. This project provides for a shelter with wind protection and a fire pit. Benches could be purchased or built into the structure.
The City's capital plan includes proposed funding in 2013 for a water loading dock.

This project provides for the design and construction to accommodate maintenance facility space needs. Land acquisition and conceptual design were funded in previous years. Final design is currently scheduled in 2016. Construction will consist of west side storage and salt storage ($1.8 million in 2017), construction of an office building and renovation of an existing building ($2.7 million 2017-18) and east side storage and bay renovation ($1.3 million in 2019). This schedule is based on the assumption that Qwest will renew the existing lease for another 5 years. If not, the project will be brought back before Council.

This project will provide parking enhancements, additional storage space, a gymnasium, classroom/meeting room and day care/Tiny Tots space and a new entry and fitness equipment area. The square footage to be added totals 30,000. The project was previously planned to begin in 2013, but has been moved out beyond the five-year planning period due to changes in priorities and funding availability.
The City's long-term asset management plan includes proposed funding in 2014 for a complete remodel of City Hall to optimize the use of the building.

This project provides for space necessary to accommodate additional workforce. Staff will continue to examine alternate ways to use current space, but it is anticipated that an addition/remodel will be necessary.

One option to accommodate the FasTracks station planning is to relocate the Terry Street substation from Terry Street and First Avenue and use the current site for a FasTracks station. The substation would be moved to a location about 3/4 mile away, to the area east of EcoCycle. The project is not funded in the current 5-year program.

The facilities master plan will include: an analysis of current/future City space/building requirements; interaction between departments and how they affect efficiency; development of facility locations and alternatives; development of financial analysis for each facility and alternative; and development of an action plan for implementation. The City believes the project would be a candidate for a grant from the State's Energy and Mineral Impact program.

A police services building would allow the police department to expand and better provide public safety services to the community and surrounding agencies. The building would be built to provide police and dispatch services for a minimum of 30 years.

Public Works experiences considerable public traffic every day for excavation permits, sanitation questions, vendors, meetings with City staff members, etc. Visitors must drive into the yard to reach the Customer Service desk. The yard is not designed to segregate public traffic from City operations. A new municipal services administration building is needed on or near the current Public Works site. It would house the municipal services director, public works manager, city engineer, and support staff members.

This item was deferred from an earlier year. The City plans to complete a downtown campus space study. The study will use consultant services to determine the best use of available space on the Downtown Campus and to meet needs for additional space identified in other master plans.

This future park is located between Second Creek Elementary and Stuart Middle School. The park will contain amenities such as a playground, open grassy area, shelters and a perimeter trail. The project is proposed in 2013 but not funded at this time.

Arvada's long-term plan includes a project to fund all master plan projects for the O'Kane site. These include construction of a pond, lot grading, walkways, medians, aquatics center, playgrounds, irrigation and landscaping.

This project provides for renovation of the caretakers quarters, buggy shed, milk house, outhouse and well house. It will also include new signage, an irrigation system, site improvements, a new trail head, parking lot and restrooms. At this time, the project is unfunded.

This project provides for completion of the eastern ball fields and concession building, Phase I community park improvements, central ball fields, soccer complex completion and construction of a new maintenance facility. The project is currently unfunded.

This project includes construction of a new pedestrian bridge, relocation of the existing maintenance facility, construction of the Kipling Street trail, park and trail improvements, center concession stands and parking lot improvements. The project is currently unfunded.
This unfunded project would construct a group picnic shelter and complete site improvements, parking lot lighting and concrete walkways.

records.Project: Tucker Lake Open Space Park Imp's
records.Description: The City plans to complete a parking lot, picnic shelter, trails extension and overlook development at Tucker Lake Open Space Park. The project is currently unfunded.
This unfunded project will remove and replace broken walk, improve restrooms, enhance wildlife and planting and parking lot areas.
This project will construct the upper parking lot, a floating pier, boat trailer parking and restrooms, and complete trail and habitat improvements. The project is currently unfunded.

This project provides for completion of the Nature Center xeriscape demonstration garden, Fox residence reconstruction, sewer service upgrades, natural area restoration, trail improvements and renovation of the Hansen and Kennedy homes.
This project provides for a new forensic chemistry laboratory for the Sheriff's department.

This unfunded project will purchase the Bullock Power Plant and surrounding property, and then build a public facility area. In addition, the site will be assessed for contaminants and remediated of toxic materials. The open space along the river is also to be preserved.
This unfunded project will design and build a nature center on a site near the river, which will have science labs, interpretive display space, and a community meeting room.
This unfunded project is a response to a request for a regulation skating rink that could be used for leisure skating and competitive hockey, with a possible location near the downtown area.

This unfunded project will help provide an interpretive museum and nature center at Cerise Park, featuring farmstead equipment, orchard vegetation, settlement history, river habitat, educational displays, and other valuable programs.

This unfunded project would build additional bridges across the river to access the sidewalks and business areas that are on the opposite sides, acquire and demolish the industrial buildings along S. Rio Grande Ave, and remove the railroad to replace with curb/gutter/sidewalk.
This unfunded project would provide for an outdoor amphitheater in the Cerise Park area.
For this unfunded project, the city would like to consider developing a four-year college to expand the economic base.
This unfunded project would provide for the construction of an indoor activity center to supply needed space for clubs, recreational activities, and local events.
The County plans to construct covered storage for Sheriff's District III.
This project provides for new water treatment plant filter equipment.

The City's capital plan includes funding in 2013 (moved out from 2011 in the previous capital plan) for architectural design services for Riverside Park improvements. Construction funding is not included in the current five-year program.
The City's capital plan includes proposed funding in 2013 for a Parks maintenance facility at Little Salt Wash Park.

This project includes construction of a new trailhead with parking, signage and other appurtenances at the Metcalf Road switchback leading up Metcalf Gulch. It will require retaining walls, drainage improvements and extensive trail building improvements in the area.

This project provides for renovation of the existing City Hall/library building to convert it to a public safety building. This project will follow the construction of the new City Hall/library building.

The City's five-year capital plan includes a proposed outdoor covered concrete-floored hockey rink. At this time, no source of funding has been identified to initiate the project within the five-year planning period.

records.Project: FLC Multi-Use Grass Fields, Concessions, etc.
records.Description: Previously, Cathy reported that Durango planned to advertise for design/build services for four multi-use grass fields, a concession/restroom building and a 240-car parking lot on 16 acres on the Fort Lewis College campus. She now says a design/build RFP should be issued sometime this month.
This project will address the parking lot, shelter, playground, and the parking lot trail head.
This project will fund a study for the expansion of the Service Center, addressing the overcrowding at the present Service Center facility, and provide expansion alternatives.
A full back-up Communication & Dispatch Center would enhance the city's ability to continue functionality in disaster circumstances.
The City plans the renovation of the Bay, to include re-design of the existing concessions area, office and check-in area, and staff office.
This project will construct a one million gallon potable water storage tank that would supply the airport zone and Interlocken zone by gravity.
This funding is for the design to increase the capacity of the Water Treatment Plant to 24 million gallons daily.
This project will construct a reuse water pump station to supply irrigation water to future North Broomfield (Sienna Reservoir).
Plans for this project are to construct a new water diversion and conveyance facility from Meadow Island ditch to Heit Pit.
This project will increase the capacity of reuse treatment at the Water Treatment Facility from 6 to 8 million gallons per day.
This project will design and construct a tank for reuse water, serving the development in the northern portion of Broomfield County.
This project will provide for the expansion of the Service Center which houses field operations and maintenance of vehicles and equipment.
Denver Water's capital plan includes proposed funding for construction of new multi-level outlet works at Marston Lake.
Denver Water's capital plan proposes a new headquarters facility at Cheesman Dam. Funding is not indicated in the current plan, but is to be considered when developing the next program.
This project provides for a new pump station at Hazeltine.

records.Project: Moffat TP Upgrade/Expand or Build Ralston TP
records.Description: The Department has programmed funding to either upgrade/expand the Moffat treatment plan to 300 mgd or to build the Ralston treatment plant.
This project provides for short-term improvements at the Moffat water treatment plant.
Denver Water has programmed funding beginning in 2012 for some long-term upgrades/improvements at the Moffat treatment plant.
As part of its raw water facilities program, Denver Water has programmed funding beginning in 2016 for South Boulder diversion canal replacements.
This project provides for design and construction of outlet works modifications at Ralston Dam.
This project provides for installation of a new solids removal system at the Foothills treatment plant.
Denver Water has identified the need to design and construct an annex building. At this time, no cost estimate is available and the project is not funded in the 10-year plan.
The Department has programmed funding beginning in 2012 for the remodel of the west- side complex auto garage.
The City plans to replace an electric substation and transformer.
The County's capital plan includes funding in 2012 for a remodel of Arapahoe Plaza.
This project provides for replacement of the roof on the detention warehouse.
This project will construct restrooms on the west end of the park near the tennis courts.

The current wastewater treatment plant CIP plans for digester equipment replacement and improvements between 2012 and 2017. The replacement and improvements will consist primarily of inspection and interior coating of the digester covers, replacement of the 27 year-old boilers, replacement of the mixing systems, and modifications to the digester flare.

records.Project: WWTP Blower and Aeration Basin Diffuser Proj's
records.Description: This project will provide a BOD capacity increase of secondary treatment system to increase current capacity above the 80% design threshold. It will provide additional treatment to remove nutrients and meet anticipated nutrient criteria. Additional nutrient treatment facilities may need to be on line by 2016 to meet upcoming nutrient criteria for total nitrogen and total phosphorus.

The existing MCC building and control panel are at the end of their useful life and in need of replacement. The existing MCC and controls are in a poor building space close to areas subject to ponding water and high moisture.

This project provides for replacement of the roof at the Allen water filter plant. The plant, located at 1500 West Layton Avenue, is a conventional treatment facility capable of producing 28 million gallons per day of finished water.
The Town proposes funding for improvements to the performance area concessions.

This project will construct/install a new pump station to move treated water south from Rueter-Hess Reservoir to Castle Rock. The station initially will be equipped to pump up to 5 mgd and will be expandable to pump up to 20 mgd in the future.

Colorado Mountain College moved into a new facility in 2009. The Town plans to renovate the college's old building at 103 South Harris Street. The Town purchased the building from CMC after the college moved to its new facility.
The City plans to reconstruct the dam crest on Reservoir #2, as part of its mountain water systems improvements.
The Town's capital plan proposes funding beyond 2015 for for development of Bison Ridge Park.
This project provides for construction of a fabrication building for the Museum. The project is not funded in the current five-year capital plan.
The Town has identified the need to construct a new Public Works and Parks shop building. The project is not funded in the current five-year capital program.
The digester covers at the wastewater treatment plant are aging and will need to be replaced or repaired. This study will determine whether the covers can be repaired or will need to be replaced.
The City plans to complete a new biosolids storage facility.
This project will complete phase II improvements at Broad Lake Park. The project is not funded in the current capital improvement plan.
The City's capital plan identifies the need for additional police substations. At this time, the project is not funded.
The City's capital plan identifies a project to implement a "smaller" campus plan. At this time, the project is unfunded.
The City has identified the need for additional streets and parks maintenance facilities. No source of funding has yet been identified to initiate the project.
The City's capital plan includes a project to complete a central stores facility. The project is not funded at this time.
This project provides for roof and seating improvements at the Arvada Center Amphitheater. At this point, the project is not funded.
The City's capital plan includes proposed funding in 2012 for Phase I improvements at South Central Park. The cost estimate is $900,000; however, at this time, $850,000 is allocated.
This project will build a new recreation center to serve primarily citizens in the Northern Range. No funding has been identified to complete the project at this time.
This project will add a new feeder in the Holy Cross substation and purchase existing two feeders and transformer.

This project will remove the surface materials above the garage roof, which includes the concrete walls, landscape planting, brick pavers, curbing along the alley, and portions of the alley and street.

This project will provide for the construction of new employee housing, to include rental and ownership units. Costs are estimated at $2,875,000 in 2013; $3,450,000 in 2015; $3,450,000 in 2017; and $4,600,000 in 2020.
This project will provide for early planning of the BMC West affordable housing. The capital plan includes $150,000 in 2012, $250,000 in 2013 and $600,000 in 2014.

We reported on this project previously. RTD plans a new parking structure on the West light rail line at the proposed Wadsworth station. John now hopes they will get an RFP out in February for design/build services. The station will be located in the vicinity of 12th Avenue at Wadsworth. The parking structure will contain approximately 1000 spaces. It is possible RTD will issue one RFP for both this project and the Sheridan parking structure (see our project ID #66639).

This District applied for a BEST grant in 2010 for a new school, and did not receive it. Susan reports that they have applied again. They should find out sometime this summer whether or not they will get it. Even if they do, they will still need to go to voters for approval of a bond issue. They hope to build a new K-12 school. We will check back with them to find out the results of the BEST grant.

We reported previously that the Denver Housing Authority had submitted an application for federal funding for a large project at South Lincoln. Chris now says they will issue a design/build RFP in February.

Jeff reported previously that, contingent on final passage of the Town's budget on December 14, Castle Rock planned to seek consultant services for design of an outdoor pool renovation, to include the pool, bathhouse and pump rooms. Jeff now informs us that the project is included in this year's program. He expects to release an RFP very soon.
Very soon, this district plans to advertising for engineering/design for a roofing project at a high school and an elementary school.

Bill reports that it is POSSIBLE, but not decided, that the City will advertise for a new airport engineering contract. He said the Board needs to decide, then seek approval from City Council, before they move ahead, but it seems to be the direction they're headed. We will check on the status for the April Update.

We reported previously that Longmont might require consultant assistance with development of a Police firing range. Tracy now says an RFP should be issued within another month or so. The ad will be posted on the Rocky Mountain e Purchasing website. The intention is to convert an existing composting facility pre-fab building into an indoor shooting range. They may issue a design/build RFP.

The City's capital plan includes funding for a new Elks Neighborhood Park. Previously, Perry reported that the City would issue an RFP for landscape architectural and engineering services. He now says project is on hold.

Metro has hired an owner's representative for a new wastewater treatment plant downstream of Brighton. As we reported in October, they plan to advertise in December for design/build services for the new plant. Bill says the RFQ is currently scheduled for release on December 7.

We reported previously that this district hoped to complete a new fire station. In April, Charlie said he did not yet have anything more to report, but it was possible the project could move forward later in the summer. He has now clarified that the project will not involve a new selection for architectural/engineering services.

As we reported previously, Brighton expects to issue an RFP for design of Campbell Park improvements. Mark now says the project RFP should be advertised very soon. The project may be combined with improvements at the new City Hall grounds (see our project ID #71718).

In October, Norval reported that it was possible (but not yet for sure) the Division of Wildlife would issue an RFQ for a new office design near Glenwood Springs. He now says they are working on a faster track than they previously anticipated and have decided to design the project in house.
As we reported previously, Dave anticipates Metro will issue an RFP during the first quarter of 2011 for a support facilities master plan.

We reported on this project previously. Mark now says the City should advertise early this month for historic architecture services for the preparation of construction documents for the first phase of rehabilitation of the nine-acre Bromley-Hishinuma Farm Park.

Ken reports that Front Range Airport will potentially put out an RFQ/P in the first quarter of 2011 for the FAA required airport consultinag contract, for airport-specific projects and consulting. He says there is an "outside chance" they will get the request out before the end of this year.
records.Type: AS, DR, GT, MS, ST, SV, TR

records.Description: Mark reports that the City will require an Owner's Representative for the new Adult Recreation/Senior Center. It is possible they will add on to an existing owner's rep contract, or they could design to conduct a new selection process.

We reported in a Special Update in early October that Longmont's Planning Department expected to issue an RFP for historical and architectural surveys in the "flour mill" area, which is targeted as a FasTracks station area. Brien informed us on November 30 that an RFQ would be available within a day or two. They have scaled the project back somewhat and will use a less formal selection process. The RFQ should be available today or very soon.

Tom reports that the Town MIGHT seek new engineering/design services next spring for replacement of a water tank. They had a couple of firms on board for some ARRA projects. It is possible the Board of Selectmen will decide to retain one of these firms for this project.

We reported on this project previously. The District has been working on a "Preferred Storage Options Plan" (PSOP), which is intended to result in the enlargement of Pueblo Reservoir (excess capacity project). In December, Phil said they might start the environmental (NEPA) study sometime in the second quarter of 2010. In June, he said they were still in negotiations with the Bureau of Reclamation (BOR) about how to handle this part of the project. It now appears the BOR is essentially taking over the project.

This project was originally scheduled for design in 2008, but was put on hold. Jeff recently informed us he anticipates issuing an RFP next week for final design and development of construction documents. They expect to require landscape design, civil engineering, geotechnical and survey services, plus lighting design. The cost estimates from 2008 were $76,000 for design and a total cost of $1,080,000. These numbers may be adjusted at this point but we do not have updated amounts.
records.Type: AS, DR, GT, PK, ST, SV

records.Description: Previously, Bob reported that Boulder anticipated initiating design during the third or fourth quarter of this year for replacement of the roof on the Chautauqua water storage tank. More recently, he said the project had been delayed while they decided whether or not they wanted to use the roof area as a surface for a solar photovoltaic array. Construction funding is programmed in 2011. It is (still) possible they will use one of the consultants currently under a "continuing services" agreement to complete this design, when the time comes. Bob says no decision regarding this project is likely until after the first of the year.
Carl reported previously that the District was budgeting for a small feasibility study they refer to as the Granby Dam Hydro project. He now says an RFP should be issued in the late fall.

The Falcon School District plans to place a $125 million capital projects bond on the November ballot. Projects will include a new 400-student wing at Falcon High School, a new 600-student elementary school, a new 900-student K-8 school and a 400-student wing plus gyms and athletic fields at Vista Ridge High School. The District went through a process early this year to select firms in anticipation of the bond. They selected Hutton Architecture, DLR Group, H + L Architecture and Christiansen Reese & Partners.

We reported on this project previously. It calls for the development of an 82-acre community park and regional detention basin within the Upper Clover Basin neighborhood. Amenities may include lighted sports fields, concession stands, active sports courts and a small maintenance building. Last fall, Paula said they had not yet determined whether to use a current consultant or to issue an RFP. She now says they decided to go forward with an existing consultant.

Continued rehabilitation of the Montrose City Hall and Annex (Fire Station #1) will include: Masonry repairs and restoration; system upgrades for electrical, plumbing, heating and cooling; life safety improvements including fire sprinklers; restoration of defining architectural features such as windows and the east facade and tin ceiling of the historic fire station. The completed phase 1 consisted of the rehabilitation of the City Hall lobby. The project was included in the 2010 capital improvements program. However, no source of funding has been identified to initiate it this year. We will provide additional information if/when the project is funded.

We reported on this project previously. Chris now says he expects the School of Mines will advertise in the next week or two for design/build services for the renovation of Weaver Towers, a residence hall.

Jefferson County Open Space plans to advertise within the next couple of weeks or so for design/build services for a new auxiliary shop building of approximately 5,580 square feet, a paved parking and material storage yard and covered equipment storage pole barns. The new facility will be located at 3045 Illinois Street in Golden. The RFP will be posted through the Jefferson County Purchasing Department.

Previously, Tom reported that he anticipated the City of Black Hawk would issue an RFQ for design of a new outlet to a water storage reservoir. He now says they're still dealing with some issues with the state and several objectors, so it may be several more months before they release the RFQ.

In June, Gaye reported that the District applied for BEST grant funding for the renovation of restrooms and other areas of John Mall High School to meet ADA requirements. The project has made the short list of fundable projects. The short list will go to the state board this month for final approval. Based on this, Gaye is preparing an RFQ for architectural/engineering services, and expects to complete the documents around the middle of August. Assuming the project makes the final list for funding, the RFQ should be issued sometime after mid-August.

The City's 2010 budget includes a project to complete exterior renovations to the City Hall building. Mickey says the project will depend on how much money remains after they complete the interior renovations currently underway. They expect to bid the interior work in November, so should have an idea of the cost at that time. If funding is available, they expect to advertise for a restoration architect in the late fall or winter.
Within the next couple of months, Black Hawk plans to issue an RFQ or RFP for site development and design of a new Street and Facilities Maintenance Complex.

The College hopes to begin work in 2010 on a new field house. The project was not funded by the legislature for the 2010/11 budget year. However, they hope to identify another source of funding. If they succeed, they could being an architectural/engineering selection process in July or August. (Julie Feier is the new VP of Finance and Administration, but she has not yet started work at the college.)

We reported previously that the Department of Military and Veterans Affairs hoped to move forward with an armory project in Alamosa. Bob now says he expects to advertise in August or September for architectural/engineering services.

In April, Elaine reported that she anticipated an RFP In the late spring or this summer for construction management/general contracting services for the new Education and Collections facility at the Denver Museum of Nature and Science. She now says the project has been a bit delayed but she still hopes to advertise around mid summer.

Previously, Wade said he hoped to issue an RFP for a small design/build contract for a new shop facility. He reported that the project was included in the 2010 budget, but that they would have to be meeting revenue projections by mid year for the project to move forward. He now says he has no further news, but hopes to have funding by August so they can build in the fall. We'll continue to monitor progress.

Archuleta County issued an RFP in April for design/engineering/architectural services for internal renovation of the Emergency Operations Center. Larry says they now plan to re-draft the RFP and release it sometime soon, although he couldn't say exactly when.

The Colorado Department of Agriculture/Colorado State Fair requests qualifications no later than 5:00 Monday, June 21 for plans to restore roofing systems on the 4-H Auditorium, 4-H Dining Hall, and Colorado Pavilion buildings located at the State Fair Grounds in Pueblo. A MANDATORY pre-submittal meeting will be held on Wednesday, June 9 at 9:00 am at the Colorado State Fairgrounds, VIP Colorado Club House, 1001 Beulah Avenue, Pueblo. To see the published notice, go to http://www.gssa.state.co.us/CDNotices , click on Open Notices by Agency, then Colorado Department of Agriculture, and Notice No. SHF-2010-02-027AE.

Broomfield hopes to issue an RFP this summer for master planning and design for improvements at The Bay, an aquatic park. If the staff gets the go-ahead, they'll hire a consultant to help determine the potential expansion areas for the buildings and slides.

Jim reports that the Department of Corrections will have three small Controlled Maintenance projects for renovation and security related professional services. They have not yet decided how to package the RFQ or RFQs for this work. Jim expects they'll advertise for services before the end of June.

Previously, we reported that Centennial, in cooperation with approximately 10 jurisdictions in Arapahoe County, was looking into building a new regional animal control facility. They hired a firm for some consensus building and a feasibility study. Subsequently, Karen said they could decide to pursue two facilities, one for the "east side" and one for the "west side." She now reports that they are not moving forward with the project at this time. If and when this changes, we'll let you know.

Previously, Bob reported that the Department might seek consultants to initiate design work for a new Windsor Armory, pending legislative action on a funding source. He now says he anticipates they will advertise around the end of April for architectural/engineering services.

Steve reported previously that the Department of Public Health and Environment would seek design services during the first half of 2010 for a water treatment plant for the Central City/Clear Creek Superfund site. He now says he hopes to issue an RFQ in April.

The City has allocated $500,000 in 2010 toward a project to construct a new Wildland Fire Station (7,725 sf) and Apparatus Storage facility (6,000 sf) adjacent to Fire Station 6 in Gunbarrel. The facility will be constructed to LEED Silver standards. In February, Glenn indicated that the Fire Department would apply for an Assistance to Firefighters grant as part of the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act (ARRA). He now says that, for various reasons, the project has been put on hold for 2010.
An RFQ should be out now or very soon for design to modify the flow-through bulkhead in the Reynolds Adit at the Summitville Mine Superfund site.
An RFQ should be advertised soon for architectural and site design for a new office center in Gunnison for the Divison of Wildlife.

Sharon reports that Denver Public Schools will advertise in late April or early May for new architectural/engineering prequalification statements. They typically draw from these prequalifications to select firms for specific projects.
This project provides for expansion of the terminal at the airport, to include the addition of loading bridges.
The City's Better Denver bond program includes $37,470,000 for three new branch libraries, one of which is to be located on the west side of the city.
This project provides for a satellite shop in Battlement Mesa to serve Parachute, Battlement Mesa and Road Creek.
This project provides for a 40 x 70-foot building with three bays, one office, a conference facility, lockers and a laundry room.
This project provides for a new raw water storage reservoir for the Town. The previous capital plan (2009-2013) showed this project in 2011.
This project provides for construction of trail and other improvements in Van Bibber Park.
Englewood Water's current plans include design in 2011 and construction in 2012 of an ultraviolet disinfection system at the treatment plant.
The City's long-term plan includes a project to develop a multi-use regional park facility on the Etchart property.

This currently unfunded project will construct a new wash bay at the Municipal Service Center. The wash bay, located near the fleet maintenance building, is inadequate and in need of replacement. The new wash bay system will be enclosed and include both cold and hot water spray applications, with a platform on one side to allow operators to spray the inside of truck beds and the tops of other vehicles. The drain system will provide for capturing dirt, oil and grass before it reaches the storm drain system.
The City's capital plan includes proposed funding in 2011 to renovate the learning center at the muncipal golf course.
This project will cover the warm-up arena/livestock pavilion at the Fairgrounds.
The City's capital plan includes proposed funding in 2012 for construction of a new City Hall.
The City's capital plan includes proposed funding in 2012 for a new police station.
The City would like to complete park, open space and trail development at Greenway Business Park. At this time, the project is not funded in the five-year capital plan.
The City's long-term capital plan includes proposed funding for a new Police Department facility. At this time, the project is not funded.
This project provides for design and construction of a new city shop facility. At this time, the project is not funded.
This project provides for construction of a sand-salt storage facility.

The Master Plan identified the need to enhance the edge of Nottingham Lake, particularly the areas containing riprap material on the north, south and west sides and the pump house area on the eastern edge. Amenities include a fishing pier, a shallow wading area, new pumphouse facade and improved pathways, lighting and riprap material to allow for better lake access and seating areas. It is possible the Town will use a design firm that has worked on previous phases of Nottingham Park improvements.

Due to the wet environment in the locker rooms at the Aspen Recreation Center, walls are peeling, lockers are rusting, flooring is cracking and partitions and fasteners are rusting and leaving rust stains. This project will renovate the locker rooms to correct these problems.

This project will include detailed design and implementation of recommendations for preservation and potential uses for the historic property, according to the "Anderson Park Historic Assessment." The 1.25 acre site sits adjacent to the Roaring Fork River and holds potential for additional public park benefits besides the existing housing unit for one Parks employee plus open space. At a minimum, future improvements will include long-term structural and architectural renovation of the cabin.

This project will include the design and construction of a small public restroom facility at Conner Park, located behind the Aspen City Hall. The size of the structure is estimated at 1,000 sf with two women's and two men's stalls.
This project provides for a 5 condominium unit ownership housing project in the Aspen Airport Business Center.
This project provides for development of the Kendall Park site. Expenditures are estimated at $100,000 in 2012, $1.2 million in 2013 and $300,000 in 2014.
The primary goal of this project is to complete the terminal study and design the rebuilding of the airport terminal. Also included is a parking garage.
This project will expand or build a new Family Services Center to accommodate growth in child welfare, youth services, and early childhood resources.

This proposed project is a cooperative effort between Gunnison County, the city of Gunnison, and the Gunnison Valley Animal Welfare League, to provide infrastructure for the construction of a county-wide animal shelter.
records.Type: AS, DR, MS, PK, SW, WR

records.Description: This project will build a centrally-located, heated building for a storing and protecting various public safety agencies' response equipment.

As early as 2004, the County began preliminary planning and site selection for a new Public Works facility. They worked with a firm on a space needs study. Subsequently, the project was placed on hold due to lack of funding. Marlene reports that they have selected Project One as the project manager and will advertise this week for architectural/engineering services for both the Public Works Facility and the jail.

The District's current bond program includes a project to complete a kitchen/cafeteria addition and general building renewal at Mrachek Middle School. The current schedule indicates a design consultant selection in the summer/fall of 2010.

The District's current bond program includes a project to do a complete remodel and roof replacement at Altura Elementary School. An a/e consultant selection is anticipated in the summer/fall of 2010.
Last summer, Dan reported that the District would probably put a bond measure on the 2010 ballot. He now says they do NOT plan to put a bond on the ballot this year.

We reported on this project previously. Phil still had expected to advertise for architectural/engineering services for the renovation of Kittredge Commons. The program plan was scheduled for approval in January. Phil now says the project has run into a snag, raising questions about the expenditure of funds for this project in this economy. At this point, he says it may be delayed for up to a year.

The University has advertised for a/e services for a fourth floor addition to the dental school building on the Anschutz campus at Fitzsimons. In December, they expected to advertise within a week or two for construction manager/general contractor services. Mike Barden (303-724-1038) now informs us that the advertisement was postponed because they would like to expand the scope of the project. He still expects it will be advertised by the end of February for CM/GC services. Dan Shomers is the project manager.

As we reported previously, this district has been awarded a BEST grant, and plan to remodel a historic building and to add on to an elementary school. Terry says they're still not sure how they'll proceed with the project. They might decide to do a design/build with the contractor as the prime, or they may select architectural/engineering services separately. The District hopes to receive funding by early March, after which they expect to move forward with whatever approach they select.
We reported on this project previously. Mike now says an RFQ should be advertised within the next few weeks for architectural/engineering design for a Student Health and Wellness Center.

As we reported previously, UNC has been working with Semple Brown on the programming for a new music performance center, which will entail renovation of an old theater to convert it to a performance hall (to be known as the Foundation Hall Annex). Moving beyond programming to the design phase will require additional fundraising. At this point, the project remains on hold. If and when they get to that phase, they'll be required to advertise for architectural/engineering services. We'll monitor progress.
Sam reports that Colorado Mountain College will advertise this spring for a design team for a new facility in Steamboat Springs.
The Colorado School for the Deaf and the Blind expects to advertise in February or March for architectural/engineering services for design of a total renovation of a 29,000 sf school building.
records.Agency: Colo. School for the Deaf & Blind

records.Description: Curt reports that, by the end of February if not sooner, the City will advertise for what it calls "R Contracts" - the "R" stands for "Requirements." These will be on-call contracts for services in a variety of disciplines, including architectural and various types of engineering. They'll issue one RFP and do multiple selections.
John reports that the College expects to advertise in February for an IT relocation project, to include renovation of the vacated IT space.
The City's future plans include proposed funding for major maintenance improvements at the existing Fire Station #3.
This project provides for a new District 7 substation for the Sheriff's department.
The City's capital plan includes proposed funding in 2014 for development of a future water source and its treatment.
This project provides for water storage tanks at West Glenwood and Oasis Creek.
This project provides for design and construction of south side park improvements.

This project, unfunded but considered a high priority, provides for a Regional Parks Maintenance Facility strategically located in Red Rock Canyon, to support maintenance of open space areas and regional parks.

The City plans to rehabilitate wastewater lift station A in 2012. Lift station A is a critical component in the sanitary sewer system since it pumps approximately 95% of the City's wastewater to the wastewater treatment facility. The structural integrity of the lift station must be maintained to provide continued service and to avoid bypassing wastewater flow to the City of Thornton.

records.Project: Lift Station D Force Main Modifications
records.Description: This project provides for modifications to the force main at wastewater lift station D. Lift station D was originally sized and constructed for the Water Treatment Facility reclaim ponds. Since that time, additional developments have contributed significantly larger flows to the lift station, preventing staff from pumping down the reclaim ponds and surcharging the sewer.
This project provides for installation of primary clarifiers at the wastewater treatment plant. Expenditures are estimated at $108,000 in 2011, $1,025,000 in 2012 and $100,000 in 2013.

In the previous CIP, the City programmed funding in 2013 for a new permanent fire station at Murphy Creek. The new station will replace the existing temporary station. Due to budget constraints, the project has been deferred past the five-year capital plan.
The City's capital plan includes proposed funding in the 2012 to 2015 time frame for modifications at the Wemlinger water treatment plant.

One of the City's "high priority unfunded" projects is the renovation of the City Auditorium. Improvements would include the safety items, installation of air conditioning and remodel of the main level restroom.
Included on the City's "high priority" unfunded projects list is a new Parks Maintenance Facility in the northeastern area of the city.
This project provides for replacement of the exhibit hall roof at the fairgrounds.
The County's capital plan includes proposed funding in 2011 to upgrade the kitchen at the exhibit hall at the fairgrounds.
This project will remodel the Extension building at the fairgrounds.
This project provides for a remodel of the exhibit hall at the fairgrounds.
The City has programmed $2 million in 2011 and $2 million in 2012 for water storage tank improvements.

The City has included on its list of "high priority" unfunded projects a new fire station to serve north Colorado Springs. The cost estimate includes land purchase and construction of a new station. As development progresses, the need for a station in this area will be required to meet the 8 and 12 minute response times in the northern part of the city.

This currently "high priority" unfunded project would complete a new emergency operations center. An EOC provides the physical location where City departments, enterprises and other agencies come together during an emergency to coordinate resources, response and recovery actions.

A covered storage is needed for the salt and sand stockpiles located in the public works yard. A 100 x 105 sprung structure, an engineered stress membrane structure with one door, would be purchased. The new storage shed would eliminate waste and increase usability.
This project provides for repairs and renewal at the Education Services Center #4 facility. The current schedule indicates a design RFP in early 2011.

The District's current bond program includes a project to complete renewal upgrades and window replacements at the Education Service Center #1 facility. The current schedule indicates a design start in early 2011.

The District's bond program includes a project at Gateway High School for HVAC upgrades, general repairs and building renewal. The current schedule indicates a design selection in the fall of 2010. They plan to use the construction manager/general contractor delivery method on this project, so will select a cm/gc firm shortly after selecting the a/e firm.

As part of its bond program, Aurora Public Schools plans domestic water repairs and building renewal at Lyn Knoll Elementary. The current schedule indicates an architectural/engineering selection in the fall of 2010.
This project provides for a new roof, pool building repairs and building renewal at Hinkley High School. The current schedule indicates a fall, 2010 design consultant selection.

This project, part of the District's bond program, entails a complete remodel of Lansing Elementary, to include replacement of the roof. The project is scheduled for a/e consultant selection in late 2011.
The County's capital plan includes proposed funding in 2011 to upgrade/expand the vehicle storage area for the Sheriff's office's mobile command vehicle/equipment.

The City's capital plan includes plans to purchase or construct a new general storage facility. The current plan is to construct a 5,800 sf facility at the City Yards, to be used for recycling building materials, wastes, computers and furniture and for other city operational needs. The scope may change as a result of a Downtown Office Space Study. However, due to economic conditions, the study has been placed on hold. Consequently, the storage facility project has been moved from 2011 to 2012 in the current capital plan.
This unfunded project entails researching and eventually enclosing the north patio area of the senior center to create an indoor program space.

records.Project: East Sprat Platte Alluvial Wells, Ph 2
records.Description: This project provides for the design and construction of four alluvial wells at the East Sprat Platte reservoir, and will include concrete well houses, pumps, electrical systems, controls, and piping to interconnect wells and discharge flows.

This project allows for the ongoing repairs and scheduled replacement of multiple facilities throughout the city. Planns include the Carpenter Rec Center, Fire Stations 1 and 3, and City Hall northeast and southwest wings.
This project provides the design and construction of flush toilet restrooms at sports venues, such as the Thornton Sports Complex, Carpenter Rec Center, and Northern Lights Ball Fields.
This project provides for reconstruction of the north plaza at the Main Library. Due to the size of the project, it may be designed through a Continuing Services contract or in house.
Boulder's capital improvement plan includes proposed funding in 2014 and 2015 for improvements at Foothills Community Park, located at 800 Cherry Avenue, in the northwestern part of the city.
The City plans rehabilitation of Lift Station E, including completion of the assessment and implementation of the recommendations from the assessment.

Replacement of the existing Alum tanks will require the removal and replacement of the chemical building roof. With the existing location of the Alum tanks, if there were a leak it would go directly to the treatment system and would stop the treatment of water until the Alum was removed. In addition, Alum is designated as a hazardous material requires some form of spill containment.

The City's capital plan includes a number of projects considered high priority, but for which no source of funding has yet been identified. One of them is for land purchase, design, preparation and building construction of a new Fontanero facility for engineering/maintenance.
This project will replace the existing bridge and improve retaining walls and the stilling basin on Maizeland Road. The project is currently unfunded, but considered a high priority.
This project will construct a new 13,000 sf fire station. It is currently unfunded, but considered a high priority.
This project will construct a customer waiting area at the Police Department's impound building. The project is currently unfunded, but considered a high priority.
This project provides for water pump station improvements at Front Range Airport.
The District's current bond program includes a project to repair the roof and provide other building renewal items at Pickens Tech school. The project should be initiated in late 2011 or early 2012.

We reported previously that the City hoped to build a new aquatic center. Heinz said the project would probably require a capital projects bond. The bond issue did NOT pass on the November ballot. At this point, the project is on indefinite hold. We'll provide additional information if and when the City decides to pursue another bond or other financing.

We reported previously that Adams State College hoped to release an RFQ for a renovation of the Education and Social Sciences building. In April, Erik informed us the project was on hold. He now says the College will be bonding for more project financing in the near future, so he anticipates that they'll advertise in December or January for design to renovate this building.

Previously, Erik hoped Adams State would seek consultant services for the college's music program building renovation. We last reported the status in April of this year, at which time the project was on hold with no predicted start date. Erik now says the College will bond for more project financing in the near future, so he hopes to release an RFQ in December or January for design teams to renovate this building.

We reported previously that Longmont expected to seek some engineering help for structural evaluation of the basins at the Wade Gaddis water treatment plant. Cal now says the City plans to begin with a study of the Wade Gaddis plant and then will look at some short- and long-term improvements for the Wade Gaddis and the Nelson-Flanders plants. The Wade Gaddis plant will also require some capital fixes. The City plans to use on-call consultants for at least the initial work. It is possible they'll do an RFP for some design work later in the year. We'll follow up as plans are developed.

As we reported previously, Aurora plans to advertise for design of the Highline Canal trail underpass project at Chambers Road. The project will involve civil engineering/ design of the approach to the underpass, access to an existing box culvert, a retaining wall, paving and drainage improvements and, possibly, utility relocations. The latest information is that an RFP may be issued within the next couple of weeks.

We reported previously that Denver Public Schools anticipated advertising during the first quarter of 2010 to update architectural/engineering qualifications for future school bond projects. Sharon Gonzales (sharon_gonzales@dpsk12.org) now says the Bond Director has not given them a specific timeline to advertise for the qualifications update. We'll continue to follow up.

Dean reports that the City is using Conservation Trust Fund monies for a golf course maintenance building. They'll take the site plan to City Council in early December. It is possible they'll use a stamped building. If so, they may not need an architect and they already have a project engineer. If they decide to go another direction, they could require architectural services.

records.Project: Renovation of Tolman, Rait & Pinon Halls
records.Description: The College is currently in negotiations with an architectural firm for design to renovate Tolman, Rait and Pinon residence halls. Kent reports that an RFQ for construction manager/general contractor services should be out now or very soon.

Rafael reports that the City has received a federal Department of Energy grant for an energy efficient window replacement project at city hall. He says he'll advertise for architectural services as soon as the City receives the appropriation.

John reports that RTD and Forest City/Stapleton Group are cooperating on a project to build a new park and ride at Stapleton. He says they haven't yet determined which agency will take the lead. They should decide by early 2010. We'll follow up for our next CIP Update.

As we reported previously, the Denver Museum of Nature and Science plans an addition (south extension) to the Museum, for a science education center and collections storage facility. The project will address the following: Construction of a storage facility under the existing parking lots at the DMN&S site; and, using existing space, remodel to construct classrooms, labs, a teacher education center, relocation of the library and a second traveling hall.?The Museum has selected a firm to assist with the creation of an RFP for a/e services. They expect to issue an RFP in October assuming they can work out some final legal details.

As we reported previously, the City hired a firm in 2008 to evaluate the wastewater treatment plant. Douglas now anticipates a November or December RFP for design of improvements. Improvements will involve a UV disinfection system, plus improvements to the digester complex and the headworks facilities. The current capital plan indicates a cost estimate of $7.8 million for biosolids digester improvements and $4.4 million for an ultraviolet disinfection system.

As we reported previously, the City selected design teams over a year ago for the Springhill Park Phase 1 project and the Beck Recreation Center renovation, and that both projects have been on hold. In August, Lori said the Parks & Recreation divisions within the City had been separated, but were moving back together. Due to the long delays, they were considering the possibility of starting over with new design selections on these two projects. Lori now says they have made the decision to move forward with the existing firms on both projects.

Previously, this district advertised for an owner's representative to provide assistance and advice as the District develops new facilities and remodels existing ones. They have now selected a firm for these services. Charlie reports that the District hasn't closed on the property it would like to purchase for a new station. Assuming they acquire the property and the Board funds the project in the 2010 budget cycle, the new station should move forward. Charlie expects to know more by December. At that point, they would start working on an architect selection. We'll follow up.

Mike Barden reports that the University of Colorado Denver plans to issue an RFQ within the next week for architectural/engineering services for design to add a fourth floor to the dental school on the Anschutz campus at Fitzsimons. The estimated construction cost is $5.2 million. Dan Shomers is the project manager.
Glenn reports that he MAY have a need to issue an RFQ for architectural services in the next several weeks. He did not provide details of what the services would be needed for.
Erik reports that he hopes to require architectural/engineering services for a student success center, if a grant is approved. He should know about the grant sometime in October.

Ward reports that the Grand Mesa Water Coservancy District is considering rehabilitating some breached reservoirs on the Grand Mesa, which would require civil engineering and headworks design services. He did not have a specific predicted time frame.

Diane reports that, in the next several weeks, Thornton plans to advertise for architectural/engineering and landscape architectural services for the Margaret Carpenter Recreation Center site build-out project. Diane says the staff is still working on the project scope and hasn't yet given the project an official title.

This district has placed a bond on the ballot in November. Glenn reports that most of the projects will be small maintenance type items, such as flooring, HVAC, doors and windows. However, they will also build a new transportation maintenance facility. They have already hired an architect and an owner's representative. The general contractor that worked with them previously no longer exists. They haven't yet decided whether they would bid the transportation facility or select a construction manager/general contractor. The owner's rep will help them make that decision after the election, assuming it's successful.

Sometime this month, the Littleton Housing Authority expects to advertise for planning and design for a new multi-family building, which will most likely be two-story attached townhomes, 60 units. (As we reported in August, firms are invited to send Lori an email to be added to the list to receive RFPs when they're issued. Also, our apologies, we spelled her name "Greenwall" previously. "Greenwell" is correct.)

Denver's Aviation Department plans to advertise sometime in the next few months for on-call architectural/engineering services. Services will include facilities evaluation, testing, performing studies, architectural programming, preliminary designs, aircraft parking layouts, site inspections, baggage handling systems coordination, gate systems, environmental, construction documents, plans, specifications and construction administration for various concourse additions, improvements and modifications.
records.Type: AS, CM, DR, EV, MS, ST

records.Description: We reported previously that Ridgway hoped to issue an RFP for a review/feasibility study of the raw water collection system/reservoir enlargement. The project involves a grant from the Colorado Water Conservation Board (CWCB). Greg informs us that he received permission from the CWCB on Friday, July 31, and plans to issue an RFP immediately.

The last time we reported on this project was in June of 2008. Paula now says the City plans to seek design services this year for Phase 9 improvements, which will include two trailheads along the greenway, plus parking, restrooms and site amenities. One of the sites will also include a bridge.

The City has issued its RFP for wastewater treatment plant design and construction management and on-call services. Responses are due no later than 4:00 Wednesday, August 26. A pre-proposal conference is scheduled at 2:00 Thursday, August 13 at the WWTP, 501 East Frist Avenue. The RFP is available from the Rocky Mountain e-purchasing system, https://www.govbids.com/scripts/CO1/member/unnotified/Notices/ViewOpenTitles.asp?AID=1267&AgencyName=City+of+Longmont . You must log in as a vendor to view/obtain the RFP at that site.

As part of the City's program funded through the bond passed in November, the City plans to issue a design RFP soon for renovation and upgrades to the LaAlma outdoor pool and pool house. Matt reports that an RFP is likely in August for architectural, landscape architectural and aquatic design services.

Previously, Chris reported that the City would seek consultant services for design of trail improvements along Wadsworth Boulevard. It will include trail and retaining wall design. It will not involve an underpass. Chris now says they have decided to design these improvements in-house.

As we reported previously, Thornton plans to advertise an RFP for a pool evaluation at the Margaret Carpenter Recreation Center. Diane now says she's not sure when an RFP will be issued for this project.

As we reported previously, the Department of Military and Veterans Affairs expects to seek consultant services for design of an armory in North Colorado Springs. Bob reports that the facility is expected to be located just on the east side of I-25 adjacent to the Air Force Academy. He now says the land acquisition has been delayed, but he still anticipates issuing an RFP in about a month for architectural/engineering services.

In June, Ed reported that the Division of Wildlife might issue an RFQ within a month or two for an alternatives analysis and hydrological study of the Beaver Park spillway - a dam near South Fork. He now says they decided to discuss the project with a couple of firms and to select from the state's as-needed list.

The City's 2009 budget includes $15,000 for a City Hall Relocation Study. Jay Harrington, City Manager of Cortez, reported in June that he wasn't sure whether or not they would pursue this project this year. Rick Smith now says it appears unlikely. If they do, it's possible they will either complete a few tasks in-house, or go back to a firm in Durango that completed a previous space study. If they use a competitive process at some point in the future, they wouldn't prevent firms outside the area from submitting proposals, but they do have a local firm preference policy.

The Littleton Housing Authority owns and manages public housing properties. When architectural/engineering services are required for new facilities or renovations, the Authority typically advertises for these services. It also maintains a list of interested firms to which it sends RFPs. Firms may be added to this list by sending Lori an email with relevant information. She reports that the Authority is in the process of purchasing some property for future housing. It will need to go through the zoning process before they can begin an a/e selection. They could begin the selection process within the next several months. We'll follow up.

Joe reports that IF the Department receives a State Historical Fund grant, he'll seek consultants for a project to reroof three buildings at the Fairgrounds in Pueblo. He hopes to find out this first week of August whether or not they'll receive the grant.

Ken reports that, depending on growth, the airport may require improvements to the water and wastewater plants and piping. It is possible they'll seek a utility consultant within the next 12 months or so. This is all very tentative at the moment, and will depend on the economy and its effects on their growth. We'll follow up.
Very soon (it should be this week), Metro plans to seek consultant services for a sustainability study for the new regional "Northern" wastewater treatment plant.

Cheryl Slaymaker reports that the College has been in some discussions of initiating architectural/engineering for a new residence hall. She does not yet have any details and the project is not definite. We'll follow up.
This project provides for a new water storage facility, a 15 million gallon of treated water storage reservoir, to be located near the existing Gold Hill reservoir. Construction should begin in 2014.
The County proposes funding in 2010 for expansion of regional park facilities.
The City plans to install a new retaining wall and to restore landscaping and irrigation on the north side of Orchard Road from Goldsmith Drive to Dayton.
This project proposes to construct a new indoor riding arena in 2011.
The City plans to design and construct a new Blue Zone water storage tank.
This project will design a second water storage tank serving the Orange Zone. Construction is anticipated beyond the current planning period.
This project will design and construct a new peaking water treatment facility.
The City's capital plan proposes funding in 2011 for recreation facility improvements.

The capital plan includes potential bond funding in 2014 for the next phase of improvements to the Betasso water treatment plant. A recent analysis indicates that existing treatment processes will be adequate to meet water demands in compliance with federal Safe Drinking Water Act regulations until that time.

This project provides for a new firing range, including a training facility. If the County combines the decommissioning of the existing firing range with this project, it will add another $1.5 million to the cost estimate.

This project provides for the Box Elder wastewater treatment plant, sewer mains, lift station and force main improvements. The project was originally planned to begin in 2009. It has now been deferred to 2014 and beyond.
The City will develop additional water storage capacity necessary to meet growth in Zone 5, including a reservoir to pump water to higher zones. The project was previously scheduled in 2011.
