Project design is planned in 2012 and construction in 2013. This would expand the lower level dance room and add 3,000 sf of lobby space and activity space for service enhancement.

An evaluation is scheduled in 2011 to determine when to increase water treatment capacity from 16 million gallons per day (mgd) to 32 mgd. The project is included on a list of projects that are currently unfunded in the 2009-2013 capital plan.
Located in the Village of Five Parks, Beeman Park will be developed in coordination with School District R-1 as a School-Park for the neighborhood to maximize usage.

The City's capital plan identifies the need for future water treatment facility improvements, to include an on-site 14 million gallon reservoir, disinfection system enhancements and additional solids handling systems.

The City originally planned a new fire station in the Northeast area. The project was included in the 2008 capital improvements budget, but subsequently delayed. In the 2009-13 CIP, the project is not funded and the City indicates the station will not be needed due to slower than anticipated development in the area. It may still be needed at some point in the future, beyond 2013.
The Utilities Department plans a project to complete the 1st Creek Lift Station and Force Main project.
The City plans a new Utilities operations control center. The project was originally planned to begin in 2011. It has now been deferred to 2014 and beyond.
The Utilities Department originally programmed funding in 2009 for new administrative (additional office) space. This project has now been deferred to 2014-2015.

records.Project: New Satellite Bldg, East Valley, Clifton Area
records.Description: This project will provide for a new county satellite building, approximately 9000 sf, to meet the needs of the East Valley, and might include services such as Motor Vehicle, Sheriff, and Health & Human Services.

records.Project: West End MC Rd/Bridge Shop, SO Substation
records.Description: In a previous capital plan, the County anticipated beginning work in 2009 on a new West End Mesa County Road & Bridge Shop, and Sheriff's Office Substation at the Fruita transfer site. This new shop would consolidate the Fruita, Loma, and Appleton shops at one site. The 2009-2014 capital plan shows that this project is not funded for this planning period.
The County's five-year capital plan includes proposed funding in 2012 for a new SW administration building.
The County plans funding in 2011 for the administration building.

One of the last projects anticipated as a result of the tax measure passed in November of 2006 will be Phase II of the County's government center. The County will conduct a new architectural/engineering selection for the second phase.
This project provides for design and construction of "project C" waste activated sludge (WAS) thickening at the wastewater treatment plant.
This project provides for design and construction of an 8-mgd filter plant (no. 4A) at the water treatment plant.
The Town proposed funding in 2009 for an ice rink. The project has been deferred while they wait for the completion of the Recreation Master Plan and a citizen survey.

This project provides for a new family aquatic center. The City anticipates that capital project dollars may have to be accumulated over multiple years if they cannot be appropriated in a lump sum, as the project cannot be completed in phases.

The City programs funding each year to review the condition of sewage lift station and to recommend improvements to meet current standards, and to maintain capacity appropriate for development in the drainage basin. Expenditures are estimated between $259,875 and $300,861 per year.

This project will convert the sludge storage tank (SST) located immediately west of the west primary digester to a third primary anaerobic digester. When the SST was first constructed during the 1990s plant expansion project, it was to be used only for sludge storage with the idea that it would later be converted to a third primary anaerobic digester.
The County has identified the need for a new criminal justice facility (maximum and medium security). At this time, no source of funding has been identified to complete the project.

Among the County's projects categorized as "Additional Needs/Backlogs" is a project to complete a Sheriff's Operations, Training and Coroner Facility. No funding has been identified to pursue this project.
The County has identified various services and projects that cannot be funded with current budget projections. One of the project needs is for an emergency operations facility/data center.
The County and the City of Colorado Springs have identified the need for a joint public safety substation. At this time, no source of funding is available to pursue the project.
This project would construct a work release facility for the county. No source of funding has been identified to initiate the project at this time.
The County would like to pursue a joint public safety substation with the CIty of Fountain. At this time, no source of funding has been identified to pursue the project.
El Paso County estimates a cost of $15.9 million to comply with a state mandated court expansion. At this time, the County has not identified any source of funding to complete this expansion.
The County would like to complete improvements at the Judicial Complex, but has not identified a source of funding that will permit initiating the project.

The County has identified nearly $45 million of renovations, remodel and asbestos abatement at Centennial Hall/City office building to accommodate staff shifts. At this time, no funding is available to complete this work.
The County would like to complete a facility to store the Sheriff's Department's emergency vehicles. At this time, no funding is available.
The County's long-range plan includes proposed funding for a new administration building. At this time, the project is unfunded.
The County's future plans call for an addition to the judicial complex. At this time, no source of funding has been identified to complete the work.
The County would like to build a new facility for the Department of Human Services. At this time, the project is unfunded.
The County's future plans include a new facility for the Health Department. At this time, no source of funding has been identified to complete the project.
The City plans to complete the Highpointe lift station and sewer improvements project. Funding was originally programmed in 2010-2011. It has been deferred to 2013-2014.

records.Project: Kings Pointe Central Basin Lift Sta.
records.Description: The City previously planned to complete the Kings Pointe Central Basin lift station in 2012. It has been deferred to 2015.
This project provides for new Wemlinger Zones 4 and 5 water pump stations.
This project provides for an eastern Adams County substation for the Sheriff's office.
The County's capital plan includes a project to complete a pre-trial holding facility.
This project provides for restoration of Allen House. At this time, the project is unfunded.

The City has identified the need to increase the capacity of the water transmission system. The project will add a northern transmission line pump station to supply future development in the northwest portion of the city. The first step will be a study. At this time, the project is unfunded.
This project provides for East End Clerk & Recorder's office tenant improvements.
This project provides for replacement of the roof on the CSU Extension facility.

records.Project: N. Boulder Rec. Ctr. Weight Room
records.Description: The City's capital plan includes 2010 funding to remodel the weight room at North Boulder Recreation Center.
This project provides for improvements/additions at East Boulder Community Park.

The City previously initiated a study related to future biosolids digester improvements at the wastewater treatment plant. The current capital plan indicates that the City anticipates moving forward with these improvements in 2010. The project may require bond funding.
The City's capital plan includes proposed funding in 2011 for a new digester building for the water reclamation plant.
The City anticipates completing improvements at the golf course clubhouse in 2012.
The County's capital plan includes proposed funding in 2014 for a district attorney building.
The Town plans to restore the old Town Hall as a museum. This project is Phase 2.
This project provides for a concession/restroom building, plaza paving and bleacher pads at Diamond Valley.
The Town plans to complete improvements to the pool and fitness area at the Community Recreation Center.
This project provides for a new bath house at Boardwalk Park.
The Town's long-term capital plan includes proposed funding for a collections and exhibit building for museum collections.
The City plans to complete a study and repair work on the Carpenter Recreation Center swimming pool.
This University of Colorado Denver plans to issue an RFQ in the next week or two for architectural services for multiple renovations at the Dravo building, located on 14th Street in Downtown Denver.

We reported on this project previously. The City still plans to issue a design/build RFP in June. The new Museum and Discovery Center will be located at the east end of Martinez Park at the end of North Mason Street. The current capital plan shows City funding totalling $6,183,750.

This project provides for improvements at Richards Lake Neighborhood Park. The City has programmed funding over several years to develop this park. Craig reports that the project is now on hold because the development does not yet have enough homes built to complete the park, and development has stopped for the time being.

As we reported previously, the District plans a design consultant selection in the fall of this year for a complete remodel, new roof and renewal of Elkhart Elementary. They expect to select from the firms that have submitted prequalification statements. The District anticipates selecting construction management/general contracting services for the project in the spring of 2010.

As part of its bond program, this District plans to complete HVAC, repairs and renewal of Side Creek Elementary school. The current schedule indicates a design consultant selection in the fall of 2009. The District expects to select from the firms that have submitted prequalifcation statements. Construction manager/general contractor services are scheduled for selection in the spring of 2010.

Thornton plans has advertised for a study/master plan for a museum, history and art facility (homestead site) at Lambertson Lakes. Proposals are due no later than 5:00 Tuesday, June 16. RFP documents are available for viewing at Contracts and Purchasing, 2nd floor of City Hall at 9500 Civic Center Drive. It is available for download at www.rockymountainbidsystem.com . Refer to the RFP document for information on a pre-proposal conference, if any.

The state's budget Long Bill includes funding for design of a multi-use support building for the Youth Offender system. Jim reports that an RFQ for design will be issued for this project, but he does not yet have a schedule. We'll follow up.

The Authority recently selected a firm for master planning for the South Lincoln/Osage redevelopment project. Ryan reports that he expects they will issue an RFP within the next six months for design. They may decide to do the project as a design-build. Ryan says this has not yet been determined.
Corrie reports that an RFP should be issued within the next month or two for final design of improvements at Village Greens Park North.

The CIty of Lone Tree recently selected an architectural firm for the new cultural arts center. Seth reports that they'll issue an RFQ in the next few weeks for general contracting services. The 50,000 sf center will include a 500-seat multi-use auditorium, a multi-purpose room, offices and break-out rooms, a warming kitchen, surface parking and associated site work. Firms may register on the City's website to receive notices of projects. Go to www.cityoflonetree.com/list.asp to sign up.
Kent anticipates a June RFP for design to repair/replace the roof at the Tomlinson Library building. The state's 2009-10 budget Long Bill includes Controlled Maintenance funding for this project.
The Town's 2009 capital budget included $50,000 for design of a new water storage tank. Rodney says the project is being postponed to 2010, when they expect to issue a design/build RFP.

Ed reports that the Division plans to issue an RFQ for design of an outdoor education complex. The state is trying to secure a site near Roggen for a large animal research facility. Ed says they'll complete the project in three phases of about $3 million each.

Ed reports that he expects the state will issue an RFQ in the next couple of months for design of the Gunnison Regional Service Center. The project is dependent on the City of Gunnison's annexation of land for the center.

The state's budget Long Bill includes controlled maintenance funding to replace the roof on Alderson Hall at the School of Mines. Mike reports that, if the cost estimate for design is over $50,000 or for construction is over $500,000, they'll need to advertise for consultant services. If the estimates are under those numbers, they'll use the state's as-needed contracts.

The University plans to advertise soon for design of exterior stair tower improvements (exiting improvements) at the Henderson Museum in Boulder. The project is included in the state's budget Long Bill as a controlled maintenance item.

Last fall, we reported that Grand Junction had advertised for architectural services for various anticipated projects. We asked Amy what firm had been selected and she responded that they were not satisfied with any of the proposals they received, so they're currently researching other options.

We reported on this project previously., South Adams has decided to negotiate a connection agreement with the Metro WW Reclamation District. This means a new regional treatment plant would be a Metro project. Jim says he believes Brighton is also negotiating a connection agreement with Metro, but we have not yet been able to confirm this with Brighton or Metro.
records.Agency: So. Adams Co. Water & San. Dist.

records.Description: As we reported previously, the legislature passed a funding bill in FY2008/09 (separate from the overall budget "Long Bill") for the new justice center and history museum. The history museum will precede the justice center. In February, John reported that it is possible the state will begin design on the new justice center in FY2009/10. He now says, due to general budget woes, he's not sure when they'll be able to begin the project. We'll follow up.

Previously, Ron reported that the Department expected to issue an RFQ for engineering and consulting services (including structural) for facility and equipment (sludge press) upgrades at the Argo Tunnel water treatment facility. He now says the RFQ should go out in the next week or two.
As we reported previously, Erie plans an RFP for design of a water storage tank. The status remains the same: The project has been postponed to the fall or, possibly, to 2010.

We reported on this project previously. Jim told us the College had three proposed simulation classroom/lab projects, all of which were currently on hold, including the Lowry campus project that was previously advertised. One of the other two, the Critical Incident Theater (big room) simulation lab project, he hoped would move forward. He now reports that it has been scaled back to the point that it will involve only equipment purchases and no major renovation.

As we reported previously, Urban Drainage plans to hire a consultant to complete an analysis of the Pine Gulch Dam, in cooperation with the Town of Parker. Shea indicates that the funding agreement has been signed, so they'll begin mapping soon and seek consultant services in about a month.

As we reported in January, City Council has approved plans for a 200-room hotel with associated conference center in downtown Durango. The project is contingent on the developer's obtaining adequate financing to move forward. If and when the financing is in place, the City plans to seek proposals for a design/build contract to complete a new parking structure. At this point, Greg says he's not sure anything will move ahead with the hotel project this year. We'll continue to monitor progress.

In February, Shawn reported the POSSIBILITY Parks & Rec would seek consultant services during the third or fourth quarter of this year for a shelter design and a master plan for park development. It turns out these were two separate projects. The shelter design ended up being a minor rework of existing plans, and the City decided to use the architect that prepared the original plans. The park master plan is now on hold and Shawn does not know when it might move forward. We'll follow up.

We reported previously that Diane indicated the City would seek design services for a park project. She now says Council still needs to decide what amenities to construct and at what location(s). It is possible the project could involve two sites: 136th and Holly and at the recreation center. They may build out both sites.

We reported previously that Denver plans to issue an RFP for professional services for development of a space planning standard for Denver International Airport. The RFP is now tentatively scheduled for release in April.
Mike reports that the School of Mines will see consultant services within the next few months for a program plan for a new Visitor's Center.

An RFP should be out now or very soon for design of a new truck wash facility. We have been asked to refer any contacts regarding the project to Purchasing, 303-639-7100. However, Purchasing doesn't usually have information until a project is ready to be advertised.

In the next week or two, Aurora expects to issue an RFP for design to remodel the South Maintenance Facility. We have been asked to refer contacts for this project to Purchasing, 303-639-7100. However, Purchasing may not have much or any information about it until just before it's advertised.
Within the next few weeks, Grand Junction plans to advertise for a historic structure assessment at the railroad depot.
Scott reports that he anticipates issuing an RFQ or RFP in the next month or two for design of a new events center.

Scott reports that the Estes Park Urban Renewal Authority expects to advertise soon for design of a new grandstand. We were not yet able to get more detail about this project as we have traded a couple of messages with Scott but not spoken to him in person. The project may be managed by someone else. We'll provide more detail as soon as possible.

This project provides for new restrooms in the north part of Sloan's Lake Park. The current schedule indicates issuance of a design RFP in April. The City may use an on-call contract for this project. We have not yet been able to find out a project manager's name.

As we reported previously, Alamosa is considering the need to rebuild its library/city hall complex from scratch, possibly within the next five years. The project may require a bond issue. Heinz now says it is likely they'll look at construction in 2010. They could begin an architectural/engineering selection process as early as late 2009.

Castle Rock's 2009 capital improvement budget included funding to begin work toward design and construction of a new Coachline fire station. Wayne reports that the Town subsequently determined that it will not require a new station in this area, so the project has been deleted from the program.

We reported on this project last spring. It calls for renovations to the library. Ken reports that the project was given the "green light" for this year and he expects to issue an RFP within the next several weeks or few months. They plan to limit the RFP to a selected group of firms.
Previously, Mark reported that Frisco plans to advertise in the early spring of 2009 for design/build services for some housing on town-owned land. He now says they still plan an RFQ/RFP this spring.

The Better Denver bond program includes a project to complete improvements to the Studio theater and rehearsal lofts at the Denver Performing Arts Complex. The current schedule indicates release of a design RFP in May. We have not yet obtained the name of a project manager.

This Better Denver bond project provides for the renovation of historic features at Civic Center Park, including the Greek Theater, the Voorhies Memorial and Broadway Terrace. The schedule indicates an RFP for design of the Greek Theatre in February, with construction beginning in 2010. The cost estimate for all three Civic Center improvements is $9,833,000. We have not yet been able to obtain the name of a project manager.

The Better Denver bond program includes funding for a new fire station at Lowry. The project will build a new fire station at the southern end of Lowry to meet response times for both Windsor Gardens and the Breaker?s complex.?A design RFP should be issued very soon. We have not been able to obtain the name of a project manager.

The Better Denver bond program provides $37,470,000 for three new branch libraries, one of which is planned at Stapleton. A design RFP should be issued within the next month or two for the Stapleton branch. We do not have a project manager's name for this project.
We reported on this project previously. The City plans to issue an RFP, now scheduled in February, for architecture/design of an addition to the Utilities Service Center.

As we reported previously, the University of Colorado Denver plans to design and construct a new 76,000 sf health and wellness center. Mike reports that, even though funding is available through other sources, they have to get approval from the state to spend the money. He hopes to receive the approval in May, at which time they'll begin an architectural/engineering selection process.

We reported on this project previously. Mike now says the University of Colorado Denver expects to issue an architectural/engineering RFQ within the next week or two for the renovation of Building 402 (an old barracks building) at Fitzsimons. The project manager is Dan Shomers.

We reported on this project previously. Mark now says the staff is working on the RFQ and he expects to issue it soon for architectural/engineering services for reconstruction of Berndt Hall for the Geology/Physics/Engineering Departments.

This project will restore the Voorhies Memorial at Civic Center Park. The current schedule indicates a February design RFP. The cost estimate for all Civic Center restorations (this one plus the Greek Theatre and Broadway Terrace) is $9,833,000. We do not yet have a project manager's name.

The City's bond program includes funding for new restrooms at various parks: Berkeley, Sloan's Lake, City Park, Bible Park South, Garland Park, Rosamond Park, Ruby Hill Park and Skate Park. These projects may be packaged together for design. The current schedule indicates one or more design RFPs will be issued late this spring. We have not been able to obtain a project manager's name.

The City of Alamosa has included in its long-range plan a project to complete a new fire station and training facility. The timing is uncertain. Fire Chief Don Chapman reports that the City will need to secure grants or other funding to move forward with the project.

records.Project: Phase II and Phase III Bond Projects
records.Description: Boulder Valley Schools plans to advertise within the next month or so for architectural/engineering qualifications for the projects remaining in Phase II of its current bond program, and for all Phase III projects. These projects listed individually in our "CIP Directory" report that was posted to our website on January 30. From the Main Menu, select Query Reports. On the Search page, under "Agency," enter Boulder Valley, and under Date Modified, select "On" and enter (or select from the pop-up calendar) 01/30/2009.
Castle Rock's 2009 capital improvement budget includes funding for an addition/renovation Fire Station #155. Wayne reports that the Town plans to sole source the design for this project.

Marlene reports that the County has applied for grant funding that, if received, will provide for a project to complete about two miles of gravity sewer line and an associated lift station. She expects to find out in March whether or not they'll receive the grant and, if they do, whether it will be enough to fund the project.

The City's current capital plan includes proposed funding beginning in 2010 to complete Phase IV improvements at City Park. The City is accumulating funds to begin the master plan for the northern court game complex. Phase IV will consist primarily of court games such as basketball, volleyball, in-line hockey and tennis. Additional features include a playground, landscaping, parking and picnic shelters. Expenditures are estimated at $122,000 in 2010, $400,000 in 2011, $500,000 in 2012 and $500,000 in 2013.
This project will design and construct the rebuild of this lift station.
The County plans to construct a contemporary "Visitors Center" under the existing south tower of the Sheriff's Detention Services Section.
The City plans to develop the East Side Park and Ride in 2012.

As the population of Castle Rock grows, the Town's water supply needs to grow to meet the increasing demand. The current plan is to drill a wellfield every other year and equip it in the year in between. This schedule may be revised as demand changes with population. Current expenditures are estimated at $1.5 million in 2009, $2 million in 2010, $1.5 million in 2011, $2 million in 2012 and $1.5 million in 2013.

Studies completed by warehouse professionals report that, once a warehouse reaches 85% capacity, damage, loss of inventory and reduced productivity become evident. The Metro District anticipates that additional storage space wil be required in the future as various capital projects are completed. This project provides for an expansion of the District's warehousing facilities.

The County passed a tax measure (1A) in November of 2006, which provided a funding mechanism for capital projects over several years. A new pretrial holding facility for the Sheriff's Department is now expected to be initiated within the next couple of years. The cost estimate shown here is from 2007.

This unfunded project would construct a multi-level parking structure for approximately 400 vehicles at the northwest corner of Kimbark and 3rd Avenue. The redevelopment of downtown has increased the need for additional parking.

The Solids Management Facilities Study Update found that the Dissolved Air Flotation (DAF) system needs rehabilitation and expansion. Waste activated sludge (WAS) taken from the secondary clarifiers is thickened from apprximately 1% to 4% in the DAF process. The DAF system will be expanded to process increased WAS solids in the future. Current loadings indicate that this expansion will be required around 2013.
The City's capital plan includes proposed funding for a new West Steamboat Public Safety Building to house firefighter staff and a Police Department substatiion.

This unfunded project will include a new DTR (digital trunked radio) site at Sunset Park, additional DTR upgrade to several surrounding sites, connection to the State DTR system, and adding DTR base stations to the Longmont 911 Communications Center.

This project, currently unfunded, provides for design and construction of two neighborhood parks per year. These parks will be provided in accordance with the Parks, Recreation and Trails Master Plan.

This unfunded project calls for a Downtown Transportation Station (DTTS), a multi-modal facility that will serve the fixed-route service, future rail service, and regional express bus service. Transit Services has $3.5 million available from FTA funds toward the total cost of $16 million.

This unfunded project, which is considered a high priority, includes building a new Transportation Engineering Facility to house the signal, sign, and pavement marking operations. This includes a 30,000 sf facility with parking and outside storage areas. The current 50-year old building is operationally and conditionally obsolete.
This unfunded project would design, build, and equip a new fire station in the vicinity of Sandstone Ranch.

This project will fund Phase II development on the east side of the Loveland Sports Park, to include additional multi-purpose sports fields, restroom/shelter building, parking areas and site amenities. The City's capital plan includes funding in 2016 for the design and in 2017 for construction.
This project provides for expansion of the parking areas at the Civic Center complex.
The City's future plans include a remodel of the police services building. It is currently undetermined when funding will be available.
The County plans to renovate the extension building at the fairgrounds.

The second phase of projects to be funded by the bond passed in 2006 includes improvements at Bear Creek Elementary, a 39,549 sf facility located at 2500 Table Mesa Drive in Boulder. Improvements will include interior expansion and remodels, technology upgrades, plus exterior improvements such as playground improvements and drainage upgrades. They expect to advertise soon to prequalify a/e firms.

The District's 2006 bond program included funding to complete improvements at Coal Creek Elementary. The 51,036 sf facilities is located at 801 West Tamarisk Street in Louisville. As part of Phase III, the project will include: Intercom, ventilation and interior finish improvements; irrigation system upgrades; special education spaces; small group instructional spaces; additional office space; cafeteria enlargement and kitchen upgrade; instrumental music expansion; art room expansion; play area improvements; and technology upgrades. Within the next few weeks, the District will advertise to prequalify architects for all phase 3 projects.

One of the bond-funded projects approved by voters in 2006 will complete improvements at Creekside at Martin Park Elementary, a 50,993 sf facility located at 3470 Martin Drive in Boulder. Improvements will include interior expansions and remodels, technology upgrades, playground and drainage improvements, and electrical and mechanical upgrades. The project is part of Phase II. They expect to advertise soon to prequalify a/e firms.

This project will complete improvements at the 51,269 sf Douglass Elementary school. The project will be funded through the bond passed by voters in 2006. This Phase III project will include: communication system, ventilation, electrical and other interior improvements; irrigation system upgrades; special education spaces; small group instructional spaces; additional office space; a new elevator; outdoor/play area improvements; and technology upgrades. The District already initiated the playground portion of the project. Within the next few weeks, the District will advertise to prequalify architects for all phase 3 projects.

The District plans to complete improvements to the 58,889 sf Fireside Elementary as part of Phase III of the bond program approved by voters in 2006. Improvements will include: Communication system, ventilation, electrical and other interior upgrades; special education spaces; small group instructional spaces; additional office space; a new elevator; outdoor/play area improvements; and technology upgrades. Within the next few weeks, the District will advertise to prequalify architects for all phase III projects.

The District plans improvements at this 45,786 sf elementary school, located at 1575 Lehigh Street in Boulder. The project will be completed as part of Phase II of the bond program approved by voters in 2006. The project will include communication system improvements, ventilation, irrigation, electrical service, interior finish upgrades, a new gymnasium, additional office space, additional classrooms, a new computer lab, an art room expansion, special education space, outdoor/play area improvements and technology upgrades. Phase II consultant prequalification is scheduled to begin in the next few weeks.

This project will complete improvements at the Barnard D. Ryan Elementary School, located at 1405 Centaur Village Drive in Lafayette. The existing school is a 49,176 sf facility. This Phase III project will include: Communication system, ventilation, electrical and other interior upgrades; irrigation system upgrades; special education spaces; small group instruction spaces; additional office space; cafeteria enlargement and kitchen upgrade; instrumental music expansion; art room expansion; outdoor/play area improvements (previously started); and technology upgrades. The District plans an RFQ within the next few weeks to prequalify architects for all phase III projects.

As we reported previously, this project will complete improvements at the 49,887 sf Alicia Sanchez Elementary School at 655 Sir Galahad Drive in Lafayette, as part of Phase II of the 2006 bond program approved by voters. Improvements will include intercom and fire alarm systems, ventilation, irrigation, special education spaces, small group instructional spaces, additional office space, cafeteria and kitchen enlargement and upgrade, instrumental music expansion, art room expansion, play area improvements and technology upgrades. A/E prequalification is scheduled to begin within the next few weeks.

The District plans improvements at the 63,500 sf Superior Elementary School, located at 1800 South Indiana Street. This Phase III project will include: HVAC upgrades; site irrigation and exterior masonry improvements; cafeteria enlargement; play area improvements; and technology upgrades. The District plans an RFQ within the next few weeks to prequalify architects for all phase III projects.

As part of Phase III of the bond program approved by voters in 2006, the District plans improvements at the 114,478 Aspen Creek K-8 school, located at 5500 Aspen Creek Drive in Broomfield. Improvements will include: HVAC upgrades; acoustical improvements in gyms; literacy improvements, special education improvements, curbing and drainage; outdoor play area improvements; and technology upgrades. The District plans to advertise within the next few weeks to prequalify architects for all phase III projects.

The District plans to complete improvements at the 114,478 sf Eldorado K-8 School, located at 3351 Indiana Street in Superior. This Phase III project will include: HVAC and acoustical improvements; literacy improvements; special education spaces; site/play area improvements, curbing and drainage; and technology upgrades. Within the next few weeks, the District will advertise to prequalify architects for all phase III projects.

This project will complete improvements at the 29,350 Horizons K-8 charter school, on the Burke Campus at 4545 Sioux Drive in Boulder. This Phase III project will include: Communication system, ventilation, electrical and other interior upgrades; kndergarten improvements; new science labs; new art and music rooms; gym/cafeteria expansion; computer lab expansion; IMC addition; office additions; outdoor/play area improvements; and technology upgrades. (The final determination of overall campus improvements will be determined as the facility master plan is completed.) Within the next few weeks, the District will advertise to prequalify architects for all phase III projects.

The District plans to complete improvements at the 121,676 sf Angevine Middle School, as part of Phase III of the school bond program approved by voters in 2006. Improvements will include: Communication system, irrigation, asphalt and concrete improvements; special education spaces; small group instructional spaces; additional office spaces; improved field drainage; and technology upgrades. The District plans to advertise within the next few weeks to pre-qualify architects for all Phase III projects.

This project will complete improvements at Broomfield Heights Middle School, a 107,385 sf facility located at 1555 Daphne Street in Broomfield. As part of Phase III of the program, the project will include: Intercom, fire alarm, roof and interior finish improvements; music and art room additions and remodels; gym/stage addition; classroom renovations; administration expansion; special education space, kitchen/cafeteria improvements; playfield improvements; and technology upgrades. Within the next few weeks, the District will advertise to prequalify architects for all phase III projects.

The District plans to complete improvements at the 101,008 sf Centennial Middle School, as part of Phase III of the bond program approved by voters in 2006. The project will include: HVAC, intercom, roof, restroom, site irrigation, interior and exterior improvements; a new main gym and locker rooms; upgraded science labs; an art room upgrade; basketball courts and bleachers; and technology upgrades. Within the next few weeks, the District will advertise to prequalify architects for all phase III projects.

The District plans to complete improvements at the 228,827 sf Monarch High School, located at 329 Campus Drive in Louisville. This Phase III project will include: irrigation system upgrades; external wall repairs; additional classroom space; cafeteria enlargement; restroom facilities at the sports complex; utility service extensions to the sports complex; and technology upgrades. Within the next few weeks, the District will advertise to prequalify architects for all phase III projects.

As part of the bond program approved by voters in 2006, the District plans to complete improvements at Nederland Middle/Senior High School, a 97,081 sf facility located at 597 County Road 130 in Nederland. Athletic improvements were initiated as part of Phase I. Building expansion and remodels, technology improvements, electrical and mechanical and other upgrades are part of Phase II, for which consultant prequalification is scheduled to begin in the next few weeks.

This project will complete improvements at the 76,805 sf New Vista High School, located at 700 20th Street in Boulder. This Phase III project will include: HVAC, communication system, electrical and other interior improvements; special education spaces; additional classrooms; additional office space; additional computer labs; additional storage space; site irrigation; and technology upgrades. The District plans an RFQ within the next few weeks to prequalify architects for all phase III projects.

As part of the bond program approved by voters in 2006, the District plans improvements at the Education Center, located at 6500 Arapahoe Road in Boulder. This Phase III project will include: Electrical and BAS control system improvements; and IT/technology upgrades. Within the next few weeks, the District will advertise to prequalify architects for all phase III projects.

This project is currently considered a "high priority unfunded" project. It will complete a new facility in the northern area of the city for Streets, Parks & Recreation and Cultural Facilities and Fleet operations.

This project will replace the single-ply roof on the Sheriff's office building. In 2012, the roof will be 20 years old. Given the type of roof, EDPM, it will be at the end of its normal life span. The project may be budgeted over a two-year period.
This project provides for covering the southern bank of five tennis courts at the city park tennis complex with an all-weather steel building.

records.Project: Tennis Clubhouse Renov, Restrm, Stone Seat
records.Description: This project will provide for renovation of the existing Tennis Clubhouse building adjacent to the 17 court complex in City Park, at 800 Goodnight Avenue. This includes restroom renovation, interior remodeling, and stabilization of historic stone seating amenity.
Western State College requested $3,214,968 for the 2008-09 fiscal year for renovation of Quigley Hall. The project was not funded. The latest prediction is that it may begin in 2010 or 2011.
This unfunded project would provide for a Fire Administration office building, with backup EOC (Emergency Operations Center) and Dispatch on the south end of the property at 11th and Terry Streets.
This project provides for a remodel of the front lobby at City Hall.
The City would like to replace the automated fueling systems at 11 locations. The project is currently unfunded.
This project provides for Southeast Community Park improvements at the existing park site, located at the northwest corner of Powers Boulevard and Drennan Road. It is currently unfunded.
This project would complete improvements at the Tutt Sports Complex. The project is currently on the list of "high priority unfunded" projects.
The City would like to complete pedestrian/bicycle ramps, lanes, sidewalks and retaining walls along West Uintah. At this time, the project is on the "high priority" unfunded list.

This project would complete a new fixed route service contractor office building for Transit. A NEPA process will be required. The facility would be about 9,000 square feet with parking for approximately 100 employee vehicles. The project is currently unfunded but considered a "high priority."
This project would replace car wash facilities in the Police Operations Center and Falcon substation facilities. It is currently unfunded.

Phase III of this project calls for restoration of the ranch house and barn restoration for environmental education classroom and/or other approriate uses, fencing, interpretative center, and a soft-surface trail around the hay meadow.

The Better Denver bond program includes a project to design and construct a new Human Services Office on the east side of the city. The project will construct a new 51,375 square foot office building on a to-be-acquired site for the Department's Eastside facility (Five Points Community Center).? The current office is too small and functionally obsolete to provide services? including TANF eligibility and case management.

This project is part of Phase II of the 2006 bond program, scheduled to begin in early 2009. Improvements at this school will include interior expansions and renovations, electrical and mechanical upgrades, exterior improvements such as playgrounds and drainage, and technology updates. Consultant prequalification is scheduled to begin in the next few weeks.

The City has an opportunity to construct a new community building on the north side of Fairgrounds Park and tie it into the continued development in the downtown area. The project assumes a size of 16,000 sf.
An additional fire station is scheduled to open on the east side of I-25. The new station will also be designed to function as a secondary emergency management center.
This project involves construction of various types of facilities at the Swift Gulch site and the Traer Creek Village site, mostly for transit and public works maintenance facilities.
This project will construct a new tank adjacent to existing Tank 3B, to serve the Purple Zone.
This project will construct a new tank adjacent to existing Tank 11B to serve the Purple Zone.

This project will replace corroded roof rafters, add additional roof vents, and sandblast, prime and paint the interior of the existing 6 million gallon water tank located along Highway 66 east of Lyons.

The proposed booking improvements will increase the capacity with three additional holding cells (744 sf) and three additional suicide observation (S.O.) cells (213 sf). The gym expansion will construct an additional 50 beds in an open dormitory 2-story housing design.

This project would renovate 531 White, adjacent to the Mesa County Courthouse, for reuse as additional offices for various county needs. Included are HVAC upgrade, elevator for 2nd floor access, and office construction.
This project would design exterior restrooms for use by Colorado Highway 65 visitors year round, and allow for additional restrooms for Mesa community functions.
This project provides for a tournament pavilion at the Haymaker Golf Course.

Using funding from the 2007 bond program, the Museum plans to construct a 100,000 square-foot extension on the south side of the current museum building to house a science education center (classrooms, labs, teacher education center) and artifact collections facility. The addition is intended to be highly energy efficient and will pursue appropriate LEED certification.

The City's capital plan includes proposed funding in 2010 and 2011 to complete maintenance building improvements at Olde Golf Course. Expenditures are estimated at $250,000 in 2010 and $350,000 in 2011.
The City plans to complete clubhouse improvements at Olde Golf Course. Expenditures are estimated at $150,000 in 2014, $500,000 in 2015 and $2,150,000 in 2016.

records.Project: Filter Plant 2 Filter Under Drain Repl's
records.Description: This project provides for design and construction of Filter Plant 2 under drain replacements at the rate of two filters per year, at the water treatment plant. Expenditures are estimated at $257,500 in 2010, $159,140 in 2011, $163,910 in 2012 and $168,830 in 2013.

The City's capital plan includes funding for design and SDC of Filter Plant 1 demolition at the water treatment plant. A cost estimate in 2012 of $708,000 includes the demolition plus the design of de-chlorination improvements.
The City's capital plan includes proposed funding for design and construction of de-chlorination improvements at the water treatment plant.

The City budgets funds each year for ongoing maintenance of water treatment facilities, to include renovations, renewal or replacement of facilities, equipment and infrastructure. Improvements may include: isolation line valves and pipeline repairs on the raw water supply system; clear well final chemical treatment and metering; backwash pond repairs; roof, heating and cooling and security system replacements; instrumentation and computer control system replacements; finished water pump station pump replacements; and water quality lab test instrument replacement. Some or all of the projects may be designed in-house or using on-call contracts.
The County's capital plan proposes funding in 2012 for a new west administration building in Rifle.
This project provides for a cover warm-up arena/livestock pavilion at the fairgrounds.

records.Project: Replace Seating in North End Grd Stands
records.Description: This project will replace the seating in the north end grand stands at the fairgrounds.

This project is for site improvements and design and construction of a firefighting simulator/burn building at the existing Fire Department Training facility at 3851 Elk Drive or an alternate site if necessary. Site improvements include the addition of a fire hydrant, extension of the concrete slab area and adding electricity. The new simulator will be added to the existing five story training tower, and will be equipped with two burn rooms, roof chop outs, forcible entry simulator, smoke distribution system and movable maze partition panels. The current capital plan allocates $297,000 toward the total cost of the project.
The City's capital plan includes future funding for water tank improvements. Expenditures are estimated at $1,928,000 in 2012 and $1,774,000 in 2013.

The City has programmed funding in several future years for municipal facility improvements. Specific projects will be identified and prioritized for those years when they get closer. Expenditures are estimated at $500,000 in 2012, $500,000 in 2014, $300,000 in 2015 and $1 million in 2017.
The City's capital plan anticipates expenditures over seven years for water quality/plant improvements. Expenditures are estimated at $600,000 in 2012 and $500,000 per year from 2013 through 2018.
The Town has programmed funding in 2012 for a new elevated water storage tank.

records.Project: Lift Station ST Fixed Asset Repl. Schedule
records.Description: Metro's capital plan includes a project called "lift station short-term fixed asset replacement schedule." The project allocates funding in 2011 for lift station replacement.
This project provides for phase III rehabilitation of the north secondary treatment facility.
Metro schedules central treatment plant/solids facility plan updates every five years. They anticipate expenditures of $1.2 million for a 2012-13 update and another $1.2 million for a 2017-18 update.
The County's capital plan includes funding from 2010-2012 for a snow removal equipment storage building.

This project provides for a complete remodel of Aurora Hills Middle School, to include roof replacement and building renewal. The current schedule indicates an a/e consultant selection in the fall of 2009. The District plans to use the construction manager/general contractor delivery method, so will select a cm/gc firm in early 2010.

The District's bond program includes a project to build a two-classroom addition to the Virginia Court Elementary, plus complete building renewal. The schedule indicates an a/e consultant selection in late 2011.
After land has been acquired (scheduled in 2009), this project will design and construct a new public safety building on the Klein parcel.

records.Project: East Side Parking at Walton Creek
records.Description: The proposed project will provide 60 parking spaces and a restroom facility to the Walton Creek Road and US HW 40 core trail area as well as an additional city park-and-ride area.

This project will construct a new city hall on the city-owned parking lot site adjacent to the existing city hall. This will include 40,000 sf of finished space and a full basement for storage. Additional funding will be needed beyond 2013.
This project provides design development for the next phase of the Howelsen Ice Arena expansion project to include an expanded lobby, office, and locker room space.
This project will complete the restoration of the historic Legacy Ranch and barn for educational uses, and install fencing and soft-surface trails around the hay meadow.
The District's long-term plan anticipates a major remodel of Fire Station #1 in 2012 or 2013.
This project provides for a major remodel of Fire Station #4. The District would like to initiate this project in 2012 or 2013.

The District's strategic plan includes a proposed new Sheridan branch library. The current branch is housed at Sheridan High School, where it is virtually undetected by the general populace. The space is limited and the furnishings are over 20 years old and in need of replacement. The District has purchased a 2-acre parcel at the edge of the Fort Logan facility. It is unknown when they may be able to design and construct a new facility.

This project provides for a new Kelver branch library. The current branch is housed in a modular building on land leased from the Byers School District. The Library District has been exploring any opportunities to receive land dedication from developers, and will continue to pursue options.

The District's long-term plans include a new Davies branch library building. The current Davies branch occupies uner 2,000 square feet at Deer Trail School. In 2000, the Library District purchased a small piece of property one block from the current location, with the intent to locate a new library there someday.
This project provides funding for upgrades and remodeling of the existing Fruita police building.
This park development project provides for a maintenance facility, scoreboards, a new P.A. system and other upgrades.
This project provides for reservoir and spillway improvements at Reservoir #3,
The City's long-term plan includes a project to build a new city shops facility. The project is anticipated beyond the current five-year planning period.
The Town's capital plan anticipates a new 3 million gallon water storage tank in 2013.
The Town's capital plan includes proposed funding in 2013 for a new water treatment plant expansion.
This project provides for an aerobic digester #2 at the wastewater treatment plant.
The City's capital plan includes proposed funding in 2010 for improvements at the south lift station.
The City's capital plan proposes funding from 2010 through 2012 for sewer lift station expansion.

The District would like to pursue a library in Lone Tree. They were hoping the County would pass a funding measure on November 4 but, alas, it failed. Consequently, the library project is on hold. Jamie says that, during 2009, the District will work on figuring out what to do going forward. Since they have gone to voters twice without success, they probably won't try again for at least two years. We'll continue to monitor their plans.

We reported previously that the Airport planned to seek architectural services this fall for Phase III of terminal reconstruction/expansion. Dave now says the RFP should be out within the next few weeks for an architect and program manager.

This project provides for improvements at the 44,714 sf Birch Elementary School, as part of the bond program approved by voters in 2006. The school is located at 1035 Birch Street in Broomfield. Improvements will include: Interior renovations and expansion; technology, electrical and mechanical upgrades; and playground, drainage and other exterior improvements. The project is part of Phase II. They expect to advertise this week to prequalify a/e firms.

Eisenhower Elementary will be upgraded/improved as part of the bond program approved by voters in 2006. The 53,647 sf school is located at 1220 Eisenhower Drive in Boulder. The District plans interior expansions and remodels, technology upgrades, electrical and mechanical improvements, and exterior improvements such as playgrounds and drainage. The project is part of Phase II. Consultant prequalification is scheduled to begin the first week of December.

The 56,300 sf Emerald Elementary school at 755 W. Elmhurst Place in Broomfield will be improved as part of the bond program funded by voters in 2006. Improvements will include fire alarm replacement, HVAC, an art room addition, special education space, offices and health room, exterior upgrades and technology improvements. The project is part of Phase II of the program. They expect to advertise this week to prequalify a/e firms.

As we reported previously, this project provides for improvements at the 3,316 sf Gold Hill Elementary school, as part of Phase II of the bond program approved by voters in 2006. This phase is scheduled to begin in early 2009. Improvements will include electrical, roof replacement, interior finishes/upgrades, classroom improvements, library/lunch room renovation, outdoor/play area improvements and technology upgrades. Landscaping improvements were completed as part of Phase I. A/E prequalification for Phase II is scheduled to begin this week.

As we reported previously, the District plans to complete improvements at the 52,016 sf Heatherwood Elementary, located at 7750 Concord Drive in Boulder, as part of the bond program approved by voters in 2006. This Phase II project will include communication system improvements, irrigation system upgrades, electrical & fire sprinkler system, new special education spaces, group instructional space, staff office space additions, a computer lab addition, kindergarten area reconfiguration, art and music addition, outdoor/play area improvements and technology upgrades. Phase II a/e prequalification is scheduled to begin the first week of December.

As we reported previously, this project will complete improvements at the 5,030 sf Jamestown Elementary, as part of the bond program approved by voters in 2006. This Phase II project will include electrical service improvements, roof replacement/repairs, interior finish upgrades, site drainage improvements, exterior/play area improvements and technology upgrades. Phase II consultant prequalification is scheduled to begin this week.

As we reported previously, the District plans improvements at Kohl Elementary school, as part of Phase II of the bond program approved by voters in 2006. The 54,113 sf facility is located at 1000 West 10th Avenue in Broomfield. Improvements will include HVAC, roof replacement/repairs, restroom renovations, site irrigation, paving replacement/repair, special education improvements, art room relocation, new cafeteria and kitchen facilities, small group instruction spaces, new administrative spaces, exterior/play area improvements and technology upgrades. Phase II project prequalification is scheduled to begin this week.

As we reported previously, the District plans improvements at Louisville Elementary School, as part of the bond program approved by voters in 2006. The existing school is a 58,458 sf facility located at 400 Hutchinson Street in Louisville. Improvements will include added and renovated space, other interior improvements such as electrical and mechanical and technology, and exterior upgrades such as playgrounds and drainage. This is a Phase II project, for which a/e prequalification is scheduled to begin this week.

This project will complete improvements at Nederland Elementary School, located at #1 N. Sundown Trail. The existing school is a 61,470 sf facility. The Phase II project will include: Exterior concrete, asphalt, stair and other improvements; parking and drop-off areas; playground improvements; and technology upgrades. Consultant prequalification is scheduled to begin this week.

As we reported previously, this project provides for improvements and upgrades at University Hill Elementary School, located at 956 16th Street in Boulder. The school is a 52,962 sf facility. The project, part of Phase II, will include: HVAC, electrical, fire alarm, intercom, security and clock system improvements; roof replacement; site irrigation improvements; new administrative offices; art and music facilities; small group instructional spaces; outdoor/play area improvements; and technology upgrades. Phase II consultant prequalification is scheduled to begin this first week of December.

As part of Phase II of the bond program approved by voters in 2006, the District plans improvements at the 35,123 sf Whittier Elementary School, located at 2008 Pine Street in Boulder. The project will include: Intercom, electrical, HVAC, and interior finish upgrades; art and music classroom addition; kindergarten classroom additions; gym and stage expansion; a computer lab; administration office expansion; kitchen/storage improvements; outdoor/play area improvements; and technology upgrades. Consultant prequalification for Phase II projects is scheduled to begin this first week of December.

We reported on this project previously. Fruita voters passed a bond on November 4 to finance a new recreation center. The City previously contracted with a firm to help them through the initial project phases and to get them through the bond vote process. Ken says they're still evaluating contracting options, but he says they'll most likely send out an RFP in early 2009 for a design/build contract.
Dave reported previously that he hoped to issue an RFP this year for new general aviation hangars. He now says a developer RFP should go out sometime in the spring of 2009.

Colorado State University at Pueblo advertised in May for architectural/engineering services for the remodel of the Academic Resources Center. In October, Geraldine reported that the University expected to advertise in six to nine months for construction management/general contractor services for this project. This still appears to be the anticipated schedule.

In October, Scott reported that it was possible the City would seek architectural services in 2009 for the remodel of a historic building to house the customer service department. He now says the project will move forward and he expects to release an RFP for architectural services sometime during the first quarter of the new year.

The University of Colorado Denver hopes to design and construct a new architecture and planning building. They hired RNL Design to complete some planning and predesign. The next step will be to advertise for architectural/engineering final design services. Mike reports that the project is on hold pending fund raising.

The District may build some weather shelters at Indian Tree in 2009. Marshall says he doesn't know yet whether or not they'll need some architectual assistance with these. The total budget is only $24,000.

Erie may seek consulting services sometime in 2009 for design of a water line segment and inlet structures. Kris did not have further information on the project or schedule at this time. We'll follow up.
In the next few weeks, Arapahoe County plans to advertise for construction management/general contractor services for the District Attorney's office tenant improvement project.

The Longmont Downtown Development Authority has received an economic stimulus grant for a facade improvement project. Mary indicates that the LDDA needs design ideas for this project. Interested firms are invited to contact her.
The Aspen School District passed a bond on November 4 for new employee housing. Angela reports that they'll issue an RFP for architectural/engineering services within the next few weeks.

Bill reports that Sterling plans to advertise soon for an airport consultant. He wasn't sure exactly how or when they would advertise, but said he's concerned about getting inundated with qualifications and wanted to emphasize they're only interested in hearing from firms with specific related experience and expertise with airports.
records.Type: AS, DR, MS, PL, ST, TR

records.Description: The Facility Planning, Construction, and Maintenance department is currently reviewing pre-qualification statements from interested architectural and consultant firms for the 2008 Bond Fund projects. Submitted information should include company history, a financial statement, employee history and completed projects, (i.e. design and completion costs including project owner and contact). This information will be reviewed and selected firms will be notified. Submitted information should be sent to: Mike Langlett, Executive Director of Educational Support Services, Cherry Creek School District No. 5, 4700 S. Yosemite Street, Greenwood Village, CO 80111.

Previously, the District planned to advertise in about February for architectural/engineering services for its second phase of projects in the current bond program. Lori now informs us they plan to advertise this week to prequalify firms for Phase II. They'll advertise on their website and in the Daily Journal and will send notices to firms that have expressed an interest. The specific projects to be included in Phase II are listed separately in this Update.

As we reported in August, the City's capital plan includes proposed funding beginning in 2009 for a new biosolids digester at the wastewater treatment plant. Douglas reported that he expected to release an RFP later in the fall of this year for a study to precede design and construction. He now says they're still on track for an RFP in October or November. We do not have a cost estimate for the study. Design costs are estimated at $850,000 in the capital plan.

The Adams 12 Board voted to move forward with an $80 million bond issue on the November ballot. Henry reports that the project list includes one new elementary school plus renewal and replacement projects at most schools, to include a lot of mechanical upgrades and some architectural work. They typically wait until after the vote to select consultants, but went ahead with the new elementary to meet the needed schedule. Henry says that, for other projects, they could decide to go back to the architectural firms that either designed the original buildings or the most recent renovations. No decision has yet been made on the approach.

We last reported on this project in February. CU previously hired consultants for the programming phase for an expansion of the aerospace engineering building of 72,000 gsf. They'll complete a new selection process for the design phase. Phil says if the severance tax passes on mineral leases and funding is designated for higher education, they could begin the selection process as soon as April of 2009.

We reported on this project previously Carl now says he expects the District will issue an RFP soon for preliminary design of a small hydro power project at Carter Lake. The project could lead to a full design contract for the selected firm.

We reported on this project previously. The Housing Authority plans to release an RFP for architectural services and, potentially, a joint venture with a developer, for redevelopment of Park Avenue Block 5B. Ryan now says they'll put out one or more design RFPs before the end of the year for design of Block 5B improvements.

We reported previously that Littleton planned to initiate an RFP process to design a small facility (approximately 1,500 to 2,000 square feet) to store evidence for the Police Department. In August, Phil indicated that the City Manager had discussed some options with City Council. At this point he says they're not ready to move forward. We'll continue to monintor progress.

This district will place a $125 million bond on the November ballot, to include a new high school, two new elementaries and various other items. They previously advertised for and selected an architect for the high school. Ranette Jordan (303-655-2973) reports that they will not have a complete list of the other projects until November and will not begin additional consultant selections until then.

The District plans to place a $203 million bond issue on the November, 2008 ballot. If it passes, the projects to be completed will include three new elementaries. Elementary #41 ($15.2M) would be scheduled to open in 2010; elementary #42 ($15.8M) in 2011; and elementary #43 ($16.9M) in 2011-2012. One of the schools may be an East Area magnet/focus school, possibly with different grade configurations. Mike is not yet able to provide schedule information for a/e or other consultant selections.

If the District is successful in passing a $203 million bond in November, the program will include $35.04 million for upgrades to 13 older facilities including 9 prototypes constructed during the 1970s. The 13 schools are: Arrowhead, Cimarron, Cottonwood, Heritage, High Plains, Homestead, Independence, Meadow Point, Mission Viejo, Ponderosa, Sagebrush, Trails West and Willow Creek. The program also includes $5.79 million for electrical/fire/HVAC and plumbing upgrades at elementaries. Mike is not yet able to provide schedule information for a/e or other consultant selections.

If the District is successful in passing a $203 million bond in November, it plans to build a science, math and technology program facility adjacent to Prairie Middle School. The facility is scheduled to open in 2011. Mike is not yet able to provide schedule information for a/e or other consultant selections.

The District plans to place a $203 million bond on the November ballot. If it passes, they plan renovations and remodels at Campus Middle School ($8.6M) and West Middle School ($11M). In addition, they'll complete various electrical, fire, HVAC and plumbing renovations at middle schools. Mike is not yet able to provide schedule information for a/e or other consultant selections.

The District hopes to pass a $203.55 million bond in November. If successful, the program include $3 million for design of a new high school. Mike is not yet able to provide schedule information for a/e or other consultant selections.

If the District is successful in passing a $203.55 million bond in November, the program will include $5.6 million for Overland High School (HVAC, boilers, windows, electrical and plumbing), $7.93 million for Smoky Hill High School (upgrades to technology and pool replacement), plus $9.49 million for electrcial, fire, HVAC and plumbing improvements at high schools. Mike is not yet able to provide schedule information for a/e or other consultant selections.

If the District is successful in passing a $203.55 million bond in November, one of the projects they would like to pursue is a new facility for student support programs, a student achievement resource center, Information Systems department, east area admissions office, district athletic/activities area and Special Education offices. Mike is not yet able to provide schedule information for a/e or other consultant selections.

The District hopes to pass a $203.55 million bond in November. The project list includes Arapahoe Park campus transportation, grounds and maintenance facilities. Mike is not yet able to provide schedule information for a/e or other consultant selections.

The District hopes to pass a $203.55 million bond in November. If successful, they plan to add six SPC classrooms for 9th and 10th grades. Mike is not yet able to provide schedule information for a/e or other consultant selections.

The District plans to place a $203.55 million bond on the November ballot. If it passes, one of the projects they plan to pursue is I-Team remodels of two pre-schools. Mike is not yet able to provide schedule information for a/e or other consultant selections.

We reported on this project previously. Owen now says Fort Collins should advertise an RFP any day for design of water treatment facility improvements. The contract will be for services as needed over a period of five years.

Frisco has just issued an RFP for "Design and Engineering Services for Infrastructure and Facilities at the Town of Frisco's Peninsula Recreation Area." The project will address the following elements: A new free-standing lodge facility; ice rink; tubing hill; BMX/mountain bike park; parking and roadways; and infrastructure. Proposals are due no later than 5:00 Wednesday, November 12. The complete RFP is available at www.townoffrisco.com/business/rfps.html .
