records.Description: Mark reports that the City plans to seek architectural services for historic preservation design at Bromley Farm. Firms will need to be included on the state's list of historic preservation consultants to be considered for this project. An RFP should be issued within the next couple of weeks.

This project is contingent on receipt of a grant. If funding is received, the District will seek architectural services for classroom additions at four to six schools. Mark hopes to hear soon whether or not they'll receive the grant.

The University of Colorado Denver and Health Sciences Center plans to seek architectural services for renovation of the existing Business School building. Mike reports that they're still in a fundraising mode, and it will be at least next spring before they begin an architectural/engineering selection process.

As we reported in a recent Special Update, Aurora Public Schools wil place a $215 million bond on the November ballot. If the bond passes, they plan to build four new schools and complete renovations and other upgrades at a number of other schools. We were unable to reach Amy Spatz before this update, as she's out of the office through this week. We will provide further information as soon as possible about plans for seeking architectural and engineering services for these projects.

This district will attempt to pass a bond in November for two new high schools, a new middle school, two new elementaries, a sports complex and various remodeling projects. They're in the process of selecting a project management firm, which will assist them in the procurement of architectural/engineering and other services, assuming the bond passes.

As we reported previously, Denver Public Schools hopes to pass a $454 million bond in November. Larry Williams says they do not yet have a complete list of projects. The Board will take formal action this week, after which they should have more information available. They also have not yet decided whether or not they'll hire a program management firm. They could decide to hire internal staff to manage the program. We'll follow up.
records.Type: AS, CM, MS, PK, ST, TR, GI

records.Description: Pat reports that the Parks Department is currently evaluating a building to determine whether or not it needs to be replaced. He says he should know within the next few weeks. If it is determined that replacement is necessary, they'll require architectural/engineering services. We'll follow up.

If this district is successful in passing a $49.9 million bond in November, they plan a complete renovation of the existing Cedaredge Elementary School, to include the addition of 16 classrooms plus a new library, a cafeteria attached to the new addition, mechanical and electrical upgrades, and other interior and exterior improvements. Terry says they have not made any final decisions yet about hiring architectural/engineering firms or whether to hire design/build teams. He doesn't expect they'll begin any selection processes before they know the results of the vote.

This district will place a $49.9 million bond issue on the November ballot. If it passes, they plan to complete various improvements at the four high schools (Cedaredge, Delta, Hotchkiss and Paonia), including new mechanical systems, new boilers, painting, new floors, etc. Terry says he does not expect they'll begin any design or construction selections before they know the results of the vote.

This district hopes to pass a $49.9 million bond issue in November. If they're successful, one of the projects they'll complete is to add classrooms and an auxiliary gym, plus other renovations and upgrades, at Delta High School. Terry does not expect the District will begin any architectural/engineering or contractor selections before they know the results of the bond.

The District hopes to pass a $49.9 million bond in November. They have identified various needed improvements at all elementary schools (Cedaredge, Crawford K-8, Delta 6th Grade Building, Lincoln Elementary, Hotchkiss K-8 and Paonia Elementary). Improvements will include mechanical and electrical upgrades, fire alarm systems, interior finishes, restroom improvements, HVAC improvements, roof replacements, parking and sidewalk improvements. They do not expect to begin any architectural/engineering or contractor selections until they know the results of the vote.

As we reported previously, this district plans to place a $203.5 million bond on the November ballot. Mike Langlett reports that he is accepting statements of qualifications from "select firms." We're not sure how exclusive this list is, but interested firms should contact Mike to find out what SOQs they'll accept. Mike also reports that the District does NOT intend to hire a program management firm. He also says he cannot tell us what projects will be included in the first round of architectural/engineering selections. Sorry we can't provide more helpful information. Individual projects are listed separately in this Update.
records.Type: AS, CM, DR, MS, PK, ST

records.Description: Dave Shinneman, Planning Director at Broomfield, says he has nothing specifically identified at this time that will require consultant services, but "you never know," he could need quick turnaround services from architects or other firms for drawings for projects, site plans or the like. He says these selections would be conducted pretty informally. Firms interested in doing these small, short-notice projects might want to contact Dave.
Ryan reports that the Housing Authority plans to issue an RFP within the next 30 days for the Arapahoe Co-Ops project. This project will entail master planning for future redevelopment.

This district plans to place a $350 million bond on the November ballot. The major projects identified in the Alameda neighborhood include the final phase of the master plan for replacement of the high school, building improvements at Deane Elementary, additional at Patterson International and Stein Elementary and a partial renovation and addition at Kendrick Lakes Elementary. Project schedules will not be available until after the vote.

Jeffco Schools hopes to pass a $350 million bond in November. The program includes a number of projects in the Arvada neighborhood. These include: An auxiliary gymnasium addition and renovation at Arvada High Schoool; a building addition and partial remodel of Foster Elementary; various interior an some exterior upgrades at several other elementaries; and technology and other improvements at Arvada and North Arvada Middle Schools. The District does not plan to develop project schedules until after the vote.

The District hopes to pass a $350 million bond in November. The program includes various proposed improvements in the Arvada West neighbhorhood's schools. The largest is an office and classroom addition, interior finishes, classroom technology upgrade and a new roof at Vanderhoof Elementary. Additional security, technology, interior and other improvements are proposed at Allendale, Campbell, Fairmount, Fremont and Stott Elementaries and Drake Middle School. The District plans to develop project schedules after the vote.

Jeffco Schools hopes to pass a $350 million bond in November. The program includes projects at several schools in the Bear Creek neighborhood. The major projects are an addition and renovation, site circulation, building security and classroom technology upgrade at Green Gables Elementary ($2,716,854) and interior finishes, kitchen remodel, building security, playground, classroom technology upgrade at Kendallvue Elementary ($1,452,960). Other remodels, technology upgrades, etc. are planned at Peiffer, Red Rocks and Westgate Elementaries and Carmody Middle School. The District plans to develop project schedules after the vote.

If the District is successful in passing a $350 million bond in November, it plans a number of projects at Chatfield neighborhood schools. The largest will be an administration/cafeteria addition, furniture, fixtures and equipment, building security, classroom technology upgrade and kitchen remodel at Stony Creek Elementary ($3,267,350). A turf field and classroom technology upgrades are planned at Chatfield Sr. High ($933,750) and a remodel and other upgrades at Coronado Elementary. Other improvements will be completed at other schools. The District plans to develop a/e selection schedules after the vote.

If the District is successful in passing a $350 million bond in November, it plans various improvements at Columbine neighborhood schools. The largest will include: An auxiliary gym addition, locker remodel, roofing, turf field, and other upgrades at Columbine High ($7,418,435); and master plan phase I addition/remodel and other upgrades at Ken Caryl Middle ($5,960,674). Various improvements are planned at Columbine Hills, Dutch Creek, Governor's Ranch, Leawood and Normandy Elementaries. The District plans to develop a/e selection schedules after the vote.

The District hopes to pass a $350 million bond in November. If they're successful, they plan to complete improvements at several schools in the Dakota Ridge neighborhood. The largest projects include: A kitchen addition and interior remodel, HVAC upgrade, building security and classroom technology upgrade at Colorow Elementary ($2,497,983); and a turf field, building security and classroom technology upgrades at Dakota Ridge High ($957,485). Security, technology and other upgrades are planned at other schools. The District plans to develop a/e selection schedules after the vote.

If the District is successful in passing a $350 million bond in November, they plan several projects at schools in the Golden area. These include: A partial renovation, interior finishes, windows, security, electrical and technology upgrades at Kyffin Elementary ($769,173); water ditch repair and upgrade at Golden High ($871,500); plus various other improvements at other elementaries and Bell Middle. The District plans to develop a/e selection schedules after the vote.

If the DIstrict is successful in passing a $350 million bond in November, they plan a number of projects in the Green Mountain neighborhood. The largest will be a new elementary school in the Tamarisk area ($13,072,500). Another major project is a kindergarten/office area addition, remodel, site improvements, classroom technology upgrade, windows and building security at Foothills Elementary ($4,672,525). Security, technology and other improvements are planned at several other elementaries. The District plans to develop a/e selection schedules after the vote.

If the District passes a $350 million bond in November, the program will include various projects in the Jefferson neighborhood. Major projects include: $11,007,125 for phase I of the master plan, roofing, heating, ventilating and air conditioning, a turf field, classroom technology upgrades and building security at Jefferson High ($11,007,125); and an addition/remodel, windows, building security and classroom technology upgrade at Edgewater Elementary ($3,749,980). The District plans to develop a/e selection schedules after the vote.

The District hopes to pass a $350 million bond in November. The proposed program includes several projects in the Lakewood neighborhood, including a $2,154,894 project at Eiber Elementary for a classroom addition, interiof finishes, building security, classroom technology, cafeteria expansion/renovation and a roof upgrade. Various smaller projects are planned at other schools. The District plans to develop a/e selection schedules after the vote.

The District hopes to pass a $350 million bond in November. Proposed projects include various improvements in the Pomona neighborhood. The largest include: An auxiliary gym and music addition, turf field, science classroom remodel and classroom technology upgrade at Pomona High ($6,280,403); an administrative addition, interiof finishes, building security, lighting, site improvements and classroom technology upgrades at Parr Elementary ($2,353,724); and a kitchen addition and interior renovation, site improvements, building security and classroom technology upgrade at Zerger Elementary ($3,263,997). The District plans to develop a/e selection schedules after the vote.

The District will place a $350 bond issue on the November ballot. The proposed program includes projects at various schools in the Ralston Valley neighborhood. The largest include: Land acquisition and construction of a new 480-student capacity northwest area elementary ($14,940,000); phase I implementation of the master plan at Oberon Middle ($10M); phase II replacement of classrooms at Sierra Elementary ($9,960,000); and land acquisition for a new northwest area high school ($3M). The District plans to develop a/e selection schedules after the vote.

The District hopes to pass a $350 million bond in November. Standley Lake neighborhood projects will include: Kindergarten/office area/challenge area remodel, security, interiors, kitchen, electrical/plumbing and classroom technology at Witt Elementary ($2,891,049); admin/auxiliary gym addition, HVAC, interior renovation, a turf field, classroom technology upgrade, building security etc. at Standley Lake High ($11,605,167); plus various smaller projects at other schools. The District plans to develop a/e selection schedules after the vote.

If the District passes a $350 million bond in November, Wheat Ridge neighborhood projects will include: A phase II addition/remodel at Wheat Ridge High ($10,582,500); an admin addition/remodel, interior finishes, classroom renovation, windows, kitchen equipment and technology upgrade at Prospect Valley Elementary ($8,121,797); plus smaller projects at other neighborhood schools. The District plans to develop a/e selection schedules after the vote.

If the District passes a $350 million bond in November, it plans over $13 million in improvements at 15 charter schools. The District does not plan to develop a/e selection schedules until after the vote.

If the District passes a $350 million bond in November, it will allocate $28,637,253 to projects at option schools, special schools and programs district-wide. The largest projects include: Replace the Jeffco Open School on the existing site ($11,827,500); replace Long View HS on the existing site ($3,004,225); and remodel, add building security and add a therapy pool at Miller Special ($5,021,125). Various other remodels and upgrades are also included in the program. The District does not plan to develop a/e selection schedules until after the vote.

If the District passes a $350 million bond in November, $30,103,421 will be allocated to mountain schools. Projects will include: Phase II of master plan, classroom technology and building security at Evergreen Middle ($9,975,000); auditorium/auxiliary gym addition, pump house improvements, classroom technology and a teacher work area remodel at Conifer High ($8,406,150); phase II of master plan, building security and technology upgrades at Wilmot Elementary ($4,743,355); a kindergarten addition, roof improvements, windows, security and technology at Marshdale Elementary ($3,388,523); plus other smaller projects.

If the District passes a $350 million bond in November, it plans to allocate $11.75 million to accessibility improvements, abatement due to construction, parking lot paving and classroom relocations to support construction. The District does not plan to develop a/e selection schedules until after the vote.

The District's proposed $350 million bond program includes allocations for various support facility improvements, to include: Colorado Dept. of Health sewer requirements; IT data center capacity improvements; internet expansion/upgrades; network connections and power for classroom technology; Quail Street complex - district-wide facility archives renovation/addition; West Transportation building security; and elevator and HVAC improvements a the Education Center. The District does not plan to develop a/e selection schedules until after the vote.

We last reported on this project in October of 2007. The District had been discussing building a new headquarters facility. It would need to pass a bond or identify other financing to proceed with this project. The District considered putting a bond on the November, 2008 ballot, but has decided not to. We'll continue to follow any progress with this project.

We reported previously that, as part of the $86 million bond program approved by voters in November of 2004, the District planned two new bus transportation facilities. In April, Shannon said they been unsuccessful in acquiring land for such a facility and funding was extremely limited at that point. She encouraged us to keep checking with her and says "one of these days" something will happen. We checked with her for this Update and the status remains essentially the same. They still have no site for the facility, so there's no movement.
records.Type: AS, CM, DR, MS, PK, ST

records.Description: We reported on this project previously. Adams County purchased 95 acres on the east side of E-470, intending to eventually consolidate county offices on that site. The County passed a tax measure (1A) in November, 2006 to help provide funding for the project. The campus will consist of a number of buildings. The administration building is the first one planned. Previously, we suggested that they would seek design services at some point. We must have misunderstood Pat, because he now says they are already working with Gensler as the architect.
records.Type: AS, CM, DR, MS, PK, SW, ST, WR

records.Description: Kris reports that the Town expects to issue an RFP "soon" for this new water storage tank. The project will construct an additional above ground 1.5 million gallon treated water storage tank for Zone 3 and 4B. There is a contingency allocation of $450,000.

We reported previously that the existing White Barn, currently on the Golden Farms property, would require structural engineering and design to restore it to a fully functional facility. In June, Dan said the project would probably be removed from the program, at least for this year. He now says they will not pursue this project and will divert the funds to a project to replace the office building at Union Reservoir (likely to be a modular building).

We reported on this project previously. The Aeronautics Division of the Colorado Department of Transportation hopes to seek consultant services for some airport layout plans. The project will be partially federally funded. Congress still has not reauthorized the program that would fund this project. Until Congress acts, the project will have to remain on hold. As we reported in June, if and when funding becomes available, Travis plans to release three or four separate RFPs. They have not yet identified which airports will be included in the RFPs. We'll continue to follow up.

In February, Kris McDaniel reported that the Town planned to issue an RFQ or RFP for a community park design, but did not have a definitive date yet for advertising the project. In April, he said Parks & Recreation was working on an updated schedule. In June, he indicated that the project was on hold. It's now being managed by the Parks & Rec Department. Amy Teetzel reports that an RFP will be coordinated by the Owner's Rep, Olsson Associates. Ernest Rodriguez, at Olsson, says they're drafting an RFP and hope to advertise within the next several weeks. The project will include design and construction documents for a new 42-acre park.

In February, Wayne reported that, within the next month or so, Boulder County expected to issue an RFP for consultant services for a space needs study for the Human Services agencies. In April, Wayne said the project was on hold and he wasn't sure when it might "get a life" again. He now informs us that it is likely to start soon but will be done in-house.

Earlier in the year, we reported that the County planned a countywide housing/needs assessment study. At that time, Tom reported that the project would be handled through the State Division of Housing but the County would manage it. He anticipated the State would give the County a list of vendors, but said he was interested in hearing from firms that provide these services. He now says the State Division of Housing will handle the entire process and will probably use its list of firms to select from, rather than advertising.

The School of Mines' capital plan includes additional student housing. In April, Mike said the project was not currently funded, so there was no specific schedule to initiate it. He now says it is likely they'll seek architectural/engineering services for design of a new residence hall within the next six months.

In June, we reported that this project would use funding made available through a federal mineral lease bill, and administered through the state using certificates of partication. Erik has now clarified that the funding will NOT come from this source, but from student voted bonds. The multi-use facility will include housing and other uses. Erik hopes to issue an RFQ in September for a housing master plan and program, then design of a new facility. They also plan to hire a construction manager/general contractor for the new building and major housing renovations.

This district is looking toward placing a bond on the November, 2008 ballot. A large part of the funding will go toward new boilers. They also will build one new school and one addition. Terry reports that the last time they built a new school they did a design/build contract and it worked pretty well, so he suspects they'll use the same approach. He now says that the Board will make a final decision in August whether or not to put the issue on the ballot. At this point, he does not expect they would begin a selection process before the vote.

In June, Joe predicted an RFP would be issued within a couple of weeks for design of spillway improvements at Jefferson Lake dam. He now says they have started the internal process to get ready to advertise. He predicts the RFP will hit the street during the first or second week of August.
Within the next couple of weeks, Ridgway plans to seek consultant assistance for a project that will design and construct two new tennis courts at Ridgway Athletic Park.
Jennie reminds us that the Authority selects for most consultant projects from a short list it compiles and updates annually. They advertise toward the end of the year to update the list.

Scot reports that the Town has been conducting master planning of the Chamonix site. They expect to complete this planning process in the next month or so. Depending on "what happens next" with the project (located in West Vail), he says they might issue an RFP for actual design of the fire station and employee housing that are contemplated on that site. We'll follow up.

Brad reports that they City might seek consultant services in the next few months for design of parking and a large picnic shelter at Great Plains Park. At this point, Brad is not sure how the project will proceed. We'll follow up.

Philo reports that, in September, Steamboat Springs plans to advertise for architectural/engineering services for an expansion of the Public Works facility. The expansion entails 3600 square feet including two bays for the water/wastewater utility group, office space and equipment space.

Western State College requested $3,117,803 for FY2008/09 for renovation of Taylor Hall. Stephen says the project is funded, but he does not yet have a schedule to advertise for a/e services. We'll follow up.

This project was funded in the state's budget "Long Bill." It provides for improvements to the physical environment of the inpatient/residential units at the Colorado Mental Health Institutes at Pueblo and Fort Logan, to reduce the risk of patient suicide and/or self-harm. Kris indicates that the Department will advertise for a/e services soon.

In April, we reported that this project appeared to be making the cut for funding by the legislature. However, it was not included in the final budget "Long Bill." The proposed project included renovations, upgrades to fire alarms, sprinklers, secure entrances, communication systems, and egress. Also proposed was the addition of space to the existing building.

We reported on this project previously. The RFQ has now been issued, and responses are due no later than Friday, June 27 for airport engineering services for a list of projects to be completed over the next five years. The current list of projects includes runway and taxiway improvements, ramps, parking aprons, a de-icing pad and other items. Interested firms may contact Doug Montgomery for further information or a copy of the RFQ.

In February, Peg reported that the District was working with DLR on a needs assessment. She also indicated that they were in the process of selling an existing school building to fund the first round of improvement projects they'll need to complete. She now informs us that the needs assessment has been completed. However, the sale of the school building stalled. We'll continue to follow up to find out when they might be looking at defining and starting some projects.

records.Project: Morrison Nature Ctr./Star K Ranch Garage
records.Description: A few months ago, Aurora advertised a design/build contract for a one-car garage for a city vehicle and a picnic type shelter at Star K Ranch/Morrison Nature Center. Mark reports that they received only one response, so they plan to advertise the project again. The RFP should go out soon.

Scott reports that the University will advertise beginning June 9 for construction management/general contractor services for renovation of Turner Hall. A MANDATORY pre-submittal meeting will be held on Tuesday, June 17 and responses will be due July 1.

As we reported previously, RTD is working toward an approach called the Public/Private Partnership Pilot Program, which will entail hiring a team to design, build, operate and finance improvements, including the Gold Line, East Line and the commuter rail maintenance facility. Following in "Industry Forum" in July (see our project ID #66833), they'll issue an RFQ focusing on the major players, the primes taking on the major responsibility. They'll short list up to four firms by the end of the year, then expect the primes to fill out their teams.

The County's capital budget includes funding for a new outside restroom facility at the rodeo grounds. Melody reports that they're hoping to apply for a GOCO grant for this project. They may seek design services sometime in the next few months. The project would be on the fall grant schedule, if awarded.

The legislature passed a funding bill (separate from the overall budget "Long Bill"), for the new Justice Center and History Museum. The History Museum will move forward first. Joseph Bell now indicates that they have used a team led by Tryba for the large project at the existing museum, and will probably continue with the same firm for the new museum.

This project is in the very preliminary discussion stages and is being driven by a private effort within the community. It will depend largely on private donors to become a reality. If it moves forward, it will entail a synthetic turf athletic complex. Tom says the City should know by September or October how sincere potential donors are for this project. Until that time, he will not have any additional information. We'll follow up.

In a Special Update earlier in May, we reported that the Department of Corrections would issue an RFQ for architectural services for the Ft. Lyon Correctional Facility Phase III expansion project. Jim Ramsey reports that the RFQ for this should be out this week.

Tom reports that Denver Health will require architectural services for a new dialysis center. They have hired Trammell Crow for property management services. Trammell Crow will be involved in the process for this project. When we spoke to Tom, he wasn't sure how the selection process would be handled, i.e., whether or not it will be advertised publicly. If it is advertised, the RFQ/P should be out within about the next 30 days.

Arapahoe County is getting close to a deal to purchase a new facility for the District Attorney's office. Assuming the negotiations wrap up as expected, they plan to issue an RFP soon for architectural services for a tenant finish project, to adapt the building for use as the new DA's office.

The City was successful in passing a ballot issue to fund a 350-seat performing arts center. Seth says they'll issue an RFQ/P eventually, but have a lot of community work to do first. He says PLEASE do not call him about the project at this time. Firms may register on the City's website to receive notices of projects (we'll also monitor progress). Go to www.cityoflonetree.com/list.asp to sign up.

Janet mentioned that she expects to require consultants for a new park project in 2009, and could be ready to issue an RFP toward the end of 2008. We did not get any details at this point, but will find out more before the next Update. This may be Mehaffey Park, which was postponed from this year. We'll follow up.

The Denver Museum of Nature and Science hopes to issue an RFP soon for design service for interior renovations at the museum. Design will need to be completed in time for the 2009 May to October construction window.

This project may or may not present an opportunity for a competitive selection. South Suburban will require consultant/design services for several smaller pool and park upgrade projects in Lone Tree. They haven't decided how to handle the selection - they may put together a package and hire an architectural firm for everything, or they may act as the "consultant" and hire subconsultants. It is also possible they'll direct select a firm without issuing an RFP. (Just a heads up in case they decide to do an RFP.)

Previously, the University hired a firm/team for a feasibility study and program plan for an expansion of the Aerospace Energy Systems building. They await additional funding to move forward to the next phase. It is at least possible they'll do a new consultant selection when they move to final design.

The University has been working with a consultant on a program plan for a new Geosciences building at Pod D near the McAllister Center. The building will house ATOC, INSTAAR, CIRES, Energy and Sustainability in the Research Park. Phil reports that the project awaits funding. They could continue with the same firm into design, or they may conduct a new selection process - when funding becomes available.

Brighton School District 27J requests letters of interest no later than 4:00 Wednesday, June 18 for a project they describe as: "Develop Educational Specifications and Programming for High School Services and Facilities." The complete letter of interest requirements are included on page 18 of the June 2 edition of the Daily Journal, or you may contact Ranette Jordan, Construction Technician.

Phase II improvements to Lincoln Park will include park lighting, landscaping, construction of parkways and amphitheater construction. Steve reports that they're still in the planning phase, working on the scope of improvements. He says they'll need assistance with "some sort" of design at some point: Possibly architecture/landscape architecture, or civil engineering, or both. They may be ready to put something out within the next couple of months.

Previously, we reported that the City of Montrose was working toward an expansion of the Pavilion facility as a multi-generational facility. The District's attempts to pass an earlier bond failed. They considered putting an issue on the ballot again this spring. They decided not to run another bond, but will pursue improvements in phases. In about a month, they'll issue an RFP for design of improvements to the lobby, customer service area, administrative offices, restrooms, a multi-purpose room and conference room.

The Judicial Dept. previously hired a program management firm for a proposed new Colorado Center for Justice and relocation of the Colo. History Museum. If the project is funded for the next phase in a future year, they expect to seek architectural/engineering services. The program management includes identifying a new site for the History Museum, so that the justice center can expand onto the museum's current site. The new museum will also require a/e services in a future year. They still await final legislative funding decisions.

The School of Mines project for Hall of Justice improvements (to include demolition and asbestos abatement), was included in the "supplemental" funding bill in 2007, SB263. Mike reports that they'll need consultant services for this demolition and abatement project. He does not have a specific schedule.

We reported on this project previously. The School of Mines submitted plans for an addition to Brown Hall for the Engineering Department. Mike indicates that this project is on the "long-term needs" list, and that they'll need a design team at some point. At this time, adequate funding has not yet been identified.

Previously, Tinneal reported that Moffat County MIGHT have a project late in 2007 or early in 2008 for design to remodel the courthouse. She now says they're applying for a grant in the April 1 cycle to do a feasibility study for a new building at the public safety campus and then to remodel the courthouse. She hopes they'll find out within a couple of months whether or not they'll receive grant funding. If they do, they'll advertise for architectural/engineering services. We'll follow up.

We reported last fall that the St. Vrain district was considering placing a capital projects bond on the ballot in November of 2008. Steve says it still appears they'll move forward with a bond on this year's ballot, but nothing has been approved by the Board. They still do not have details about the projects or the magnitude of the propsed bond. Steve now says he does not expect to begin any consultant selections before the vote. We'll follow up.
records.Type: AS, DR, MS, PK, ST, TR

records.Description: Bill reported previously that funding was approved in the 2008 budget to do the engineering and design for a new sanitary sewer lift station. An RFP should be issued within the next couple of months. The new lift station will serve the Community Center, Justice Center, Exhibit Barn and possible future demand.

UNC requested funding from the legislature for the 2008-09 fiscal year for interior renovation of the Butler Hancock building. It now appears unlikely the project will be funded by the legislature for FY2008/09. We'll follow up once the state budget has been finalized.

In February, Richard indicated that, should this project survive the state's budgeting process, the Department would seek a/e services. He now informs us this is a continuation project, and a/e services are already in place.

The University submitted a request for FY2008-09 funding for a remodel of the library. The project was #46 on the Governor's prioritized list. Geraldine confirms it's not looking good for funding this year.

One of the controlled maintenance projects the Department anticipates will receive FY 2008/09 funding approval is for a new roof at the Fort Logan facility. Chris expects they'll advertise for consultant services fairly soon. The RFQ is currently being prepared.

As we reported previously, the University has funding available for renovation of Turner Hall. They decided to use the CM/GC delivery method. Scott anticipates issuing an RFQ for architectural/engineering services within the next few weeks. They're still trying to determine the extent of funding that will be available. Scott says it could be up to $10 million.

Within the next month or so, the Department of Military and Veterans Affairs expects to issue an RFQ for architectural/engineering services for improvements at the Fort Lupton armory building. It is possible they'll use the cm/gc delivery method. Interested firms are encouraged to watch for the ad.
One of the projects in the School of Mines' capital plan is a new parking garage. No specific funding has yet been identified to initiate the project. At some point, they'll require a design team.

Sometime in the next few months, Aurora may seek consultant services for some work at reservoirs, to include inspections of five dams, inundation studies and an emergency action plan. An alternate contact is Joe Kleiner, 720-859-4302.
Very soon, Mesa State College plans to issue an RFQ for architectural services for the remodel of Houston Hall.

The City has hired a consultant to complete an assessment of the recreation center. Steve expects they'll present the results to City Council in June. At that point, he anticipates that Council will decide what improvements need to be done and plan for them in future years. There is no funding available in 2008 to initiate any renovation or remodeling projects. We'll monitor progress.
It is possible RTD will seek design services this year for the relocation of a bus maintenance facility. John says he has no details on this project yet. We'll follow up.

Gilpin County requests qualifications no later than 5:00 Tuesday, April 15 for design-build services for a new parking structure. The structure will be a two-story, 15,000 sf facility to support the new Justice Center, at 2960 Dory Hill Road in Golden. The project will be turn-key and phases will include programming, design, construction, commissioning and warranty. Contact Bill Paulman for a copy of the RFQ.

We don't typically report on private projects, but this one was forwarded to us so we'll pass it along. Special Transit is a private non-profit organization in Boulder that provides transportation for seniors and people with disabilities. They seek architectural/engineering services for a new central facility, to be approximately 56,000 square feet to house the primary administrative, operations and maintenance functions. For further information or a copy of the RFQ, go to www.specialtransit.org .

The District's capital plan includes $100,000 in 2008 for design of drop structures along the lower reach of Sand Creek in Commerce City. The City will provide matching funds. Paul does not yet have a schedule for initiating the project.

This project provides for revitalization of the 137,388 sf Clark Building, which houses various programs, including Instructional Services, the Dean of Library Arts, Economics, Foreign Languages and Literature. The project will upgrade mechanical/electrical systems, improve accessibility and replace fixed seating. A design RFQ/P is anticipated this winter.

Beginning in 2008, the District plans to design and construct a replacement facility for the Irwin/Green Mountain Center preschool. The current schedule indicates a project start in August, 2008 with completion in 2010.

This project provides for improvements to the public address system, art area, doors, electrical, HVAC and site lighting at Kendallvue Elementary. The current schedule indicates an August, 2008 project start.

As part of the current (2005-2010) bond program, Jeffco Schools plans phased addition/renovation projects (phases 2 and 3) at Ralston Elementary. The current schedule indicates an August, 2008 project start.
This project provides for a Longview/Johnson replacement facility on the Lifelong Learning Center parcel. The project is scheduled to start in early 2008 and to be completed in June of 2009.

We reported on this project in December. This project provides for the revitalization of the Industrial Sciences building. The current schedule indicates a winter RFQ for architectural/engineering services.

We reported on this project previously. Aurora plans a transit oriented development project in the area of the Iliff North station. Funding requested through DRCOG has been approved. Loretta reports they're working on getting the IGA approved, after which they'll issue an RFP to begin a consultant selection process for this station area planning project.
records.Type: AS, DR, MS, PK, PL, ST, TR

records.Description: In late 2006, Charlie predicted that, in the second half of 2007, the Pinery Water and Wastewater District anticipated advertising for design of a new water storage tank. He now says they're starting to seek County approval, but won't proceed beyond that, probably at least until 2009. Things could change if development picks up.

As we reported previously, DIA is developing a scope of work preparing to advertise for design services to relocate Passport Inspection in the CBP facility from level 5 to level 7. An RFP is currently "in development."

As we reported previously, the City plans to expand the existing Hatfield Chilson Recreation Center to meet demand and growth in the community. They anticipate a 20,000 sf expansion, to be designed in 2008 and constructed in 2009. Ken confirms that the project is still planned, but he does not yet have a time frame for issuing an RFQ or RFP. The Council will hold its retreat soon - Ken hopes to have some direction after that. We'll follow up.

We reported previously that the Historical Society requested funding for FY 2007/08 for an expansion of the Ute Indian Museum in Montrose. The project was approved in the "supplemental" funding bill. They expect to issue an RFP in the next month or two. The project is #20 on the Governor's list of prioritized projects for FY2008/09, with an additional $2,098,598 proposed. The Governor's office is recommending funding of the top 23 projects on the list. However, the legislature is free to make changes before budget adoption.

We reported on this project previously. Northglenn voters emphatically defeated a tax issue on November 6 that would have funded demolishing the recreation center and city hall complex to allow for private development on the existing 40-acre site, and to relocate the recreation center and city hall to adjacent public land. Steve now says the project is on hold, that the Council has made no decision regarding process or direction. We'll continue to monitor the project.
This project provides for design and engineering services for the expansion of the Concourse A East Commuter Facility. An RFP is still "in development."
We reported on this project previously. Aurora plans an RFP for design/build services for a Meadow Hills maintenance cold storage building. The RFP should be advertised very soon.

Alamosa is currently completing a citizen committee review process looking at the future rebuild of the library/city hall complex. They are considering a ballot issue in November of 2009. It is possible they'll begin an architectural/engineering selection process as soon as late 2008. We'll monitor the process.

Previously, we reported that the County planned to seek architectural/engineering services for a small satellite road and bridge facility at Arboles. Chris now reports that the staff is meeting this week to discuss this and other Road and Bridge projects. Partially due to changes at the upper levels of County government, they do not yet have a good handle on the 2008 budget. We'll follow up.
As we reported in December, CSU anticipates advertising this winter for design of an addition to and remodel of Braiden Dining Hall.

We reported on this project in December. This project provides for an addition and renovation at the Health and Exercise Science center. A winter RFQ is planned for architectural/engineering services.

The University would like to construct a new "End Zone" building, to include a strength and conditioning center, coaches' and other offices and other related facilities. Scott reports that this is a project unlikely to be funded by the state, so they're in the process of seeking private funding. We'll monitor progress.

The County is currently working on a courtroom expansion project that they expect will meet their court facility needs for the next five to seven years. Subsequently, they'll need a new facility. They're considering future financing options and timing. Sometime between 2008 and 2013, they'll probably go to the voters for a bond or some financing mechanism to fund a new court facility. They may also look at detention needs at the same time. We'll monitor the process.
Sometime later in 2008, Pueblo County expects to begin an architectural/engineering design selection for a new judicial center.

This is a multi-year project to upgrade the water pollution control facility to meet stringent ammonia-nitrogen, total inorganic nitrogen and, possibly, total phosphorus limits by the next permit cycle (2011). The City plans to seek a consultant in 2008 to perform a comprehensive design study, followed by equipment installation and construction in 2009-2010, to provide additional aeration capacity and changes to the existing blower units and/or the addition of new additional blowers. Chuck does not have a specific time estimate to issue an RFP.

Development in Greeley will require expansion of the capacity of lift stations. Development will typically be asked to pay for the upgrades, but the City may have to pay up front for construction. Chuck anticipates issuing a design RFP in the late summer or fall.

This tentative project is #8 on the the Governor's office's priority list for recommendation to the legislature, but there is no guarantee of funding. The project would remodel the Kipling Village group homes to improve the environment for individuals, and to avoid severe citations and deficiencies. The legislature will make funding decisions in the spring. If it's funded, a/e services will be required. However, they may select a firm from the state's as-needed list.

The Town of Avon has issued an RFP for "Public Works and Transportation Facilities Design," for new facilities to support operations of the Public Works and Transportation Departments. Proposals are due no later than 5:00 Monday, February 25. Questions must be submitted by February 13. The RFP is available on Avon's website at www.avon.org/bids.asp?bidID=2 .

The District failed to pass a tax measure in November of 2007. Patty now reports that "chances are" they'll put a mill levy override on the ballot in November of 2008. If they do, and if it passes, it will fund the Parker library (aready started), a Lone Tree branch and a Castle Pines North branch. The Castle Pines North library will be a rented space requiring tenant finish.

In the next month, Longmont plans to advertise for on-call architectural services to provide services as needed for City projects. The contract(s) will have an initial term of one year, with options to extend for up to four additional one-year terms.

John reports that the City will place a bond issue on the ballot in May. If it passes, it will fund some park projects and, possibly, a cultural center. They will not begin a consultant selection process until they have secured funding. He did not provide more specifics about projects at this time.

CU is currently in the program planning phase for a Geoscience building, a wet lab building to be located in the research park. They will seek plan approval in March, then try for special legislative funding so they can begin the project in FY2009/10. If all goes well, they'll start design around the spring of 2009.
Scott reports that it is possible UNC will require a consultant selection this spring for a couple of controlled maintenance roofing projects.
In February or March, Mesa State expects to advertise for construction manager/general contractor services for the Student Housing project.
Sometime in February, Breckenridge plans to seek an architectural firm to evaluate structures for Town Hall needs into the future.

In early February, the Parks & Recreation Department plans to issue an RFP for design of two swimming pools for the Aquatics Division. We did not receive any further details. They'll post the RFP on their website, www.denvergov.org .

Phase III of the Service Center will house the Streets, Solid Waste, Traffic Engineering, Street Project Engineering and Storm Water Divisions, plus equipment to support those operations. Expenditures are estimated at $1,100,000 in 2009, and $10,000,000 in 2010.
The City plans an expansion of the Street Shop facility, estimated to cost $540,000 from the Water and Sewer utility funds for their portion of the facility.

The Auraria Higher Education Center has identified the need for a South Classroom renovation and addition. They submitted a funding request for $3,774,872 in FY2008/09 to initiate the project. The project is #47 on the priority list developed by the Governor's office, which is recommending funding of only the top 23 projects, so this one is unlikely to be funded in this next fiscal year. It is possible they'll request funding again for FY2009/10.

The University requested $1,684,015 in FY2008/09 funding to initiate renovation of the existing science building. The project is #45 on the Governor's office's priority list. Only the top 23 are recommended for funding, so this one is unlikely to be approved in FY2008/09. It is not yet known whether or not they'll resubmit the project for FY2009/10.

records.Description: The City plans to design and construct a new clearwell at the water treatment plant.
The City plans a project in 2012 to complete a new wastewater treatment plant solids handling facility.
The bond program includes funding in 2008 for a geotechnical and structural evaluation at Powderhorn Elementary. The scheduled start date is August of this year.
Improvements at Stott Elementary will include the public address system, art area, code compliance issues, interior lighting, plumbing and site lighting.
This project provides for improvements to the art area, HVAC/Controls and kitchen hood at Slater Elementary. The current schedule indicates a January, 2010 design start.
This project entails art studio and HVAC improvements at Stevens Elementary.
The District plans improvements to the art area, code compliance and HVAC improvements at the Dennison Opportunity School facility.

This project provides for improvements to the public address system, plus the art and chemical areas, the clock/bell system, electrical, food service and plumbing at Arvada Middle School. The current schedule indicates an August, 2008 design start, with completion in 2010.

Improvements at Drake Middle School will include the art area, auditorium sound, electrical, food services and HVAC system. The project is currently scheduled for a January, 2008 start with completion in September, 2009.
This project provides for replacement of the roof at Mandalay Middle School, scheduled for design start in January of 2008 with completion in April of 2010. The RFP has not yet been issued.

Improvements at Oberon Middle School will include public address system, electrical, interior finishes and building renovation. Design is scheduled to begin in August, 2008 with a construction completion date of July, 2010.
Improvements at Wheat Ridge Middle School will include the art and chemical areas, HVAC and interior finishes.
This project provides for renovation of Arvada High School. The project is currently scheduled to start in October of 2008 with completion in November, 2010.

The current bond program includes a project to complete improvements to the art and chemical areas, electrical, food service and lighting at Green Mountain High School. The project design is currently scheduled to start in January of 2009.

This project will complete improvements to the art and chemical areas, food service, HVAC and plumbing systems at Jefferson High School. The projected start date is April, 2009 with completion in November of 2010.

The District plans for replacement, site lighting and site improvements at Lakewood Memorial Stadium. The revised design start time is August of 2008. The budget has been revised downward from an original estimate of $1.4 million to $460,720.
The City plans improvements at the Lakewood Reservoir dam in 2011.

The City's capital plan includes a project to expand the reclaimed water treatment plant from its current capacity of 7 mgd to 10 mgd. This expansion was planned for the original design and construction of the plant and consists of adding filter and pump areas only. The current plan indicates expenditures of $5.9 million in 2011. Additional funding may be needed in future years.

This project will remodel the Elkins House, including electrical, mechanical, ADA accessibility (kitchen, bath, stairways, etc.), carpeting, interior paint and fixtures. The current schedule indicates a January, 2009 start with 18 months estimated time to completion.
This project provides for improvements to the Airport electric substation feeder.
The City's capital plan includes proposed historic preservation funding in 2010 and 2012 for depot rehabilitation and restoration. The project was moved out one year from the previous capital plan.
This project will replace the roof at the District Shops and Operations Center buildings. The roof is original to the building and has reached its life expectancy.

The University's capital plan includes a project to complete a new wing for the Chemistry program. They requested funding from the legislature for FY2008/09. However, the project is #43 on the Governor's list of prioritized projects. The Governor's office is recommending funding of only the top 23 on the list, so this project is unlikely to be funded in the coming fiscal year.
The University hopes to complete a new environment, sustainability and renewable energy building.

This project includes demolition of practice fields and parking area; development of a trail and landscape improvements; installation of irrigation; and construction of multi-purpose fields. It may require closing the ditch with underground pipe. The undeveloped park area is 15.26 acres west of the ditch. Costs include $2,670,500 for construction, $88,800 for "other," and a $267,100 contingency.
This project will replace existing town wells as they reach the end of an assumed 25-year lifespan.

This project includes construction of site improvements, storage facilities, and a building addition at the south Maintenance Facility. Costs are estimated at $2,000,000 in 2009, and $2,614,000 in 2010.
The City plans to complete improvements to the Sunset Ridge water storage reservoir.
This project will design and construct a new water storage reservoir in Zone 5. Expenditures are estimated at $1 million in 2010, and $1.5 million in 2011.
The City plans to complete additional reclaimed water pump stations and storage facilities, beginning in 2010.

This project will replace the communication houses at the Alameda and Downtown Littleton light rail station platforms. These facilities are currently made of painted steel but will be upgraded to stainless steel or aluminum, to match the materials of the other communication houses. The existing facilities are corroding due to exposure to the elements and magnesium chloride chemicals. The exterior needs to be replaced with better materials to protect equipment.
Fort Collins' capital plan includes proposed funding in 2009 for development of Staley Neighborhood Park.

This project is not currently funded. It would relocate Fire Station 4 and build a new facility. The existing Station 4 was built in 1981 as a house on a residential lot, with an oversized garage. It is too small to house necessary equipment, is incapable of being renovated to meet ADA standards and has no room for expansion to four-person company.

This currently unfunded project calls for acquisition of primary land for a full park facility, and includes a bath house/changing room that was formerly a separate project, #PR-103. It is recommended that the Union Reservoir Master Plan (#PR-138) be completed before implementing this project.

This unfunded project would provide for an outdoor leisure/activities pool, including water spray features, a lazy river attraction, and several small scale water slides. Also included is a mechanical room and restroom/changing facilities.

The Central Treatment Plant Facility Plan identified the need to provide additional ammonia removal capability at the Plant in the future due to increased loadings and a lowering in the allowable discharge limits. This project will construct two new aeration basins in the North Secondary System to treat increased flows and loads conveyed to the Central Treatment Plant. Costs include funding for a study, design and construction.

This unfunded project provides for a second full-service Recreation Center, to include a full size ice rink and a competitive swimming pool including a spectator area, a leisure pool, fitness room, teen center and other programming spaces to be defined through public meetings. Year #1 ($45,000) proposes conducting a feasibility study to identify community interest in the City's providing this amenity.

This project provides for the acquisition, planning, design, and construction of a north side lift station to connect properties from the I-25 corridor to the North Water Reclamation Facility. The station will coordinate with the north side interceptor. The project total includes $200,000 for acquisition, $3,704,400 for construction and a $700,000 contingency. It may be moved to an earlier date with developer contributions.
The plans for this project address the Butterfield restroom and associated needs.
This unfunded project replaces the existing mobile home that is currently being used as the Park Ranger office with a fabricated structure. It would also include a shop maintenance site.
This unfunded project calls for the construction of a new Museum Collections Storage Facility to house the artifact collection of the Longmont Museum and Cultural Center, approximately 10,000 sf.
This project provides for renovation of the Municipal Office Complex (MOC) to fully house the Traffic Engineering Division and the traffic operations center.

records.Project: Olde Course & Mariana Butte Clubhouses Imp's
records.Description: This project provides for improvements to the Olde Course Clubhouse and the Mariana Clubhouse. This project will be necessary if the Golf Enterprise does not move forward with a $4 million revenue bond to replace the club house.
The City's Power Enterprise plans a project in 2010 to complete the Crossroads substation.
This project would design, renovate and construct an addition to the "old" Police Services building at 300 LaPorte Avenue. The project was proposed in 2008 but is not currently funded.
This project provides for the design and installation of an additional digester at the wastewater treatment plant.

The County has allocated funding from 2010-2012 for development of new and existing Open Space parks to provide public access, including utilities, parking areas, restrooms, shelters, roads, bridges and other improvements. Specific parks will be identified at a later time.
records.Type: AS, BR, MS, PK, SW, ST, WR

records.Description: The center of the City's cultural life for 27 years, the Lincoln Center is in need of improvements and renovation. This project will provide new lighting, carpeting, restrooms, better acoustics, modern conference facilities and an elevator to the balcony. The current two-year budget allocates $2,217,436 to the project in 2009.
The City anticipates initiating community park improvements in 2009.
These improvements include the installation of an energy dissipating inlet (EDI) structure and the replacement of the rake arm mechanism within each clarifier.
This project provides for a new systems biotechnology building on the Boulder campus. The timing is subject to future funding approval.

This project will complete improvements at Flatirons Elementary, as part of the 2006 bond program approved by voters. The school is a 33,468 sf facility. The project is scheduled as part of Phase II. Improvements will include intercom, electrical, HVAC, classroom additions, art and music room additions/remodels, gym/stage expansion, special education classrooms, cafeteria improvements, administration/student health space expansion, exterior/play facilities and technology upgrades.

This project will complete improvements at the 69,518 sf Escuela Bilingue Pioneer (Elementary) School, located at 101 East Baseline Road in Lafayette. Improvements will include fire alarm, roof replacement/repair, restrooms, kindergarten renovation, IMC expansion and remodel, administrative and health space expansion, special education classroom addition/remodel, music classroom renovation, outdoor play area upgrades, and technology improvements.

During Phase II of the 2006 bond program, the District plans improvements at the 117,057 sf Nevin Platt and Platt CHOICE Middle School, located at 6096 Baseline Road in Boulder. The project will include intercom system upgrades, electrical, HVAC, science classroom renovation, art classroom renovation, auditorium support improvements, consumer studies renovation, auxiliary gym expansion, band/choir room expansion/improvements, administrative spaces, a tech shop expansion, exterior/paving improvements and technology upgrades.

The water reclamation facility has a number of concrete tanks that are partially buried. Such tanks are subject to pressure from groundwater in the surrounding soil. When the tanks are emptied for maintenance, groundwater pressure can crush the tanks. This project will construct dewatering wells to lower the groundwater table at the water reclamation facility.
The City's capital plan includes proposed funding in 2011 and 2012 for development of Cundiff Park.
Durango's five-year capital plan includes proposed funding in 2012 for improvements at Holly Park.
This project provides for a new parking structure at 7th and Camino.
This project provides for solar collectors at the wastewater treatment plant.
The City's capital plan includes a project to rebuild the electric substation in North Glenwood.
The City's capital plan has programmed funding in 2012 for a new ADA compliant pool bathhouse at Mineral Palace.
The City's long-term plan includes a proposed new performing arts center. Andy Bass reports that they're working on getting support for the project. He says it may not happen in the next year or two.
In the next two to three years, Cortez hopes to be able to fund a new golf course pro shop.

Littleton Schools recently finished projects from an $85 million bond passed in 2002. Within the next two to three years, they expect to conduct a new needs assessment, which may lead to another bond vote in about five years. It is likely they'll use a consultant for the needs assessment.

The County's long-term plans include a proposed new courts building. The County Commissioners and staff have identified the need and continue to discuss funding alternatives. Shannon Carter reports that the project is unlikely to be initiated in 2008.

UNC is requesting funding for the 2008-09 fiscal year for student services building improvements. The project is currently #55 on the Governor's prioritized list. It is likely only about the top 23 projects will make the cut for funding in the next budget year.
Vail is working on a public-private partnership deal that will eventually result in building a new parking structure at Lion's Head.
This project will provide for a new water storage tank adjacent to existing Reservoir 3B to serve the Purple Zone.
This project will construct a new water storage tank adjacent to existing Reservoir 11B to serve the purple zone.

This project provides design and construction of additional solids handling facilities for the Wastewater Treatment Plant, including an additional digester, new belt press, and additional dissolved air flotation thickener.
This project will provide a bank of 8 tennis courts all in one location and will also have a fifty-car parking area and restroom facility separate from a park facility.

Western State College requested funding in FY2008/09 for renovation of and an addition to Richardson Hall. The project is #34 on the Governor's prioritized list. Only about the top 23 priorities are expected to be funded, so this project is unlikely for funding in the coming fiscal year.

The Department of Military and Veterans Affairs requested funding from the legislature for FY2008/09 for the Lakewood Readiness Center. The project is #38 on the Governor's prioritized list. The Governor's office is recommending funding for only the top 23 projects on the list, so this one is unlikely to make it for the coming fiscal year. It remains to be seen whether or not the Department will request funding again in FY2009/10.

The Department of Human Services requested FY2008/09 funding for an expansion of the Sol Vista Youth Services Center. The project is #40 on the Governor's prioritized list. Only the top 23 are recommended for funding. It remains to be seen whether or not Human Services will request funding again in FY2009/10.

Human Services requested funding for FY2008/09 for Operational Master Plan improvements. The project is #41 on the Governor's prioritized list. The Governor's office is recommending that the top 23 projects on the list be funded, so this one is unlikely for the coming fiscal year. It remains to be seen whether or not Human Services will request funding again in FY2009/10.

Colorado Northern Community College requested FY2008/09 funding from the legislature for the Craig Academic Center. The project is #44 on the Governor's prioritized list. Only the top 23 are being recommended for funding, so this project is unlikely to be funded this next fiscal year. It is possible the college will request funding again in FY2009/10.
The University's long-range capital plan includes proposed funding to renovate the existing engineering building.
records.Agency: Univ. of Colo. at Colo. Springs

records.Description: Fort Lewis College requested funding in FY2008/09 for a south/east expansion project. However, the project is #48 on the priority list released by the Governor's office, which is recommending funding of only the top 23 on the list. So this project is unlikely to be funded in FY2008/09. It could be resubmitted for the next fiscal year.
The District's current bond program includes improvements at Fitzmorris Elementary, including building envelope (fascia and soffit) upgrades and HVAC improvements.
The City's capital plan proposes funding in 2009 for new shop facility for Sanitation.
This project provides for construction of a permanent stage/band shell in Cole Park.

The County's five-year plan includes a project to complete a needs assessment and to establish a community task force to develop and implement a recruitment and expansion action plan to meet growing cild care and local foster care demands.
The County's capital plan includes proposed funding in 2009 for Sheriff's office improvements at Battlement Mesa.
Highlands Ranch's capital plan provides for improvements at Historic Park. Funding is projected at $876,311 in 2010, with additional funding of $1,550,000 required in the future.
The City's capital plan includes proposed funding for data center improvements: $100,000 in 2010, $200,000 in 2011 and $400,000 in 2016.
This project provides for improvements to the Eaton House museum in 2010.
This project provides for building construction for museum collections storage and exhibits.
The Town has programmed funding in 2012 for a new Town Hall building.
This project provides for phase II improvements at Venezia Community Park. It is proposed to begin in 2009, but is currently unfunded.
Garfield County's capital plan includes proposed funding in 2011 for new 40-bed intensive residential facility for Community Corrections.
This project provides for baffling system improvements at the Semper water treatment facility.
The University's 5-year capital plan includes a project to complete a new "H" wing at the physics building. The timing will depend on future funding approval from the state and/or other sources.
The University has identified the need for a new faculty office building. The project will be dependent on state or other future funding.
The University's five-year plan includes a project to complete a space systems science and energy facility. The project timing will depend on state or other future funding.

The University's five-year capital construction program includes a project to complete capital renewal improvements at the Hellems and Guggenheim buildings. Project timing wil depend on state and/or other funding.
The University's five-year program includes a project to complete a research office building.
CU has identified the need to renovate the Christol chemistry building on the Boulder campus.
This project provides for a new performing arts center at CU Boulder.
The University hopes to use "cash funds" (as opposed to funding provided through the state legislature) for a future computational sciences center.
The Univerity's five-year capital program includes a project to complete this phase of renovations/remodel at Williams Village.
The University's five-year capital program includes funding for the South Classroom building. The project start time will depend on future funding from the state and/or other sources.

records.Description: The University's long-range plans include the Research Complex 3 at the Fitzsimons campus.
This project provides for a lab fit-out at the science building on the Denver campus. They hope to identify sources of "cash" funding, as opposed to a state appropriation.
The University's long-range capital plan includes a project to complete a new health and wellness center.
This project provides for a future new parking structure. They hope to identify "cash" funding, as opposed to a state appropriation.
The University's long-range plans include renovation of the Red Cross building.
The University has proposed a future project to complete the Anschutz Campus Union at Fitzsimons.
The University's long-range plans include a new general classroom building on the Auraria campus.
The University's long-range plan includes a project to complete a technology/classroom/office building on the Auraria campus.
This project provides for a new arts building on Auraria's downtown Denver campus.

The Auraria Higher Education Center has proposed a future project to complete a new library/study center. The capital plan indicates an initial funding request of $8,136,000 in FY2012/13, with additional funding required in future years.
This project provides for Sand Creek wastewater treatment plant improvements.
This project provides for improved septic hauling facilities.
The City's capital plan includes proposed funding for restoration of the Mac Brewery building. At this time, all capital projects have been place on hold due to budget constraints.
The City has proposed a project to complete restoration work on the Boodle Mill building. At this time, all capital projects are on hold due to budget constraints.

This tentative project is #5 on the Governor's office's priority list or projects to be recommended to the legislature, but there is no guarantee of funding. The project calls for the restoration and repairs of the enclosure of the capitol dome. The legislature will make funding decisions later in the spring.

records.Project: Pueblo CC, Academic Bldg, LC Renov
records.Description: This tentative project is #23 on the Governor's office's priority list (his office is recommending the top 23 projects on the list), but there is no guarantee of funding. This project, for Pueblo Community College, would renovate unfinished space in the basement of the Academic Building to house the Learning Center.
The City plans to complete Crossroads Booster Station improvements in 2010.
This project entails design and construction of a 2 MG water tank.
This project addresses the Horseshoe Substation and associated needs.
This project will address needs associated with the West Sub to the Horseshoe Sub.

The Luce property will be incorporated into Coal Creek Park. Amenities will include a skatepark, playground and shelter, parking lots, and a concession stand. ADA upgrades will be required with improvements to fields, landscape, and irrigation.

Two fishing jetties will be added to provide access when experiencing lower water levels at the Erie Reservoir. The additional jetties will ensure an improved year-round recreational use for park users.

The airport terminal can no longer support the level of air and passenger traffic. A community goal is to build passenger volume over time. The current facility has outlived its useful life and, because of code issues, needs to be replaced. It is estimated to be 35,000 sf smaller than what is needed to support the existing and projected passenger levels. Parking areas will also need to be reconstructed.

In 2004, the Fairgrounds built a structure to hold 24 new horse stalls. The building was designed to be extended to the west for future growth. A total of 19 stalls were lost during the 2007 grandstand renovation project. This project is the first step to start replacing these stalls.

The Fairgrounds needs to replace the makeshift concession stand that was located behind the grandstand. The new concession stand will be attached to a new restroom facility. The County hopes to receive a GOCO grant for the restrooms, then will add the concession building. When designing the restrooms, electric, sewer and water needs to a concession stand will be considered.

We reported on this project previously. An a/e RFP for design to remodel fire station #1 was issued earlier in the year and subsequently cancelled. Curt now says he still hopes to issue a new RFP soon. The project will involve renovating this historic structure and adding needed facilities. (Curt describes the building as "historic," but it's not officially registered as an historic structure.)

We reported on this project previously. The City may seek consultant services at some point for a levee design and FEMA review project along the Colorado River in one of the lower downtown areas. The project is on hold for the time being. We'll provide additional information as it becomes available.

This project provides partial funding for improvements at Springhill Park. The City expects to fund the park over several years. In early 2008, the City plans to seek consultant services for construction documents for improvements to this existing park.

We reported on this project a number of times in the past. The project will remodel the portion of the administration building at the wastewater treatment plant that previously housed the water quality laboratory. The City ended up using a basic design completed some time ago, and have hired a construction company to complete improvements, so no additional consultant services will be needed.

In October, we reported that it was possible that, within the next several months, Arapahoe County would seek architectural/engineering services for new courtrooms. They'll add up to eight new courtrooms and remodel a couple of floors in two buildings. Shannon now reports that they decided to continue into design with DLR Group, the company that completed the needs assessment study.

We reported previously that the School of Mines anticipated an RFQ for design of renovations to the top floor of the General Research Laboratory building. Mike now says they're still waiting for the "funding picture" to become more clear, but they still may require a/e services for this project. We'll follow up.

We reported on this project previously. Longmont now expects to issue an RFP very soon, possibly this week, for design/build services for a biosolids dewatering project that will include more than just basic operation services.

We reported on this project previously. Sam now says Colorado Springs Airport hopes to issue an RFQ/P by the end of the year for consultant services in connection with a project to demolish the old terminal facility on Fountain Boulevard. The project will include structural engineering considerations, utilities and, possibly, grading to prepare the area. The project will also include design for placement of a small waste disposal facility that needs to be moved.

records.Project: Coll. of Perf. & Visual Arts/Foundation Hall
records.Description: UNC requests qualifications no later than 2:00 Friday, December 21 for a Facilities Master Plan for the College of Performing and Visual Arts (Center for Musical Performance project, notice #UNC-RFQ-08-02). A MANDATORY pre-submittal meeting is scheduled at 11:00 Monday, December 12 at UNC Parsons Hall, 411 20th Street in Greeley. To obtain the RFQ, contact Barbara Taylor, Business Manager, 970-351-22132, or barbara.taylor@unco.edu , or go to www.unco.edu/facility/planning/projects.htm .

Grand Junction has advertised for design of Phase III improvements at Canyon View Park. The project will entail primarily construction documents for a tennis complex and additional parking. It will include construction observation services. The construction budget is approximately $640,000. Proposals are due no later than December 20. The RFP is posted at www.govbids.com/scripts/co1/public/openbids/viewsolicitations.asp .

Voters in this district approved a bond in November for four projects. One is a new 48,000 sf recreation center. Once they have an owner's representative under contract, they will begin work on an architectural/engineering contract for this project.

Voters in this district passed a bond in November that will fund four projects, one of which is a new 48,000 sf recreation center. Another will demolish the existing gold course pro shop/clubhouse and build a new one. A third involves infrastructure and a concession/restroom building at a 40-acre park. The last is replacement of the irrigation system (already designed) at an 18-hole golf course. The District plans to issue an RFP very soon for an owner's representative for this project.

District voters passed a bond in November that will fund four projects, one of which is a new golf course pro shop/clubhouse. They plan to demolish the existing building and construct a new one. They're currently in the process of completing a site survey. They have not yet developed a specific schedule for initiating an architectural/engineering consultant selection process.

Voters approved a bond in November to fund four projects at Frasier Valley Metro Recreation District. One of the projects involves infrastructure and a restroom and concession building at a 40-acre park. They have not yet developed a schedule for release of a design RFP.
The Department of Aviation is developing an RFP for on-call architectural/engineering design services for 2007-2009 projects. The selected firm will perform miscellaneous tasks through work orders.
DIA is currently developing an RFP to hire a firm to provide on-call architectural/engineering services for 2007-08 projects. Services will be provided for miscellaneous projects using task orders.

We reported on this project previously. Boulder is partnering with RTD to develop a project at 30th and Pearl for a transit center and housing. The City has now prepared and is ready to issue an RFP for master planning of the 11-acre site, then site design and design of the bus facility. The RFP is completed and under review by RTD. Micki hopes to release it soon. The City has a website for the project, www.bouldertransitvillage.net .
records.Type: AS, CM, DR, MS, PK, ST
