records.Description: The District originally scheduled a January, 2007 start date for a comprehensive renovation of the Jefferson County Open School Opportunity School facility. The project has not yet been initiated. We're not sure what the schedule will be, but will follow progress.

We reported on this project previously. It was approved in the 2006 budget. Rick Anderson said Adams County Parks expected to seek landscape architectural services for a redesign of Rotello Park, an existing park of approximately 26 acres. He now says they will probably do the project in-house.

The proposed East Corridor commuter rail line consists of a 23.6 mile line connecting downtown Denver and the eastern portion of the Metro area to DIA. It will include five stations. John now reports that RTD's intent is to pursue this under a "Public Private Partnership Pilot Program (or PentaP)": To find a private partner to design, build, operate and finance the project. He predicts it will be about a year before they initiate this process.
records.Type: AS, DR, MS, PK, ST, TR

records.Description: The new Gold Line FasTracks light rail line is an 11.2-mile line that will connect downtown Denver with western Arvada, to include seven stations. The project will also include minor highway improvements. In August, we erroneously reported that this project would be designed by the railroad. It's actually the Northwest corridor that BNSF will design. John says RTD will use the Public Private Partnership Pilot Program (PentaP) for this one: to seek a private partner to design, build, finance and operate the project. Project initiation is about a year away.
records.Type: AS, DR, MS, PK, ST, TR

records.Description: RTD's FasTracks program includes a 10.5-mile corridor connecting the southeast corridor light rail line at I-225 and Parker Road to the east corridor rail line at Peoria and Smith Roads. The project will include seven light rail stations. An environmental assessment and preliminary engineering have been initiated. The EIS will cover the rail portion but not the road portion of the project. John reports that RTD expects to complete this project as a design/build. He does not yet have an estimated time frame for initiating the project.
records.Type: AS, CM, DR, MS, PK, ST, TR

records.Description: This FasTracks project provides for commuter rail service extending for 18 miles and connecting Thornton, Northglenn and Commerce City to downtown Denver. The project will include eight rail stations and new and improved park-and-rides. The current schedule indicates a design RFP in 2008 with design completion in early 2011. They now have a draft EIS. John reports that the project will be completed using traditional means (e.g., design-bid-build). He hopes to begin design selection by the end of 2008.
records.Type: AS, DR, MS, PK, ST, TR

records.Description: We reported on this project previously. In August, Phil indicated that he expected to advertise in the fall for design of a new basketball practice facility. He now says the project will require some programming, for which he expects to select from the state's as-needed consultant list. It appears likely it will be completed as a design/build, which should be advertised in about a year.

We reported on this project previously. The project includes design of a short extension of Meridian Road, in the vicinity of Highway 24 and south of Highway 24, to include a new park and ride. Andre now says it should be advertised before the end of November.

We reported on this project previously. Ridgway will seek consultant services for design of a new wastewater lift station. They're still working on identifying a funding source. It may be several more months before the project proceeds to design. Firms interested in this or other projects in Ridgway are encouraged to contact or visit Greg Clifton, Town Manager. The address is P.O. Box 10 (physical address 201 N. Railroad Street), Ridgway, CO 81432.

We reported on this project previously. It entails a 20-foot by 200-foot pole building to provide needed covered parking for vehicles and equipment. Phase 1 will build a 20' x 120' building and Phase 2 a 20' x 80' building. No specific schedule has yet been set to initiate the project. Tom now indicates that the project will not be initiated in 2007.

In June, Paul indicated that, within the next few months, the School of Mines might issue an RFQ for program planning for new housing and dining facilities. We did not get an update on the status of the project for our August Update. Paul now says project initiation is "to be determined."
We reported on this project previously. Dennis now predicts that Front Range Airport will issue an RFP within the next two to three weeks for a new airport engineering services contract.
records.Type: AS, DR, EV, GT, MS, ST, SV, TR

records.Description: We reported on this project previously. Phil anticipates a design/build RFP in early November for renovation of Andrews Hall (a residence hall), as part of a program to upgrade residence halls campus-wide.

Patrick reports that Front Range Community College plans to seek engineering services for a complete fascility audit. He expects they'll select a firm from the state's as-needed consultant list. Firms on that list may contact him for additional information or to discuss the College's needs.

The rail lines for the Northwest Corridor of FasTracks will be designed and constructed by the railroad. RTD will be responsible for design and construction of the stations. John says they'll move forward to design as soon as they're able to complete an agreement with the BNSF Railroad. He hopes to initiate the project by the end of 2008.
The Airport's current engineering contract expires at the end of 2007. Within the next month, they expect to advertise for qualifications for a new multi-year engineering contract.

East Grand Schools will place a bond question on the November ballot, for additions and remodels at the Granby and Frasier Valley elementaries and the high school. They do not expect to select an architectural team (or teams) until after the vote. Neenan has done some preliminary drawings. Interested firms may send letters of interest (don't send full-blown SOQs at this point). The address is P.O. Box 125, Granby, CO 80446.
Colorado State University should have an RFQ out now or very soon for architectural/engineering services for a new $45 million academic instruction building.
Colorado State University should have an ad out now or very soon for architectural/engineering services for a new $20 million residence building.

Greg reports that CSU may seek consultant services in the next few months for design of some "smaller projects," such as roofing projects and smaller remodels. He didn't provide a lot of specifics. It is possible some or all of these projects will be small enough for them to select from the state's as-needed consultant list.
Very soon (possibly this week), the Colorado State Buildings and Real Estate expects to advertise an RFQ for "In-house" tenant planning and design services.

The Department of Community Resources plans to issue an RFP on October 25 for engineering/design to renovate the two swimming pools at Carmody Recreation Center. One pool is indoors and the other is outdoors.

Jeffco Schools has a number of smaller projects in its current bond program that have not yet been initiated. Some are scheduled to start between early and mid 2008. They entail improvements such as electrical and mechanical, plumbing, interior lighting, clock/bell systems, P/A systems, etc. Many are smaller projects, and may be grouped for the purposes of hiring engineering or other consultant services.

We reported on this project previously. Brian Pinkerton (Program Engineeer) reports that an RFQ should be advertised within the next month or so for design support services for a one-mile stretch on the south side of Black Hawk. They'll use what they call a "blended team" approach, with CDOT's in-house designers working side by side with the consultant.
records.Type: AS, BR, CM, DR, EV, GT, ST, SV

records.Description: This project provides for the renovation of the 21,660 Ekeley building. An earlier five-year capital plan indicated funding needs totalling $12,220,000. The project was proposed for this fiscal year. It was included in SB 263, which provides additional capital funding, if available, for a number of projects beyond the basic Long Bill. Phil still hopes they'll know by about September whether or not adequate funding will be available for this project. If approved at that time, CU will seek design consultant services.

The University has proposed a project for capital renewal of the Ketchum Arts & Sciences building. The cost estimate from an earlier five-year plan totalled $12,879,314. The legislature included this project in SB 263, for potential funding if adequate funds are available. Phil still hopes to find out around September about funding availability. Assuming approval, CU will seek consultant services for this project.

We reported on this project previously. The City plans to seek a/e services for two new fire stations. This will entail moving two stations, based on a matrix study they have completed to determine where stations need to be. Esco now reports that they're still holding public meetings, but are also preparing an RFQ for architectural services. The RFQ may be issued as soon as the Chief approves it.

This project provides for the final phase of addition and renovation at Creighton Middle School, planned to begin in August of 2007 for completion in September of 2009. Kathie was unclear whether or not a/e services had already been selected for this project. If so, please ignore this item.

This project provides for improvements to the art area, building envelope, food service, HVAC and site lighting at Pomona High School. The projected start date is January of 2008 with completion in May of 2009. An RFP should be issued within the next several months.

We reported on this project previously. Aurora plans to seek planning services for transit oriented development in the area of Fourth Avenue north of City Place. Funding has been approved. The station area planning RFP should be out very soon. The City expects to combine this project with the Colfax & I-225 TOD project under one design contract.
records.Type: AS, DR, MS, PK, PL, ST, TR

records.Description: We reported on this project previously. The project is a review of support facilities at the entire plant site, as opposed to a building by building approach. It will evaluate current uses, problems and issues; determine future needs for changes; identify opportunities for cost savings; and provide a recommended plan. Jim now reports that an RFP has not yet been developed and it's possible the project will be incorporated into a task order under the Black & Veatch/Brown and Caldwell Capital Project Management program.
We reported on this project previously. The School submitted a federal grant application for a research park planning study. They now expect to issue an RFQ in August for this study.

This project will develop the 10-acre park site across from City Hall on 92nd Avenue. The master plan included detailed walls, planting areas, extensive fountain work and garden designs. Because of its location, this is not a traditional neighborhood park but more of an urban park that will include a lot of hardscape. The cost estimate is from $1.24 to $2 million. The current five-year plan includes funding totalling $1.24 million. Kathy reports that the timing is not yet certain, as they're still working on funding sources. It may not be initiated before 2008.
We reported on this project previously. The District plans a fall advertisement for design of a new high school. No specific time frame has yet been established.
We reported on this project previously. Amy says Aurora Public Schools will seek an architect in the fall to design a new prototype for K-8 schools. No specific timing has been established.

We reported on this project previously. The District is currently completing some facility planning. Tina Goar (the Superintendent) indicates they'll need some renovations and other improvements. She would like to issue an RFP for a firm to assist them with cost estimates for some of the projects/needs they have identified. In June, she reported she was working on providing some requested information to the Board. She now says she has no new information, but hopes to by late August or early September. We'll follow up.

The legislature approved this project in a "supplemental spending" bill, contingent on adequate funding being available to move forward with them. This supplemental funding includes $185,000 for program planning to replace the Human Services Department's Youth Services Center. The earliest they expect to know whether or not funding is available for this project will be the third week in September. It is likely that the firm selected for program planning will continue with design when it's funded. The entire project will cost in the "tens of millions."
"Sometime soon," Fort Lewis College plans to advertise for architectural/engineering services for a new residence hall.

Pagosa Springs has hired RBC Dain Rauscher as bond counsel for a potential bond for a new recreation center. They're also working with Barker Rinker Seacat on some preliminary planning work. Mark says they may put a bond issue on the November ballot or, possibly, next April. If the project has sufficient community support, he expects they'll go through a competitive a/e selection process when they're ready for design. They won't initiate this process until after a public vote. We'll monitor progress.

The Authority recently advertised for a/e services for Park Avenue Redevelopment, Block 4B. Jinnell indicates that there will be additional phases of this redevelopment in the future. It is possible they'll advertise in late 2007 for home ownership units.

The Authority recently advertised for a/e services for redevelopment of Block 4B, Phase V of the Park Avenue Redevelopment project. Jinnell indicates that there will be additional phases in the future. She predicts they'll advertise sometime in 2008 for redevelopment of rental units.

The Englewood School District is beginning the planning process for future capital improvements. Through the sale of property, they expect to have some funds available for shorter term improvements, and are also thinking about a larger program that may involve a bond issue in a couple of years. They would like to complete a needs assessment process that would result in a list of priorities for both short- and long-term projects. Qualified firms interested in providing these needs assessment services may contact Peg LaPlante by email.

Denver's Department of Aviation requests proposals no later than 2:00 Monday, October 1 for financing, development and operation of a pet care and boarding facility at DIA. A MANDATORY pre-proposal conference is scheduled at 10:00 Wednesday, August 8 at the Green Valley Ranch recreation center, 4890 Argonne Way in Denver. A site visit will follow the conference. Documents are available at www.flydenver.com/diabiz/bizops/proprfp.asp .

This project provides for complete replacement of the main courthouse elevator. The elevator is experiencing an increasing failure rate. Some of the hydraulic and mechanical components are obsolete. Complete replacement with state-of-the-art components is the most cost-effective approach.
This project provides for development of a 4,550 sf nature/nordic center at Cucumber Gulch.

This project is contingent on funding through the legislature's "supplemental spending" bill, which will release funds as available in September. If they get the go-ahead, the Department will need consultant services to reroof their office building at Ft. Logan. It is possible they would use the state's as-needed contracts for this work.
The District plans to complete improvements at University Hill Primary School, as part of the bond program approved by voters in 2006.
As part of the bond program approved by voters in 2006, the District plans improvements at the Peak to Peak K-12 charter school, located at 800 Merlin Drive in Lafayette.

As part of the 2006 bond program, Boulder Valley Schools plans improvements at Arapahoe Ridge High School and Technical Education Center, a 121,631 sf facility located at 6600 Arapahoe Road in Boulder.
This project will complete improvements at the Boulder Preparatory (charter) High School, located at 5075 Chaparral Court in Boulder.
In addition to its funded capital plan, the City has developed a list of "high priority" unfunded projects. Improvements at the Senior Center is ranked #9 on this list.
The City's list of high priority unfunded projects includes the development of Venezia Community Park.

The water reclamation facility is 20 years old. Wastewater treatment is an inherently corrosive process, and many pieces of equipment operate continuously. This project will replace aging equipment and rehabilitate structures and piping at the plant.
This project will replace the 20-year-old membrane roof at the wastewater reclamation facility buildings.
The Town's capital plan includes proposed funding in 2008 to complete new office space for Parks & Recreation.
The Town proposes to design and construct a new indoor swimming pool, with expenditures estimated at $2.5 million in 2009 and $2 million 2010.
This Parks & Recreation project will complete an addition to the gymnasium.
In 2012 or later, the Town proposes to complete a new performing arts auditorium.
This project provides for a collections storage and exhibit building for the museum.
The Town plans to complete a new fishing and breakwater pier at Windsor Lake.
The County's budget includes a project to complete some stabilization and other improvements at Cardinal Mill. They plan to issue a design/build RFP soon for this work.

As we reported previously, the City's capital plan includes a project to relocate the wastewater treatment plant. Mike now says he has not yet begun preparing the RFQ, so does not have a specific ad date. He would appreciate it if consultants would not call or ask to meet with him at this time. He expects to solicit services to develop plans to be approved by the Colo. Dept of Public Health & Environment for phased construction. The first phase may be a pipeline between the old and new sites, including ROW acquisition.

We reported on this project previously. Robert had indicated an RFQ/P would be issued for design-build services to place a new roof on the historic Denver City and County building. The project will include roofing, drainage and historic preservation. Robert now hopes a design/build RFP will be released sometime around the 15th of June.

In February, we reported that DPS was looking into possibly running a capital projects bond in November of 2007. At this point, Larry indicates it is looking less and less likely they'll put a bond on the ballot this year, and more likely it will be November of 2008. In preparation for a new bond program, they typically create a prequalified list of architectural and engineering firms. They select firms from this list as projects are initiated. We'll continue to monitor the process.

We reported on this project previously. Wayne now predicts an RFP within the next couple of weeks for a/e services for a 5,000 sf, two-story building on a lot next to the existing fire training tower. The facility will provide for the training needs of Fire Department personnel and other departments. The building will include a large multi-purpose room, restrooms, a kitchenette and mechanical rooms. The second floor will consist of several smaller breakout rooms.

As we reported previously, the Airport's current five-year contract for airport engineering services will expire at the end of 2007. In April, Dave anticipated advertising within the next couple of months for a new multi-year contract. He now says the only project they expect to be funded, a taxiway resurfacing, will be handled under the current contract, so they have decided not to advertise this year to replace this contract.
records.Type: AS, DR, GT, MS, ST, SV, TR

records.Description: We reported on this project previously. Denver still plans an RFQ for on-call contracts for various engineering/design projects throughout the year related to general civil, structural and transportation engineering. Larry says the RFQ should be out within 30 days. They expect to select three to five firms to provide services as needed for three to four years.
records.Type: AS, BR, DR, ST, TS, TR

records.Description: This project calls for the development of a community park of approximately 81 acres within the Upper Clover Basin neighborhood. Design is scheduled in 2007 and Phase I construction in 2008. Design will explore joint facility placement with St. Vrain Valley School District on the Silver Creek High School property and park lands. Phase 2 design ($300,000) is currently scheduled in 2011. The RFP for master planning and phase 1 design should be out now or very soon.

RTD is finalizing the site selection/acquisition for a commuter rail maintenace facility. John had hoped they'd issue a design RFP in the late spring or summer. The latest information is that they still need to make some decisions about delivery methods and some other issues before the project can proceed.

We reported on this project previously. Fort Lewis College plans to seek architectural/engineering services for the College Union building. They may renovate the existing building, raze it and build a new building, or something in between. Mark expects to issue an RFQ within the next month or two.

We reported on this project previously. Bill indicated he would like to seek consultant services this year for a roofing design for the Justice Center roof replacement project. He hoped to develop a scope of work and cost estimates for construction in time to present them for budget approval in 2008. He now says "more than likely," this project will not be initiated until next year.

Previously, Bill reported that he had hoped to secure funding and look for an architecture firm to design a small building or shed to house the sanitary sewer lift station, plus mechanical engineering services to design better redundancy at the station. His latest information is that "more than likely," this project will not be initiated until 2008.

We reported on this project in April. At that time, Mike estimated a third quarter RFQ for a 20-year town-wide facilities plan. He now says he expects to release on RFQ on Monday, June 4. The plan will focus on both general municipal buildings and recreational facilities.

In April, we reported that the City expected to seek consultant services to design a concession building at Water Tower Park. Mark now informs us that the football association ended up designing the project to the City's satisfaction, so they will not require outside services.

In the fall, CU expects to advertise for architectural/engineering services for a new multi-purpose community center called the Center for Community, which will be a combined dining hall and office building (with a parking garage) on Regent Drive.

The County's capital budget for 2007 included $100,000 to complete a Bodo campus master plan. Janalee now reports that they have expanded the scope to cover additional properties - most but not all of the County's buildings. They're currently calling the project Space Needs Assessment Update and Conceptual Master Plan. The RFP should be out today or early next week.

Previously, the City completed the renovation of the ranch house at Churches Ranch. 2007-2008 funding provides for a master plan for future completion of renovations at the barns, silo and other outbuildings. Kim now reports that he's working on an RFQ, and it should be issued soon.

The Housing Authority's plans include redevelopment of Sun Valley, located at 990 Alcott Way. The area is near a stop on the light rail line. Jinnell reports that DHA is waiting for the City to formulate its transit oriented development plans for the area before the Authority moves forward with this redevelopment project. It is difficult to predict when that will be. We'll stay in touch.

As we reported in a Special Update in October of 2006, the Housing Authority's plans include redevelopment of the South Lincoln facilities at 1000 Osage Street. Before initiating the project, DHA is waiting for the City to develop its plans for transit oriented development in the area. It is difficult to predict when this project will move forward. We'll follow up.

In April, we reported that Greeley planned to issue an RFQ for general engineering on-call services, to cover a number of disciplines. They are now thinking of doing several separate RFQs, one of which will be for architectural services. These contracts may only be used for projects with fees up to $25,000. Steve predicts it will be another couple of months before the RFQ will be issued.
The County's capital plan includes a project to design and construct a new h20 pump station in District II with a MgCL tank. No specific schedule has yet been determined for initiating the project.

Grand Junction's City Council has approved funding for initial conceptual and preliminary design of a new police facility. The staff has begun preparing an RFP, which may be out in about a month. They emphasized to us that one of the selection criteria will be specific experience in designing police facilities (NOT just other municipal facilities, such as recreation centers or city halls, etc.). An alternate contact is Troy Smith (at the same phone #).

Kathie reports that the District will probably advertise around August for about five projects associated with the current bond program. We asked her if she could identify which projects and she responded that she could not at this time. We'll try to get more specifics for the next Update.

Within the next few months, the Department of Corrections should seek consultant services for a Controlled Maintenance project that will repair or replace cellhouse showers (Phases I and II) at the Buena Vista Correctional Facility.

Our project ID #63134 describes a "spring load restriction" program proposed by Rio Blanco County. Dave now reports that The Industry Group, a consortium of oil and gas companies, may want to take a different approach, which could involve a toll booth. If they pursue this, Dave has informed The Industry Group that it will have to hire consultants to complete any needed studies and come up with fee schedules, etc. The project could use the same funding originally planned for the spring load restriction project, but will not be managed by the County directly.

The legislature funded a Department of Military & Veterans Affairs project to complete code compliance and building system upgrades at the Pueblo, Colorado Springs and Sterling armories. Richard anticipates that a design RFQ will be issued within the next few months.
records.Agency: Colo. Dept. of Mil. & Vet. Affairs

records.Description: The legislature funded a project to complete a District Cooling Plant No. 2 at Colorado State University in Fort Collins. Tom Moss predicts a fall design RFQ.

No specific schedule has yet been established to initiate this project, but Greg reports that, "at some point," the County will require a complete justice center design. We'll follow up as plans and schedules are formulated for this project.

The legislature funded a Controlled Maintenance project that provides for various improvements at the Department's Insectary in Palisade, including roof repairs, replacement of the humidification system, balancing and HVAC work, and lighting replacement. We spoke with Joe Dean in April, at which time he said consultant services would be needed for this project. We were unable to connect with him prior to this Update, so did not get the latest information about timing of an RFQ.

The City's 2007 capital budget included $150,000 for master planning at the municipal service center the recreation center. Mike Brown in Parks says the funds were released within the past couple of weeks. He says he's not aware that anyone has been assigned the project yet. We'll provide additional information as we are able to get it.

Phil hopes for a fall design RFQ for heating and cooling plant improvements and the associated tunnel system. They have not yet decided whether to combine these two elements into one contract or to split them into two separate ones.

CU hopes to initiate the consultant selection process in the fall for an expansion of the Joint Insititute for Laboratory Astrophysics (JILA). The project will consist of a 40,000 sf addition which will expand the S wing and add office and lab space.

The District plans an addition to the Dakota Ridge High School building, to increase the capacity of the school to 1750 students. Kathie anticipates advertising for a/e services in the next few weeks.

We reported previously that the District might begin an architect selection by March for a new 50,000 sf branch library in Parker. They hired Muir & Associates as an owner's rep. The project will be combined with a Town performing arts center. The District and Town have identified 14 architectural firms they plan to invite to express interest and submit qualifications. In about June, they'll narrow the field to three to participate in a design competition. The winner will get the job and the two other firms $10,000 each for their participation.

We reported on this project in February. The Town's 2007 program includes a project to complete a new 1000 acre-foot raw/reuse water storage reservoir. Consultant services will be required for design. No timeline has yet been established to initiate the project.

As we reported previously, Erie's 2007 program includes a project to initiate siting, alternate siting, analysis and concept planning for a new Public Works facility. The cost estimate includes $400,000 for property acquisition, $525,000 for engineering and planning and $3.5 million for construction. Dennis reports they have not yet set a schedule for initiating the project.

We reported on this project previously. Black Hawk plans an RFP for design of a new 1 million gallon potable water storage tank. The project was delayed from 2006 due to some issues related to land for the tank. Philo now reports that they're still trying to secure some easements and it could be a few more months before they release the RFP.

We reported on this project previously. The District will plan/design a new branch library in Falcon. In February, Mike indicated they were waiting to find out if they'd receive a federal grant, and had recently had to redo the application. At this point he says there has been no change or progress on the project, and it may be six months before they're ready to issue an RFP. They plan a facility of approximately 4,000 square feet.

We reported on this project in February. The Town's 2007 capital budget includes a project to expand the water reclamation facility. Dennis reports that they received a $495,000 Dept. of Local Affairs grant and have begun some electrical and mechanical work. They expect to solicit and award other contracts later this year.

A remodel of the electric building's meeting room and break room area is planned to provide adequate facilities for the Longmont Power staff. The current meeting room was part of an addition to the Electric department in 1994. Since that time, staff members have been added and the authorized capacity for this room will be exceeded without additional space. As we reported previously, the project will require a/e services, but there's no specific schedule yet.

This project consists of evaluation and construction of improvements at the Wade Gaddis Water Treatment Plant to upgrade treatment processes for future water quality and to meet future demands. Specifically, it will consist of basin and structural repairs and replacement or rehabilitation of filters and control valves to maintain operation of the plant in the future. Cal anticipates a design/build RFP around July.

The University of Colorado at Denver & Health Sciences Center has advertised for design of a Pharmaceutical Research Center, which will be a new 105,000 sf building on the Fitzsimons campus. Mike now predicts a May advertisement for construction management/general contractor services.

The Library Board has directed staff to work toward putting a library funding question on the November, 2007 ballot. If the measure is successful, one of the projects to be funded is a new Castle Pines North branch. This would be a store-front type of facility of about 6500 square feet. Rob Muir of Muir and Associates (303-477-3430) is working as owner's rep for the district. If the ballot issue passes, they may begin architectural/engineering selection late this year or early in 2008.

We reported on this project in February. The Library Board has directed staff to work toward placing a library funding question on the November, 2007 ballot. This project is not in the current planning for the bond, but Jamie indicated that it could possibly be added. The historic research center is located in Castle Rock and the District is beginning to have concerns that it's not large enough. We'll monitor progress on this project.

Greeley plans to advertise an RFP soon with the intention of selecting engineering firms in various disciplines for onoing, on-call contracts. The contracts are expected to remain in place for three to five years. These contracts may be used only for projects with up to $25,000 in fees.
records.Type: AS, DR, MS, SW, ST, TS, TR, WR

records.Description: Within the next month or two, Steamboat Springs plans to advertise for consultant services for a Yampa River Structural Master Plan.
If the project is funded by the legislature, Northern Colorado University may need a roofing consultant for a roof replacement project.

Within the next few months, El Paso County may seek consultant services for a tenant finish project. George reports that he is unable to provide any more specific information about the project at this time, based on guidelines from the Procurement Department.

Within the next few months, El Paso County may seek a/e services for design of a parking garage expansion. George reports that, due to Procurement guidelines, he is unable to provide any more specific information at this time.

Previously, the City contracted with Integra Engineering to complete an evaluation of water quality issues associated with the Chautauqua water storage tank. Brad reports that the study is almost complete and he expects to have design needs. He anticipates issuing a design RFP within the next month or two.

The City's capital plan includes a 2007 project to complete Fox House development improvements. The plan indicates expenditures of $175,000 in 2007 and $900,000 in 2008. Mike indicates that the staff has not received the go-ahead to initiate the project. We'll follow up.
The University expects to advertise in April for design of the Norlin Library Information Commons project.

The County's capital plan includes a project to replace the gun range. Jim reports that they're leaning toward designing the project in house, but it's a bit too early to tell - they could possibly have consultant needs. We'll follow up.

The District is planning a new library in Highlands Ranch, if a financing measure passes on the November ballot. They have not yet developed a schedule for issuing a design RFP. The District has hired Rob Muir of Muir Associates as owner's representative. We'll provide additional information when available.

If a potential funding measure passes in November, one of the projects the District plans to complete is a branch library in Sedalia. The District has hired Rob Muir of Muir and Associates as owner's representative. Rob did not have an estimated time frame for issuing an a/e RFP for this project.

In 2005, Aurora planned a design/build RFP for the North Maintenance facility at Chambers & Smith Roads, which involves site improvements, a building remodel and a new traffic building. The project was subsequently cut from the five-year capital program. It is still identified as a need, but is not yet funded.
The City plans a new lift station and force main to provide sanitary services to the North Aurora growth area.
This project will expand the capacity of the existing pump station at the Kuiper Water Treatment Plant.
This project provides for a new Utilities operations and maintenance facility in the southeast area near Quincy and E-470.
This project provides for a sewer lift station and force main at the West Fork of Second Creek to serve the area near DIA.
This project provides for a new pump station in the vicinity of the Wemlinger water treatment plant, to accommodate new growth in Pressure Zones 4 and 5. The project may be designed in-house.
The City's capital plan includes a project in 2008 to complete improvemetns at Saddle Rock East Neighborhood Park.
This project provides for improvements at East Quincy Highlands Neighborhood Park.
The City has identified the need, but no funding, for a community events center and parking garage.
The City's Facilities and Services Master Plan, Phase II, identified the need for an eastern tier library. At this time, no source of funding is available for the project.
The Facilities Services Master Plan, Phase II, recommended an addition to the North Central Recreation Center. At this time, no source of funding has been identified to complete this project.

The City's Facilities and Services Master Plan, Phase II identified the need for a South Central area community recreation center and library. No source of funding has been identified to complete the project.
The City's Facilities and Services Master Plan, Phase II identified the need for a new south or southeast area maintenance facility. At this time, no funding is available to complete this project.

The City's Facilities and Services Master Plan, Phase II identified the need for a future animal shelter in the southeastern area of Aurora. The project is not funded in the current five-year program.

records.Project: Aurora Sports Park Champ. BB Field
records.Description: In the Phase II Facilities and Services Master Plan, the City identified a project to complete an Aurora Sports Complex championship baseball field. The project is not funded in the current five-year capital plan.
The City's Facilities and Services Master Plan, Phase II recommends southeast area athletic fields and buildings improvements. No source of funding has been identified to complete this work.
The City's Facilities and Services Master Plan, Phase II identified the need for an MJC remodel for Police Administration/District 2. No source of funding has been identified to complete the project.
This project, identified in the Facilities and Services Master Plan, Phase II provides for a new police station for District 2. At this time, the project is unfunded.
The Facilities and Services Master Plan, Phase II identifies a project to complete Phase I of a Public Safety complex. The project is not funded in the current capital plan.
The City's Utilities Department has programmed funding in 2009 for a central facility.
This project provides for a new water storage reservoir in the eastern part of the service area.

The District is currently completing projects as part of a bond program. In 2008, art, chemical, clock/bell, electrical, HVAC, lighting and food service area improvements are planned at the following schools/facilities: Arvada Middle; Bradford Primary; Columbine; Coronado; Drake; Fremont; Glennon Heights; Governor's Ranch; Kendallvue; Mandalay; Maple Grove; Martensen; Marchdale; Oberon; Peiffer; Pennington; Pomona; Pleasant View; South Area Transportation; Trailblazer Stadium; West Area Transportation; Westridge; and Witt.

The District plans improvements such as art, food service area, HVAC, electrical, clock/bell and paging & P/A system improvements starting in 2009 at the following schools and facilities: Bergen Meadow; Columbine Hills; Eiber; Foothills; Fitzmorris; Foster; Green Gables; Green Mountain High School; Kendrick Lakes; Peck; Red Rocks; Sheridan Green; Standley Lake; Stein; Stober; Stott; Ute Meadows; Warder; Westgate; and Zerger.

Jefferson County Schools plans improvements such as art areas, HVAC, electrical, lighting and clock/bell improvements in 2010 at the following schools and facilities: Green Mountain Elementary; North Area Transportation; Patterson; Prospect Valley; Slater; Stevens; Swanson; Weber; and Wheat Ridge Middle.
Jefferson County Schools plans a partial replacement of the Lifelong Learning Center at Longview, plus site drainage, lighting, utilities and traffic improvements.
The District's capital program includes a project in 2008 to complete a geotechnical/structural evaluation of Powderhorn Elementary.
The District plans building envelope and lighting protection (TVSS) improvements at Secrest Elementary.
The County has programmed funding in 2009-2010 for implementation of the facility master plan for a Public Works facility.
The City's capital plan includes proposed funding for the Ford Warren branch library. The project may be included in a bond issue in 2007 or 2008.

The City has allocated $60,000 in 2007 and a proposed $3,684,000 in the capital plan toward a police administration building upgrade/remodel. These funds are being accumulated until sufficient money is available to complete the project.

The City has allocated $338,000 in 2007 toward projects to renovate existing fire facilities. A total of $4,051,582 is proposed in the current capital plan. Funds will be accumulated until sufficient money is available to complete the work.

Last year, we reported that the County would place a tax issue on the November, 2006 ballot to expand jail/detention space. The tax measure did not pass, it will be at least a couple of years before they pursue this project. This will be a long-term project that will eventually require two tax issues, probably ten years apart. We'll continue to monitor it.
records.Type: AS, DR, MS, PK, SW, ST, WR

records.Description: We reported on this project in December. The City plans to acquire land for a full park facility to be determined by an updated Master Plan. The plan will look at the existing operation and provide cost estimates for moving the operation at the time of reservoir expansion. Dan is currently working on an RFP for the master planning; it should be out within the next few weeks. Acquisition and construction will take place after the master plan update. Neither is funded in the 2007-2011 capital plan. The cost estimate for acquisition is $1 million.
We reported on this project previously. David now he expects the Pitkin County (Aspen) Airport to issue an RFQ/P in late March for architectural services for design of a new terminal.

We reported on this project previously. It entails a feasibility study for a Colorado River Levee from Highway 50 to Highway 340. Don Newton now informs us the project has been postponed until City Council makes some land use decisions later this year. We'll monitor progress.

The District passed an $89 million bond on the November, 2006 ballot, primarily for two elementaries and two middle schools. The elementaries are prototype designs and one of the middle schools is started. Terry reports that they have not decided how to proceed on the second (future) middle school. They may decide to use a prototype design, or may advertise for new design services. Terry says he can't predict when this decision will be made, as they're focused on getting the current projects off the ground. We'll follow up.

We reported on this project previously. Ron now says he's not sure when they'll get started on the a new transportation facility. Escalating construction costs have created a budget issue. We'll continue to follow up.

As we reported previously, the District will require a/e services for design to remodel a church building to be converted to an alternative high school. Ron now says he's not sure when they'll be able to issue an RFP for architectural services. Escalating construction costs on other projects have put the squeeze on the budget. We'll continue to monitor progress.

As we reported previously, the City has selected a site for a new fire training center on 63rd Street, and has been using a consultant for conceptual planning. On November 7, the City passed a sales tax increase to fund this project. The County will also contribute $3.7 million. Glenn now reports that "things have changed" and they expect to issue an RFQ any day for architectural design services. They decided against the design/build approach. From the statements of qualifications submitted, they'll subsequently issue an RFP to selected firms.
DIA plans to remodel the existing Module 2, level 5 men's and women's restrooms. The RFP is currently in development, with no specific release date.

We reported on this project previously. Colorado Springs hopes to initiate design of a new fire station in the eastern part of the city. A specific site has not yet been selected. Curt indicates that the project may be initiated in 2007, but not within the next few months.

In December, Tom reported that, after the first of the year, the Town of Breckenridge might seek a/e services for design of a new child care facility. He now indicates that the project is still in the plan but they're not ready to issue an RFP yet. We'll follow up.

As we reported in December, Loveland plans to move ahead in 2007 with design of a new Fire Department burn building. They have developed a "fairly lengthy" list of criteria to be included in the building, following tours of several other area burn buildings. Ken now indicates they are reviewing information from a couple of firms and may decide to select a consultant without going through a formal RFP process.

Grand Junction advertised in late September for design of a water slide at Orchard Mesa Community Center Pool. They received no responses to the RFP. They plan to reissue the RFP as a design/build project. Shawn now indicates this RFP will be issued sometime this spring.

We reported on this project in December. Grand Valley Transit, in cooperation with Mesa County, now plans to advertise in March for design/build services for a new Grand Valley transfer/operatons facility. The project will involve funding from CDOT, estimated at $3.2 million.

We reported on this project previously. The City still plans a February advertisement for design of the Zone 3 pump station upgrade. The project consists of the design and construction of one 25 MGD booster pump station and associated piping to replace the existing large pump.
The County's capital improvements budget for 2007 includes a project to expand and remodel the court space for new district judges.

The 2007 capital budget includes funding for a facilities condition assessment, which will establish an inventory and facilities infrastructure asset mnagement plan for all major facility assets, including HVAC, plumbing, electrical systems and others. Samela reports that consultant services will be needed for this project, but no schedule has yet been set to initiate the selection process.

The 2007 capital budget includes a project to develop this existing Open Space park for a shelter and other improvements to provide quality educational opportunites. B. J. indicates that they may require architectural/engineering services for structural elements on the shelter. No specific schedule has yet been established to initiate the project.

In a December Special Update, we reported that Lance told us he expected to seek cm/gc services after the first of the year for the Capitol Office Building project. He now informs us that, with the change of administration, everything has to get reapproved, agency Executive Directors confirmed by the House and Senate, etc., and so everything is on hold. We'll follow up.

The County failed to pass a tax measure in November of 2006 that would have funded replacement of the old county courthouse in Loveland. They're now considering other options, including the purchase of a building in Fort Collins that may require a/e services for remodeling. He's not sure yet how large a project this might be (the $4-$5 million is his rough estimate). They're required to provide special storage for voting machines, with climate control, security measures including cameras, etc. We'll follow up as plans become more defined.
Brighton plans to seek consultant services in the next few months for design of a concession stand/office/storage building at the Brighton Sports Complex.

This fire station is a ranch house with an apparatus bay attached. The building needs to be remodeled to address current needs. The Town plans to advertise within the next month or so for a/e services. Modifications will include the addition of bay doors to the apparatus bay, added bedrooms and bathrooms, reconfiguration of the basement to meet the department's central supply needs and expansion of the driveway.

Robert reports that the Design and Construction Management Division's on-call architectural contracts will be up for renewal in late 2007 or early 2008. It is possible they'll renew existing contracts at that time, but will probably advertise. They'll enter into three contracts with maximum expenditures of $480,000 each. Sometimes they extend current contracts if they've been underutilized. We'll keep you posted.

We have mentioned previously the possibility that the Colorado Judicial Department would take over the location currently occupied by the Colorado History Museum and that the Museum would relocate. Joseph Bell recently informed us that the Historical Society has already pre-selected an architect for the new Museum, even though they have not selected a site and are not sure how or when it will proceed.
Adams State has one potential project programmed for this year: Renovation of the "Old Art" building for the Community Partnerships project.

The City's capital plan includes a new recreation center project. They're currently working with a consultant on a feasibility study. Depending on the study report and a bond issue going to voters in November of 2007, they will probably need a/e services in the future. We'll follow up.
This project provides for either the purchase or construction of a general storage facility at the airport to accommodate increased storage needs within the Parks & Recreation Department.
As part of a long-term project that was begun in 2002, the City plans a 2010 project to complete a new finished water storage facility for the high pressure zone.
The City's capital plan proposes a project that will rebuild the western gate at the Botanic Gardens. The existing gate has degraded from weather and age.

Proposed renovations at the Botanic Gardens' Morrison Center include: installation of a new HVAC system; repair and return to function the restrooms; repair and return to function the electrical system; repair and return to function the greenhouse; and repair and return to function the classroom.

The current stage roof at Red Rocks does not blend with the environment and is in contrast with the historic architecture of the amphitheatre. This project will design and construct a stage roof that raises and lowers as needed for events and is in keeping with the architecture of the facility.

This project proposes to add a new west end entrance at the Coliseum. The orientation of the building puts the main doors at the east end and the main parking area at the west end. This project will design and construct a new entrance at the west end, in conjunction with other projects.
The barn is old and dilapidated. The City recommends either replacing the barn in its entirety or making aesthetic improvements by coating the exterior and upgrading the windows.

The concourse space is limited and doesn't provide adequate space for patrons and exhibitors. This project proposes to demolish the non-structural panels on the south and north side concourses and to add cantilevered additions providing additional square footage for exhibit space.
Limited food and beverage opportunities exist for patrons of the facility. This project will renovate the southwest corner of the concourse into a food court.

This project provides for exterior renovation of the main building at the Coliseum. Many areas of the concrete exterior have spalled and exposed structural reinforcement. The City plans to design and apply an appropriate surface coating or facade to the coliseum exterior.
The Coliseum has inadequate storage facilities. This project will construct an addition to the facility for needed storage.
The load-in facilities are inadequate, resulting in long, laborious load-in and load-out of shows. This project will widen the load-in ramp and doorways.

This project provides for restoration activities at Barnum Park, to include automating the existing manual irrigation system and building a new picnic shelter, restrooms and concrete walks meeting ADA standards. It will also also include renovation of an existing multi-purpose field.
This project provides funding for expansion of the Berkeley Recreation Center.
This project provides for the relocation of the Parks & Recreation Department's East Maintenance District Headquarters.
The City proposes a weight room addition (new wing) at Eisenhower Recreation Center. The new wing will also provide additional space for other acitivities.
This project provides for a major expansion of the outdoor swimming pool at Garfield Park.

This project will relocate the Parks & Recreation Department's Northwest District maintenance headquarters. The facility will be moved out of Sloan's Lake Park to a new facility, location to be determined. The most promising sites are currently considered to be in the vicinity of 46th and Pecos. The project could entail construction of a new facility or rehabilitation of an existing building.
The Parks & Recreation Department's capital plan includes proposed funding for development of Weir Gulch Park, in accordance with the master plan.
The City hopes to replace the Buffalo Bill Museum Building with a new structure.

The existing Iowa Avenue underpass between Acoma Street and Santa Fe Drive provides a grade separated crossing of the Consolidated Main Line (CML) and the RTD light rail tracks for bike route D-18. This project will reconstruct the existing sidewalk on the north side of the Iowa Avenue underpass to make it ADA compliant. The existing sidewalk and staircases will be removed. Retaining wall reconstruction will allow for construction of a new sidewalk/bikeway with a wheelchair accessible profile.
The Police Department proposes to replace its Gang Bureau facility. The current facility has inadequate space. A new location has not yet been determined.
The Police Department has proposed a project to replace its pistol range. Relocation will be necessary to accommodate FasTracks facilities.
The University plans the renovation of Allison Hall, a 59,516 sf student housing facility.

This project provides for a remodel of 8,000 square feet of the third floor of the Gifford building for Food Sciences/Human Nutrition expansion. This project could be handled through a "standing order" as-needed contract used for projects with fees up to $50,000. The previous capital plan anticipated this project being completed in FY2007/08.
The University plans an addition/improvements to the 26,250 sf Painter Center, which houses Lab Animal Resources.
This project is the renovation of the 100,000 sf Aggie Village, which is occupied by Housing and Food Services.
This project will relocate the 10,000 sf food storeroom and bake shop. The previous capital plan listed this project in FY2008/09.
The University has identified the need to replace the elevators at this residence hall. The project was moved out one year from the previous capital plan.

The University's capital plan anticipates expenditures of $6.5 million per year for two years for this project, to renovate and expand the 27,253 sf Animal Sciences building. The previous capital plan anticipated an FY2006/07 project start.

This project provides for revitalization of the 100,700 sf Anatomy/Zoology building. The University anticipates requesting $1,608,000 to initiate the project in FY2010/11. Additional funding would be required the following fiscal year.

This project provides for renovation of and an addition to the Plant Environmental Research Center (PERC) at CSU, which houses Horticulture and Landscape Architecture. The project involves 2,000 square feet. The previous capital plan listed the project in FY2009/10.

This project provides for a computer systems disaster recovery cold site. If the current procedures are still in place in FY2008/09, the University could select any needed consultants from the state's as-needed standing order contracts.
This project provides for clock tower and carillon system improvements at CSU.

The University's capital plan includes a project proposed in FY2010/11 for a new 80,000 sf parking structure to be completed in conjunction with the City of Fort Collins. The University's anticipated contribution to the project is $9.5 million.
This project provides for Project 3 to implement the Student Housing Long-Range Plan. The University anticipates a 71,400 sf building.
This project provides for HVAC and kitchen improvements at Bradford Primary Elementary School.
This project will complete food service, HVAC, clock/bell, access and electrical improvements at Edgewater Elementary.
The District's bond program includes a project to complete food service, HVAC, controls, clock/bell, access and electrical improvements at Eiber Elementary.
The District plans to complete a partial replacement of Fruitdale Facility PRE.
This project provides for art studio, HVAC and plumbing improvements at Sheridan Green Elementary.
Improvements at Russell Elementary will include the art room, building envelope, code compliance and HVAC upgrades.
This project will complete improvements to the building envelope at Secrest Elementary.
Improvements at Stober Elementary will include the art area, building envelope and plumbing system.
This project will complete improvements to the art area and HVAC system at Ute Meadows Elementary.
The District plans improvements to the art area, electrical, HVAC, plumbing and site lighting at Westridge Elementary.
This project provides for improvements to the building envelope at Columbine High School. The projected start date is August, 2008 with completion in May of 2009.
The District plans improvemens to the building envelope at the North Area Transportation facility.
This project provides for a replacement facility and site improvements at the Facilities Services Shop location.
This project will complete a facility utilization study/concept plan for the Quail Street Service Center. The project is scheduled to start in November of 2009 with completion in December of 2010.

The entire greenhouse complex at the Botanic Gardens is over 35 years old and has reached its life expectancy. Almost 80% of the structures cannot be repaired given the age, moisture damage and system degradation. The existing single pane glass and single wall construction make energy efficiency impossible.
This project will fix the leaky roof on the arcade building at the Denver Coliseum.
Limited food and beverage opportunities exist for patrons of the Coliseum. This project will upgrade existing concession space in conjunction with other projects.
This project provides for concourse restroom upgrades at the Coliseum. The current restrooms are antiquated.
Dressing rooms are antiquated. This project will design and construct new dressing rooms and a handicap ramp.
The Coliseum has limited kitchen facilities, restricting the ability to prepare catered functions. This project will design and construct catering facilities.
The City proposes to complete improvements to the backstage area at Red Rocks Amphitheater.
The City plans restoration of the historic Berkeley Park boat house.
The City proposes funding for an expansion of the College View Recreation Center.

records.Project: Civic Center Pioneer Fountain Pk. Imp.
records.Description: This project provides for Civic Center Pioneer Fountain area improvements.

This project provides for new restrooms at Cranmer Park. Based on the Restroom Master Plan completed in 2004, this park site meets the established criteria that warrant a restroom based on the amount of recreational activity for a particular location in the park.

Due to the narrowness of the entry and exit points at the main gate, the main entrance to the Botanic Gardens will not allow for rapid evacuation of visitors during an emergency. This has been identified as a major life/safety issue.
This project provides for rehabilitation of the Parks & Recreation Department's East District maintenance facility.

The City has identified the need to relocate and replace the Parks & Recreation Department's Northeast District office facility when the existing facility is converted into the new Stapleton District office.
This project provides for improvements to the Parks & Recreation Department's Southeast District headquarters building.

records.Project: St. Charles Rec. Center Weight Rm.
records.Description: The City has proposed funding for a weight room addition at the St. Charles Recreation Center.
This project provides for an expansion of pump station capacity to accommodate growth and increased demand on the water system.
This project will complete the Cherryvale pump station, to accommodate growth in demand on the water system.
The University proposes a project to complete the renovation of the chemistry lab - Still endowed chair. In the previous capital plan, this project was proposed in FY2006/07.
This project provides for a 1,353 sf cage wash facility at the Foothills campus. The previous capital plan listed this project in FY2006/07.

This project will revitalize and replace deteriorated items at the 55,461 sf Aylesworth Hall. A number of programs are currently housed in this building. Expenditures are estimated at $549,600 in FY2008/09 and $3,114,400 in FY2009/10.
This project provides for a food animal isolation barn at the Veterinary Medical Center. The project was moved out one year from the previous capital plan.
The University proposes funding in FY2007/08 for an ambulatory service center at the Veterinary Medical Center. The project was moved out one year from the previous capital plan.
This project provides for the second addition to the Student Recreation Center. The previous capital plan listed this project in FY2007/08.
This project provides for an equine isolation/CCU at the Veterinary Medical Center. The project was moved out a year from the previous capital plan.
The University proposes funding in FY2009/10 for improvements to the 7,655 sf Hartshorn Health Services facility.

records.Project: CO State Forest Svc. Multiple Dist. Office
records.Description: This project proposes improvements to Colorado State Forest Service multiple district offices, including Steamboat Springs. The five-year plan indicates funding of $1 million in FY2009/10. The total project cost estimate is $1,202,800.
This project will relocate the Lab of Public Archaeology (LOPA), which houses Anthropology. The project was moved out one year from the previous capital plan.
This project will expand programming and office space at the International Apartments.
The University anticipates a project in FY2010/11 to renovate the bathrooms at Edwards Hall.
The City's long-term plans include a new waver rider feature at Lincoln Park pool.

The University plans to request funding in the FY2007/08 fiscal year for improvements to this 59,000 sf building. Current building audits show that basid infrastructures, such as plumbing, mechanical and electrical systems are severely deteriorated and in need of replacement to satisfy code deficiencies, life safety protection and ADA compliance. The project was approved by the 2006 legislature and later vetoed by the Governor.
This project provides for Phase 1 development of Saccammanno Park.
The County's Human Development Department has identified the need for food distribution facility and warehouse improvements.
The current capital plan includes proposed funding in 2009 to either build a new grandstand arena or renovate the existing facility.
This project proposes to either move or build new barns at the north end of the Regional Park.
In 2005, Broomfield identified a project to develop a new outdoor pool. The project is currently on the upper third of the priority list of projects "awaiting funding."

records.Project: CO State Forest Mult. Dist. Office
records.Description: This project provides for Colorado State Forest multiple district office improvements, at La Junta and Golden.

In 2009-2010, the City plans to complete Phase III of this community park, which will build out the remainder of the 69-acre park site. The project will be designed and constructed for environmental and economic sustainability.

This project provides for the final design phase of a 2.3-mile extension of the southeast corridor light rail line to Lone Tree from its original terminus at Lincoln. This extension will include three new stations plus upgrading the 13 original T-Rex stations to accommodate four-car trains. It will also add 520 spaces to the Lincoln park-and-ride and add bicycle and pedestrian improvements at Arapahoe and Belleview.
records.Type: AS, DR, MS, PK, ST, TR

records.Description: This project provides for final design for an extension of the southwest corridor light rail line, for 2.5 miles, to Highlands Ranch, including a new end-of-line station at C-470 and Lucent Boulevard. The project will also include 1000 new parking spaces at this station. The project proposes a new staton at Bates Avenue in Englewood, subject to the City's agreement to share the cost, an additional 440 parking spaces at the Englewood City Center station, and station modifications to accommodate four-car trains.
records.Type: AS, DR, MS, PK, ST, TR

records.Description: Denver Water plans a future project to complete filter improvements at the Moffat water treatment plant.
This project provides for improvements to the recycle flow treatment process at the Moffat water treatment plant.
Based on population growth and trends, the City has determined that a new branch library will be needed in the Green Valley area of Northeast Denver.
Due to population growth and the need for new library services, the City has placed a priority on a new Latino Legacy branch in Northwest Denver.
Due to population growth and trends, the City has placed a priority on constructing a new branch library in the Stapleton area.
The City plans to modernize and increase capacity at the Solid Waste transfer site at Cherry. The facility as at capacity based on the current configuration.
This project provides for relocation of Facilities Management's Decatur facility due to the FasTracks project.
Working with Public Works, Facilities Management plans to move to existing locations or build a new facility.

An acoustical consultant has been working on a study of the concert hall and will make a number of recommendations for major facility renovations. This will probably require a mix of public and private financing. Improvements will include lighting, floors, bar upgrades, sound system reconfiguration, doors, chairs, roof replacement recarpeting, catwalks, etc.

The studio theatre project was value engineered out of the original construction project. The space was intended to be a studio theatre for tier III arts organizations to further the agency's mission of promoting and cultivatin arts groups within the city. The space is approximately 12,000 sf of core shell and unfinished space. The City has solicited a number of foundations and private organizations to contribute to the design and build-out of this space.
Facilities are inadequate for the large staff employed for events. Conference space is undersized. This project will upgrade existing space to be used for an employee break area and conference space.
The east district needs an additional recreation center to conform to the City's game plan and to meet citizen demand.
The Southeast district needs an additional recreation center per the City's game plan and citizen requests.

The City plans to install a new pump station in the vicinity of Zone 4 (near the Semper Water Treatment Facility), which will replace the current Silo pump station located at approximately 90th Avenue and Washington Parkway. The new pump station will increase redundancy in this part of the city and will better regulate water system pressures to an acceptable standard.

Staff is proposing to modify and update the Northridge water tank's cathodic protection system. The tank is located at 90th and Yates. The project will switch the system from a suspended anode system with access ports to a submerged bouyed anode system. The improvements will allow for the tank to be inspected while dry. The new system will provide better coverage of the tank interior and will not be affected by freezing water in the tanks. It also eliminates the need for multiple hand hold openings in the roof, enhancing the security of the water stored.

This project consists of demolishing and disposing of the former England water treatment plant buildings and structures in anticipation of development along the south Westminster corridor. The project is related to the development of a south Westminster non-potable system that may be located at the site.
RTD proposes a project in 2008 to complete a new bus operator training facility.

This project provides for replacement of the Stapleton park and ride with a new facility at Smith Road and Ulster. The project was proposed for 2008-2009, but is not included in the financially constrained Transit Development Plan.
RTD proposes park and ride improvements in Parker. The project was proposed to begin in 2008, but is not included in the financially constrained Transit Development Plan.
This project provides for development of the East Community Park.
The City's capital plan includes an unfunded project to develop a new public golf course.
This project provides for expansion of the Park Maintenance Center. At this time, no source of funding has been identified for the project.
Fort Collins would like to complete a new recreation center in the southeast portion of the city. The project is currently unfunded.
This unfunded project would develop a new neighborhood park in the eastern portion of the city.
This project would develop a new Edora maintenance facility for the Parks & Recreation Department. At this time, the project is not funded in the capital plan.
This project would complete a maintenance facility in the downtown area for the Parks & Recreation Department. At this time, no source of funding has been identified to complete the project.
Fort Collins would like to construct a new recreation center in the southwest area of the city. At this time, no source of funding has been identified to complete the project.
This project proposes to complete an expansion of the Fort Collins senior center. The project is currently unfunded in the capital plan.
The City has identified the need for a new sports park. However, at this time, the project is not funded in the capital plan.
The City of Fort Collins/Poudre Fire Authority has identified the need to complete a Fire training facility master plan. However, the project is not funded in the current capital plan.
The City's long-term capital plan identifies the need for a new parking structure in Downtown in the future. At this time, no source of funding has been identified to implement the project.
The City has identified the future need for expansion of the Transfort bus facility. The project is not funded in the current capital plan.
This project provides for the second phase of the traffic operations management center. The project is not funded in the current capital plan.

This currently unfunded project (PR-18) calls for the development of McCall Lake into a nature/park site including parking, semi-improved trails, restrooms and picnic facilities. The project first appeared in the capital plan in 1989.

This plant's current capacity is 13 mgd, with effective treatment of 11-12 mgd due to backwashing. The plant was designed for expansion in 5 mgd increments. This proposed expansion of 5mgd would bring the plant's capacity to 18 mgd, which would meet the City's demand under existing or proposed development. The current plan is for design in 2011 and construction in 2012.

This project provides for a new booster pumping station. The current capital plan indicates that the existing station was to be upgraded in 2006 as an interim measure, then replaced in 2008. The new station will serve the Yellow and Blue zones and will transmit water to Reservoir 3, which serves the Purple zone. The project will enable the Town to eliminate the old pump station at Reservoir 2.
This unfunded project will design, build and equip a new fire station at 11th and Terry. It will include administrative offices and a community room.

This project, unfunded but proposed in the 2007-2011 capital plan, will complete the Memorial Park Aquatic & Fitness Center. The project includes renovating the obsolete pool at the Memorial Park Aquatic and Fitness Center into a gym. The new floor plan will provide opportunities for a wide variety of recreational activities.

This project, unfunded but proposed in the current capital plan, includes safety improvements, fire sprinkler system, ADA improvements, plumbing and electrical updates, HVAC repairs, resurfacing of flooring and interior and exterior renovation.

This project, unfunded but considered a high priority for 2007-2011, includes the restoration of deteriorated stonework, new tuck pointing to prevent further water infiltration, thorough cleaning of the stone facade, and repair/replacement of damaged stone blocks.

records.Project: New Fire Station at Wolf Ranch
records.Description: This unfunded project, provides for the purchse of land and construction of a new fire station in the vicinity of the Cordera and Wolf Ranch developments.
A building audit in 2005 indicated that minior repairs to electrical, plumbing, HVAC controls and the building envelope are needed. The project is not currently funded in the five-year program.

The City plans to increase the capacity of the transmission system with additional northern transmission line and pump station to supply future development. Funding for a study has been allocated for 2010.
This project provides for new permanent restrooms at Lake Arbor Golf Course.
Loveland's capital plan includes proposed funding beginning in 2009 for a new fire station in the eastern portion of the city. Expenditures are estimated at $250,000 in 2009 and $1,050,000 in 2010.

The City's capital plan indicates that the Golf Enterprise is proposing to issue $4 million in revenue bonds in 2009 to help fund construction of new clubhouses at both the Olde and the Mariana Butte Golf Courses. The cost estimate for both clubhouses is over $5.4 million.

The City's capital plan includes proposed funding for improvements to the maintenance building and club house at the Mariana Butte Golf Course. This project will be necessary if the Golf Enterprise does not pursue a revenue bond to replace this club house.
This project provides for a transportation museum for the city. At this time, the project remains unfunded.
The City's capital plan identifies the need for a future Fort Collins Museum storage facility. At this time, the project is not funded.
This project provides for restroom improvements in the ski resort base area.

The City's capital plan includes proposed funding beginning in 2008 for Barker Dam outlet repairs/improvements. Repairs to this system are necessary to assure safe and reliable water deliveries to the Betasso Water Treatment Plant from Barker Reservoir. Priority work includes repairs to the Barker gravity pipeline and the Barker-Kossler penstock.
The City plans for improvements at Buckhorn Lakes, including signs, restrooms, campground and road improvements.
The City's capital plan allocates funding in 2010 ($898,000) and in 2012 ($885,000) for major park development. Specific park projects will be identified as the fund years approach.
The capital plan allocates funding in 2010-2011 for development of a neighborhood park. The specific location will be identified at a later time.
The City's capital plan allocates $1 million in 2008 for new shops.
The City's capital plan includes proposed funding in 2010 for an expansion of the City shops.

The City's capital plan includes proposed funding to construct a restroom facility at the Cheesman Gate (west end of the grounds) of the Botanic Gardens. The existing port-o-lets product service and health issues for the public.
This project will replace the entire roof of the main building at the Botanic Gardens. The roof leaks. It is near high voltage lighting units, which creates health and safety issues.

The City plans improvements to Duck Lake at the Denver Zoo. Water quality is poor to the extent it creates a potential public and wildlife health concern. The project will dredge the lake, construct a wetland edge, install shoring at the island edge, repair the seat wall and install an aeration system.
The City's capital plan proposes a project to restore five Carnegie library branches to historic standards.
This project will plan and build a new court child care facility at the Justice Center site.
The City has identified the need to repair or replace the roof at Fire Station 25.
This project will complete reservoir/spillway improvements at Reservoir #3 at Pinion Mesa.
The City has programmed a future project to develop a multi-use regional park. The project is not funded in the current five-year capital plan.
The City's future plans include the design and construction of a community recreation center. The project is not funded in the current capital plan.
This project will improve the discharge at the dam at Enoch's Lake. The project is not funded in the current capital plan.
This future project will repair the breach in Reservoir #1. No source of funding has yet been identified to complete the work.
This project provides for repairs to Reservoir 1 at Pinion Mesa. The project is currently unfunded.
The City has identified a future need to build new city shops. The project is not funded in the current capital plan.
The City proposed, beginning in 2005, a major remodel of its comunity center. The project is currently considered the highest priority project that is still "awaiting funding."
In 2005, Broomfield identified a project to complete an upgrade to the water park at The Bay. The project is currently on the list "awaiting funding."

Broomfield first requested this project in 2005, which would develop a new multi-purpose competitive swimming pool. The project is currently on the upper third of the list of projects "awaiting funding."
The County's capital plan includes project in 2008 to upgrade the commercial kitchen at the fairgrounds.
This project provides for improvements to the horse barn at the fairgrounds.
The County plans to renovate the exhibit hall at the fairgrounds.
This project provides for construction of a household chemical collection facility.

Denver Water's capital plan includes a project beginning in 2011 to complete improvements to the Lower Chatfield Reservoir pump station. Expenditures are estimated at $200,000 in 2011, $1.2 million in 2012 and $1.8 million in 2013.

This project provides for conversion of the Elizabeth Street pump station to Capitol Hill pumping. Expenditures are estimated at $100,000 in 2010, $1.5 million per year for the next two years and $280,000 in 2013.
The Pinery Water and Wastewater District may seek consultant services in 2008 for design of a new pump station.
This project provides for a two-story addition to the Public Works Department's Roslyn Building G.
The City plans a new fire station in the Lowry/Windsor Gardens neighborhood to improve service delivery.

The City has identified the need for a new fire station in the Gateway Pena Corridor, to improve service delivery. The project is not funded in the 2007-2008 plan but is considered a priority for "one-time infusion" funding.
The City has identified the need for a new fire station to improve service delivery to the Stapleton North area. The project is not funded in the 2007-2008 plan, but is considered a high priority.
The City plans to complete an assessment to explore a regional police academy facility, to replace the existing Denver academy facility.
Denver plans to complete an assessment, then replace Police District 5's leased facility. They'll either purchase and remodel an existing building or build a new one.

The City plans to replace Police District 6's leased facility. Following an assessment, they'll either purchase and remodel an existing building or build a new one. The capital plan allocates $15 million for the purchase of land for a new station. The project is not funded in 2007-2008, but is considered a priority for a "one-time infusion" of funding.

This project entails a citywide Department of Parks & Recreation (DPR) resource assessment/infrastructure study. The project is listed in the "improving development review and permitting" project as being DPR's responsibility.
Repairs to the barn are necessary to keep the buildings from leaking and to maintain structural integrity.

This Parks & Recreation Department project will restore the historic structure and develop a public cultural institution. Other potential funding sources include the Civic Center Conservancy/private, SHF and other preservation grants.

The Parks & Recreation Department will partner with Public Works to restore this historic structure in Civic Center. Potential external funding sources include the Civic Center Conservancy/private, SHF and other preservation grants.
This City's capital plan includes proposed funding to replace the Northwest District maintenance facility, which is inefficient and inadequate.
This project will constuct a parking structure to add 200 off-street parking spaces in Cherry Creek North. Expenditures are estimated at $3 million in 2008 and $3 million in a subsequent year.

This project will construct a new operations and maintenance facility for Public Works streets, traffic, solid waste and stormwater operations. The City anticipates that this will be required by the displacement of the existing facility due to West Corridor light rail alignment and station construction.
